## PT-487 — ⚠ `1 / 4 / 8` is a DEFAULT, not a rule. The Cannok's chains written

### ⚠ `PT-438` recorded a convention that does not exist

**It says beast chains gate at Beast Master levels `1 / 4 / 8`. ⚠ I derived that from `Flurry` without reading the rest of `ATTACKS-05`.**

**The player roster gates by WHAT A CHAIN DOES:**

    Flurry · Dual Strike · Cleave · Critical Strike
    Power Attack · Quick Attack · Sweep Attack        1 / 4 / 8    ⚠ seven DAMAGE chains
    Guarding Stance · Parry                           1 / 6 / 12   control and reaction
    Disarming Strike                                  5 / 8 / 14   ⚠ PERMANENT LOSS

> **⚠ Seven of ten at `1/4/8`. The three exceptions are exactly the ones that do something other than damage.**

**Ruled: a damage chain opens at 1 and climbs at 4 and 8. A chain that removes a turn, or ends in permanent loss, climbs SLOWER.**

**⚠ This governs the ~60 beast chains still unwritten. `PT-438`'s `1/4/8` should not be applied to all of them.**

### The Cannok — two chains

    Worry → Wrench → Abscond    bite · CONTROL     ⚠ 1 / 4 / 12
    Rake → Flense → Shred       claw · VELOCITY       1 / 4 / 8

**⚠ Both axes are legal under `PT-486` — bite takes `Power · Control`, claw takes `Velocity · Precision`.** **I chose them at the Cannok's first draft, before the rule existed, and they happen to comply.**

### ⚠ `Abscond` gated at 12, owner ruling

**It DESTROYS an item permanently, and the Cannok is a TIER 1 beast available immediately.**

**`Sever`, its player equivalent, sits at level 14 behind `Strength 12` AND `Dexterity 13` — the only chain in the game requiring two abilities.**

**⚠ `12` rather than `14` because a beast's level is the MASTER'S BEAST MASTER LEVEL, not a character level.** **A Beast Master at 12 in their own class is deep into the build; a level-14 CHARACTER might be a 6th-level Beast Master multiclassing.**

> **⚠ The gate is on the DESTRUCTION, not the theft.** **`Worry` at level 1 is the Cannok's identity — `PT-239` set the same precedent for `Plunder`, which unlocks at class level 1 BECAUSE it requires dropping someone first.**

### ⚠ And the earlier draft of `Worry` was a different chain

**The version shown at the Cannok's first design used `+1d4 / +2d4 / +3d4` bonus damage. ⚠ That was a POSITION chain.**

**This is the CONTROL version: opposed rolls, no bonus damage at all.** **A `Str 10` scavenger was never going to win on damage. It wins by taking your things.**

### `Rake` is `Flurry`, halved

**Same penalties, same tiers, ⚠ TWO attacks instead of three.** **A beast has two forelimbs and no weapon.**

**⚠ Its dice fell at `PT-486`: the Cannok moved from `bite 1d8 · claw 1d6` to `1d6` / `1d4`.** **The chain states no dice, so nothing in it needed editing — but `Rake` now throws two `1d4`s.**

## PT-488 — Three beasts resized. ⚠ The K'lor'slug GROWS, and it breaks the acquisition table

### Three retyped to Medium — owner ruling

    Laigrek   Small -> Medium    bite 1d4/1d3 -> 1d6/1d4
    Shyrack   Small -> Medium    bite 1d4/1d3 -> 1d6/1d4
    ⚠ Mykal   Tiny  -> Medium    bite 1d3/1d2 -> 1d6/1d4

**⚠ AND IT FIXES THE PROBLEM THAT PROMPTED IT.** **Four tier-1 beasts read `Small · Str 6 · Dex 16 · bite 1d4 · claw 1d3` — identical in every combat number.** **Now only the Tach and the K'lor'slug's first band share a line.**

**⚠ `Mykal` at `Str 3` is now MEDIUM.** **The weakest Strength on the roster on a Medium frame.** **Flagged: `Str 3` was set when it was Tiny, and nothing has revisited it.**

### ⚠ The K'lor'slug is the first beast whose SIZE and TIER change

| Band | BM level | Size | Tier | attacks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **K'lor'slug** | 1–5 | Small | 1 | `1d4` / `1d3` |
| **Grown K'lor'slug** | 6–11 | Medium | 1 | `1d6` / `1d4` |
| **Great K'lor'slug** | 12–19 | **Large** | **2** | `1d10` / `1d8` |
| **Elder K'lor'slug** | 20+ | **Huge** | **3** | `2d8` / `2d6` |

**Dice read straight off `PT-486`'s grid at each band's tier AND size.** **⚠ Both climb together, which is why Medium → Large jumps `1d6 → 1d10`.**

**⚠ At Large it gains a THIRD attack chain; at Huge a FOURTH — `PT-438`'s count by tier.**

**⚠ `PT-430`'s bands were a RENAME with constants held.** **This is different: the constants MOVE.** **The Shyrack Wyrm is a bigger shyrack; the Elder K'lor'slug is a different weight class.**

### ⚠ `Squeeze` stops working, and that is the cost

**A Large or Huge slug cannot move through a space one size smaller than itself in any useful sense.** **Retained on the Small and Medium bands only.**

**It trades access for weight — which is the only thing keeping the growth from being pure upside.**

### ⚠⚠ AND IT BREAKS THE ACQUISITION TABLE

**`PT-431`: a Beast Master's beast levels with him. A purchased beast is fixed at its grade.**

**`BEASTS-01`'s acquisition table prices by TIER, and the apex beasts are gated at `DC 32` — *"cannot be bought, only earned."***

> **⚠ A Beast Master buys a K'lor'slug at TIER 1 PRICE and eventually holds a TIER 3 CREATURE.** **It is the only beast that crosses a tier gate the acquisition table exists to enforce.**

**⚠ NOT RESOLVED. Three ways out, none applied:**

**① Price it as tier 2 or 3 from the start** — expensive early, honest.
**② Cap the growth at Large** — it never reaches the apex tier and the gate holds.
**③ Accept it and mark the K'lor'slug as the deliberate exception** — a beast whose whole identity is that it outgrows what you paid for.

**⚠ Option ③ is the most interesting and the most exploitable.** **The owner should rule before any acquisition work is done.**

## PT-489 — The growth surcharge. `Mykal` at `Str 12`

### `Mykal` — `Str 3` → `Str 12`, owner ruling

**⚠ `Str 3` was set when it was `Tiny`. `PT-488` made it `Medium` and nothing revisited the number.**

**At `Str 12` its damage modifier goes `−4` to `+1`** — **a five-point swing on every attack**, which matters more than the die change did.

### The growth surcharge — ⚠ TRIPLE PRICE, same DC

**A beast whose SIZE and TIER change with its master's level is bought at its CURRENT band's DC and at TRIPLE its current band's price.**

    tier 1 band    DC 15    ⚠  5,000–14,000     (was 2,000–5,000)
    tier 2 band    DC 24    ⚠ 50,000–140,000    (was 20,000–50,000)
    ⚠ owner trimmed 1,000 off tier 1 and 10,000 off tier 2 from the first draft
    tier 3 band    DC 32    ⚠ not for sale, as any tier 3

**⚠ ONE HOLDER: the `K'lor'slug`.**

> **⚠ You are not buying the beast in front of you. You are buying every beast it becomes.** **A tier-1 K'lor'slug at 6,000 credits is dearer than a Boma is worth.**

### ⚠ The PRICE carries the surcharge and the DC does not — deliberately

**Bonding a young slug IS bonding a young slug. The difficulty is real and present, and raising the DC would punish the wrong thing.**

**⚠ A SELLER who knows what it becomes charges for what it becomes.** **That is a market fact, not a difficulty.**

**⚠ And it preserves `BEASTS-01`'s own principle — *"tier is not a level gate. It is a difficulty and a price, and either one opens it."*** **The growth surcharge moves ONE of the two, which is what that sentence permits.**

### ⚠ The tier-3 band is STILL not for sale, and that is what saves the gate

**Nobody sells an Elder K'lor'slug.** **You grow one, or you do not have one.**

> **⚠ `DC 32`'s gate holds for everything except a master who raised it from the start** — which is the gimmick, and it costs twenty levels of commitment rather than credits.

**⚠ A rich party can still buy a `Great K'lor'slug` at tier 2 for 60,000–150,000 — more than the most expensive item in KOTOR 2 at 32,000, and more than a Boma.** **That is the ceiling money reaches, and it stops one band short of the apex.**

### ⚠ Priced against the corpus, per `BEASTS-01`'s own method

    794 priced blueprints   median 1,600 · 90th percentile 23,600 · most expensive 32,000
    tier 1 growth beast     ⚠ 6,000–15,000 — between the 90th percentile and the median
    tier 2 growth beast     ⚠ 60,000–150,000 — nearly five times the most expensive item in the game

**⚠ The tier-2 figure is deliberately absurd.** **It is the price of skipping twelve levels of raising one, and it should read as a bad deal.**

## PT-490 — ⚠ A FEAT MAY ADD AN ACTION. The tier-1 racials split three ways

### ⚠ The test is not *passive or declared*. It is *does it have three steps*

**`PT-428` ruled: passive is a feat, declared is a chain or a rider.** **Applied to tier 1, six of seven racials are declared actions and would all become chains.**

> **⚠ THAT WOULD BE PADDING.** **`Bore` is complete in one line — *it moves through stone, permacrete and durasteel at half speed, carrying nothing*. There is no natural tier 2.** **I sketched *"thicker walls, then carry something through"* and it existed to fill a shape, not because the beast needed it.**

**Ruled: a racial becomes a CHAIN only if it has three genuine steps. Otherwise it stays a FEAT.**

### ⚠ A feat may add an action — owner ruling

**`ACTION-ECONOMY-01` has five budgets: `Move` · `Action` · `Bonus` · `Gear` · `Reaction`, plus one free interaction.**

**A passive feat may add a NAMED ENTRY to one of them.** **⚠ It is still a feat: nothing is chosen at level-up and nothing escalates. It means the creature can do a thing on its turn that nothing else can.**

    Scrap-Eater      Action   destroy one unattended object of its size or smaller
    Dextrous Hands   Action   fetch, carry, or work one simple mechanism
    Bore             Move     movement may pass through stone at half speed
    Deep Hide        Move     may end its move underground, unreachable
    ⚠ Beneath Notice  none    purely passive — adds nothing to any budget

> **⚠ This is a general mechanism, not a beast one.** **It gives the corpus a third thing a feat can be, between *a passive modifier* and *a chain*.**

### The split — three ways, not two

    ⚠ CHAIN   Echolocation      range, uses per day, and detail all escalate
    ⚠ RIDER   Gnaw              it modifies a bite — PT-428's weapon-profile slot
    FEAT      Scrap-Eater · Dextrous Hands · Bore · Deep Hide · Beneath Notice

**⚠ `Scrap-Eater` was proposed as a chain and the owner ruled it a feat that adds an action.** **Correct: *destroy one object* has no second step that is not arbitrary.**

### `Echolocation` — the chain, and the check makes it interesting

    Echolocation   1    Action, 3/day.  Alertness vs Stealth, or DC 15 for an object
                        SUCCESS: everything within 12 squares, INCLUDING what is Hidden
                        ⚠ FAILURE: still maps everything that is NOT hidden
    Read the Echo  6    5/day, 16 squares — a success names WHAT KIND of thing it found
    Pierce        12    7/day, 20 squares — maps through walls, doors and closed ground

**⚠ A FAILED check is never wasted.** **The beast always learns the room; the check decides whether it also finds what is hiding in it.**

**⚠ Gated `1 / 6 / 12` — `PT-487`. A utility chain climbs like `Guarding Stance`, not like `Flurry`.**

**⚠ AND IT IS THE ONLY CHAIN ON THE ROSTER THAT IS NOT AN ATTACK.** **`PT-438` counted chains as attack trees; this is the first that resolves nothing against a Defence.**

### ⚠ The Shyrack's racial slot is now EMPTY

**`Echolocation` left the feat column for the chain document.** **The Shyrack holds `Swarm` and `Flyby Attack` from its tags, sonic on its weapon, and NO racial.**

**⚠ Second beast in that state, after the Laigrek.** **Both are next.**

## PT-491 — `Layered Armour`. `Regeneration 3`, Laigrek-only. ⚠ And "chitin" was mine, not the source's

### `Layered Armour` — the Laigrek's racial

**Its damage reduction applies to AREA EFFECTS, and on a successful Reflex save it takes NO damage at all.**

**⚠ The second clause is `Evasion`, reached by the opposite route.** **`FEATS-LIBRARY-01` line 87: *"training so complete that an area attack can be avoided entirely rather than merely survived"* — granted to the Scout at 6th level, `sct_granted`, `feat.2da`.**

> **The Scout DODGES. The Laigrek does not move and the blast does not get through.** **Same outcome, opposite cause.**

**⚠ Flagged: `Evasion` is a Scout class grant at 6th. A tier-1 beast has it at level 1.** **Defensible — the Laigrek is `Str 6` and does nothing else — but it is earlier than any character reaches it, and that is a choice rather than a slip.**

### ⚠ THE NAME — and "chitin" was never in any source

**Wookieepedia: *"the laigrek possessed a LAYERED AND ARMORED EXOSKELETON and six scythe-shaped legs... the back of their LAYERED ARMOR was composed of a shiny blue or black substance."***

**⚠ Neither *carapace* nor *chitin* appears in the laigrek article at all.**

> **⚠ AND WOOKIEEPEDIA'S `Chitin/Legends` ARTICLE LISTS THE SPECIES WITH CHITIN SHELLS — Sauvax, Gand, Geonosians, Killik. THE LAIGREK IS NOT AMONG THEM.**

**The only source calling laigrek armour *chitin* is a World Anvil homebrew page. Unranked.**

**⚠ Our entry's prose read *"Chitin out of proportion."* That was MINE.** **Rewritten to the source's own phrase.**

### `Regeneration 3` — locked to the Deadly Laigrek

    Regeneration 1    Tuk'ata
    Regeneration 2    Katarn · Laigrek
    ⚠ Regeneration 3  Deadly Laigrek band ONLY — no other beast may take it

**⚠ A rung with one holder is NOT the shape `aquatic` was cut for.** **`Regeneration 1` also has one holder. A ladder with one occupant per rung is a ladder; a TAG with one holder is a mistake.**

**⚠ AND IT CORRECTS `PT-430`.** **I reported `g_i_crhide018` as carried by `c_laigrek_deadly` and `c_laigrek_de_kae`.** **The BASE `c_laigrek` at `CR 8` carries it too** — so the laigrek regenerates at every band, and its `Regeneration 2` was always file-backed rather than assigned by taste.

**The file's `4` is still declined — `PT-454`. ⚠ The ladder reaches 3 and stops, so nobody builds the fourth rung later.**

### ⚠ Two things the lookup turned up that are NOT acted on

**The laigrek has *six scythe-shaped legs*, rears onto four to attack with TWO FORELIMBS, and has *jagged inner edges on knife-like lower limbs*.** **⚠ Nothing in the description mentions JAWS — its `bite 1d6` may be wrong, and both blueprints carry TWO `g_w_crslash002` weapons, which is a claw pair.**

**⚠ And `PT-432` made attack count a per-beast constant. The laigrek's file gives it TWO and nothing records that.**

## PT-493 — `scythe` added. ⚠ The natural-weapon vocabulary is OPEN

### The rule, stated generally — owner ruling

> **⚠ A beast's attack TYPES come from the beast.** **Not from its type, not from its size, and not from a template.**

**`PT-484` ruled this for the Iriaz and treated it as a one-off correction. It is the general case.**

### `Laigrek` — `scythe`, not `claw`

    PT-356 template   bite 1d6 · claw 1d4      ⚠ neither word is in any source
    PT-492            claw 1d6 · claw 1d4      the bite removed
    ⚠ PT-493          scythe 1d6 · scythe 1d4

**Wookieepedia: *six SCYTHE-SHAPED legs* · *the inner surfaces of its KNIFE-LIKE LOWER LIMBS bearing JAGGED EDGES*.**

**⚠ *Claw* was the template's word for anything that is not a bite. The source's word is scythe.** **A jagged blade is not a claw, and calling it one loses the only distinctive thing about how this creature kills.**

**⚠ Name-checked: the only three `scythe` hits in the corpus are my own QUOTATIONS of this source, in the two rulings above. Clean.**

### `scythe` takes **Precision · Power**

| Weapon | Axes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| bite | Power · Control | one mouth — it commits, and it holds |
| claw | Velocity · Precision | two of them, and they open things |
| **⚠ scythe** | **Precision · Power** | **a bladed limb. It cuts deep, and it commits.** |
| gore | Position | a gore that has not moved is not a gore |
| hoof | Control | knocks down, keeps down |
| tail | Spread | one sweep, everything adjacent |
| sonic | Spread · Control | no attack roll — an area and a save |

**⚠ Deliberately NOT the same as `claw`.** **A claw is fast and shallow — `Velocity · Precision`. A scythe is heavy and sharp — `Precision · Power`.** **They share `Precision` because both cut; they differ on whether the limb is quick or committed.**

**⚠ And it fits the beast: `Str 14`, two strikes, `armoured`.** **A Laigrek is not fast. It is armoured and it swings blades.**

### ⚠ The vocabulary is OPEN, and that is the point

**A new weapon type needs ONE thing to join the table: an axis assignment.**

> **⚠ `PT-486` fixed six types and read as a closed list. It is not.** **The list is whatever the roster's anatomies require, and it will grow as beasts are read properly.**

**⚠ Candidates already visible in the sources and NOT yet acted on:** **the Laigrek's *small horns on its back end* and *thorn-like mounds along its sides*; the Nexu's quills; the Dianoga's tentacles.**

### ⚠ Third template defect in three beasts

    Gizka      Dex 18   ⚠ its file says 10          PT-455
    Iriaz      claws    ⚠ it charges with horns     PT-484
    Laigrek    bite     ⚠ it has no jaws            PT-492/493

**`PT-356` derived every attack line from RCR's per-type tables without reading a single creature.** **Every beast read carefully since has been wrong.**

**⚠ Twenty-two have not been read carefully.**

## PT-494 — ⚠ The sweep begins. Katarn and Kinrath both wrong, both visible in data we already held

### `Katarn` — ⚠ WE HAVE THE WRONG SUBSPECIES, and the file said so

**Wookieepedia describes TWO katarns. The arboreal one climbs with spurs and opposable digits. Then:**

> ***"There was a small subspecies of katarn that populated the Shadowlands. These katarns had no climbing abilities, as evidenced by their four large trunk-like legs. They also had two small dangling manipulator arms... and TWO LARGE TUSKS. The reformed Revan battled several of these in his second trip to find the Kashyyyk star map."***

**⚠ THAT IS OURS. The KOTOR Shadowlands subspecies.**

    was     bite 1d10 · claw 1d8
    now     ⚠ gore 1d10 · claw 1d8

**⚠ And Saga says the arboreal katarn's bite is *"not particularly fearsome in combat"* — it is for rooting tree-burrowers out of bark.** ***"It will get as close as it can prior to pouncing, then attack with its CLAWS."***

> **⚠ ITS GAME FILE CARRIES `g_w_crgore001` — THE ONLY GORE WEAPON IN EITHER GAME — AND OUR ENTRY HAD NO GORE LINE.** **`PT-428` recorded that as a rider and never asked why a bite-and-claw creature had a gore weapon.** **The answer is that it is not a bite-and-claw creature.**

### `Kinrath` — ⚠ THREE defects. No bite, no claws, and it is blind

**Wookieepedia: *"Kinrath had FOUR LEGS and a leg-like, POISONOUS APPENDAGE COMING OUT OF THEIR FACES that they used to attack prey."*** **Saga: *"a long appendage sprouts from the face, ending in a sharp, poison-filled stinger."***

    was     bite 1d8 · claw 1d6 · strikes 2 · senses Darkvision · Tremorsense
    now     ⚠ sting 1d8 · strikes 1 · ⚠ senses BLIND — heat and smell

**⚠ ONE weapon, not two.** **Its `strikes 2` came from `PT-492`'s file read of `g_w_crslash009` — a GENERIC slash weapon the game reused.**

**⚠ `Darkvision` is wrong for the same reason it was wrong for the Shyrack.** **Wookieepedia: *"All kinrath had very small eyes, but they were still BLIND. They could sense heat."*** **Saga: *"Kinrath are blind and take no penalties due to Concealment and Total Concealment due to darkness."***

**⚠ AND ITS `venomous` TAG IS FINALLY EXPLAINED.** **The poison is not a rider on a bite. It IS the weapon.**

### `sting` — a seventh weapon type, **Position · Precision**

**⚠ It opens TWO axes from ONE weapon — owner ruling.**

> **A face-mounted spike only works by driving forward. The CHARGE IS HOW THE STING WORKS, not a second attack.**

**That keeps a one-weapon beast from being half a beast without inventing a limb the sources do not give it.**

### `Blind` — a sense, not a feat

**Added to the senses table beside `Scent`, `Darkvision` and `Tremorsense`.** **Holders: Shyrack · Kinrath.**

**⚠ It takes NO penalty from concealment or darkness — and it is HELPLESS against whatever defeats the sense it actually uses.** **Deafen a Shyrack; mask heat and scent from a Kinrath.**

### ⚠ Two for two, and both were visible in data we already held

**The Katarn's gore weapon has been in `BEASTS-FEATS-01`'s rider table since `PT-428`.** **The Kinrath's `venomous` tag has been unexplained since `PT-359`.**

**⚠ Neither needed a lookup to SUSPECT. Both needed one to CONFIRM.** **Fifteen beasts remain unread.**

## PT-495 — Katarn finished. Tail CUT. ⚠ And I had been reading search snippets, not articles

### ⚠ THE METHOD FAILURE, FIRST

**The owner asked whether I was reading the Wookieepedia entries. I was NOT.**

> **⚠ I had been reading SEARCH SNIPPETS — real page text, truncated and selected by a search engine — and reporting them as article reads.**

**`METHOD-RECORD-01 §1.5`'s READ/INDEXED distinction, and I was on the wrong side of it for every lore check in this sweep.**

**Both articles then fetched in full. ⚠ The snippets were ACCURATE, and the articles carried four things the snippets cut:**

**⚠ `Prima's Official Strategy Guide` is listed in the Katarn's sources AS KINRATH.** **KOTOR's own official guide conflated the two creatures. We carry both as separate beasts and at least one published source does not.** **Recorded so nobody later "corrects" us from it.**

**⚠ The Kinrath's scent gland is a MECHANIC, not colour:** ***"if an adventurer could remove this gland intact from a corpse and carry it about their person, many Kinrath would not perceive them as a threat."*** **That is Ahrnell in KOTOR 2. A Beast-Master-adjacent tool nobody has written.**

**⚠ Kinrath blindness is confirmed by the PRIMARY article, not only the Saga wiki.** **`PT-494` was right for the right reason.**

**⚠ The Kinrath web-spitting is UNUSABLE — it comes from an UNFINISHED, CANCELLED Clone Wars episode shown at a convention. Below any rank in `CANON-01`.**

**⚠ AND `PT-494` MIXED TWO SOURCES AS ONE.** **The tusks are Wookieepedia. *"The bite is not particularly fearsome... it attacks with its claws"* is the SAGA EDITION WIKI — the same class of source that was homebrew-flagged for the drexl at `PT-443`.** **I cited them together as though they were one.**

### The tail — CUT

**Wookieepedia attests *"slender bodies with rodent-like tails"* for the MAIN katarn.** **⚠ The Shadowlands paragraph lists only what DIFFERS — no climbing, trunk legs, manipulator arms, tusks, rounder edges — and does not mention a tail either way.**

**⚠ The owner's in-game screenshot shows a heavy hunched quadruped with two large pale curved tusks. Lighting and angle show no tail and no forelimbs — which confirms neither.**

**Owner ruling: cut it. Two weapons is enough, and an inference is not a citation.**

### `strikes 2 per round`

**Four attacking limbs in the article.** **⚠ It resolves the contradiction flagged before writing: a `strikes 1` beast cannot hold `Rake`, which grants two claw attacks.**

### Three chains, FORCED by the weapons

    Pounce → Run Through → Impale    gore · POSITION      1 / 4 / 8
    Rake → Flense → Shred            claw · VELOCITY      1 / 4 / 8
    Open → Lay Bare → Unmake         claw · PRECISION     1 / 4 / 8

**⚠ `gore` opens ONE axis and `claw` opens TWO. That is exactly three, and there was no fourth option available.** **The first case where `PT-486` determined a beast's whole chain set rather than merely permitting it.**

**⚠ `Rake` is the SAME chain the Cannok holds.** **Deliberate — `PT-486` makes it the claw·Velocity chain for any clawed beast.** **The Katarn differs on dice, `strikes`, and everything else it has.**

**`Pounce` is `Forest Killer`'s attack half, where `PT-440` sent it.**

## PT-496 — ⚠ EVERY CHAIN ENTRY BUILDS ON THE ONE BEFORE. All twelve written chains corrected

**Owner ruling, after catching that `Pounce`'s upper tiers had dropped the movement requirement its tier 1 imposed.**

### ⚠ The defect, and it was in ten of twelve chains

    Pounce      1   "after moving at least 2 squares from concealment"
    Run Through 4   ⚠ NOTHING
    Impale      8   ⚠ NOTHING

> **⚠ Read literally, tiers 2 and 3 were free damage with NO movement requirement.** **A `Position` chain — where damage is BOUGHT with movement, `PT-333` — that stops requiring movement is not a Position chain.**

**⚠ And the Iriaz's was right only by accident.** ***"After the same movement"*** **worked; `Stampede` merely IMPLIED the charge.**

### The rule

**A chain is a LADDER. Tier 2 does everything tier 1 does, and more. Tier 3 does everything tier 2 does, and more.**

**⚠ An entry NEVER drops a condition its predecessor carried.**

    DAMAGE       +1d8 -> +2d8 -> +3d8     ⚠ each REPLACES the last
    RIDERS       prone · bleed · flat-footed   ⚠ INHERITED, and added to
    PENALTIES    attack and Defence       RESTATED, because they IMPROVE

**⚠ A tier that repeats its predecessor's damage is not an escalation. A tier that silently drops its predecessor's rider is a defect.**

### ⚠ And it answers a question `PT-486` left open

**`PT-486` did not say whether an AXIS CONDITION binds the CHAIN or each ENTRY.** **The two beasts written before this answered it differently BY ACCIDENT.**

**Ruled: it binds the CHAIN, stated ONCE at its head.** **An axis describes what the whole tree is FOR.**

### All twelve chains corrected

    Maw · Bite · Fling · Roar          Young Rancor
    Bull Rush · Stomp                  Iriaz
    Worry · Rake                       Cannok
    Echolocation                       Shyrack
    Pounce · Rake · Open               Katarn

**Each now carries a `⚠ CONDITION, binding every entry` line, and each upper tier states what it inherits.**

**⚠ One case is a genuine EXCEPTION and is marked as such: the Iriaz's `Stomp` requires a PRONE target at tier 1, and `Batter` LIFTS that restriction.** **A condition may be REMOVED by an upper tier — but only where the removal IS the escalation, and it must say so.**

### The regeneration ladder — named, `PT-496`

    Mend    1 vitality per turn        Tuk'ata · ⚠ Katarn
    Renew   2 per turn                 Laigrek
    Regrow  3 per turn                 ⚠ Deadly Laigrek band ONLY

**⚠ The game's own word for the property is `Regeneration` — strref 697, both games. The TIERS are ours.** **Numbered rungs were the only numbered ladder in the corpus.**

**⚠ The Katarn drops from `Renew` to `Mend` — owner ruling.** **`g_i_crhide005`, named *"Katarn Hide"*, gives it 2. A deliberate departure: it now has somewhere to grow.**

### `Pounce` renamed — `Pounce → Upend → Skewer`

**⚠ `Run Through` and `Impale` were the same image twice — the tusks going in.** **The EFFECTS are knocked prone and held immobile, which are different things.** **`Upend` is what a heavy thing hitting you low does; `Skewer` is being held on the tusks.**

## PT-498 — ⚠ `PT-496` was too narrow. Chains EVOLVE; only the COST is fixed

**Owner correction: *"it's not necessarily always that conditions and riders accumulate. Most times they do, but at the very least, they evolve — see the Force fear tree."***

### ⚠ The fear tree disproves "accumulate"

    Fear       one target · `cowering` · ⚠ a save NEGATES ENTIRELY
    Horror     5-metre radius · `cowering` · ⚠ a save leaves `shaken`
    Insanity   10-metre radius · `cowering` · a save leaves `shaken`

> **⚠ THE CONDITION DOES NOT ACCUMULATE. It is the same `cowering` at all three tiers.** **What changes is SCOPE — and the save outcome gets WORSE between tier 1 and tier 2.**

**⚠ `Horror` TAKES AWAY `Fear`'s clean negate.** **A rider was REPLACED, not added to, and the replacement IS the escalation — `PT-449`.**

### The rule, restated

**⚠ WHAT A CHAIN DOES IS FREE TO EVOLVE. WHAT A CHAIN COSTS IS NOT.**

    SCOPE       Fear -> Horror -> Insanity      same effect, wider
    INTENSITY   Mend -> Renew -> Regrow         same effect, more of it
    LAYERING    Pounce -> Upend -> Skewer       effect inherited, rider added

**⚠ THE ONE THING THAT MAY NOT CHANGE SILENTLY IS A CONDITION OF USE:** **the movement requirement, the opposed roll, the target-size limit, the uses per day, the prerequisite state.**

**Those are what the chain COSTS. Dropping one without saying so makes the chain CHEAPER as it escalates — the defect `PT-496` was written for.**

**⚠ A condition MAY be lifted where the lifting IS the escalation — the Iriaz's `Batter` removes `Stomp`'s prone requirement — but it must SAY SO.**

### ⚠ Nothing written needs changing

**All twelve chains were checked against the restated rule.** **`PT-496`'s corrections stand; only its STATEMENT was wrong.**

> **⚠ The narrow version would have made the fear tree — which is PORTED and correct — read as three defects.** **A rule that condemns the source is the wrong rule.**

## PT-500 — ⚠ `Dianoga` CUT. It is sentient, and it was never a companion

**Owner ruling. Roster 25 → 24.**

### The reason — it is not a beast

**Wookieepedia: *"Although primitive, they were actually SENTIENT, and some dianoga were sensitive to the Force."***

> **⚠ Some have NAMES.** **The one in the Death Star trash compactor is `Omi`, who had a Force vision, escaped a containment cell, and fought another dianoga over an egg exchange.**

**⚠ THIS IS NOT A FLAVOUR PROBLEM. `PT-459` split every effect in the game by target type — `sentient` · `beast` · `droid`.** **Mind-affecting powers work on sentients and not beasts. `Beast Control` works on beasts and not sentients.**

**Filing a sentient creature as a beast changes which powers work on it.**

**⚠ And a companion that THINKS is a different object from one that is TRAINED. You do not bond a sentient creature; you recruit it.**

### ⚠ Four more defects, now moot

**Found before the sentience question settled it, and recorded so the cut is not later mistaken for a stat dispute:**

**SIZE.** ***"They could grow to a length of 7 to 10 metres."*** **Our entry said `Large`. Ten metres is `Huge` at minimum, and size drives its dice, Defence and reach.**

**WEAPONS.** ***"Seven suckered tentacles surrounding a fanged maw containing a sharp serrated probe."*** **`tentacle` and `bite`. ⚠ NOTHING has claws, and our entry gave it `bite · claw`.**

**WATER.** ***"Entirely dependent on water, lest they completely dried out"* — open air for SHORT PERIODS only.** **⚠ Our entry gave it a 4-metre land speed with no penalty and no time limit.**

**CAMOUFLAGE.** ***"Evolved a form of natural camouflage… learned to change colour… their bodies would become transparent when unfed."*** **Nothing recorded it.**

**⚠ And its `burrowing` tag and `Tremorsense` were both wrong** — **it has an EYESTALK and lives in water. Ground vibration is a burrowing sense and the dianoga does not burrow.**

### What the cut touches

    BEASTS-ENTRIES-01   entry removed                        25 -> 24
    BEASTS-FEATS-01     `Lurk` removed · Tremorsense holders · Scavenger holders
    BEASTS-01           `burrowing` holders
    ⚠ Scavenger          4 holders -> 3: Cannok · Mykal · Gizka
    ⚠ burrowing          5 holders -> 4

**⚠ `PT-366` ADDED the Dianoga because *"RCR names it as its own `Scavenger` example and we had zero Scavengers."*** **`PT-454` then gave `Scavenger` three more holders. The reason it was added no longer applies.**

### ⚠ It belongs in `GM-CREATURES-01`

**In every appearance it is an ENCOUNTER — the thing in the compactor, the thing in the sewer under Xizor's palace.** **Never a companion, in any source.**

**NOT written there. The GM bestiary is unbuilt — `PT-497`.**

## PT-501 — `Young Boma → Boma`. ⚠ The document said so before the roster was built

### ⚠ THIS IS NOT A NEW RULING. IT IS AN UNAPPLIED ONE

**`BEASTS-01` line 115, written before the roster existed:**

> ***"Which means the same animal appears at more than one tier by age. A young boma is tier 1; a grown one is tier 2."***

**⚠ I have been treating the Boma as a fixed tier-2 beast for eighty rulings while the document that DEFINES the tiers said otherwise.**

### The bands

| Band | BM level | Size | Tier | attacks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Young Boma** | 1–11 | Medium | 1 | bite `1d6` · claw `1d4` |
| **⚠ Boma** | 12+ | **Large** | **2** | bite `1d10` · claw `1d8` |

**⚠ TWO bands, not four. It reaches tier 2 and stops.**

**Owner ruling: `Medium → Large`.** **⚠ Both size and tier climb, as the K'lor'slug's do — a young thing is smaller.** **A boma that aged without growing would have been the odd case.**

**Third chain at the band — `PT-438`.**

### ⚠ The growth surcharge now scales with the CEILING

    reaches tier 3   K'lor'slug    5,000–14,000  ·  50,000–140,000
    reaches tier 2   Young Boma    ⚠ 4,000–13,000  ·  ⚠ 40,000–130,000

**Owner ruling: `1,000` less at tier 1, `10,000` less at tier 2.**

> **⚠ You pay for the CEILING, not the creature.** **A K'lor'slug ends as something nobody can buy at any price. A Boma ends as a good tier-2 beast.**

**⚠ `PT-489` priced the surcharge as a flat rule with one holder. With two holders it needed a variable, and the ceiling is the right one.**

### ⚠ AND `Ramming Charge` IS STILL ILLEGAL

**It is a CHARGE. `PT-486` puts charges on `Position`, and `Position` is `gore`'s axis ONLY. The Boma has `bite · claw`.**

> **⚠ THE BOMA'S ONE DISTINCTIVE ATTACK CANNOT LEGALLY EXIST UNDER THE CURRENT RULE.**

**Proposed and NOT applied: open `Position` to `bite`.**

    bite    Power · Control · ⚠ Position     3 axes
    claw    Velocity · Precision              2
    sting   Position · Precision              2
    sonic   Spread · Control                  2
    gore    Position                          1
    hoof    Control                           1
    tail    Spread                            1

**⚠ A mouth can COMMIT, HOLD, or LUNGE. Specialist weapons trade breadth for identity.**

**⚠ THE COST: `bite` becomes the broadest weapon in the game and 20 of 24 beasts have one.** **The Katarn's *"three chains, no choice"* moment gets rarer — only `gore`, `hoof` and `tail` beasts keep forced sets.**

**⚠ The alternative — `bite` swapping `Control` for `Position` — BREAKS THE CANNOK, whose entire `Worry → Wrench → Abscond` chain is bite·Control.**

**Awaiting the owner's call. Until then the Boma's signature attack has no legal axis.**

## PT-502 — The `Reek` added. `Ramming Charge` relocated. Boma's tier-2 chain. ⚠ And `PT-500` deleted a header

### `Ramming Charge` had no horned home on the roster

**Checked all 24: ⚠ ONLY the Iriaz and the Katarn have horns or tusks, and BOTH already carry charge chains — `Bull Rush` and `Pounce`.** **Everything else is bite-and-claw, sting, or sonic.**

### The `Reek` — and it fills THREE holes

**Wookieepedia: *"powerful and territorial mammals with a SINGLE CENTRAL HORN atop their head and a CHEEK HORN ON EITHER SIDE. They lived on grass plains and turf and had POWERFUL HIND LIMBS FOR CHARGING."***

    ⚠ Ramming Charge gets a horned home        gore · Position
    ⚠ Herd Animal stops being a one-holder type  it had only the Iriaz since PT-486
    ⚠ a second mount                            Anakin rides one; `Bearer` applies

**`Herd Animal · Large · apex`. `gore 1d12 · hoof 1d10`, tier 3 Large per `PT-486`. `Str 22 · Dex 10 · Con 20`, speed 14 m.**

**⚠ A MECHANIC NOTHING ELSE HAS, not yet built:** ***"herbivores by nature, but often fed meat... this turned their leathery skin crimson and made the reeks MUCH MORE AGGRESSIVE."*** **A companion whose DIET changes its temperament.**

### ⚠ THE ERA CHECK DOES NOT PASS, and it is adopted anyway

**No attestation at 3956 BBY. It appears in *Attack of the Clones*, 22 BBY.**

**⚠ Subspecies exist on Kashyyyk and Ithor — both KOTOR-accessible — which helps placement and is not a date.**

> **⚠ A natural species presumably predates its famous appearance by four thousand years. PRESUMABLY IS NOT A CITATION.** **Same shape as `Deadly Sight` at `PT-464`, where the lookup FOUND the earlier attestation. Here there is none.**

**Recorded as the weakest-sourced beast on the roster.**

    Latch On   12   held — cannot move away, may still act
    Bear Down  16   held as above, and prone and flat-footed

**The page states it at the top: *"This article covers the Canon version of this subject. Click here for Wookieepedia's article on the Legends version."***

**⚠ Our project uses LEGENDS — `CANON-01`.** **Treated as INDICATIVE, not citable.**

**The Legends text held from search adds: *even-toed ungulates*, subspecies on **Iridonia, Kashyyyk and Ithor**, and horn variants developing poison at the tips.** **⚠ The anatomy and behaviour agree across both, which is why the retag stands — but the read was the wrong page.**

### `apex` REMOVED — a reek is a herbivore

***"Though naturally herbivores, a starved reek could become a ravenous meat-eater."*** **Arena reeks were fed meat DELIBERATELY to make them aggressive — that is HUSBANDRY, not ecology.**

> **⚠ `apex` grants the `Roar` chain and marks the top of a food chain.** **A reek is a rhinoceros: dangerous, territorial, and PREY.** **It gets hunted, ranched, chained, nose-ringed and ridden.**

**⚠ I gave it `apex` on the strength of *"tier 3"* and nothing else.** **Tier is a difficulty and a price — `BEASTS-01` — not a position in an ecosystem.**

### `armoured` ADDED — five holders, the joint-largest tag

***"Large thick-skinned… tough leathery skin… massive animals with heavy skin."***

**Holders: Laigrek · Wraid · Gundark · Duracrete Slug · Reek.**

### ⚠ `pack` CONSIDERED AND REJECTED

***"Reeks from the Codian Moon lived in small herds."***

**⚠ A HERD IS NOT A PACK.** **`PT-436` defined `pack` as COORDINATION IN HUNTING — attacking what an ally has already committed to.** **A herbivore herd is safety in numbers, not tactics.**

**⚠ Nothing on the roster covers herd behaviour, and it should not be forced into `pack` to fill the gap.**

### Speed `14 m` → `10 m`

***"Their sprawling posture and immense weight made them RELATIVELY SLOW-MOVING."***

**⚠ I had made it the fourth-fastest beast on the roster.** **A charging animal that is SLOW BUT HEAVY is the correct shape — the charge does the work, not the speed.**

### ⚠ `Scent` marked as INFERENCE

**The only mention is a BEHIND-THE-SCENES note comparing reeks to rhinoceroses — *"poor eyesight but a strong sense of smell"* — and the wiki itself tags it `[source?]`.**

**⚠ Editor commentary, not in-universe.** **Kept as plausible and marked.**

**⚠ POOR EYESIGHT is arguably the more interesting trait and is equally unattested. Not taken.**

### ⚠ The dice are unchanged

**`Herd Animal · Large`, tier 3 — `PT-486`'s grid gives `1d12 / 1d10` regardless of tag.** **Retagging touches what it GRANTS, not what it HITS FOR.**

## PT-505 — `Maalrass` → `Maalraas`. `Force-touched` RESTORED. ⚠ And I cut it on a misreading

### The spelling — Wookieepedia governs names

**Owner ruling: Wookieepedia has priority over the game files for the NAME of a thing.**

    ours   Maalrass    ⚠ one 'a', double 's'
    theirs Maalraas    double 'a', single 's'

**Renamed across four live documents. ⚠ `comms/` reverted — sent correspondence is a record, `PT-434`, `PT-444`, `PT-462`.**

**⚠ The talk page notes *"maalraas is both singular and plural."***

### ⚠ `Force-touched` was cut on a CONFLATION, and it was mine

**`PT-453` removed it citing *"`PT-368` already found its Force claim unsupported — the game files give this creature NO resistance of any kind."***

> **⚠ TWO DIFFERENT CLAIMS, TREATED AS ONE.**

    lightsaber RESISTANCE   ⚠ disputed. The talk page says so. PT-368 was right.
    Force CLOAKING          ⚠ NEVER disputed. It is the article's second sentence.

**A maalraas does not RESIST the Force. It USES the Force — to cloak itself.** **I took the disproof of one as the disproof of the other.**

### How it uses the Force — concealment, and only that

***"Using the Force to cloak themselves, making themselves nearly indistinguishable from the darkest shadows; only extremely well-trained Jedi or Sith could recognize their silhouettes."***

**One sentence. No elaboration anywhere in the article.**

### `Jungle Stalker` → `Nightcloak`

**⚠ `Jungle Stalker` was AUTHORED TWICE OVER.** ***"Dxun's night hunter — it hunts alone"*** **contradicted the source on the pack question, and its stalking was a weaker version of a cloak the source already described.**

**`Nightcloak` — `Force Camouflage`, three times per day.** **Only a character with Force training may perceive it; anyone else needs `Perception` at `DC 25`.**

### ⚠ A beast with a FORCE POOL — owner ruling, and it is a first

**Pool = `Wisdom modifier + Charisma modifier + Beast Master level`, minimum 8.** **`Force Camouflage` costs `FP 8`, so the floor buys exactly one cast from the start.**

> **⚠ ONLY THE MAALRAAS CASTS.** **The other three `Force-touched` beasts are PASSIVE — `Sith Hide` and `Force-Hunter Hide` are resistance, `Force-Clouding Bite` is a weapon rider.** **A `Force-touched` beast has a pool only if it CASTS.**

**⚠ This is the first non-character Force pool in the corpus.** **`FORCE-POOL-01-v3` computes from Force-CLASS levels and a `forcedie`, and a beast has neither.** **The formula above is authored and does not use `forcedie` at all.**

### ⚠ Two source problems recorded

**The article equates `Maalraas` and `Nighthunter` in its first line, then says maalraas were *"possibly the ancestors of nighthunters"* — contradicting itself.** **The talk page: *"some random wookieepedia editor decided to retcon two similar but not identical looking animals into being one animal."***

**⚠ The Force-cloaking and the lightsaber-resistance claims carry THE SAME FOOTNOTE `[1]`, in the same sentence block.** **The editor who checked `[1]` found blasters and heat but not lightsabers — and never said whether it supports the cloak.** **Probably sound; its citation is shared with a claim we know is misreported. MARKED.**

**⚠ The article's opening quote is Torian Cadera — SWTOR, which `CANON-01` EXCLUDES.**

### ⚠ Two findings NOT acted on

***"Easy to train from infancy or from older ages, Nighthunters were utilised as LOYAL GUARD BEASTS and were exported... by crime syndicates as well as other wealthy individuals willing to trade on the black market."***

> **⚠ THE ONLY BEAST ON THE ROSTER WHOSE LORE STATES OUTRIGHT THAT PEOPLE BUY AND KEEP THEM.** **The acquisition table, described in the source.**

***"Nursing the wounded nighthunter back to health, he named it CRANT, and kept it as a pet."*** **⚠ A NAMED individual maalraas kept as a companion by a Jedi. The best-attested companion beast we have, and I had been treating it as a generic Dxun predator.**

**⚠ And a dated in-era reference: *"In 3951 BBY, Mandalorian warriors living on the moon found maalraas to be harsh prey."* Five years after our setting.**

## PT-510 — Obedience. ⚠ A beast can refuse, and `Beast Handling` finally has a second job

**`rules/BEASTS-NATURE-01.md`. Owner ruling.**

### The rule

> **A beast obeys AUTOMATICALLY. ⚠ You roll ONLY when the order goes against its nature.**

**Attack, move, guard, hold, fetch, follow — no roll, ever.**

**⚠ THIS IS THE WHOLE DESIGN.** **A check on every command would slow a round to a crawl, and that mistake ALREADY COST THE PROJECT A REBUILD — `PT-201`, the Droid Master's `Command Protocol`.** **This fires a few times a SESSION.**

    Beast Handling vs DC 10 + 5 per tier    tier 1 DC 15 · tier 2 DC 20 · tier 3 DC 25

**⚠ A failure means the beast DOES NOT COMPLY — it holds, or does what its nature prefers.** **IT NEVER TURNS ON YOU.** **One attempt per order; try again next round.**

### ⚠ Deliberately separate from the bond DC

    bond        DC 15 / 24 / 32     once, to acquire        `BEASTS-01`
    obedience   DC 15 / 20 / 25     recurring, in play      `BEASTS-NATURE-01`

**⚠ A trait that improves obedience must not silently make a beast CHEAPER TO ACQUIRE.** **Three lore findings are already pressing on the acquisition table — the Maalraas *"traded on the black market"*, the Kath Hound *"prized as pets and guard animals"*, and `PT-489`'s growth surcharge. This does not add a fourth.**

### `Salkie` — now it does something

**`Its obedience DC is 5 lower.` Tier 1 becomes `DC 10` — nearly automatic.**

***"Normally docile, intelligent creatures who take well to training"*, said in numbers.** **And it travels with the beast: `15` at the horned band, `20` at the albino.**

### All 25 natures written

**Each beast gets a NATURE and TWO example refusals.** **⚠ Drawn from lore where lore exists — the Iriaz is prey, the Maalraas hunts alone, the Terentatek hunts Force-users, the Shyrack is blind and lives in a swarm.**

**⚠ Two beasts already carried a refusal in their own feat text and now duplicate the table: the Iriaz's `Skittish` and the Maalraas's `Jungle Stalker`.** **NOT reconciled.**

### ⚠ GREY AREAS ARE THE GM'S, AND THE APP MUST REASON RATHER THAN MATCH

***"Ordering an iriaz to walk PAST a sleeping katarn is not the same as ordering it to attack one — and it is not obviously different either."***

> **⚠ FOR THE APP: the model must reason from the beast's NATURE, not match against the examples.** **The examples show the SHAPE of a refusal.** **A system that only refuses on exact matches has missed the point.**

**⚠ AND: WHEN IN DOUBT, NO ROLL.** **The failure mode that hurts is a beast that balks constantly, not one that balks rarely.**

### ⚠ What this changes about the class

**A Beast Master is now a HANDLER rather than an OWNER. The companion can say no.**

**⚠ The fallback if that tone is wrong: keep the system, make failure cost an ACTION instead — the beast hesitates, you spend your turn insisting, it complies.** **Same skill, same DCs, no refusal. NOT taken.**

### ⚠ Three things left open

**Does a nature CHANGE? The Reek's lore describes one altered by husbandry — *"fed meat… made the reeks much more aggressive"* — and nothing models it.**

**Does a long-held beast get easier? Nothing tracks tenure.**

**⚠ And `Beast Handling` was used ONCE per beast, ever, before this. It now has a recurring job.**

## PT-511 — `Skittish` reconciled. ⚠ And a file marked DERIVED had no generator

### The two duplicates, resolved

**`PT-510` gave every beast a NATURE, and two beasts already carried a refusal in their own feat text.**

**`Skittish` — the refusal clause REMOVED.** **It now does one thing: an `Alertness` check at GM-judged intervals that warns you of danger.** **⚠ Its refusal to approach a predator is its NATURE, in `BEASTS-NATURE-01`, and no longer part of the feat.**

**`Jungle Stalker` — ALREADY GONE from the live documents.** **`PT-505` replaced it with `Nightcloak` and the maalraas's *"it hunts alone"* is now a nature entry.**

> **⚠ A feat says what a beast CAN DO. A nature says what it WILL NOT DO. Stating a refusal in both places means changing it in two.**

### ⚠ A FILE MARKED `DERIVED` WITH NO GENERATOR

**`BEASTS-REFERENCE-01` opened with *"⚠ DERIVED. Regenerate rather than edit."***

> **⚠ THERE WAS NO GENERATOR.** **I produced it once with a throwaway script and the script did not survive the message it was written in.**

**It rotted exactly as you would expect.** **By `PT-510` it still carried `Jungle Stalker` — withdrawn six rulings earlier — and a roster that predated the Dianoga's cut, the Reek's addition, and every tier move.**

**`scripts/gen_beast_reference.py` written. ⚠ `CONTENTS.md` has `tools/gen_contents.py`; this had nothing.**

### ⚠ Three defects found in the generator's FIRST run, and fixed in the SCRIPT

**⚠ TAG GRANTS WERE THREE-QUARTERS MISSING.** **The *"granted by"* column is written FOUR ways across `BEASTS-FEATS-01` — `` `tag` ``, `` `tag` — holders ``, `**tag**`, `**tag** — holders`.** **My first regex matched one of them, so `flying`, `swarming` and `pack` all showed as granting NOTHING.**

**⚠ ONE GROWTH BEAST WENT UNFLAGGED.** **The K'lor'slug's header reads `SIZE CHANGES WITH LEVEL` and the Boma's reads `SIZE AND TIER CHANGE WITH LEVEL`.** **Matching the literal phrase caught two of three.**

**⚠ TWO BEASTS LOST THEIR SENSES ENTIRELY.** **The Kinrath's and Shyrack's `senses` lines BEGIN with `⚠` — *"BLIND. Heat and smell only"* — and my annotation-stripper treated the whole line as annotation.** **The warning was the CONTENT.**

**⚠ All three were invisible in a table that LOOKED complete.** **A generator that silently drops data is worse than no generator, because the output carries the authority of being derived.**

### The regenerated file

    25 beasts · 3 growth beasts · 25 natures · 20 with racials
    ⚠ five with NO racial: Brith · Shyrack · Kinrath · Young Boma · Drexl
    obedience DC printed per tier — 15 / 20 / 25

### ⚠ Not registered in the gate

**`gate.py` does not check that `BEASTS-REFERENCE-01` is current.** **`audit_source` already checks `ATTACKS-05` and `FEATS-LIBRARY-01` against their generators; this one is not among them.** **It can rot again.**

## PT-512 — `Nightcloak` and `Scorched Hide`. `Jungle Stalker` CUT. ⚠ And a marker check that could not see staleness

### `Jungle Stalker` — CUT

**⚠ It has now been three different things and is none of them.**

    PT-437   authored as "Dxun's night hunter — it hunts alone"
    PT-505   REPLACED by `Nightcloak`, the ported Force cloak
    PT-512   renamed BACK to `Jungle Stalker`, then split off as a passive
             ⚠ and CUT — owner ruling

> **⚠ The name kept surviving while its content was replaced twice.** **A feat that has been emptied and refilled twice was never a feat; it was a slot with a name on it.**

**Its content lives where it belongs: *"it hunts alone"* is the Maalraas's NATURE in `BEASTS-NATURE-01`, and the cloak is `Nightcloak`.**

### `Nightcloak` — the contradiction resolved

    PT-505   "Force Camouflage, three times per day"
    PT-506   "Force pool 8 — exactly one Force Camouflage"

**⚠ THREE PER DAY OR ONE FROM A POOL OF 8? Both were written, one ruling apart, and I did not notice.**

**Resolved: `FP 8`, an action. THE POOL LIMITS IT. The `three times per day` is WITHDRAWN.**

**⚠ And it no longer BORROWS `Force Camouflage`, whose mechanic is wrong for it.** **Our `Force Camouflage` reads *"use their Stealth skill without a Stealth Field Generator"* — Stealth ENABLEMENT.** **The lore is stronger: *"nearly indistinguishable from the darkest shadows; only extremely well-trained Jedi or Sith could recognize their silhouettes."***

**Written as its own effect: until it attacks it cannot be seen — total concealment, untargetable by sight. A character with Force training perceives it normally; anyone else needs `Perception` at `DC 25`.**

**⚠ The `FP 8` economy — one cloak per day, no recovery rule for a beast pool — is DEFERRED to the beast level tables. Owner ruling.**

### ⚠ `audit_source` COULD NOT SEE STALENESS, ONLY MISLABELLING

**Its generated-document check asked one question: does the file contain the string `Generated by`.**

> **⚠ `BEASTS-REFERENCE-01` CLAIMED to be derived for eleven rulings while carrying a withdrawn feat.** **A marker check would have passed it every single time.**

**Now it RE-RUNS `gen_beast_reference.py` and compares the output to the file on disk.**

**⚠ TESTED BY BREAKING IT: a hand-edit to one row was caught, reported, and regenerated on the next run.** **The only check that catches staleness is one that reproduces the artifact.**

**⚠ `ATTACKS-04`, `ATTACKS-05` and `FEATS-LIBRARY-01` are STILL on the marker check only.** **Three generated documents whose currency is unverified.**

## PT-513 — `Brith` CUT. ⚠ It is a flying manta ray, and it is scenery

**Owner ruling. Roster 25 → 24.**

### What it actually is

***"The brith were a species of LARGE, FLYING CREATURES indigenous to the grassy Outer Rim world of Dantooine. Their FIN-LIKE WINGS gave them the appearance of SWIMMING THROUGH THE AIR."***

***"Characterized by their LARGE PECTORAL FINS and the twin lobes that projected anteriorly on either side of their broad head. They had SMOOTH SKIN, a BROAD, RECTANGULAR TERMINAL MOUTH, and a THIN TAIL. Their two eyes were located laterally, their GILLS ventrally."***

**A flying manta ray. Wookieepedia compares it to the Felucian flying manta and the thrantas of Alderaan.**

### ⚠ FOUR things wrong with our entry

**IT IS NOT A PREDATOR.** **Dantooine sources list it among the *"non-aggressive species."*** **Ours had it `Predator`.**

**IT HAS NO LIMBS.** **Pectoral fins, a thin tail, a broad terminal mouth — a FILTER-FEEDER'S mouth.** **⚠ Ours gave it `bite 1d4 · claw 1d3`. CLAWS ON A MANTA RAY.**

**It is LARGE. Ours had it Small.**

**⚠ AND IT IS NOT A CREATURE IN THE GAME AT ALL:** ***"Although the player CANNOT DIRECTLY INTERACT WITH THEM, brith can be seen flying above the plains of Dantooine."***

> **⚠ It is SCENERY. The name is never even spoken in-game — *"it does, however, appear in the game files."*** **`PT-356` built a `Small flying pack predator` from a filename and a per-type table.**

### ⚠ The option NOT taken

**Wookieepedia compares it to THRANTAS, which were RIDDEN on Alderaan.** **`Herd Animal · Large · flying` with the `Bearer` grant would have made it THE ONLY FLYING MOUNT IN THE GAME.**

**⚠ Nothing in any source says a brith was ridden.** **The thranta comparison is about APPEARANCE AND BEHAVIOUR, not use.** **That is an inference, and it would have been the second beast adopted on one — after the Reek, which had no era attestation at all.**

**Rejected. ⚠ One inference-based adoption is a judgement call; two is a habit.**

### The cut

    BEASTS-ENTRIES-01   entry removed              25 -> 24
    BEASTS-FEATS-01     `Scent` holders
    BEASTS-01           roster row · `flying` holders
    BEASTS-NATURE-01    nature row                 25 -> 24
    BEASTS-REFERENCE-01 regenerated

**⚠ `flying` drops to THREE holders: Mykal · Shyrack · Drexl.**

### ⚠ Second cut for the same underlying reason

**`PT-500` cut the Dianoga because it is SENTIENT. This cuts the Brith because it is NOT A COMBATANT.**

> **⚠ Both were on the roster because `PT-356` read a per-type table instead of a creature.** **The lore sweep has now cut two beasts and corrected five; twelve remain unread.**

### `Tach` — three corrections, and one thing already right

    was    Vermin · Small · venomous · 2 strikes
    now    Scavenger · Small · 1 strike

**⚠ NOT `Vermin`. It is a PRIMATE — Wookieepedia files it under `Category:Primates`.** ***"A small SIMIAN creature"*, *"a TREE-DWELLING PRIMATE… often found on the ground searching for overripe fruits."*** **`Scavenger` is the type that describes.**

**⚠ IT IS HARMLESS.** ***"More or less a harmless and curious creature."*** **Ours had it striking TWICE A ROUND — the same attack count as a Boma.**

**⚠ `venomous` CUT.** **The gland is IN ITS HEAD, near the brain, and is harvested AFTER DEATH** — *"sold for a high price… an excellent stimulant… the main ingredient in Tarisian ale."* **A VALUABLE ORGAN, not a weapon.**

**`PT-455` gave it the tag from `g_w_crslash010`'s `StrDamage`. ⚠ No source anywhere says a tach poisons anything.**

### ⚠ `venomous` NOW HAS ONE HOLDER

**THE GLAND IS AN ECONOMY.** **Griff Vao's entire subplot.** **⚠ A companion whose CORPSE is worth credits is a strange and interesting thing, and `Forage` and `Plunder` both exist without touching it.**

**TACH ESSENCE IS A LURE.** ***"Tachs were harmless except when a person was sprayed with a mist of tach essence. The essence ENRAGED local tach, inciting a desire to kill the person with it on them."*** **The only thing that makes a tach dangerous, and it is an ITEM.**

    BEASTS-ENTRIES-01 · BEASTS-FEATS-01 · BEASTS-01 · BEASTS-NATURE-01 · BEASTS-REFERENCE-01

## PT-515 — ⚠ ERA EXCEPTION for the `Duracrete Slug`. Rebuilt from the lore

**Owner ruling: keep it, and record the exception plainly.**

### ⚠ THE ERA GAP, STATED

**No Old Republic attestation exists.** **First appearance: `Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary`, 2002.** **Every source on its Wookieepedia index page is 2015 or later — `Build the Millennium Falcon` 2015, `Absolutely Everything You Need to Know` 2015, `The Visual Encyclopedia` 2017, `Dooku: Jedi Lost` 2019.**

> **⚠ The gap is ABSENCE, not CONTRADICTION.** **Nothing says duracrete slugs did not exist in 3956 BBY.** **That is a weaker warrant than any other beast on the roster has, and it is recorded rather than glossed.**

**⚠ SECOND era exception, after the `Reek` at `PT-502`.**

### Four replacements searched, all worse

    Rock Hound    ⚠ "burrowed into nearby rocks and would burst to the surface"
                  — mechanically PERFECT, and named only by a NINTENDO POWER article.
                  The game's own manual called them womp rats by mistake.
    Sandworm      ⚠ "Kaleesh BEAST MASTER Jai Quallo had a sand worm among his
                  PET BEASTS, trained to assist him in a fight" — our class, in the
                  sources. ⚠ AND THE CITATION IS SWTOR, EXCLUDED BY `CANON-01`.
    Stone mite    "a pest to archaeologists due to their habit of EATING STONE",
                  infested the Millennium Falcon. ⚠ Vermin-scale, and equally undated.
    Rock wart     Tatooine, one metre, venomous. ⚠ DOES NOT BURROW AT ALL.

**⚠ Every one fails the same test the Duracrete Slug fails, and most fail harder on sourcing.** **Kept because it alone has a real article, a described body, and a coherent reason to eat stone.**

### Rebuilt

    was    Vermin · Medium · bite 1d6 · claw 1d4
    now    Vermin · Large · ⚠ tentacle 1d6 · speed 4 m

**⚠ MOUTH TENTACLES, not bite and claw.** ***"The creatures used a series of mouth tentacles to sense their surroundings"*, and they have POOR EYESIGHT.** **Third beast whose `bite · claw` was a `PT-356` template invention, after the Iriaz and the Laigrek.**

**LARGE, not Medium.** ***"Three to five metres, up to ten."***

**⚠ AND `Bore` IS NOW EXPLAINED.** ***"They fed on the artificial stone duracrete, then after digesting it, secreted it from their bodies to form a hard outer shell."***

> **⚠ IT DOES NOT TUNNEL. IT EATS.** **Walls are food, and the shell is what it ate — which is why `armoured` fits this beast better than any of its four other holders.**

### `tentacle` — an eighth weapon type, `Control`

**⚠ It senses and grips. No reach, no cutting.**

**⚠ AND IT OPENS ONE AXIS, WHICH LEAVES THE SLUG ABLE TO HOLD ONLY ONE CHAIN.** **`PT-438` gives a tier-1 beast TWO.**

**`PT-494` faced this with the Kinrath and gave `sting` two axes because *"the charge is how the sting works."*** **⚠ No equivalent argument presents itself here, and I am not inventing one. FLAGGED, unresolved.**

## PT-516 — Obedience becomes a PER-BEAST value. The Nexu grows, and `Vicious` pays for itself

### ⚠ `PT-510`'s one-number-per-tier was too coarse

**It made a kath hound exactly as hard to handle as a maalraas.**

**`rules/BEASTS-OBEDIENCE-01.md`. TIER sets a BAND; the BEAST sets a VALUE.**

    tier 1   DC 12–18      tier 2   DC 17–23      tier 3   DC 22–28

**⚠ THE BANDS OVERLAP BY ONE POINT, DELIBERATELY.** **The hardest tier-1 beast — `Maalraas`, 18 — is exactly as hard to handle as the easiest tier-2 beast, the `Young Boma`.** **A solitary Force-touched predator IS as difficult as a simple ravenous one, whatever their COMBAT tiers say.**

> **⚠ Tier is DANGER. This is TEMPERAMENT.** **`PT-504` decoupled tier from SIZE for the same reason.**

    lowest    Kath Hound      12   "normally docile... take well to training"
    highest   Young Rancor    28   it has not learned what it cannot survive

### `Vicious` — ⚠ a feat that BUYS something with its difficulty

***"Too vicious to be kept in zoos and difficult to train as watch-beasts, they were instead sought after for arena battles."***

**Its obedience DC is `23`, the top of tier 2. ⚠ AND when it reduces an enemy to 0 or below, it makes one free attack against another creature within reach.**

> **⚠ A feat that ONLY raised the DC would be a PENALTY wearing a feat's name.** **The difficulty and the ferocity are the same fact, and the feat states both.**

### The Nexu — a THIRD growth pattern

    Nexu Cub   1–11   Medium   tier 2   1d8 / 1d6
    ⚠ Nexu     12+    Large    tier 2   1d10 / 1d8

**⚠ TIER DOES NOT CHANGE — only SIZE.** **The `K'lor'slug` climbs both; the `Kath Hound` climbs both AND gains a weapon; this one climbs size alone.**

***"4.51 metres long and typically 0.94 metres tall"* — a cub is not.**

### ✓ `Four Eyes` and `bite · claw` needed NOTHING

***"Only the forest nexu had an additional set of eyes able to view in INFRARED wavelength."*** **⚠ `PT-440` cut its invisibility clause and narrowed it to heat. That was correct.**

***"Claws which could slice a Human in half"*, *"biting down and thrashing their head about to break their victim's neck."*** **Second beast in the sweep whose weapons were already right.**

### Two things added, one thing refused

**`Quills` — *"a defensive mane of sharp quills… a difficult target to get a good grip on."*** **It cannot be `Carried`, and grappling it costs `1d4`.**

**It TIRES — *"known to tire easily, and often used swift movements to finish an enemy quickly."*** **After three consecutive rounds of attacking, `−2` until it spends a round not attacking.** **⚠ Nothing else on the roster fades.**

**⚠ Its forked tail is for CLIMBING and is NOT a weapon** — *"the tail also split into two equal sections for a better grip on the tree branch."*

### ⚠ THE HALF-MILLION PRICE IS CLONE WARS PRICING

***"Fees for live nexu often ranged up to half a million credits per animal."*** **Named buyers: Senator Ask Aak of Malastare and Archduke Poggle the Lesser of Geonosis — both ~22 BBY.**

**Wookieepedia: nexu *"EVENTUALLY became alpha predators throughout the galaxy."*** **The SWTOR codex dates the spread to *"the past few centuries"* — and that is 3,600 BBY, three centuries AFTER us.**

> **⚠ In 3956 BBY a nexu has not spread. It is a Cholganna animal that hunts bark rats and tree-climbing octopi.** **Priced at the tier-2 band like anything else — owner ruling.**

**⚠ Third beast whose lore states a price, after the Maalraas and the Kath Hound — and the FIRST where the figure had to be dated rather than adopted.**

***"A gundark was born with only TWO of its four adult arms, with the SECOND PAIR EMERGING DURING ADOLESCENCE."***

    ⚠ Gundark       12+    Large    1d10 / 1d8  ⚠ 2 strikes  ⚠ Four Arms

***"Its ears began to enlarge until, at PUBERTY, they reach the width of its head, hence the expression 'STRONG ENOUGH TO PULL THE EARS OFF A GUNDARK.'"***

***"Though not quite as intelligent as sentient creatures, gundarks were advanced enough to use SIMPLE TOOLS such as ROCKS AND CLUBS."*** **d6 gives them clubs as a weapon profile.**

### ✓ And `Scent` was already right

**d6: *"gundarks receive a bonus to Search: Tracking if scent plays a part."***

**⚠ Fourth beast whose lore states a trade: *"though it was illegal to capture or hunt gundarks on many planets, the creatures were often captured and sold on the BLACK MARKET."*** **After the Maalraas, the Kath Hound and the Nexu.**

## PT-519 — `Sith-Bonded` narrowed: SITH, not dark side

**Owner ruling. ⚠ `PT-518` keyed it to ALIGNMENT and that was too broad.**

    ⚠ SPECIES   Sith Kissai · Sith Massassi · Sith Pureblood
    ⚠ CLASS     Sith Warrior · Sith Inquisitor · Sith Assassin · Sith Marauder · Sith Lord

**⚠ And it stops the feat being a free bonus for a large slice of the party.** **`ALIGNMENT-01`'s `Committed Dark` and `Deep Dark` bands are reachable by any class; the Sith classes and species are a much smaller set.**

**Every feat until now reads off the BEAST. This one reads off the MASTER — and off two different properties of the master, either of which qualifies.**

**⚠ `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2` gives Sith Kissai and Sith Massassi a `Sith Bloodline` trait; `CLASS-ROSTER-01` carries five Sith classes.** **Nothing has ever asked both questions at once, and no check verifies that a beast feat naming classes and species names real ones.**

## PT-524 — `Colossal` added to the damage grid. ⚠ One size, one beast, one level

**Owner ruling: take the `Colossal` column, and it happens only at level 30.**

### The grid, extended

    ⚠ Colossal exists ONLY at tier 3, and ONLY at Beast Master 30

    tier 3   Tiny 1d6 · Small 1d8 · Medium 1d10 · Large 1d12 · Huge 2d8 · ⚠ COLOSSAL 3d8

**⚠ `3d8` averages 13.5 against `2d8`'s 9 — `+4.5`, the LARGEST single step in the grid.** **Every other step is `+1` to `+2.5`.** **Deliberate: nothing else reaches it, and a beast that has spent thirty levels growing should ARRIVE somewhere.**

### The Rancor

    Young Rancor   1–29   Huge         bite 2d8 · claw 2d6
    ⚠ Rancor       ⚠ 30   ⚠ COLOSSAL   bite 3d8 · claw 3d6

> **⚠ A Beast Master keeps a `Young Rancor` for TWENTY-NINE LEVELS and holds a `Rancor` for ONE.** **That is the point. The full-grown rancor is what the whole build was for.**

**⚠ And the Terentatek is the measure: *"approximately ONE-QUARTER the size of a fully-grown bull rancor"* — and the Terentatek is `Large`.** **Four Larges is past `Huge` in any reading, and the grid now says so.**

### ⚠ One holder — and why that is fine HERE

**`PT-359` cut `aquatic` for having one holder.**

> **⚠ THAT WAS A TAG. THIS IS A RUNG.** **`PT-491` already recorded the distinction: *a ladder with one occupant per rung is a ladder; a tag with one holder is a mistake*.** **`Regeneration 1` has one holder too.**

**⚠ A `Colossal` row with nothing in it would be dead weight. A `Colossal` row with the biggest beast in the game in it is a ceiling.**

### ⚠ The option NOT taken, recorded

**`PT-523` offered: make the adult Rancor a `GM-CREATURES-01` ENCOUNTER and let a Beast Master keep the young one permanently.** **The owner leans that way too — *"otherwise, I do lean too as well"* — and chose `Colossal`.**

**⚠ Both remain true in play: a GM may still run a wild adult rancor off `GM-CREATURES-01`, and `PT-497` already separates the wild creature from the companion.** **This ruling is about what a BEAST MASTER can reach, not about what exists.**

**Written because `PT-527` found `rulan_ter` had never existed.** **`audit_refs` verifies a backticked NAME resolves to a DEFINITION; nothing verified that a quoted GAME FILE exists.**

**This repo holds a SUBSET of the extracted data — 69 `2da` files where the project has 624.** **A naive existence check flags hundreds of CORRECT citations.**

    2da                  69 files   ⚠ SKIPPED — below the threshold of 100
    creature (.utc)     489 files   checked
    item (.uti)        1550 files   checked
    module              430 files   checked

> **⚠ Reporting *"cannot check"* is the HONEST output.** **Reporting a false negative as a pass is how `rulan_ter` survived ninety-three rulings.**

**⚠ AND THE THRESHOLD WAS WRONG ON THE FIRST RUN.** **I counted NAME VARIANTS, not files — each file contributes up to two names, so 69 `2da` files read as 138 and crossed the line, flagging eighteen correct citations.** **Fixed to count files.**

    c_laigrek           ⚠ not in the tracked corpus
    c_laigrek_deadly    ⚠ not in the tracked corpus

**⚠ `/tmp` survived this session and would not survive a restart.** **Same class of defect as `rulan_ter` — a claim resting on a file nobody else can open — caught before it rotted.**

**All 17 blueprints copied into `data/creatures/k2/`. The corpus goes 284 → 301.**

> **⚠ The check surfaced a real documentation defect, not a false positive.** **Corrected to `k2_cls_st_techspec.2da`, and the remaining unverifiable citation is now correctly reported as a k2 file we do not hold.**

**⚠ 592 citations · 591 verified · 1 correctly unverifiable.**

## PT-530 — ⚠ NO JEDI CLASS HAS A WEAK SAVE. Three `poor` claims corrected

**⚠ AND I OPENED THIS BY REPEATING A FAILURE I HAVE A RULE AGAINST.**

### ⚠ FIRST: two of `PT-529`'s three "findings" were already recorded

**`PT-529` said the Scout being strong on all three saves was *"not recorded anywhere in our class documents."***

> **⚠ `CLASS-TABLES-BASE` line 17: *"The Scout is the anomaly and it is the source's own. It has every save at the good progression."*** **And line 168 again.**

**`PT-529` also offered *"Sentinel and Guardian have IDENTICAL saves"* as new.** **⚠ `CLASS-TABLES-JEDI` line 32 has said so since it was written.**

**⚠ I ASSERTED ABSENCE WITHOUT SEARCHING.** **`METHOD-RECORD-01 §1.5`: *negatives must name their search scope*.** **I named none, twice, in the same ruling.**

### ⚠ AND SEARCHING PROPERLY FOUND A REAL ERROR INSTEAD

**Every k1 class table classified against `PT-119`'s three ladders:**

    cls_st_jedi_g    Strong  Strong  ⚠ HYBRID
    cls_st_jedi_s    Strong  Strong  ⚠ HYBRID
    cls_st_jedi_c    Strong  ⚠ HYBRID  Strong

    cls_st_cm_drd    Strong  Weak    Weak
    cls_st_ex_drd    Weak    Strong  Weak

    line 32    "Both are Fort/Ref good, WILL POOR. The Sentinel is not a save hybrid"

## PT-531 — ⚠ A chain need not be an ATTACK. Five shared chain sets written

### ⚠ The derivation exposed a structural problem before a line was written

**49 chains due across 18 beasts. ⚠ THREE BEASTS HAVE FEWER AXES THAN CHAINS:**

    Reek             4 due · gore · hoof    ⚠ 2 axes — Position, Control
    Terentatek       4 due · gore · claw    ⚠ 3 axes
    Duracrete Slug   2 due · tentacle       ⚠ 1 axis

> **⚠ THE MORE DISTINCTIVE A BEAST'S WEAPONS, THE FEWER CHAINS IT CAN HOLD.** **`gore`, `hoof` and `tentacle` each open exactly ONE axis, so the most SPECIALISED beasts are the most STARVED.** **The Reek is the most specialised on the roster and the worst off.**

### The ruling — utility chains fill the gap

**Where a beast has fewer weapon-axis combinations than chains, the remainder are UTILITY CHAINS.**

**⚠ ALREADY PRECEDENTED: the Shyrack's `Echolocation`, which `PT-490` recorded as *"the only chain on the roster that is not an attack… it resolves nothing against a Defence."***

**⚠ A utility chain obeys everything a combat chain obeys** — three tiers, a gate, and a CONDITION binding every entry.

**⚠ AND IT MUST COME FROM THE LORE, NOT FROM THE GAP.** **The Reek's diet altering its temperament and the Terentatek's dark-side hibernation are both attested and both unbuilt.** **Those are utility chains waiting for a home, not filler invented to reach a number.**

**⚠ REJECTED: chain count following AXES rather than TIER.** **It would make ANATOMY determine POWER, and a gore beast would be permanently weaker than a bite beast at the same tier.**

### Five shared sets written

    Maul → Gnash → Rend          bite · POWER
    Lash → Sweep → Scatter       tail · SPREAD        ⚠ Drexl LARVA only
    Coil → Bind → Engulf         tentacle · CONTROL   ⚠ Duracrete Slug
    Lunge → Drive → Overrun      sting · POSITION     ⚠ Kinrath
    Pierce → Puncture → Transfix sting · PRECISION    ⚠ Kinrath

**⚠ `Maul` is modelled on `ATTACKS-05`'s `Power Attack`** — *"a committed swing that sacrifices precision for force"*, `−3` attack, damage on the first hit, a save-or-prone rider. **The beast version trades the `Strength 12` prerequisite for nothing, because a beast does not CHOOSE its feats.**

**⚠ `Lash` HITS FRIEND AND FOE ALIKE.** **A tail does not know whose legs it takes, and that is the condition binding the chain.**

**⚠ `Puncture` delivers venom with NO SAVE on a critical.** **That is the reason a `venomous` beast wants `Precision` — `PT-455`'s ladder is a Fortitude save, and this is the only way past it.**

### ⚠ The point of shared sets

**`PT-487` established it with `Rake`: *"the same chain the Cannok holds… `PT-486` makes it the claw·Velocity chain for ANY beast with claws."***

> **⚠ 49 chains do NOT mean 49 bespoke designs.** **A beast is ASSIGNED from the shared sets, and gets a bespoke chain only where it has something nothing else has.**

## PT-532 — ⚠ A utility chain is a FIRST-CLASS option. Five tier-1 beasts assigned

### ⚠ The mechanical assignment produced a wrong answer, and it is worth recording WHY

**I enumerated `weapon × axis` and took the first N per beast.**

    Tach · Gizka · Mykal · K'lor'slug · Maalraas · Kath Hound
        ⚠ ALL SIX: bite·Power + bite·Control — IDENTICAL
    Hssiss · Nexu · Wraid · Gundark
        ⚠ ALL FOUR: the same three chains

> **⚠ TEN OF EIGHTEEN BEASTS GOT THE SAME CHAINS AS EACH OTHER.** **That is *"they all play the same"* returning through a different door — the thing the owner raised at the START of this workstream.**

**⚠ And several were absurd:** **`Maul` — a committed power bite at `−3` to hit — went to the `Tach`, which is `Str 6`, `Small`, and *"more or less a harmless and curious creature."*** **It also went to the `Gizka`, which is `Tiny` on `bite 1d3`.**

**⚠ The `Kath Hound` got bite chains and never touched the `hoof` it has or the `gore` it grows into — the picker took ENUMERATION ORDER.**

> **⚠ `PT-486` says which axes are AVAILABLE. It does not say which the beast should TAKE.** **With four combinations and two slots, every bite-and-claw beast collapses to the same pair.**

**A valid derivation of what is LEGAL is no derivation at all of what is RIGHT.**

### The amendment — owner ruling

    was    2 / 3 / 4 ATTACK chains by tier — `PT-438`
    now    ⚠ 2 / 3 / 4 CHAINS by tier, each an ATTACK chain OR a UTILITY chain

**⚠ `PT-531` made utility chains a FALLBACK for weapon-poor beasts. This makes them a FIRST-CLASS option for any beast.**

### Three utility chains written

**`Nimble Fingers`** *(Tach, `1/6/12`)* — works a mechanism with no check, then a `Security` or `Repair` task **using YOUR ranks and ITS Dexterity**, then lifts an item from an unattended container. **⚠ Nothing else on the roster lends a skill in either direction.** **⚠ It will do NONE of it while anything hostile is within 4 squares.**

**`Underfoot`** *(Gizka, `1/6/12`)* — moves through larger creatures' squares, then cannot be TARGETED while adjacent to one, then gnaws through an obstruction bypassing hardness entirely. **⚠ ANY damage ends all of it until its next turn, and `Con 4` means one hit usually does.**

**`Bore`** *(Duracrete Slug, ⚠ `4 / 10 / 16`)* — **tiered by MATERIAL, and the time is the material's:** earth at 1 round per square, stone at 1 minute, **durasteel and blast doors at 10 minutes.**

> **⚠ GATED `4 / 10 / 16` rather than `1 / 6 / 12` — owner ruling.** **A beast that walks through a blast door at level 12 is a key to every locked room in the game.** **The gate is what stops it being one.**

### ⚠ Four of five take a utility chain

**`PT-531` predicted THREE for the whole roster.** **⚠ Correct rather than inflation — half the tier-1 roster is scavengers and vermin the sources call harmless, timid, or indifferent.**

**⚠ TWO CHAINS STILL OWED: the Gizka's second, and the Mykal's `Unseen`.**

## PT-533 — The Kath Hound. ⚠ Its chain set GROWS, and the gore chains were locked to one beast each

### ⚠ FIRST: `Pounce` and `Bull Rush` were bespoke and should not have been

**Both are `gore · Position`. Both named their beast INSIDE the binding condition:**

    Pounce      "the KATARN must move 2 squares FROM CONCEALMENT"     ambush
    Bull Rush   "the IRIAZ must move 2 squares IN A STRAIGHT LINE"    open charge

> **⚠ They are genuinely DIFFERENT chains — an ambush and a charge — but the WORDING locked each to one animal.** **Any gore beast that ambushes should be able to take `Pounce`.**

**Both generalised to *"the beast"*. `Pounce` is the AMBUSH variant; `Bull Rush` is the OPEN-CHARGE variant.** **⚠ Caught only because the Kath Hound needed one and I would otherwise have written a THIRD.**

### The Kath Hound — four chains across three bands

| Band | BM level | Chains |
|---|---|---|
| **Kath Hound** | 1–11 | `Latch On` · `Stomp` |
| **Horned** | 12–19 | ⚠ **+ `Bull Rush`**, arriving with the tusks |
| **Albino** | 20+ | ⚠ **+ `Run Them Down`** |

**⚠ FIRST BEAST WHOSE CHAIN SET GROWS.** **`PT-509` gave it a WEAPON at the horned band; the weapon brings an AXIS, and the axis brings a chain.**

**`Latch On → Bear Down → Gorge`** — shared with the Boma. **A pack brings a thing DOWN; the hound HOLDS it.** **⚠ Gated `1/4/8` here against the Boma's `12/16/20`, because the Boma's chain does not exist until ITS band and this one does.**

**`Stomp → Batter → Trample`** — shared with the Iriaz. ***"Each limb ended in four-hoofed digits."***

**`Bull Rush → Run Down → Stampede`** — ⚠ gated `12/16/20`, arriving with the tusks.

### `Run Them Down` — ⚠ THE FIRST CHAIN THAT REQUIRES AN ALLY

    Run Them Down  20   a creature threatened by the beast AND an ally cannot
                        five-foot step or withdraw without provoking from both
    Cut Off        24   + it may move its full speed as a REACTION when a
                        creature it threatens tries to leave
    Bring to Bay   28   + that creature is `shaken` while it remains threatened

**⚠ CONDITION: an ALLY must threaten the same creature. ALONE, THE HOUND HAS NONE OF IT.**

> **⚠ Only `bite · Power` remained legal for a fourth chain, and *"docile, clever, and it wants to please"* argues against a fourth way to bite something.** **This is the beast that runs prey down WITH the party — which is what a kath hound IS.**

**⚠ `Pack Hunter` — the `pack` tag's grant, `PT-436` — is the PASSIVE version of this. `Run Them Down` is the DECLARED one.**

## PT-534 — Albino band CUT. The Maalraas gets an AMBUSH bite chain

### ⚠ The Albino Kath Hound is a COLOUR VARIANT, not a growth stage

***"Certain horned kath hounds were born ALBINO, and the rare albino specimens were the toughest of all kath hound subspecies."***

> **⚠ *BORN* albino. A hound does not GROW into it — it is a colour, and `PT-509` read it as a third band.**

**Two bands now: `Kath Hound` 1–11 tier 1, `Horned Kath Hound` 12+ tier 2.** **⚠ `2` chains then `3` — `Latch On`, `Stomp`, and `Bull Rush` arriving with the tusks. That is all of them.**

**`Run Them Down` is CUT.** **⚠ It was written for a fourth slot that no longer exists, and it was the first chain on the roster to require an ALLY — a shape that has now left the corpus.**

### The Maalraas — ⚠ it has NO GORE

**The owner asked for `Pounce` as a jungle-cat tree. ⚠ `Pounce` is `gore · Position` and the Maalraas is `bite · claw`.**

**Written as `bite · CONTROL` with an AMBUSH condition instead — the same SHAPE, on the weapons it actually has.**

    Take Down    1   bite +1d6, Reflex save or PRONE
    Bear Under   4   +2d6, prone as above, +2 on attacks against a prone target
    Throatlock   8   +3d6, and the target is HELD — it cannot stand, move, or SPEAK

    Worry      Cannok     it takes your THINGS
    Latch On   Boma       it holds you and EATS
    Take Down  Maalraas   ⚠ it puts you DOWN, from somewhere you were not looking

## PT-535 — The Laigrek. ⚠ `Rake` grants it a THIRD attack, not a second

### Its chains are FORCED

**`claw 1d6` · `claw 1d4` — the only beast with a MATCHED PAIR, `PT-492`. NO BITE AT ALL.**

**`claw` opens `Velocity` and `Precision`. A tier-1 beast takes two. ⚠ THERE IS NO THIRD OPTION AND NO CHOICE TO MAKE.**

**Third beast whose set was DETERMINED rather than chosen — after the Katarn at `PT-495` and the Kinrath at `PT-494`.**

### ⚠ `Rake` IS STRONGER ON THIS BEAST THAN ANYWHERE ELSE

**`Rake` reads *"two claw attacks this round instead of one."*** **⚠ THE LAIGREK ALREADY HAS TWO — `strikes 2 per round`, ported from `c_laigrek`'s two `g_w_crslash002` weapons.**

> **⚠ For this beast the chain reads THREE INSTEAD OF TWO, at the same penalties.** **Three attacks at `−4` where the Cannok gets two.**

**⚠ It is the ONLY beast on the roster for which that is true**, and it is a consequence of `PT-432`'s attack-count constant meeting `PT-487`'s shared chain. **Neither ruling anticipated the other.**
