## PT-618 — ⚠⚠ I RAN A GENERATOR THAT WROTE TO THE WRONG DIRECTORY, AND COMMITTED THE RESULT

**⚠ `PT-617` generalised `audit_source`'s derived-file check from ONE file to a LIST — and adding `FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md` to it made me RUN `gen_feats.py` TO TEST IT.**

> **⚠⚠ `gen_feats.py` WRITES TO THE REPO ROOT, NOT TO `rules/`.**

    _OUT = os.environ.get('KOTOR_OUT', abspath(join(_HERE, '..')))

**⚠ `KOTOR_OUT` IS UNSET, SO IT DEFAULTS TO THE PARENT OF `scripts/` — THE REPO ROOT.**

**⚠ IT CREATED A SECOND, DIFFERENT `FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md`:**

    ⚠ ./FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md          35,449 chars   258 entries · 93 chains
    ⚠ ./rules/FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md   107,622 chars   221 entries · 90 chains

**⚠ NOT COPIES. DIFFERENT DOCUMENTS WITH THE SAME NAME AND DIFFERENT COUNTS.**

### ⚠⚠ AND I COMMITTED IT

**⚠ `a2f8f11` CARRIES THE STRAY FILE.** **I read the gate output AFTER the commit ran in the same command — the gate said `DO NOT SEND` and the push had already happened.**

> **⚠ THE GATE IS ONLY A GATE IF IT RUNS BEFORE THE COMMIT.** **Chaining `gate && commit && push` in one shell line put the check and the action in the wrong order.**

**Removed from the index and from disk.**

### ⚠⚠ AND THE REAL FILE'S HEADER IS FALSE

**`rules/FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md` carries *"Generated by `scripts/gen_feats.py`. Do not hand-edit."***

> **⚠ IT IS HAND-MAINTAINED. Every feat edit this session — `PT-559`, `PT-568`, `PT-590`, `PT-615` — went into it BY HAND and none was lost, because the generator has never written there.**

**⚠ `PT-511`: *"a file marked DERIVED with no generator ROTS."*** **⚠ THIS IS THE INVERSE AND IT IS WORSE: A HAND-MAINTAINED FILE MARKED GENERATED INVITES SOMEONE TO REGENERATE IT AND LOSE EVERYTHING.**

**⚠ `FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md` IS EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED FROM `audit_source`'s derived list, WITH THE REASON WRITTEN IN THE SCRIPT.**

### ⚠ What the generalisation was still worth

**`CLASS-TABLES-AUTHORED.md` is now verified alongside `BEASTS-REFERENCE-01.md`.** **Two real derived files, both checked, and the third correctly kept out.**

**Owner: *"address the failures and fix whatever is causing them, making sure the failures aren't results of things functioning as intended."***

    PT-552   markers broke a machine-read HEADING        ⚠ CHECK RIGHT · I was wrong
    PT-570   a RATE table looked like a class table      ⚠ CHECK WRONG — fixed then

### ⚠⚠ AND THE GAP HAD BITTEN FOUR TIMES

**`audit_refs` builds its vocabulary from every document that DEFINES chains, feats, powers, species traits and tags. ⚠ IT NEVER LEARNED ABOUT CLASS NAMES OR CHASSIS NAMES.**

    PT-582   `Squad Protocol` · `Master Protocol`                 → unbackticked
    PT-585   `Protocol Droid` · `Probe Droid`                     → unbackticked
    PT-621   `Protocol` chassis                                   → unbackticked

**⚠ Same shape as `PT-466` (tags) and `PT-499` (section-format feats): THE OWNER DOCUMENT EXISTED; THE READER DID NOT.** **38 class names and 7 chassis names added. Backticks restored.**

### ⚠ AND THE CHECK IS NARROWER THAN I THOUGHT

**⚠ IT IS A KEYWORD HEURISTIC, NOT A VOCABULARY SCAN.** **It reports a backticked name ONLY if it contains `Attack`, `Strike`, `Shot`, `Fire`, `Sweep`, `Guard`, `Circle`, `Protocol`, `Instinct`, `Sneak`, `Ambush`…**

**⚠ `Protocol` IS IN THAT LIST — because `Command Protocol`, `Squad Protocol` and `Master Protocol` ARE REAL CHAINS.** **The chassis fired on a word that belongs to a feat ladder.**

**⚠ FIX TWO — my test — planted a fake name that contained NO KEYWORD, so it passed correctly and I read that as the check being blind.** **⚠ AND A `cp` RESTORE HAD ALREADY RUN BEFORE THE CHECK READ THE FILE, so the first test never existed at all.**

**⚠ Verified properly with `Nonexistent Strike` — reported, as designed.**

### ⚠⚠ AND RESTORING THE BACKTICKS FOUND A REAL BUG

> **⚠ `Squad Protocol` AND `Master Protocol` WERE NOT IN `feats_core.json` AT ALL.**

**⚠ NEITHER WAS `Command Protocol` — NOR `PT-201`'s ORIGINAL `Squad Doctrine` AND `Master and Servants`.** **THE ENTIRE LADDER LIVED IN MARKDOWN AND HAS NEVER BEEN IN THE FEAT DATA.**

## PT-629 — ⚠ PERCENTAGES CONVERTED. And the 320 hits were really 16 families

**`PT-475` queued this. `PT-559` and `PT-560` had already removed two.**

### ⚠ THE COUNT WAS MISLEADING

    ⚠ 320 raw hits
       102  ⚠ ITEM PROPERTY DUMPS — `DamageImmunity (Fire) 10%`
        34  probability tables — `FORCE-AWAKENING` shows a `d20` target
             WITH its odds beside it. ⚠ THAT IS A GOOD FORMAT.
        24  ⚠ ANALYSIS PROSE — *"62% of the round"*, *"18% behind"*.
             ⚠ REASONING, NOT RULES.
       ⚠ 16 FAMILIES of live mechanic

### ⚠⚠ I ARGUED THE 102 ITEM DUMPS WERE SOURCE RECORDS AND SHOULD BE LEFT. THE OWNER OVERRULED, CORRECTLY.

> **⚠ `ITEMS-03`'s `Properties` COLUMN IS WHAT A PLAYER READS AT THE TABLE.** **`DamageImmunity (Fire) 10%` IS a live mechanic, not an extraction artefact.**

**⚠ THE RECORD SURVIVES BECAUSE THE CONVERSION SITS BESIDE IT, NOT OVER IT:** **`DamageImmunity (Fire) ⚠ DR 2 (10%)`.**

**⚠ 103 CONVERTED ACROSS FOUR FILES. NONE LEFT.**

### The ladder — percentage ÷ 5

    5% → DR 1 · 10% → DR 2 · 15% → DR 3 · 20% → DR 4 · 25% → DR 5
    30% → DR 6 · 50% → DR 10 · 75% → DR 15 · 90% → DR 18 · ⚠ 100% → IMMUNE

**⚠ IT LANDS ON `PT-527` EXACTLY: the `armoured` tag is `DR 5`, and `DR 10` at Large.** **50% → `DR 10` matches a ladder already in use.**

**⚠ AND IT IS SLIGHTLY GENEROUS AT REALISTIC DAMAGE — 10% of a 12-point blaster hit is 1.2, and `DR 2` rounds up.** **It favours the player holding the item, which is the right direction for gear they paid for.**

### The feats and chains

    ⚠ Inner Strength · Ignore Pain   −5/−10/−15%  → `DR 1 / 2 / 3`
    ⚠ Master Toughness               −10% over 20 → a further `−2`
    ⚠ Emergency Reboot               10/25/50%    → 1 vitality · a quarter · half
    ⚠ Self-Diagnostic                +25/50/100%  → `+1d4` · `+1d8` · DOUBLE
    ⚠ Riposte · Bolt Return          +50%         → HALF AGAIN, rounded down

### ⚠ WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT

**⚠ `Killer's Instinct`'s *"20% chance on a critical"* — IT IS ALREADY A `d20` ROLL WEARING A PERCENTAGE. `17+`.** **A formatting fix, not a mechanic change.**

**⚠ Force ceiling degradation at `10/20/30% of cost` — `PT-475` TESTED AND HALVED THESE FROM `20/40/60`.** **The numbers are load-bearing, and a player computes them ONCE PER CAST off a figure already on the sheet.**

> **⚠ THE TEST THAT MATTERED: does a player compute this AT THE TABLE, or ONCE?** **A `−10%` on every hit is a tax on every roll. A `20% of cost` is one subtraction you were already doing.**

### ⚠ Three edits missed and were caught by checking

**⚠ `Inner Strength` AND `Ignore Pain` ARE NOT IN `feats_core.json` AT ALL — markdown only, like the `Command Protocol` ladder at `PT-622`.**

**⚠ AND FOUR ROWS HAVE TWO SPACES AFTER THE PIPE, NOT ONE — the same spacing trap as `PT-584`.** **Four `str.replace` calls matched nothing and reported nothing. Fixed by line number.**

## PT-630 — `Assassin Protocols` on a `d20`. ⚠ And it was NOT `Killer's Instinct`

**Owner: *"let's still say the d20."*** **⚠ `PT-629` ATTRIBUTED THE `20% chance` TO `Killer's Instinct`. IT IS `Assassin Protocols`.**

    was  ⚠ On a critical hit, 20% CHANCE to deal unstoppable damage equal to
         ¼ OF THE TARGET'S REMAINING LIFE
    now  ⚠ On a critical hit, ROLL AGAIN: on `17+` you deal `4d6` unstoppable
         damage. Fortitude at `DC 10 + your level` negates.

### ⚠⚠ THE SECOND PERCENTAGE WAS THE WORSE ONE

**⚠ `PT-629` SPOTTED THE `20%` AND MISSED THE `¼ OF REMAINING LIFE` SITTING BESIDE IT.**

> **⚠ A FRACTION OF A NUMBER THAT CHANGES EVERY ROUND IS WORSE THAN A FRACTION OF A FIXED ONE.** **`PT-475`'s complaint — *"a player must know a total, compute a fraction, and round"* — is at its sharpest when THE TOTAL IS THE TARGET'S CURRENT VITALITY, which the attacker may not even know.**

**⚠ `4d6` — average 14 — is roughly a quarter of a mid-level target and it is ROLLED, NOT COMPUTED.** **And it does not scale with how hurt the target already is, which removes a perverse incentive: the old version got WEAKER the more you had already done.**

### `17+` on a `d20` is 20%

**⚠ EXACTLY THE SOURCE RATE. No rebalancing, only a change of instrument.**

### ⚠ AND IT IS THE FOURTH MARKDOWN-ONLY FEAT THIS SESSION

**`Assassin Protocols` is NOT in `feats_core.json`.** **⚠ After `Command Protocol`'s three tiers at `PT-622`, and `Inner Strength` and `Ignore Pain` at `PT-629`.**

> **⚠ `FEATS-LIBRARY-01.md` AND `feats_core.json` HAVE DIVERGED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND NOTHING CHECKS IT.** **`audit_featsplit` verifies the two COPIES of the JSON match each other — it does NOT verify the JSON matches the MARKDOWN.**

**⚠ RECORDED. That check does not exist and should.**

## PT-641 — ⚠ `audit_status.py`, check 34. The gap the OWNER'S DOUBT found

**`PT-640` recorded me calling `GAP-002` open four times when its own file's line 3 said `CLOSED`.** **⚠ THE OWNER'S QUESTION CAUGHT IT. NOTHING I HAD BUILT COULD.**

### ⚠ WHY CHECK 32 COULD NOT SEE IT

**⚠ `audit_openitems` READS THE AGENDA and finds closures the agenda STILL LISTS. `GAP-002` was never ON the agenda — the false claim lived in PROSE, in a header I wrote myself.**

### How check 34 works

    ⚠ read every document's own `**Status:**` header
    ⚠ keep those declaring CLOSED, SETTLED or DECIDED — 15 of them
    ⚠ look for any OTHER document calling that same subject
      open, unresolved or undecided

### ⚠⚠ AND MY FIRST RUN WAS FOUR HITS, ALL FOUR FALSE

    ⚠ AGENDA-UPDATED     ⚠ SAYS `SUPERSEDED` ON LINE 1. A superseded file is a
                         RECORD OF AN OLD STATE and is MEANT to carry stale
                         claims. ⚠ MY CHECK REPORTED IT ANYWAY.
    ⚠ INFLUENCE-01       *"depends on the mastery table in `ALIGNMENT-01`"* —
                         a DEPENDENCY, not a status claim
    ⚠ BEASTS-FEATS-01    a BEAST'S POOL is unresolved; `REST-AND-MEDITATION-01`
                         merely appears in the sentence
    ⚠ SPECIES-FEATS-DRAFT  *"still open"* about SCHEMA QUESTIONS, with
                         `GAP-002` elsewhere in the line

> **⚠ THREE OF FOUR WERE THE SAME FAULT: THE SUBJECT AND THE OPEN-LANGUAGE WERE IN THE SAME LINE BUT NOT THE SAME CLAUSE.**

**⚠ TIGHTENED: the two must sit within 60 CHARACTERS of each other, and a file declaring itself `SUPERSEDED` is skipped.**

### ⚠ Break-tested in both directions

**⚠ Planted *"`GAP-002` remains open and is the largest unresolved decision"* into `AGENDA-CURRENT` — REPORTED, naming the file, the subject's real status, and the offending line.** **Removed it — silent.**

    ⚠ check 32   a closure the AGENDA still lists
    ⚠ check 34   a closure PROSE still denies

**⚠ THE FIRST NEEDS THE ITEM TO BE ON A LIST. THE SECOND DOES NOT — which is why it catches the case that got past everything else.**

**Owner ruling on size. ⚠ `LOOT-01 §4c` FELL BACK TO *"party level"* — A HEADING WITH NO RULE UNDER IT, IN A SHIPPED MECHANIC, FOR THE WHOLE PROJECT.**

    ⚠ MULTIPLAYER     each player + ⚠ ONE companion each  = 2 per player

### ✓ `PARTY LEVEL` — the definition that was missing

> **⚠ THE HIGHEST CHARACTER LEVEL IN THE PARTY. PLAYERS ONLY.**

**⚠ HIGHEST, NOT AVERAGE: average PUNISHES A PARTY FOR BRINGING IN A NEW PLAYER.** A level-14 group recruiting a level-4 friend drops to 11 and sees worse loot **for being welcoming.**

                           let one class RAISE THE PARTY'S LOOT TIER BY BUYING

**⚠ THE OWNER PROPOSED PER-PLAYER LOOT — *"PVE for loot, not a shared thing."* ⚠ I AGREED WITH THE INTENT AND NOT THE MECHANISM.**

> **⚠ EVERYONE GETS THINGS THAT SUIT THEM AND THE COUNT PER BODY STAYS ONE.** **⚠ It delivers the owner's intent without multiplying the drop rate by party size.**

## PT-657 — ⚠⚠ CREDITS. The shared/separate choice turns out to be SOCIAL, not economic

**Owner ruling: the purse is chosen by the players at campaign start.** **⚠ SINGLE PLAYER IS ALWAYS ONE PURSE — there is nobody to share with.**

### ⚠⚠ THE CHOICE DOES NOT CHANGE HOW MUCH MONEY EXISTS

    ⚠ shared, 4 players     ONE purse funding EIGHT loadouts
    ⚠ separate, 4 players   FOUR purses funding TWO loadouts each
    ⚠⚠ SAME EIGHT

> **⚠ IT MOVES WHO HOLDS THE CREDITS, NOT HOW MANY ENTER THE WORLD.** **⚠ SO NEITHER OPTION NEEDS COMPENSATING, and the table can pick on taste.**

### ⚠⚠ WHAT SCALES IS LOADOUTS, AND TWO PLAYERS IS FREE

**⚠ A PARTY DOES NOT NEED CREDITS PER PLAYER. IT NEEDS THEM PER BODY THAT CARRIES GEAR.**

    players   loadouts        multiplier
      1       ⚠ 4  (1+3)      ×1
      2       ⚠ 4  (2+2)      ⚠⚠ ×1 — EXACTLY THE SOLO PARTY
      3         6  (3+3)      ×1.5
      4         8  (4+4)      ×2

**⚠⚠ TWO PLAYERS IS THE SOLO PARTY WITH THE COMPANIONS REDISTRIBUTED. FOUR BODIES EITHER WAY, AND IT NEEDS NO ADJUSTMENT.**

> **⚠ THE CURVE IS `×1 · ×1 · ×1.5 · ×2`, NOT `×1 · ×2 · ×3 · ×4`.** **⚠ SCALING BY PLAYER COUNT WOULD HAND A FOUR-PLAYER PARTY DOUBLE WHAT IT SHOULD SEE.**

**⚠ THAT FALLS OUT OF `PT-655`'s PARTY SIZES AND I DID NOT EXPECT IT.** **The single-player 1+3 and the multiplayer 1+1 happen to meet at two players.**

### ⚠ The multiplier is carried by the ENCOUNTER, not the drop

**⚠ `PT-655` FIXED LOOT AT ONE ITEM PER BODY AND IT STAYS.**

**⚠ A PARTY OF EIGHT FIGHTS MORE BODIES THAN A PARTY OF FOUR. MORE BODIES IS MORE LOOT WITHOUT TOUCHING THE DROP RATE** — and it falls out of something a GM was doing anyway.

### ⚠ And the tier curve says WHEN the purse choice matters

    ⚠ tier 1   median      40      ⚠ THE STEEPEST STEP IS THE FIRST
    ⚠ tier 2   median   1,500      ×37
    ⚠ tier 3   median  10,115      ×6.7
    ⚠ tier 4   median  25,500      ×2.5

**⚠ AT TIER 1, SEPARATE PURSES MEAN FOUR PLAYERS EACH SAVING TOWARD A 500-CREDIT ITEM. ⚠ AT TIER 4 THE DIFFERENCE IS NOISE.**

**⚠ ONE CONSEQUENCE STATED: A PLAYER WHO LEAVES A SEPARATE-PURSE PARTY TAKES THEIR CREDITS.** **⚠ `PARTY-01 §6` already rules that a departing COMPANION takes their equipment; this is the same principle one level up.**

**⚠ `PARTY-01` IS COMPLETE.**

## PT-658 — ⚠⚠ TWO CURVES. The table gets quarters; the app gets the strict product

**⚠ `PT-657` PRICED LOADOUTS AND SAID `×1` AT TWO PLAYERS. THE OWNER CAUGHT IT.**

> **⚠ MY MATHS COUNTED HOW MANY LOADOUTS EXIST AND IGNORED HOW MUCH OF WHAT DROPS LANDS USEFULLY.**

**⚠ A SOLO PLAYER CONTROLS ALL FOUR BODIES AND POOLS EVERYTHING. NOTHING IS STRANDED.** **⚠ TWO PLAYERS CANNOT — a crystal that suits one build is dead weight to the other, and `PT-655`'s instanced filter routes items to WHOEVER OPENED THE CONTAINER, not to whoever needs them most.**

**⚠ THE OWNER'S `1.25` IS A ROUTING-LOSS ALLOWANCE, AND IT IS A REAL COST I HAD NOT PRICED.**

### The two curves

| Players | ⚠ TABLE | ⚠ APP |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ×1 | ×1 |
| 2 | ×1.25 | ×1.25 |
| **3** | ⚠ **×1.75** | ⚠ **×1.88** |
| 4 | ×2.5 | ×2.5 |

> **⚠⚠ THEY AGREE EVERYWHERE BUT THREE PLAYERS. AT TIER 2 THE GAP IS 195 CREDITS.**

### ⚠ The table gets quarters because a GM has no calculator

    ⚠ ×1.25   the amount, plus a quarter
    ⚠ ×1.75   ⚠ DOUBLE IT, THEN TAKE OFF A QUARTER
    ⚠ ×2.5    double it, plus half

**⚠ `1.88 × 3,400` MID-SESSION IS A CALCULATOR. ⚠ THIS IS A TABLETOP GAME FIRST AND AN APP SECOND.**

### ⚠ The app gets `1.88` because it holds the per-player share FLAT

    ⚠ strict product = loadout ratio × routing loss = 1.5 × 1.25 = 1.875

    app     2 → 0.625 · 3 → 0.627 · 4 → 0.625   ⚠ FLAT
    table   2 → 0.625 · ⚠ 3 → 0.583 · 4 → 0.625

> **⚠ NOBODY IS PUNISHED FOR THE SIZE OF THEIR GROUP.** **⚠ THE ENGINE HAS NO REASON TO ROUND AND EVERY REASON NOT TO.**

**⚠ THE TABLE'S ONLY COMPROMISE IS A THREE-PLAYER GROUP SITTING 7% LIGHT — inside the noise of ONE BAND-5 ROLL, and a GM may round up if it ever bites.**

### ⚠ And `4` was moved from my own recommendation

**⚠ I FIRST PROPOSED `×2.25` AT FOUR PLAYERS. ⚠ `×2.5` MAKES THE TABLE AND THE APP AGREE THERE, and four is the FULL TABLE — the size that matters most.**

**⚠ IT ALSO MAKES THE DIVERGENCE A SINGLE ROW.** **A rule that differs in one place is a rule people remember; one that differs in three is two rules.**

## PT-660 — ⚠⚠ `EXPERIENCE-01`. The missing half of the core loop

**⚠ CATALOGUING THE CORPUS FOUND FIVE SYSTEMS NOTHING OWNED. ⚠ THIS WAS THE BIGGEST.**

> **⚠⚠ THIRTY-SEVEN CLASSES HAD PER-LEVEL TABLES AND NOTHING SAID HOW YOU REACH THE NEXT LEVEL.** **Six mentions of XP across 104 documents, all of them in passing, in files about other things.**

### ⚠⚠ THE TABLE IS A FORMULA, AND THAT IS WHY IT REACHES 30

> **⚠ XP TO REACH LEVEL `N` = `1000 × (N−1) × N ÷ 2`**

**⚠ VERIFIED AGAINST `exptable.2da` AT EVERY ROW 1–20. EXACT, NOT APPROXIMATE.**

**⚠⚠ ROW 21 IS `0xFFFFFFFF` — A SENTINEL, NOT A VALUE. KOTOR STOPPED AT 20 AND MARKED THE CEILING WITH A MAX-INT.**

    KOTOR's cap   level 20   190,000
    ⚠ OURS        level 30   ⚠ 435,000 — FROM THE FORMULA, NOT AUTHORED

> **⚠ THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON TO PORT A FORMULA RATHER THAN A TABLE. A TABLE STOPS WHERE THE FILE STOPS.**

### ⚠ The award curve — `xpbaseconst.2da`, sign inverted

**⚠ THE FILE READS FROM THE CREATURE'S SIDE. `leveldiff −8` means the CREATURE is eight below.** **⚠ WE STATE IT FROM THE PLAYER'S SIDE, WHICH INVERTS THE SIGN AND IS THE ONLY CHANGE MADE.**

    ⚠ an even fight    ×1.00
    ⚠ +8 or more       ×4.00
    ⚠⚠ −8 or more      ×0.00

### ⚠⚠ THE FLOOR IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ROW IN THE FILE

> **⚠ A CREATURE EIGHT OR MORE LEVELS BELOW YOU IS WORTH NOTHING. THAT IS THE FILE'S OWN NUMBER.**

**⚠ IT IS WHAT STOPS A LEVEL-20 PARTY FARMING CANNOKS, AND IT MEANS `DEATH-AND-DIFFICULTY-01`'s GRIND WORRY NEVER NEEDED ITS OWN RULE.** **⚠ THE XP TABLE ALREADY REFUSES TO PAY FOR IT.**

### ⚠ Two rulings the corpus forced

**⚠ COMPANIONS TAKE NO SHARE — same principle as `PARTY-01 §2`, and `BEASTS-ENTRIES-01` already ties a beast's level to its master's.**

**⚠ AND THE DIFFERENCE USES THE INDIVIDUAL'S LEVEL, NOT `PARTY-01`'s PARTY LEVEL.** **⚠ Party level is the HIGHEST, for loot tiers — using it here would PUNISH A LOWER-LEVEL PLAYER TWICE, with a smaller multiplier AND an even split.**

> **⚠ A NEW PLAYER IN A HIGH-LEVEL GROUP EARNS THE `×3` AND `×4` ROWS AND CATCHES UP. THAT IS THE POINT.**

### ⚠⚠ SOLVING WITHOUT FIGHTING PAYS THE SAME

**⚠ A RULE, NOT A SUGGESTION.**

**⚠ A SYSTEM THAT PAYS ONLY FOR KILLS TEACHES PLAYERS TO KILL, AND KOTOR IS A GAME WHERE `Persuade` OPENS AS MANY DOORS AS A BLASTER.** **⚠ `ALIGNMENT-01` WOULD BE DECORATION IF THE XP TABLE QUIETLY PRICED MURDER HIGHER.**

### ⚠⚠ KOTOR 2's ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR — AND IT IS NOT A SLOWER RATE

> ***"ALL YOUR PARTY MEMBERS GAIN EXPERIENCE AT THE SAME RATE, even if they aren't in your active party."***

    ⚠ 500 × N × (N−1)   ===   1000 × (N−1) × N ÷ 2

## PT-673 — ⚠⚠ THE GENERATOR MAY MAKE THE SHIP A PROBLEM. IT MAY NOT MAKE IT ABSENT

**Owner: *"the conditions should be defined and set up by the DM/campaign. It is not something that should happen randomly… there should be a clear path to getting it back."***

> **⚠ AGREED, AND THE REASON IS A SOFTLOCK RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE.**

### ⚠⚠ WHY THE GENERATOR MUST NEVER TAKE IT

**⚠ `PT-666` GAVE THE GENERATOR ROOMS AND ENCOUNTERS. ⚠ LOSING A SHIP IS NEITHER — IT IS A CAMPAIGN STATE CHANGE.**

    ⚠ CRAFTING-01 §5     *"always succeeds at a base"*  → NO BASE, NO CRAFTING
    ⚠ PARTY-01 §5        free swap at rest              → FROZEN ROSTER
    ⚠ DROID-MASTER-01    held droids sit at the base    → UNREACHABLE

**⚠ `PT-672` MADE THAT A FEATURE — *"three existing rules losing their precondition together"* IS A REAL STAKE.**

> **⚠⚠ BUT A STAKE NEEDS AN AUTHOR. ⚠ A GENERATOR COULD CREATE THE LOSS AND NOT THE WAY BACK.**

### ⚠ THE RECOVERY GUARANTEE

**⚠ IF A CAMPAIGN PACKAGE TAKES THE SHIP, IT MUST STATE THE WAY BACK BEFORE IT TAKES IT.**

    ⚠ RECOVERY     the same hull, returned
    ⚠ REPLACEMENT  a different hull, given or earned
    ⚠ SUBSTITUTE   ⚠ a TEMPORARY BASE carrying the three systems until a
                   hull exists again

**⚠ KOTOR DID THIS TWICE AND NEVER STRANDED THE PLAYER. ⚠ THE `Ebon Hawk` IS TAKEN AT PERAGUS AND CRASHED ON MALACHOR, AND BOTH ARE AUTHORED WITH THE RETURN ALREADY WRITTEN.**

**⚠ A GM MAY TAKE THE SHIP FOR A SCENE, A SESSION OR AN ARC. ⚠ THEY MAY NOT TAKE IT WITHOUT KNOWING HOW IT COMES BACK.**

### ⚠ What the generator MAY do

    ✓ DAMAGE IT     ⚠ a repair is a COST, not a state change
    ✓ STRAND IT     ⚠ the base still functions where it sits
    ✓ PUT SOMETHING ABOARD IT
    ⚠⚠ IT MAY NOT REMOVE IT

> **⚠ THE LINE IS THAT THE GENERATOR MAY MAKE THE SHIP A PROBLEM AND MAY NOT MAKE IT ABSENT.**

**⚠ AND THAT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS `PT-323`'s PARTY-COMPOSITION FILTER — *"a party with no droid gets nothing"* — ⚠ A RULE THAT EXISTS TO STOP THE ENGINE PRODUCING AN OUTCOME NOBODY CAN USE.**

      A FACTION OR SPECIES   Gamorrean · Bothan · Czerka · Echani ·
                             Exchange · GenoHaradan · Jal Shey · Karakan ·
                             Kubaz · Eriadu · Nagai · Nikto · Zeison Sha
      OR A FUNCTION          Accuracy · Insulated · Infiltrator ·
                             Defensive · Detonator · Precision · Survival ·
                             Stabilizer · Automation · Dominator

**⚠ FOUR OF FORTY-ONE BREAK IT: ⚠ `Eriadu Strength Amplifier` ×2, `Gamorrean Wargloves`, `Deflect` — ⚠ AND MINE MADE FIVE.**

***"Cured hide over the knuckles and a strap across the palm. Every pit on Taris sells them at the door, and every fighter who has broken a hand once buys a pair."***

> **⚠ THIS ONE DID NOT, AND NOTHING WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT. ⚠ `audit_itemnames` CHECKS THAT A NAME **RESOLVES**, NOT THAT IT **FITS**.**

### ⚠⚠ THE IDENTITY GAP IS REAL AND IT IS ABOUT **CONSUMABLES**

**⚠ THIRTEEN CLASS HOOKS EXIST AND ⚠ EVERY ONE ACTS ON A **PERSON** — you, an ally, an enemy, a droid.**

    ⚠ TIER 1 · Salvage Charge   ⚠ recover a mine after the encounter,
                                `Demolitions` at tier DC `+5`.
                                ⚠ ON A FAILURE IT DETONATES.
    ⚠ TIER 2 · Live Placement   ⚠⚠ PLACE A MINE AS A BONUS ACTION,
                                IN COMBAT
    ⚠ TIER 3 · Nothing Wasted   ⚠ recover a grenade that dealt no
                                damage · ⚠ and no longer wait for the
                                encounter to end

**⚠ PRE-PLACEMENT ONLY FIRES WHEN A GM TELEGRAPHS A FIGHT. ⚠ A BONUS-ACTION MINE WORKS IN EVERY ENCOUNTER.**

    ⚠⚠ AND THE CHARACTER IN IT TAKES THE TURRET'S OWN DAMAGE DIE,

> **⚠ AND IT MAKES THE SEATING DECISION REAL: ⚠⚠ THE TURRET IS THE DANGEROUS SEAT AND THE COCKPIT IS NOT.**

**⚠ A CHARACTER REPAIRING A STATION IS ⚠ AT THAT STATION. ⚠ IF IT IS HIT AGAIN, THEY ARE THE ONE IN IT.**

> **⚠ THAT IS WHAT TURNS THE UNSEATED ROLE FROM A ⚠ CHORE INTO A ⚠ CHOICE — ⚠ THEY ARE VOLUNTEERING TO STAND IN THE PLACE THAT JUST EXPLODED.**

## PT-796 — ⚠⚠ COMPONENT 4: SHIP STATS, DERIVED FROM THE K1 BESTIARY

### ⚠⚠ 4.1 · VITALITY = 10 × CR — and it comes from real data

**⚠ `PT-790` PARSED ⚠ 205 K1 CREATURES. ⚠ THEIR MEDIAN HP PER CR BAND **IS** THE GAME'S OWN CURVE:**

    ⚠ CR 1 → 8    CR 5 → 50    CR 10 → 116   CR 20 → 350

**⚠ `10 × CR` FITS AT ⚠ 21% MEAN ABSOLUTE ERROR ACROSS 14 BANDS.**

> **⚠ AND THE REAL CURVE IS ⚠⚠ NOT SMOOTH — ⚠ CR 6 SITS **BELOW** CR 5, AND CR 12 BELOW CR 11. ⚠ A DESIGN CURVE SHOULD NOT REPRODUCE THAT NOISE.**

**⚠ I FIRST TRIED `CR × (8 + CR/2)`, WHICH FIT THE ENDS AT `+0%` AND `+3%` AND ⚠ MISSED CR 14 BY `+75%`. ⚠ THE SIMPLER FORMULA IS WORSE AT THE ENDS AND ⚠ BETTER EVERYWHERE.**

### ⚠ 4.2 · DEFENCE = 10 + CR — and it makes `PT-795` computable

**⚠ A HIT BEATING `Defence` BY 10 HITS A STATION. ⚠ AGAINST AN EVEN-CR OPPONENT THAT IS ⚠⚠ ROUGHLY ONE ROLL IN TEN.**

> **⚠ A GUNNER'S SEAT EXPLODES ABOUT ONCE EVERY TEN INCOMING SHOTS. ⚠ FREQUENT ENOUGH TO FEAR, RARE ENOUGH NOT TO DOMINATE.**

**⚠ `PT-795` ASSERTED THE RULE WITH ⚠ NO WAY TO KNOW ITS FREQUENCY. ⚠ NOW THERE IS ONE.**

### ⚠ 4.3–4.4 · SPEED 4 SQUARES · TURRETS `2d8` – `5d8` BY TIER

**⚠ 400 METRES A ROUND CROSSES `MEDIUM` IN ONE MOVE AND ⚠ CANNOT CROSS `LONG` — ⚠ WHICH IS WHAT MAKES `CLOSE THE GAP` WORTH AN ACTION.**

**⚠ A **Blaster Rifle** IS `1d12`, AVERAGE 6.5. ⚠ A TIER-1 TURRET IS `2d8`, AVERAGE 9 — ⚠ AND IT IS ALSO THE DAMAGE A CHARACTER TAKES WHEN THEIR STATION IS HIT.**

### ⚠⚠ 4.5 · THE SHIP SCALES WITH THE PARTY

**⚠ ITS `CR` IS THE PARTY'S LEVEL — `ENCOUNTER-01 §2`. ⚠ A LEVEL-3 PARTY FLIES A 30-VITALITY HAWK; ⚠ A LEVEL-15 PARTY FLIES A 150-VITALITY ONE. ⚠ SAME SHIP, SAME SEATS.**

> **⚠ THAT IS HOW KOTOR ITSELF WORKS — ⚠ THE `Ebon Hawk` IS NEVER UPGRADED AND NEVER OUTCLASSED.**

### ⚠⚠ 4.6 · AND THE BALANCE PROBLEM IS NOW MEASURABLE

    ⚠ LEVEL-5 PARTY  ⚠ 50 vitality · Defence 15
    ⚠ ITS OUTPUT     ⚠ turret `2d8` + forward gun `2d8` = ⚠ 18/round
    ⚠ EVEN-CR ENEMY  ⚠ 50 vitality
    ⚠⚠ A FIGHT LASTS ⚠ THREE ROUNDS

**⚠ SHORT — AND SHORT ⚠⚠ BECAUSE THE `Ebon Hawk` HAS TWO GUNS.**

> **⚠ WHICH CONFIRMS THE STEP-BACK READ: ⚠ THE PROOF-OF-CONCEPT SHIP IS TOO SMALL, AND ⚠ THE FIX IS MORE SEATS ON BIGGER SHIPS — ⚠ NOT DIFFERENT NUMBERS.**

## PT-805 — ⚠⚠ COMBAT ROLES, AND FOUR NAVIES THAT FIGHT DIFFERENTLY

### ⚠⚠ AND THE DOCTRINE CAME OUT OF THE LORE, NOT THE DESIGN

> **⚠ A SITH ENGAGEMENT IS ⚠⚠ AN AMBUSH YOU CANNOT RUN FROM. ⚠ `PT-802`'s SHUTTLE COUNTDOWN DOES NOT WORK AGAINST THEM ⚠ UNTIL THE INTERDICTOR IS DEAD.**

**⚠⚠ THE MANDALORIANS — *"we are already aboard."* ⚠ THE `Basilisk` IS RIDDEN *"down into the ATMOSPHERE OF A WORLD FROM SPACE, using GRAVITATIONAL FORCE AND THE ELEMENT OF SURPRISE."***

> **⚠ A MANDALORIAN FLEET DOES NOT TRADE FIRE. ⚠⚠ IT CLOSES AND BOARDS — ⚠ AND THE `Q-Carrier`, THE `Shaadlar` TROOPSHIP AND THE BASILISK ⚠ ALL SERVE THAT ONE IDEA.**

**⚠ THE REPUBLIC — *"hold the line."* ⚠ THE `Hammerhead` IS *"the Republic's LINE SHIP"*, AND ⚠ FIGHTERS SCREEN IT. ⚠⚠ IT IS THE ONLY FACTION THAT FIGHTS THE WAY A PLAYER EXPECTS.**

**⚠⚠ THE EXCHANGE AND HUTTS — *"we do not fight."* ⚠ ONE ARMED FREIGHTER AND ⚠ NO GRUNTS, NO CARRIER, NO SUPPORT. ⚠ THEY WOULD RATHER SELL YOU SOMETHING.**

### ⚠⚠ FOUR FACTIONS, FOUR DIFFERENT FIGHTS, NO NEW RULES

    ⚠ VS SITH         ⚠ KILL THE INTERDICTOR OR YOU CANNOT LEAVE
    ⚠ VS MANDALORIANS ⚠ KEEP THEM AT RANGE OR YOU ARE BOARDED
    ⚠ VS REPUBLIC     ⚠ A STRAIGHT FIGHT
    ⚠ VS CRIMINALS    ⚠⚠ THEY BREAK OFF

> **⚠ THE `Interdictor` AND THE `Basilisk` DO THE SAME WORK FROM OPPOSITE ENDS: ⚠⚠ ONE STOPS YOU LEAVING, THE OTHER ARRIVES WHETHER YOU LIKE IT OR NOT.**

## PT-806 — ⚠⚠ `SPACE-AI-01`. Four doctrines, written before the engine

**⚠ OWNER: ⚠ *"develop on paper the conceptual strategy for each of the four factions for when we build the engine."***

### ⚠ EVERY FACTION ANSWERS THE SAME FOUR QUESTIONS

    ⚠ WHAT IS MY GOAL · ⚠ WHICH TARGET · ⚠ WHAT RANGE ·
    ⚠⚠ WHEN DO I BREAK OFF

**⚠ AND THEY ANSWER THEM ⚠⚠ COMPLETELY DIFFERENTLY. ⚠ THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN.**

### ⚠⚠ THE SITH — capture, not destruction

    ⚠ TARGET ⚠ THE ENGINES, THEN THE TURRETS · ⚠⚠ NEVER THE HULL
    ⚠ BREAK OFF ⚠⚠ NEVER

**⚠ THE `Interdictor` IS ⚠ PRIORITY-PROTECTED — ⚠ GRUNTS INTERPOSE, AND THE FLEET WILL LOSE THREE INTERCEPTORS TO KEEP IT ALIVE.**

> **⚠⚠ AND THE PLAYERS FIGURE THAT OUT BY WATCHING. ⚠ NOTHING TELLS THEM — ⚠ THE BEHAVIOUR DOES.**

**⚠ AND IF THE PARTY IS WINNING, ⚠ THE SITH DO NOT FLEE. ⚠⚠ THEY BOARD.**

### ⚠⚠ THE MANDALORIANS — the easiest to predict, the hardest to stop

    ⚠ TARGET ⚠ WHOEVER IS NEAREST — ⚠⚠ IT DOES NOT CALCULATE
    ⚠ RANGE  ⚠⚠ CLOSE, ALWAYS

> **⚠ A PLAYER LEARNS THE MANDALORIAN PLAN IN ⚠ ONE ROUND. ⚠⚠ KNOWING IT DOES NOT HELP.**

**⚠ AND A BASILISK BELOW HALF VITALITY ⚠⚠ RAMS. ⚠ IT WAS NEVER MEANT TO COME BACK.**

### ⚠ THE REPUBLIC — the only faction that plays properly

**⚠ IT TARGETS THE BIGGEST THREAT AND ⚠⚠ WITHDRAWS AT 25% HULL.**

> **⚠⚠ WHICH MAKES IT THE **TUTORIAL FIGHT**. ⚠ A PARTY THAT LEARNS SPACE COMBAT AGAINST THE REPUBLIC LEARNS THE **RULES**; ⚠ ONE THAT LEARNS IT AGAINST THE SITH ⚠ LEARNS TO PANIC.**

**⚠ AND ITS WITHDRAWAL IS THE ONLY MERCY IN THE SYSTEM.**

### ⚠⚠ THE CRIMINALS — and they TALK first

**⚠ AN `Exchange` ENGAGEMENT OPENS WITH ⚠ A DEMAND, NOT A SHOT. ⚠ `Persuade` IS A VALID ANSWER AND ⚠⚠ THE ONLY FACTION WHERE IT IS.**

> **⚠ THE ONE SPACE ENCOUNTER A PARTY CAN END ⚠⚠ WITHOUT ROLLING AN ATTACK.**

### ⚠⚠ AND THIS IS THE **INTENT** LAYER OF THE ENGINE PATTERN

**⚠ *"THIN AI OVER A DETERMINISTIC ENGINE — INTENT, RESOLVE, NARRATE."***

    ⚠ WITHOUT THESE  ⚠ EVERY ENEMY SHOOTS THE NEAREST TARGET AND
                     ⚠⚠ ALL FOUR FACTIONS PLAY IDENTICALLY
    ⚠ WITH THEM      ⚠ THE SAME RULES PRODUCE ⚠⚠ FOUR DIFFERENT GAMES

**⚠ AND EVERY BEHAVIOUR IS ⚠ TRACEABLE TO A SOURCE LINE — `PT-805`. ⚠⚠ NONE OF IT IS INVENTED PERSONALITY.**

### ⚠⚠ `PT-809` SAID *"only `VV` has no item row — and it needs one."* ⚠ THAT WAS WRONG.

**⚠ IT IS ⚠ `g_i_pazcard_019`, ⚠ *"Pazaak Card +/- 1/2"*, ⚠⚠ 500cr — ⚠ AND IT IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE CARD IN THE GAME.**

> **⚠ I MATCHED THE FIVE 2DA CODES AGAINST ⚠ FOUR ITEM NAMES AND ⚠⚠ DECLARED A GAP INSTEAD OF CHECKING THE FIFTH. ⚠ THE NAME *"+/- 1/2"* DOES NOT LOOK LIKE *"value change"*, AND ⚠ I STOPPED AT THE NAME.**

**⚠ THE FIVE K2 SPECIALS ARE ⚠ EXACTLY `g_i_pazcard_019` – `023`. ⚠ THE RESREFS RUN IN ORDER AND ⚠⚠ THE SET IS CLOSED.**

### ⚠⚠ AND `g_i_pazcard_013`–`018` ARE THE `*n` CARDS

**⚠ THE 2DA WRITES `*1`–`*6`. ⚠ THE ITEM TABLE WRITES `+/-1`–`+/-6`. ⚠⚠ SAME CARD, TWO NOTATIONS, AND NOTHING HAD CONNECTED THEM.**

### ⚠⚠ THE PRICE CURVE RUNS BACKWARDS — and it IS the strategy

    ⚠ +1 ⚠⚠ 100cr · +2 75 · +3 50 · +4 25 · +5 12 · ⚠ +6 ⚠⚠ 5cr

> **⚠⚠ A `+1` COSTS TWENTY TIMES A `+6`.**

**⚠ NOT A PRICING ERROR — ⚠ IT IS THE GAME TELLING YOU HOW TO PLAY. ⚠⚠ THE GOAL IS **EXACTLY 20**, SO A SMALL ADJUSTMENT IS WORTH MORE THAN A BIG ONE.**

**⚠ AND THE DUAL PREMIUM WIDENS WITH VALUE: ⚠ `±1` IS `2×` ITS PLAIN TWIN, ⚠⚠ `±6` IS `10×`. ⚠ A PLAIN `+6` IS NEARLY USELESS; ⚠ A `±6` SAVES YOU FROM A BUST. ⚠⚠ THE SIGN IS THE VALUE.**

### ⚠ THE DECK AND SIDE DECK ARE UNIQUE, AT 0cr

**⚠ `g_i_pazdeck` AND `g_i_pazsidebd001` — ⚠ BOTH UNIQUE, BOTH FREE.**

> **⚠⚠ SO A CHARACTER **HAS** A PAZAAK DECK. ⚠ IT IS NOT BOUGHT AND NOT LOOT — ⚠ YOU START WITH IT AND YOU BUILD IT BY BUYING **CARDS**.**

### ⚠⚠ AND `Pazaak Cards In Hand` IS A WEAPON

**⚠ `w_pazaak_01` — ⚠ `1d8`, threat `20`, `×2`, 25cr.**

> **⚠ A JOKE ITEM AND ⚠ A REAL WEAPON ROW. ⚠⚠ IT SHOULD STAY — ⚠ A CHARACTER BEATING SOMEONE WITH A FISTFUL OF PAZAAK CARDS IS EXACTLY THE TONE.**

### ⚠⚠ THE FEEL, NAMED

> **⚠⚠ GOING FASTER MAKES YOU WORSE AT GOING FAST.**

    ⚠⚠ ACCEL ⚠ HOW MUCH A PAD GIVES YOU
    ⚠ FRAME  ⚠ HOW LITTLE A CLIP COSTS YOU

## PT-813 — ⚠⚠ THE DECISION CLOCK. And running out of time is not a penalty

**⚠ OWNER: ⚠ *"forcing players to make a QUICK DECISION… that's the right idea. Make things tense. And the bike upgrades, one at least, could give them EXTRA TIME."***

### ⚠ EACH SEGMENT, A LINE — and TEN SECONDS to call it

    ⚠⚠ INSIDE   ⚠ DC `+3` · ⚠ pad gives `+5`
    ⚠ OUTSIDE   ⚠ DC `−2` · ⚠ pad gives `+1`

**⚠ `PT-812` HAD THE RIDER MAKING ⚠⚠ NO DECISIONS — ⚠ FOUR ROLLS AND A NUMBER. ⚠ THIS IS THE FIX, AND ⚠ THE OWNER FOUND IT.**

### ⚠⚠ AND THE TIMER EXPIRING MEANS THE **SAFE** LINE

**⚠ I FLAGGED THE TRAP: ⚠ A TIMER THAT PUNISHES A SLOW PLAYER TESTS ⚠⚠ THE PLAYER'S REFLEXES, NOT THE CHARACTER'S NERVE.**

> **⚠ SO THE CLOCK ⚠⚠ NEVER TAKES A ROLL AWAY. ⚠ IT ONLY TAKES THE **RISK** AWAY.**

    ⚠ A FAST DECIDER  ⚠ GETS THE AGGRESSIVE OPTION
    ⚠⚠ A SLOW DECIDER ⚠ RIDES CONSERVATIVELY AND STILL FINISHES

**⚠ AND IT IS THE TRUER SIMULATION: ⚠⚠ A RIDER WHO HESITATES DOES NOT CRASH. ⚠ THEY JUST DO NOT TAKE THE LINE.**

### ⚠⚠ AND `Accel` BUYS SECONDS — a better job than `PT-812` gave it

    ⚠ NONE 10s · ⚠ T1 12 · T2 14 · T3 16 · ⚠⚠ T4 18 SECONDS

**⚠ `k2_swoopupgrade.2da`'s `Accel` IS ⚠ HOW FAST THE BIKE RESPONDS. ⚠⚠ AT THE TABLE THAT IS HOW LONG THE RIDER HAS TO THINK.**

> **⚠ AND IT IS THE FIRST UPGRADE IN THE PROJECT THAT ⚠⚠ BUYS THE **PLAYER** SOMETHING RATHER THAN THE CHARACTER.**

## PT-831 — ⚠⚠⚠ THE PARSER BUG. The GFF header has TWELVE DWORDs, not fourteen

**⚠ `PT-830` HAD TO MATCH EFFECTS BY ⚠ CONTENT BECAUSE THE `.uti` PARSER ⚠ COULD NOT READ THE STRREF. ⚠⚠ THE REASON WAS A ONE-LINE BUG.**

### ⚠⚠ THE HEADER UNPACK WAS WRONG

**⚠ `/tmp/gffread.py` READ ⚠ `struct.unpack_from('<14I', d, 8)` AND NAMED FOURTEEN FIELDS.**

> **⚠⚠ A GFF HEADER CARRIES ⚠ TWELVE. ⚠ SO EVERY NAME AFTER THE SIXTH WAS SHIFTED, AND ⚠⚠ `fdo` — THE FIELD **DATA** OFFSET — WAS ACTUALLY `FieldIndicesOffset`.**

**⚠ EVERY STRING READ FROM A WRONG BASE. ⚠ THAT IS WHY `Tag` AND `TemplateResRef` RETURNED ⚠ BINARY GARBAGE FOR THE ENTIRE PROJECT.**

    ⚠ BEFORE  ⚠ TemplateResRef `''` · Tag `'\x00\x0e\x00...'`
    ⚠⚠ AFTER  ⚠ TemplateResRef `'g_w_fraggren01'` · Tag the same

### ⚠ AND THE NUMBERS WERE NEVER AFFECTED

**⚠ FIELD TYPES ⚠ 0–5 ARE STORED ⚠⚠ INLINE IN THE FIELD ARRAY, NOT IN FIELD DATA. ⚠ SO `PT-796`'s ⚠ 205-CREATURE VITALITY CURVE AND ⚠ EVERY CR READING ⚠ WERE CORRECT.**

> **⚠⚠ THE BUG DESTROYED ONLY THE **TEXT**, AND ⚠ TEXT WAS THE ONE THING NOBODY HAD ASKED THE PARSER FOR UNTIL TODAY.**

### ✓ TYPE 12 ADDED — `CExoLocString`

**⚠ `Description`, `DescIdentified` AND `LocalizedName` ARE ALL TYPE 12, WHICH THE OLD PARSER ⚠⚠ SILENTLY SKIPPED. ⚠ THE STRREF LIVES IN ITS SECOND DWORD.**

### ⚠⚠⚠ AND THE JOIN IMMEDIATELY CONTRADICTED `PT-830`

    ⚠ CONTENT MATCH  ⚠ *"Piercing, 24pts · Range: Medium"*
    ⚠⚠ THE JOIN      ⚠ *"Piercing, 20pts · Range: LONG"*

> **⚠ `PT-830`'s SEARCH FOUND ⚠⚠ THE WRONG STRING. ⚠ THE POINTER FINDS THE RIGHT ONE.**

**⚠ THAT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR DOING THIS PROPERLY, AND ⚠⚠ IT PROVED ITSELF WITHIN A MINUTE OF THE FIX.**

### ✓ 1,360 OF 1,360 ITEM FILES NOW RESOLVE A DESCRIPTION

    ⚠ Frag Grenade        ⚠ Piercing 20 · 4m · Long · DC15 half
    ⚠ Sonic Grenade       ⚠ Sonic 20
    ⚠ Concussion Grenade  ⚠⚠ Damage: NONE — it is a debuff
    ⚠ Adhesive Grenade    ⚠⚠ Damage: NONE

## ⚠ ① THE QUEST GENERATOR — ⚠⚠ AND THE MECHANISM IS THE ANSWER TO OUR HARDEST PROBLEM

**⚠ 265 TEMPLATES. ⚠ `QRC` IS MESSAGE PANELS WITH TYPED SLOTS; ⚠⚠ `QBN` IS DECLARATIONS PLUS A TASK LANGUAGE:**

    ⚠ `Item   _reward_      gold`
    ⚠ `Person _questgiver_  group Questor`
    ⚠ `Place  _mondung_     remote dungeon9`
    ⚠ `Foe    _monster_     is Nightblade`

> **⚠ *"SYMBOLS BIND TO A ⚠⚠ **KIND WITH CONSTRAINTS**, ⚠ **NEVER TO A SPECIFIC THING**, AND THE LOGIC ONLY EVER ADDRESSES THE SLOT. ⚠⚠ **THE QUEST CAN'T CONTRADICT ANYTHING BECAUSE IT NEVER NAMES ANYTHING** — ⚠ IT STATES **THE SHAPE OF WHAT IT NEEDS** AND THE BINDER FINDS A FIT."***

**⚠ ⚠⚠ THAT IS THE MECHANISM FOR GENERATING INTO A CANON THAT FORBIDS THINGS. ⚠ `PT-1011` CALLED IT *"THE HARDER PROBLEM AND THE INTERESTING ONE."* ⚠⚠ DAGGERFALL SOLVED IT BY **NEVER NAMING ANYTHING**.**

## PT-1098 — Class moves before Ability Scores, and a duplicate PT-1097 was caught while filing this

Owner ruling. Class is now step 4 in CHARACTER-CREATION-01, Ability Scores step 5 — swapped from the order set at PT-1091. Reasoning given: a class's priority abilities should be visible on screen before a player assigns scores, not after. Updated in CHARACTER-CREATION-01 section 3, and in the droid mapping table where class as SPECIALISATION was tagged step 5 and is now step 4.

Checked every other step-number reference in the document before editing — steps 1-2 preceding step 6 for the skill cap, steps 8-10 sitting after feats, lifestyle preceding equipment for the starting economy, and the droid step-2/model equivalence. None of them depend on the internal order between class and ability scores, only on both preceding skill points, which is unchanged. One reference needed updating; it was found and fixed.

And while filing this, audit_rulings.py blocked the gate on an unrelated collision: PT-1097 existed twice in the corpus, with different prose but the same underlying finding, both citing Atlas commit 8852499 and the same fifteen-world sample. This was an accidental double-write, not two decisions competing for one number. The duplicate has been removed, keeping the fuller of the two entries. Rule 4, check before writing, would have caught this before it was ever written twice; it caught it after, which is the fallback the check exists for.

## PT-1099 — Force Powers becomes step 8, and a rule we were already following gets named for the first time

Owner ruling. Force Powers creation step inserted right after Feats — step 8 — and everything from Profession onward shifts down by one (Profession 9, Lifestyle 10, Upbringing 11, Equipment 12, Name/Appearance/Backstory 13). The step is conditional: it exists only for a class that grants Force Powers. For a class that does not, the step is not shown, not greyed out — it does not render.

Placement inside the after-feats region is by category, not dependency, and the document now says so directly: Force Powers and Feats are both build choices; Profession, Lifestyle and Upbringing are background choices. Step 8 sitting immediately after step 7 keeps the two build steps adjacent rather than splitting them across the background block. The dependency reasoning still holds underneath that — Force Powers spends nothing from the skill-point budget, drawing instead from POWER-COSTS-01's own pool, so it cannot invalidate anything decided at step 6 any more than Profession or Lifestyle can.

Confirmed against the source before writing this: the KOTOR wiki states plainly that a player cannot receive Force Powers without a Jedi class, and the level-up screen does not present a Force Powers tab to a Soldier, Scout, or Scoundrel at all. Not disabled. Absent.

And the owner named something bigger than a step placement. This project has been doing exactly this — hide a locked-out option rather than show it disabled — three times already, in three separate rulings, none of which named it as a shared rule: Gender becomes Voice for a droid, droids skip Lifestyle entirely by owner ruling, and droids skip Upbringing entirely at PT-962 because it is organic only. Three independent instances of the same idea, and it took a fourth for anyone to say it out loud. Stated now as the governing rule for every future case: if a prior choice makes a later step meaningless, that step does not render. A player never sees the door that was never going to open.

## PT-1100 — The character creation structure, corrected against source and locked

Owner confirmed the mockup. Structure locked as: KOTOR own numbered sidebar for the visual and structural shape, since TRACE-08 found it is already a hub in KOTOR own idiom rather than tabs. NWN progressive-unlock discipline for ordering, since NWN has no Back or Next anywhere in its chargen and instead enforces order by disabling every button past the current step. Hiding, not disabling, reserved for genuinely inapplicable steps. KOTOR own live before-and-after arrow preview, shipped at character creation in 2003, as the model wherever a choice changes a derived number.

This corrects an assumption written into the vision doc two turns ago and I want that named plainly: I described the structure as NWN's step-by-step wizard flow before checking, and that flow does not exist in the source. The correction was caught by sending a Claude Code exploration pass before locking anything, not by getting lucky.

And two other sections of the vision doc updated on the same finding. The dashboard section gains a direct precedent: TRACE-08 confirms KOTOR own overlay hides the Force bar entirely, per party slot, for a non-Force character, not an empty bar. The nostalgia UI section, previously an honest open gap, is now answered: KOTOR ships its GUI as typed controls with absolute rectangles in a fixed 640 by 480 space, an explicit control-type enum, textures by name, and text through the same string table as dialogue — genuinely liftable. NWN ships a relative-offset scene graph that means little without resolving a template chain, and is not a good lift target, though it was still the right source for the ordering discipline above.

Two mockups were built before this locked, at the owner's request, specifically to make the structure legible before committing to it. Both are explicitly rough on visual specifics — the owner named that directly, distinguishing structure-is-locked from pixels-are-not. The lock icons, exact numbering treatment, and general visual polish remain open for a later pass.

## PT-1101 — Package main menu locked, checked against source rather than assumed twice

Owner confirmed the final mockup. Structure and layout both checked against actual source before locking, correcting two assumptions written into the vision doc originally and confirming a third that had been right by accident.

Confirmed against all three games' actual panel data, TRACE-09: KOTOR 1 is New Game, Load Game, Movies, Options, Exit, with a hidden developer module list and warp button the manual would never mention. KOTOR 2 reuses that panel wholesale. NWN's outer menu is New Game, Load, Multiplayer, Movies, Options, Exit.

Continue does not exist in any of the three, checked exhaustively across every panel. Adding it anyway, explicitly marked in the doc as ours rather than a borrowing, since the natural place for it in NWN's own chain does not have one either and that absence is not obviously a mistake worth correcting silently.

Music was a half-right guess. No jukebox in KOTOR 1 or NWN. KOTOR 2 has a complete one, including tracks that unlock as the player progresses. And the file that looks authoritative for K2's menu, the base panel, would have said no music button exists at all — it only shows up in the resolution-specific panels actually used on screen. Recorded as a standing methods note, not just a menu-specific fact.

Other content browsing, which I had proposed folding into this screen, is moved to Console Home instead. NWN's equivalent sits at the level of choosing which package, not inside one already chosen, and I corrected this in the same session before it locked rather than after.

Final order: Continue highlighted by default, then New Game, Load Game, Movies, Music, Options, Exit to Library. Exit is renamed deliberately, since leaving this screen returns to Console Home rather than closing the app.

Layout corrected against an actual K2 screenshot the owner provided, not assumed from the source read alone: centered bordered button stack rather than left-aligned, package title in the top-left corner separate from the buttons, and background art filling the full screen rather than a side panel. No KOTOR artwork reproduced in any mockup; placeholders are marked as placeholders.

Three mockups were built across two rounds of correction before this locked, each catching something the previous one had wrong.

## PT-1102 — Package main menu gains a collapsible party rail, and multiplayer party math gets its own section

Owner confirmed. Party rail added to the locked package main menu: the same roster from the multiplayer lobby, docked to the right edge at a compact scale, collapsible via a persistently visible tab so it is never more than one click away in either state. Interaction confirmed working in the mockup itself before locking, not just described.

Corrected an assumption of mine along the way, checked against PARTY-01 rather than invented: multiplayer party math is not empty seats filling with companions toward a fixed total. Solo fields three companions; multiplayer fields one per player, scaling with headcount rather than a cap. A package's player limit is a cap on human seats specifically, and the lobby is a roster built from that cap, with a live subtitle stating the current formula as headcount changes.

A new section 6 was added to APP-UI-VISION-01 to hold this properly, since the lobby and party math had been discussed and locked but never written into the document itself. Trailing sections renumbered, 6 to 7 and 7 to 8.

And a real requirement was surfaced without being designed: friends, invites, and in-game messaging need a genuine account system underneath them, not a locally-typed name. Flagged in both the party rail note and section 6, picked up separately from the screen-by-screen pass.

The human DM idea remains open and deliberately unwritten into the vision doc — engine resolves everything, AI drafts narration for the DM to send or edit, a copilot surface for suggestions, and the DM keeps every actual call — refined further toward a narrator-relay role rather than a full authoring one, and explicitly not locked. Framed by its own nature to survive changes in how the underlying AI works, since it is described by what it does rather than by any specific current capability.

## PT-1103 — Live visibility locked: one screen, three states, geometry-aware, and it closes ENGINE-SPEC-06 section 4

Owner ruling, confirmed. One screen, not a separate map pulled up on purpose. The tactical view a player is actually playing on renders three states at once: directly in front of the player right now, fully lit; somewhere previously visited but not currently occupied, dimmed and drawn from memory; somewhere never visited, blank. A room switches from blank to lit only once physically entered and stays at least dimmed from then on.

Visibility is geometry-aware, not distance-aware, by explicit owner instruction: blocked by walls and closed doors specifically, not revealed by a radius around the player regardless of what stands in the way. Confirmed against the weaker reading before locking — a proximity bubble that ignores walls was named and rejected in favor of this one.

Corrected against source before locking rather than assumed: the three-state lit/dimmed/blank pattern is not from either game. KOTOR's own map is binary, seen or not, staying fully clear forever once revealed with no dimming and no decay. NWN's actual play view has no fog of war at all, confirmed directly by TRACE-11. This is genuinely new design, marked as such in the doc the same way Continue and the account system were.

And the memory stays a display concern only. CANON-01 v2's local layer is already a projection, narrow to what is currently relevant, not a standing authority. The dimmed-room memory sits on top of that as a convenience for the player, not something the rules engine tracks or depends on. The engine's live context stays exactly as narrow as already decided.

This closes ENGINE-SPEC-06 section 4, previously unresolved. Choosing a visible grid at all had already forced absolute positioning as the answer; this ruling is what made that choice real rather than hypothetical. SW-7 is now unblocked in principle, though still on the acceptance ladder and not yet built. The five-metre problem from PT-1067/Q13 is unaffected and remains a playtest item, not a ruling — a separate question about how a radius rounds against grid squares, not about whether positions are absolute.

APP-UI-VISION-01 section 3 rewritten to hold this properly, replacing a speculative note that had connected fog of war to CANON-01 without having actually checked the connection. TRACE-11s tile grid finding also added as the structural precedent for the 2D grid itself, alongside the finding that KOTOR own map has no coordinate system to build on at all.

## PT-1104 — Dialogue check tags and multiplayer dialogue locked, both checked against source rather than assumed

Owner confirmed. Four TRACE passes (12, 13) plus direct owner rulings on everything the research could not settle.

Gate schema: all_of was already in RULES-02, nestable with any_of, sitting unsurfaced in ENGINE-SPEC-03 for eight rulings. This is the exact AND-versus-OR distinction KOTOR five separator spellings could never express, since typed bracket text has no way to nest or show precedence. Ours already had it. Surfaced properly now as section 4b.1.

Tag vocabulary: all eight skills kept as real checks, following the recommendation that in a structured field an unused skill costs one entry while cutting it forces an author around the system in typed text, exactly the drift the source data showed. Lie kept as a manner tag with no check at all. Threaten retired, folded into a real Intimidate check, explicitly marked as our own choice since KOTOR own Intimidate was manner-only, never gated, in every single occurrence surveyed.

Rendering, checked directly rather than inferred a second time after getting it wrong once: KOTOR reply list has exactly one styling slot for the whole listbox, confirmed by reading the panel data itself, not even hover states in the file. Plainness was a tooling limit of the era, not a design choice. Ours renders the same way, plain and inline with no pill or badge, but with the bracket text colored, which KOTOR had no capability to do at all. Three colors, three distinct meanings: amber for a real check showing no number until clicked and then revealing a separate panel with the DC as the headline figure, muted gray for a manner tag, teal for a background-gated option. Marked explicitly provisional by the owner rather than final, to be revisited once an actual build exists to test against.

Outcome-as-a-separate-line, the failure mode that let typos like Force Persaude ship silently to retail because the interface never knew it was rendering a check: cannot happen to us the same way, since a pass and a fail are already different nodes in a real tree by construction, not two loosely associated strings.

Stage directions confirmed as a real, needed category and explicitly left unbuilt.

Multiplayer dialogue: multiple players share one conversation, one picks at a time, the screen is identical and synchronized for everyone present, anyone nearby may join at any time, the initiator chooses whether to wait for others or start immediately, a yield-first-then-roll resolution when more than one player wants the same pick, whoever wins uses their own stats for whatever follows, and the initiator controls advancing plain NPC lines. Checked against NWN, the one reference game with real live multiplayer dialogue, then extended well past what any source covers by direct owner ruling. One thing named and explicitly not solved: what happens if the initiator disconnects mid-conversation.

Six mockups were built across this thread before any of it locked — two exploring the pill-versus-inline question, several exploring the check-reveal interaction — none of them treated as final until the underlying research actually existed to check them against.


---

## PT-1105 — The scroll window, shifting layout, zoom range, action economy UI, and tile art direction all locked in one pass

Owner confirmed across an extended thread of mockups. Six real design pieces, all checked against TRACE-14 or built as working interactions before being written in, none left as conversation only.

Scroll window: a continuously accumulating log distinct from dialogue's replace-based window, carrying narration, party exchanges, and non-dialogue rolls. Rolls here are player-initiated, not automatic-with-opt-out, overriding my own recommendation by deliberate owner call — an active turn where the player is already choosing what to spend each action-economy budget on should have them roll too. This matches, rather than contradicts, the two-stage check reveal already built for dialogue, which already used a roll button rather than an automatic result.

Multiplayer: same shared, synchronized rule as dialogue, with every line tagged by speaker, whether player, NPC, or DM.

Layout shift: rather than one fixed arrangement, the screen shifts between a flowing state, grid and scroll compact together, and a paused, decision-focused state, grid grown and scroll dimmed, triggered whenever the game genuinely needs a player's decision. Modeled on TRACE-14's finding that KOTOR lets players choose their own auto-pause moments and names the reason whenever it stops. Confirmed as an actual working toggle in a mockup before being written into the spec.

Zoom range: one continuous space from tactical through local to a full area map, extending PT-1103's one-screen principle further than originally scoped. All three freely selectable outside combat; combat locks the zoom to tactical automatically the instant a fight starts.

Action economy UI: one on-screen slot per budget, Move, Action, Bonus, Gear, Reaction, appearing only in the paused layout state. The combat math itself does not transfer from KOTOR's single-queued-action model per TRACE-14, but the compact-slot-with-full-menu-on-demand interface pattern does, confirmed as an actual click-to-expand interaction before being written in.

Tile art: direction set, not built. Real per-tile art is the plan, modeled on NWN's own toolset preview window, which lines up with TRACE-11's finding that NWN areas are already a grid of real textured tiles underneath. KOTOR's actual textures are real copyrighted art and are not being used, the same flag already raised for portraits. Placeholder flat color continues until real art is built or licensed.

APP-UI-VISION-01 section 3 rewritten to hold all of this properly. Two stale open questions removed from section 7 now that PT-1103 already answered both differently than they were phrased: the fog-of-war-versus-CANON-01 question, since memory turned out to be display-only rather than mapped to the canon layer, and the absolute-position ruling question, since PT-1103 already closed it.

## PT-1106 — BUILDER-VISION-01 created and the area/tile authoring foundation locked, started ahead of the original plan

Owner confirmed across three TRACE passes (15, 16) and an extended design conversation. A new document, since APP-UI-VISION-01 explicitly scoped itself to the player-facing app only with the builder deliberately deferred, and this grew past that boundary out of a tile-art question rather than waiting for the deferral to lift on schedule. Named plainly rather than quietly filed into the wrong document.

Foundation: the layout format is KOTOR-shaped, named pieces placed anywhere, not NWN's rigid grid, because that is the only one of the two formats that can hold both an ordinary tiled layout and a genuinely unique hand-placed room. Confirmed no genre mismatch: built, manufactured interiors are naturally the easier case for a tile system, not the harder one.

Two building modes, palette and freeform, both writing into the same underlying area format, with the combat grid drawing over either one identically once a fight starts, unaffected by which mode built it.

Interaction model adopted outright from NWN's toolset: one placement verb, many payloads, rather than a toolbar of separate tools. Applied to both modes, not only the palette one.

Area creation: two decisions only, name and art pack together on one screen, then size as a preset or exact dimensions, matching NWN's own wizard almost exactly.

The one locked-in decision worked out properly rather than left open: a palette piece's art pack locks in the moment placement begins, for the same technical reason NWN's tileset locks, since every placed piece would be an index into that pack's list. Scoped specifically to palette mode; freeform mode is not drawn from an indexed set the same way and is not subject to the same hard lock.

Area connections: confirmed as islands linked by named objects rather than touching edges, fitting the flexible foundation directly rather than merely resembling it. Bidirectional linking as two separate explicit actions, link-this-way and link-the-way-back, adopted outright as a cheap guard against a real authoring mistake.

Asset sourcing: KOTOR room models confirmed non-reusable as palette pieces, bespoke and single-use per TRACE-15, so palette assets must be built new rather than lifted. Textures for personal testing only, same temporary-placeholder treatment already established for portraits at PT-1105, never shipped.

Three open items named honestly rather than assumed solved: what our own art-pack boundary actually contains, the palette UI itself not yet screen-mocked, and whether freeform mode needs any structural guardrails at all.

## PT-1107 — Journal and message log locked, K2-specific rather than assumed from K1, with one deliberate readability departure

Owner confirmed across two mockups plus a before-and-after comparison. ## PT-1108 — Contextual targeting, the dual combat interaction settings, and the stealth presentation hybrid locked

Owner confirmed across an extended thread reconciling KOTOR combat UI research against our own turn structure. Three pieces locked, two named open and sequenced rather than forced.

Targeting: no standing target axis. A player picks an action first, and the game asks who only if that specific action needs a target. Deliberate departure from TRACE-21's finding that KOTOR runs two always-visible axes cycled identically, since that shape solves a real-time problem we do not have — our five action-economy budgets do not all need a target the way KOTOR's single action slot always did.

Two combat interaction systems: our own compact-slot-with-full-menu default, and a genuine second system, off by default, matching TRACE-14 and TRACE-21's actual spinner-cycling findings for anyone who wants the source games' specific feel. Building two real systems, accepted deliberately as worthwhile rather than scope creep, since it preserves already-researched material rather than inventing something new.

Stealth: mechanics fully untouched. SKILL-RESOLUTION-01 section 4 and ACTION-ECONOMY-01's Hide action stay exactly as already specified, an opposed check against the better of Awareness or Alertness granting the Hidden condition. Two presentation elements borrowed deliberately from TRACE-21: a real, clearly visible indicator while Hidden, correcting the source games' easy-to-miss checkbox and matching the nothing-hidden-by-default rule held everywhere else, and restoring Hidden disabling running, a real cost the source had that a bare opposed roll does not otherwise carry.

Two items named open in explicit priority order rather than assumed solved: a target-visual hybrid carrying some of the source games' flavor alongside our grid-based targeting, shape not yet decided and deliberately not mocked up before there is something concrete to react to; and Solo Mode, parked until the first is settled, having turned out to be one piece of a much larger system letting a party freely choose to split up and attempt things, deserving its own dedicated conversation rather than a decision made as a side effect of combat targeting. The Stealth-versus-Solo-Mode visibility asymmetry TRACE-21 flagged is already resolved by the stealth indicator above and does not wait on that future conversation.

APP-UI-VISION-01 section 3 extended with this material. A section-heading drop, the same class of error as PT-1107 note, was caught and corrected in the same pass before committing.

## PT-1123 — Exploration verb list drafted, and Persuade/Intimidate resolved into a general standing rule rather than a one-off decision

Owner confirmed a first-pass verb list across three categories, drafted from skills and mechanics already built rather than invented, plus one governing rule settled deliberately before the list itself, since it was recognized as likely to recur rather than being specific to two skills.

Persuade and Intimidate live exclusively in dialogue, no object-click shortcut into either. Generalized into a standing principle: if using a skill on a person requires communicating with them, it belongs to dialogue alone; if it is something physical done to a person or their things without requiring exchange, it is a normal exploration-catalog verb. Chosen specifically to prevent the same skill existing in two systems that could quietly drift apart from each other, and because dialogues existing fallback-generation system already covers ground a second path would only duplicate.

Verb list: object-directed covers Search, Open Lock, Disarm, Repair, Slice, Pick Pocket, and Track, each tied to its already-built skill, plus one consolidated Examine verb that auto-selects Xenology, Archaeology, Mysticism, or Science by what is actually clicked rather than exposing four separate buttons. Self-directed covers Rest, Meditate, using an item, and Force powers, all already built in REST-AND-MEDITATION-01. Party-directed covers Wait here, carrying Solo Mode from PT-1122, plus follow/regroup and trade.

Confirmed gaps recorded as deliberate rather than oversights: Alertness stays passive and automatic; Beast Handling and Pilot surface only when contextually relevant rather than sitting as permanent entries; Acrobatics, Athletics, and Swim stay folded into grid movement rather than becoming separate chosen actions.

Screen placement and the separate quickbar question both remain open, unchanged from PT-1122.

## PT-1173 — Downtime menu visibility split: permanent ineligibility hides, situational unavailability flags

Confirmed real gates from source before building visibility logic, rather than guessing. REST-AND-MEDITATION-01: Meditate is Force-sensitive characters only. CRAFTING-01 section 6: Craft is anyone, skill is the only gate, not class-locked. DROID-CONSTRUCTION-01 section 4: Build a Droid is locked to exactly three classes, Machinist, Droid Master, Engineer, anyone else NO; section 5 additionally requires all four parts and a workbench or Portable Workbench on hand.

This splits the four downtime options into two real categories, not one. Force-sensitivity and the droid-building class lock are permanent traits fixed at creation, matching PT-962s governing rule directly: if a prior choice makes a later step meaningless, that step does not render. Meditate is hidden entirely for a non-Force-sensitive character. Build a Droid is hidden entirely for a character in none of the three eligible classes.

Missing crafting components or missing droid parts and a workbench is a different kind of thing. Anyone is eligible to craft; a character simply carrying zero components today is not the door was never going to open, it is the door is open and you are out of key material right now. Locked: Craft always shows for any character, since the class gate does not apply, but displays a flagged unavailable state when zero components are carried. Build a Droid, for an eligible class, shows normally when parts and a workbench are on hand and shows the same flagged unavailable state when they are not, on top of already being hidden entirely for an ineligible class.

Rest has no gate at all and always shows active.

## PT-1174 — Owner ruling: three real entry points into the downtime menu, gated by one universal party-consent requirement

Owner ruling. The downtime menu (PT-1172, PT-1173) is proposed, not triggered directly, from three real surfaces:

    BUTTON        a direct camp control, available while exploring, out of combat
    SAFE LOCATION  being at base or the ship, reusing the existing REST-OR-SAFE-LOCATION
                   category PARTY-01 section 5 already uses for companion swapping
    TYPED          a natural-language alternate input, typing the intent directly
                   into chat rather than pressing the button, e.g. I want to break for camp

All three do the same thing: they open a proposal, not an immediate action.

The real mechanical core, in the owners own words: everybody in the area has to decide in order, since time passes naturally. Downtime advances the shared game clock for the whole party at once, so no single player can unilaterally spend everyone elses time. Read as a real design choice, not incidental phrasing: consent is collected in order, one player at a time, consistent with the ordered-resolution pattern this project already established for other shared multiplayer decisions, rather than a simultaneous show-of-hands. Every player present in the area must agree before the period actually begins and time advances. A single player declining stops the proposal outright.

> **⚠ SUPERSEDED BY `PT-1175`.** The unanimous-consent line above is replaced by a real majority vote at 50% or over. Kept here because the ordered-collection reasoning and the area/companion scoping above it still stand — only the pass threshold changed.

> **⚠ FURTHER SUPERSEDED BY `PT-1176`.** The area/companion scoping called "still stands" in the note directly above is no longer accurate on the area half: "the area" is replaced by "the planet" as the actual vote scope. The companion-exclusion half is untouched.

Companions and other NPCs present do not get a vote; this is a decision among the human players sharing the area, matching every other place this project has drawn that line.

Single-player: trivially satisfied, since there is only one player to consent.

Mechanism for what counts as the same area, and the actual consent-prompt UI, is next.

## PT-1175 — Owner ruling: camp proposal passes on a real vote, 50% or over, not unanimous consent

Owner ruling, correcting PT-1174s unanimous-consent line. Camp is a real vote among the human players present in the area, collected in the same ordered, one-at-a-time sequence PT-1174 already established. It passes at 50% or over, not strictly over 50%: a tie passes. Two yes votes out of four players is enough. One yes out of two players is enough.

Everything else PT-1174 set stands unchanged: companions and NPCs do not vote, the three entry surfaces (button, safe location, typed) are unaffected, single-player is trivially satisfied, and the vote is a real gate on the same shared game clock, not a formality.

## PT-1176 — Owner ruling: camp vote scope is the planet, not local proximity within it

Owner ruling, correcting the area scope PT-1174 left open. The vote is not scoped to the same map, module, or immediate vicinity within a location. It is scoped to the same planet. Every human player currently on that planet gets pulled into the vote regardless of which module or wing they are actually standing in, whether thats the Sith base or the Jedi enclave on the same world.

The ship is not a planet, so it is not covered by planet scope, and needs no separate rule to say so: a ship in transit or docked is already its own bounded shared space by definition, distinct from wherever it last dropped the party. Everyone aboard the ship at the time of a ship-triggered proposal is, trivially, everyone in that scope.

Everything else stands unchanged: three entry surfaces (PT-1174), ordered one-at-a-time vote collection (PT-1174), 50%-or-over passing threshold with ties passing (PT-1175), companions and NPCs excluded from the vote (PT-1174).

## TRACE-60 — classsel.gui / classsel_p.gui / cg_class.gui, all three READ. Both premises in the request were wrong; the real finding is sharper

Real files: K1 classsel.gui, gui.bif idx 5, 12,367 bytes, 640x480. K2 classsel_p.gui, idx 13, 13,057 bytes, 800x600, with _x console variant. Same _p/_x convention TRACE-59 confirmed for the galaxy map and TRACE-58 for the crafting family  now three independent confirmations, treat as settled.

Both screens are 18 controls with identical structure: title, instruction, heading, SIX 3D model viewports, six selection buttons, one description label, one back button.

Six viewports, all rendering simultaneously, not one that swaps  structurally nothing like the galaxy maps single 3D_PlanetModel. Slot 1 is drawn larger than the other five in both games. Six slots for three classes is three classes times two sexes: the screen picks class and sex at once.

THE REAL FINDING, and it corrects the framing this agent brought to the request. Not a layout constraint on authoring, and not a deliberate minimal-prose choice. A third thing: the mechanics were authored in full, structurally, and the control is roughly a tenth the size needed.

Measured both sides. dialogfont16x16 mean glyph advance approx 10px at 16px height gives K1 LBL_DESC 510x39 usable, approx 51 chars per line by 2 lines, approx 102 chars. K2 LBL_DESC 632x40 usable, approx 63 by 2, approx 127 chars. Two lines, both games.

The actual strings are not prose. K1s Soldier description is 320 chars with 14 newlines  a 15-line authored stat block: two-word header, Hit Die: dN, a Proficiencies list one per line, then Skill Points. Rendered into a two-line label, it overflows by 7.5x. Scoundrel is a 10-line block, 5x over. Hit Die sits at character 21 in every description in both games, a fixed authoring convention: mechanics lead, proficiency list and skill points follow.

So the widely-repeated community criticism, which this agent relayed uncritically into the request, is right about the symptom and wrong about the cause. Players may well have seen one line. But nothing was hidden by choice and nothing was constrained at authoring time. The writers produced a complete structured stat block for all 8 classes in each game, and the UI gave it two lines.

Priority 2, a clean negative twice over: the panel displays no numeric fields at all  18 controls, none capable of holding a number. But all 16 class descriptions across both games contain hit die, skill points, and a specific dice value in their text. The mechanical data is not absent from the screens data; it is inside the one string the screen cannot fit.

Priority 3, NWN. cg_class.gui, aurora_gui.bif idx 26, 3,255 bytes. Structurally different: a class listbox plus ctl_cg_help, a dedicated help pane rather than a fixed label. Descriptions run 642 to 1,237 chars against KOTORs 174 to 320, roughly 4x longer. Structure is the mirror image  NWN leads with a prose paragraph and trails three mechanical bullet lines; KOTOR leads with mechanics and trails prose. Both put the numbers in the string. NWN solved the problem by sizing the container, not by adding data widgets. No numeric fields on NWNs panel either.

Recommended button confirmed present, strref 127. Whether it defaults to Fighter is engine behaviour, not readable from panel data, and is NOT confirmed.

Explicit caveat carried from the extraction: the string-to-control mismatch is certain, measured on both sides. What the engine does with the excess is not readable from the files. LBL_DESC is a Label, not a ListBox, so no scrollbar and no scrolling exist  but whether it clips, wraps-and-clips, or shrinks to fit needs the running game. Every one of those outcomes is unflattering at a 15-into-2 ratio.

Design consequence, stated by the extraction and worth carrying verbatim in substance: the lesson is not add mechanical fields KOTOR omitted. KOTOR already wrote the stat block, then could not show it. Size the container to the content that already exists.

## PT-1191 — Class screen design consequence: size the container to the stat block that already exists, and a correction to this agents own framing

TRACE-60 corrects a claim this agent brought into the extraction request uncritically. Relaying the community criticism that KOTOR hid its class mechanics behind a single flavour line, the request asked whether that was a layout constraint on authoring or a deliberate choice. Both premises were wrong. The mechanics were authored in full  a 15-line structured stat block for Soldier, 10 for Scoundrel, Hit Die at character 21 in all 16 descriptions across both games  and the description control is a two-line label. Overflow of 7.5x on Soldier alone.

Real instance of a named failure mode this project already tracks: a claim circulating through multiple sources acquiring false solidity without anyone reading the primary. The criticism was right about what players experienced and wrong about why, and this agent passed it along as established rather than as a claim to test.

Design consequence adopted: do not add mechanical fields on the theory that KOTOR omitted them. It did not omit them. Size the description container to the stat block that already exists, and the screens real defect is fixed without authoring a word of new content. NWN independently confirms this is the right move  same engine, same authoring instinct of putting mechanics in the string, roughly 4x longer descriptions, and a dedicated help pane rather than a fixed label. NWN solved it by sizing the container, not by adding data widgets.

Structural findings carried into our design: six simultaneous model viewports is a KOTOR-specific solution to picking class and sex at once, three classes by two sexes, and does not transfer  our sex/gender pick is already its own step 3, locked at PT-1190, and we have 18 base classes rather than three. The description container being generously sized is what transfers.

Open, deliberately unresolved: what the source engine actually does with the overflow  clip, wrap-and-clip, or shrink-to-fit  is not readable from panel data and needs the running game. Does not block our design, since we are sizing to fit rather than reproducing the overflow.

Both files self-consistent, and both .mdx lengths match their headers exactly  10,198/6,400 for the blaster pistol, 37,803/11,936 for the lightsaber. Nothing corrupt, and the pair really is required: the .mdl carries structure, the .mdx carries vertex data, and the header size field proves the .mdl expects a specific .mdx alongside it.

Internal model names are cased differently from their filenames  w_Lghtsbr_001 and w_BlstrPstl_001. Anything matching models by name should not assume the filename casing.

Node structure, walked from the root:

    lightsaber       7 nodes, 4 levels deep, root -> Dummy01 -> lshandle01 -> 4 plane meshes
    blaster pistol   5 nodes, 3 levels, root -> two hook dummies + BlstrPst mesh -> Mesh03

THE LIGHTSABER CARRIES FOUR NAMED ANIMATIONS: powered, powerup, powerdown, throwout, plus throwback. This is the file-level confirmation of what TRACE-62 observed visually  the screenshot shows the blade ignited because the model itself ships an ignition state, not because the screen composites a separate effect. The four plane242/239/241/240 meshes are the blade planes, two of them flagged 0x821 against 0x021 for the others, the difference being the blade geometry that the animations drive.

The blaster pistol has NO animations and instead carries two attachment dummies, bullethook and muzzlehook  where the projectile spawns and where the muzzle flash renders. Two weapons, two entirely different data shapes, and the difference is exactly the difference between a weapon that turns on and a weapon that fires.

Bounding data is identical on both and is clearly not real geometry bounds: min (0,0,0), max (-5,-5,-1), radius 5.0. A max smaller than its min on every axis is a placeholder or an engine-ignored field, not a measurement. Do NOT use these to size a viewport  that number would be wrong. Real extents would have to come from the .mdx vertex data.

Design consequence for the upgrade screen: TRACE-62 established the lightsaber renders vertical and ignited. This confirms the ignition is intrinsic to the model and named powered, so a rebuild showing a lit blade is restoring an authored state rather than inventing a presentation effect.

## TRACE-64 — component_p CREATE and BREAK are ONE row in two modes, proven by coordinates, and every button carries a real string reference

Follow-up parse of component_p.gui ahead of designing the Workbench, checking what TRACE-61 recorded but did not interrogate.

THE TWO BUTTON ROWS ARE ONE ROW. Both sit at identical y, and four of five share exact x positions: 119, 219, 345, 599. Only the fourth slot differs, CREATE_LIGHTSABER at x463 w120 against BREAK_USEABLE at x469 w110, because the two modes genuinely need different fourth categories. So the screen does not stack a create row above a break row; it swaps one row in place. Same trick as LB_SHOPITEMS and LB_INVITEMS, the two listboxes stacked at one rectangle, and the same trick chemical_p uses for its two description listboxes. Three instances of stack-and-swap on one screen  it is this screens governing pattern, not an incidental saving.

Real mode structure recovered:

    CREATE   Armor . Ranged . Melee . Lightsaber . Misc
    BREAK    All . Weapons . Armor . Useable . Misc

BREAK leads with All, which CREATE has no equivalent of, and that asymmetry is real: you break down everything indiscriminately, you create one specific category at a time.

EVERY BUTTON CARRIES A GENUINE STRREF, and the numbering is itself evidence. The BREAK set is tightly clustered, 48544 to 48549, authored together in one pass. The CREATE set is scattered across 42296-42298, 435, 649  three from one block, two from very low numbers, meaning Lightsaber at 435 and Misc at 649 reuse strings that already existed elsewhere in the game rather than being written for this screen. The BREAK feature was authored as a unit; the CREATE row was assembled from parts.

Placeholder confirmed again: LBL_RELATEDSKILL ships literal My Skill with the no-strref sentinel, identical to chemical_p. Same unwired control on both screens. The three value labels, credits, cost and stock, all ship literal 999999, a width-testing placeholder rather than real data.

We hold the reference numbers but not dialog.tlk, so the actual words behind these strrefs remain unknown. Category names above are inferred from the control tags, which are unambiguous, not from the string table.
