## TRACE-67 — Parser bug found and fixed; class-vs-cross-class is a TEXT HEADER, not a colour; skills.2da carries a per-class flag AND a recommendation rank; seven feats can flip it

A parse correction first, and it was this agents error. TRACE-66 reported COLOR fields as null across the skill rows. They are not. COLOR uses GFF type 17, a three-float Vector, which this containers parser did not handle and silently returned None for  122 instances of it. Read as no colour data when the truth was the instrument could not read the field. A wrong-shape negative in this projects own taxonomy: searched correctly, wrong instrument. Parser patched for types 16 and 17 and committed; every .gui read from here carries real colour.

Real values, verified independently after the fix, and they are the house palette:

    <SKILL>_LBL          BORDER #0D5945   TEXT #1AB28C
    <SKILL>_POINTS_BTN   BORDER #FFFFFF   HILIGHT #FFFFFF   TEXT #1AB28C
    <SKILL>_PLUS/MINUS   BORDER #1AB28C   HILIGHT #CCCCB2

All eight rows identical, so the substantive finding stands: colour was never the mechanism. But populated-with-house-values is materially different from empty  an engine override would have to replace a colour, not fill a blank.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM IS A TWO-STATE TEXT HEADER. CLASSSKL_LBL swaps between an adjacent string pair, 38152 Class Skill and 38153 Cross-class Skill, and two further strings carry the consequence to the description pane: 42178, class skills cap at current level plus 3, and 42179, cross-class at half that. Geometry confirms the intent  CLASSSKL_LBL at (410,174) sits directly above LB_DESC at (410,210), so it is a header for the description pane serving whichever row is highlighted, not a per-row annotation. Category plus consequence, stated in words.

SOURCE OF THE FLAG IS DATA, NOT CODE, and richer than expected. skills.2da carries TWO columns per class across fifteen class prefixes, thirty columns total: <cls>_class as a boolean, and <cls>_reco as a recommendation rank from 1 best to 8 worst. So BTN_RECOMMENDED is driven by genuine per-class authored data rather than NWNs fixed answer  a real point in K2s favour over its own ancestor.

AND THE FLAG IS MUTABLE. feat.2da rows 183 to 189 are seven feats, CLASS_SKILL_AWARENESS through CLASS_SKILL_TREAT_INJURY, whose entire function is converting a cross-class skill into a class skill, with prerequisite text stating the skill is currently cross-class for that character. Direct consequence for our rebuild: class-skill status is per-character mutable state, not a static lookup from class. Persuade is the sole exception with no conversion feat.

## TRACE-68 — Skill Focus is real but disabled; Class Skill conversion is live and K2-only. Verified independently in our own feat tables

Owner recalled a focus visual for skills. Chased and resolved: the memory is of a real mechanic, but not the one that shipped working. Every claim below verified directly against feat.2da for both games in this containers own holdings, not accepted on report.

    K1   8 x XXXX_SKILL_FOCUS_*   all prefixed, all disabled
         0 x CLASS_SKILL_*        the feature does not exist in K1
    K2   8 x XXXX_SKILL_FOCUS_*   same eight, still disabled
         7 x CLASS_SKILL_*        UNPREFIXED, live

XXXX_ is BioWares disabled-row convention, and the surrounding live feats confirm it  TWO_WEAPON_FIGHTING, ARMOUR_PROF_HEAVY and CAUTIOUS all sit unprefixed in the same table. So Skill Focus was authored in both games and shipped unobtainable in both.

The live mechanic is K2s alone: seven feats converting a cross-class skill to a class skill, one each for Awareness, Computer Use, Demolitions, Repair, Security, Stealth and Treat Injury. PERSUADE HAS NO CONVERSION FEAT  seven, not eight, verified rather than assumed. The one social skill cannot be bought into.

Two consequences for our build, both real. First, class-skill status is per-character MUTABLE STATE, not a static lookup from class, because a feat can flip it mid-campaign. Any screen showing this has to read character state. Second, the sources own answer to how to display it is a two-state TEXT HEADER above the description pane per TRACE-67, not a colour  and since our aptitude is the same mechanic under SKILLS-01s own renaming, that answer transfers directly.

Incidental worth keeping: the package tables offering the full Skill Focus and Class Skill sets are named packftbarb, packftbard, packftcler, packftdruid, packftfight, packftmonk, packftpala, packftrang, packftrog, packftwiz  D&D classes that do not exist in KOTOR. NWN inheritance sitting in K2s data, matching CHARACTER-CREATION-01s own finding that seven K1 tables carry NW_ resrefs and the chargen is NWNs reskinned. The tables named for real KOTOR classes carry a much thinner set, and K1 has no package tables at all.

## TRACE-69 — ⚠ AUTHORED .gui COLOURS ARE NOT WHAT RENDERS. Owner screenshot overturns TRACE-67 and TRACE-68s colour conclusion

Owner supplied a screenshot of K2s chargen skills screen after both this agent and Claude Code concluded colour was never the mechanism. The owner was right and both analyses were wrong.

IDENTIFICATION IS CERTAIN, by arithmetic not eye. Predicted control positions from skchrgen_p.gui land exactly on the image at 1920x960: the three bottom buttons at x180/492/804 with widths 288/288/384, eight rows at a 41px source pitch, and CLASSSKL_LBL at (984,278) 720x44. It is the file this agent parsed.

THE FINDING: every control listed above carries authored TEXT colour #1AB28C in the file. The screenshot renders the eight skill NAME labels and the CLASS SKILL header in AMBER/GOLD, with teal reserved for chrome, values, and description text. The engine overrides authored colour at runtime.

So TRACE-67s verified colour values were real, but they are the files INTENT, not what a player sees. Anything this project concludes about colour from a .gui alone is provisional until seen rendered. Recorded as a standing caution: .gui colour is authored intent, not observed output.

What survives from TRACE-67 and TRACE-68: the mechanism is still the two-state text header, CLASSSKL_LBL, swapping between Class Skill and Cross-class Skill. The screenshot shows exactly that header, reading Class Skill for the highlighted Awareness row, sitting directly above the description pane. Still not a per-row marker  all eight skill names render amber regardless of their class status.

So the honest synthesis is: colour IS present and IS part of how this screen reads, contrary to both prior conclusions, but it distinguishes label from chrome rather than class skill from cross-class. The class distinction remains carried by the headers text. The owners memory of a colour was correct; the inference that colour therefore marked class status was not.

Also visible and worth keeping: the minus and plus controls are mutually exclusive per row and reflect state rather than class  rows at 4 show minus, rows at 0 show plus, with Remaining Points at 0. And the description pane leads with Related Attribute: Wisdom, a per-skill governing-attribute line this project has not yet accounted for in its own skills screen.

## PT-1198 — Owner ruling: Upbringing and Profession merge into BACKSTORY at step 4, and a real contradiction between two of our own documents is resolved

Owner ruling, arrived at while checking whether aptitude sources changed the creation order. They do, and the check surfaced a contradiction this project had been carrying unnoticed.

THE CONTRADICTION. CHARACTER-CREATION-01 3 justifies placing Upbringing and Profession late, at steps 9 and 11, on the stated ground that none of them feeds the skill-point cap, citing PT-705 that UPBRINGING-01 grants nothing mechanical. SKILLS-01 11.2 says the opposite in its own table: Background aptitude comes from HOMEWORLD and UPBRINGING always, plus a THIRD from PROFESSIONS-01 if the player gives up their starting item per PT-695. Upbringing cannot both grant nothing mechanical and always grant an aptitude. SKILLS-01 is the more specific and more recent statement and is followed.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. Aptitude halves the cost of a rank, 1 point instead of 2, and raises the cap from half level plus 3 to level plus 3. A player spending skill points at step 6 without knowing their full aptitude set is spending at prices that later steps will change. Three of the five aptitude sources in SKILLS-01 11.2 currently land AFTER step 6: Skill Focus feats at 7, Profession at 9, Upbringing at 11.

THE RULING. Upbringing and Profession merge into a single step named BACKSTORY, placed at step 4, immediately after Species, Homeworld and Gender and BEFORE Class. Both are chosen there, and both resolve their aptitude grants there. The three who-you-are sources SKILLS-01 names  species, homeworld, background  now all complete before any point is spent.

⚠ NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED: step 13 is currently NAME, APPEARANCE, BACKSTORY, and PT-1180 placed portrait selection there. Two steps cannot both be called Backstory. The step 13 item is prose the player writes; this new step 4 is two structured choices. One of them needs renaming and the owner has not been asked yet.

⚠ ALSO OUTSTANDING: Lifestyle, currently step 10, was not mentioned in this ruling. It touches starting credits rather than skills so it does not share the aptitude problem, but it is a background choice now separated from the other two. And PT-695s conditional third aptitude depends on giving up a starting item, which is decided at Equipment  now step 12, still after Backstory. That dependency runs backwards and needs its own decision.

## TRACE-70 — Runtime pulse and colour override confirmed as REAL MECHANISMS; authored PULSING verified zero across 322 fields; the amber remains unexplained

Claude Code report on the two runtime questions. The verifiable half was checked here independently rather than accepted.

VERIFIED IN THIS CONTAINER, counts match exactly: skchrgen_p 120 PULSING fields, abchrgen_p 108, ftchrgen_p 36, abilities_p 58. 322 total, every one zero. The source authored no pulse on any chargen or ability screen.

BUT AUTHORED ZERO DOES NOT MEAN NOTHING PULSES, and this is the substantive finding. The GUI layers render condition is reported as three independent triggers: the authored pulsing flag, OR hover on a clickable control, OR selection state. The authored field is one of three. So every plus and minus button and every row on these screens is eligible to pulse on touch or selection with PULSING set to 0 throughout. The pulse is global rather than per-control  a shared pulseOpacity sampled from the menu manager and applied as an opacity multiplier across border, highlight and text.

AND THE SAME PATH REPAINTS TEXT COLOUR: when the condition is true, text is set to defaultHighlightColor, so a hovered or selected control stops rendering at its authored colour. That is a SECOND independent route by which the files teal is not what renders, alongside TRACE-69s amber finding.

The real K2 engine carries a debug command highlightparams color alpha pulse frequency  a global highlight system with runtime colour, alpha, pulse toggle and frequency, none of which exist in any panel file. Correctly flagged as the most likely candidate for the amber and correctly NOT claimed as confirmed.

A REAL NEGATIVE on the in-game panel: GUICreatureSkill, the proto builder for those rows, varies colour on exactly one condition, selected, and contains no class-skill check, no skills.2da read, and no per-skill branch. But it does not apply to the chargen screen, which has no listbox  skchrgen_ps eight rows are individually authored controls. So the negative is real for the in-game panel and does not settle the chargen screen.

THE AMBER IS STILL UNEXPLAINED. Ruled out: any 2DA, since K2 has no GUI colour or palette table at all; and the chargen menu logic, which contains no colour manipulation. Not ruled out: the global highlight system. Honest not-determined rather than an inference dressed as an answer.

⚠ STANDING CAUTION, now widened. TRACE-69 established that authored colour is intent rather than output. This extends it: treat EVERY authored visual field on these panels  colour, pulsing, and plausibly alignment and alpha  as a default the engine may replace. Two of the three sources here are the reimplementation rather than the engine, and this project has repeatedly found its TSL side thin; engine strings win where they disagree.

## PT-1200 — The conditional third aptitude is FORWARD-LOOKING. Steps stay final once left

Closes the backwards dependency flagged at PT-1198. PT-695 grants a third background aptitude from PROFESSIONS-01 only if the player gives up their starting item, but Backstory now sits at step 4 and Equipment at step 11, with Skill Points spent at 7 in between.

Owner ruling: option 1 of two. The aptitude is FORWARD-LOOKING. No repricing, no reordering.

The real consequence, stated plainly rather than left to be discovered: aptitude does two things, halves cost per rank and raises the cap. Arriving at step 11, after points are spent at step 7, THE COST HALF IS WORTHLESS FOR THIS LEVELS POINTS. Only the cap raise still applies, and only where headroom remained. So the trade is a real starting item for a benefit that does nothing at level 1 and begins paying at level 2.

That is defensible and thematically right  you traded your gear for training that pays off from here on  but it is a weaker deal than it looks, and a player could reasonably expect immediate value. ⚠ THE EQUIPMENT SCREEN MUST SAY SO. The offer has to state that the aptitude applies from the next level, not this one. An unstated forward-looking benefit reads as a bad trade discovered late.

The governing principle this preserves, and the reason option 2 was declined: EVERY STEP IS FINAL ONCE LEFT. Repricing skill costs at step 11 would mean step 7 is not actually finished when the player leaves it, which is the shape this whole creation flow has avoided  each step resolves and stays resolved.

## TRACE-71 — Feat chaining is fully data-driven and pips is the display field. Red is authored in seven files but NOT on the feat screen

Parsed with this projects own scripts/parse2da.py rather than by hand. k2_feat.2da carries 245 rows and 90 columns, and the chain structure is entirely in the data:

    successor      123 feats   links FORWARD to the next tier
    prereqfeat1    122 feats   links BACK to what gates it
    masterfeat      21 feats   the umbrella a chain belongs to
    pips           242 feats   THE TIER NUMBER

PIPS IS THE ANSWER TO HOW A CHAIN DISPLAYS. Worked example, verified: POWER_ATTACK row 28 pips 1 successor 17; IMPROVED_POWER_ATTACK row 17 pips 2 prereq 28 successor 83; MASTER_POWER_ATTACK row 83 pips 3 prereq 28. Three feats, one chain, and the row itself carries its position in it. 242 of 245 feats have a pip value, so it is near-universal rather than a special case.

Note prereqfeat1 on the master tier points at 28, the FIRST tier, not the second. The chain is not a strict linked list on the prerequisite side even though successor makes it one going forward.

RED: authored red exists in seven K2 panel files at seven distinct values  #94362E computer_x, #B20000 equip_p, #BD1C00 mipc28x6_p, #CC0000 maininterface_x, #E50000 maininterface_x, #FA0000 optkeyentry_p, #FF0000 in mipc28x6_p, top_p and top_x. So red is a real part of this interfaces vocabulary.

⚠ BUT NOT ONE OF THEM IS ON ftchrgen_p, AND THE FEAT SCREEN HAS NO AUTHORED RED AT ALL. So the red the owner recalls on feats is, like the amber at TRACE-69, an engine-applied runtime state rather than an authored field. Consistent with TRACE-70s finding that the render path repaints text colour independently of what the file says.

The likely condition is prerequisites unmet, computed per row from prereqfeat1 and the other gating columns  mincharlevel, minattackbonus, minstr, mindex, minint, minwis, reqskill, and five orreqfeat columns. That is an inference from the available columns, NOT confirmed, and follows the same honest limit as the amber: the panel file cannot settle a colour the engine applies.

## PT-1202 — Feats screen structure locked: a three-column icon grid, one chain per row. ⚠ WITH AN OPEN ACCURACY DEBT ON CELL SPACING

Locked after two wrong rebuilds and an owner screenshot that corrected both. Recording the error plainly because it is the point.

The .gui gives control geometry and labels only; it contains no rendered image, so every visual claim beyond position and size was inference presented as fact. THE FEAT ICON WINDOW MUST BE MADE TO MATCH THE GAME EXACTLY before this screen is built. Real cell dimensions, real gutters, real row pitch, checked against a screenshot rather than derived. ## TRACE-72 — pwrlvlup_p is ftchrgen_ps twin, but the Force power DATA will not fit its grid

Parsed ahead of designing step 9. The screen is a near-clone of the feat screen: 13 controls, identical positions, identical 800x600 panel, identical 56px row height, identical three-button footer at the same coordinates.

Three real differences from ftchrgen_p:

    row width   257 feats   ->  264 powers
    padding       4 feats   ->    0 powers
    naming    BTN_SELECT    ->  SELECT_BTN

The naming flip, prefix against suffix, is an authoring tell: two otherwise cloned screens built by different hands or at different times. 264 divided by three is 88px per cell against the feat screens 85.7.

BUT THE DATA DOES NOT MATCH THE LAYOUT, and this is the finding. k2_spells.2da holds 282 rows and its chain structure is nothing like feat.2das:

    masterspell      EMPTY ON ALL 282 ROWS  no master-group layer at all
    prerequisites    89 of 282 only         193 powers are standalone
    compound         25 of those 89 encode TWO prerequisites in one field,
                     underscore-joined, e.g. 47_12, 18_24, 43_35

Feats separate prereqfeat1 and prereqfeat2 into their own columns; powers pack a set into one field. Different authoring convention for the same idea.

CHAIN SHAPE, mapped: 46 roots, and depth is NOT uniform. 28 chains are two deep, 16 are three deep, only 2 reach four. And they BRANCH  FORCE_POWER_WOUND is the prerequisite for BOTH CHOKE and KILL, so it is a tree, not a line. Worked examples verified: SLOW to AFFLICTION to PLAGUE; DRAIN_LIFE to DEATH_FIELD; LIGHT_SABER_THROW to its ADVANCED form.

⚠ CONSEQUENCE FOR OUR BUILD, flagged rather than designed around silently: a fixed three-column grid holds the feat data cleanly because feats are uniform three-tier chains. It does NOT hold this. A power row would need variable width for depths of one, two, three and four; branches would need to fork rather than run straight; and 193 of 282 powers would sit alone in column one with two empty cells beside them. The source shipped the same grid for both screens regardless, which is worth knowing before copying it  the layout was reused, not designed for this data.

Owner request, recorded to BUILDER-VISION-01 8 rather than only here so it sits with the rest of the builders open scope.

The builder should let an author DEFINE new entries in these categories, not merely place existing ones. Noted while parsing the sources own tables, which makes the shape clear: feat.2da and spells.2da are plain row-and-column data carrying an icon reference, a description string reference, prerequisite links and per-class availability flags. A new feat or power is a new ROW, structurally, not new code. Skills are the same shape.

So a functional authored power implies an effect system the builder can address, which is a far larger commitment than a row editor. Recorded as the open question rather than assumed away.

## PT-1204 — Force Powers screen locked: icon grid with arrows BETWEEN columns, variable chain depth, and TWO independent colour channels

Locked from the owners screenshot, which answered the question TRACE-72 raised about whether a three-column grid could hold non-uniform chains. It can, and the mechanism is simple: GREEN ARROWS SIT BETWEEN THE COLUMNS, and a row stops where its chain stops. A three-deep chain draws three icons and two arrows; a two-deep chain draws two and one; a standalone power draws one icon and no arrows. No empty cells, no padding to a fixed width. That is how the source absorbs depths of 1, 2, 3 and 4 in one grid.

Right column confirmed live, in order: the power name as a bordered header, an armour-restriction line where one applies, the description, and a THREE-ROW COST TABLE reading BASE COST, ADJUSTMENT, COST PER USE. That table confirms in the running game what TRACE-60 could only infer from string references  the three-row block on this screen is a Force-power cost readout, not a skill rank readout.

⚠ TWO INDEPENDENT COLOUR CHANNELS, and they must not be conflated in the build:

    ICON ARTWORK   by alignment. Verified in k2_spells.2das goodevil column:
                   E on 30 powers, G on 28, and - on 224. Dark, light, neutral.
                   A real authored field, not a render effect.
    BOX BORDER     by selectability. Red box means the player CANNOT take it,
                   the same hard state PT-1202 locked for feats.

So a red icon inside a red box means a dark-side power that is also unavailable  two different facts wearing the same colour for unrelated reasons. Worth stating plainly because the obvious implementation, one colour per row, would silently merge them.

⚠ SAME ACCURACY DEBT AS PT-1202, carried forward deliberately. Cell size, gutters and arrow spacing in the mockup are approximated. pwrlvlup_ps rows are 264 wide with PADDING 0 against the feat screens 257 and PADDING 4, but as the feat screen proved twice, the files geometry does not describe what the cells actually look like. THE POWER ICON WINDOW MUST BE MATCHED TO THE GAME EXACTLY before this screen is built, same as the feat window.

## PT-1205 — HOMEWORLD absorbs UPBRINGING and is renamed ORIGIN. Lifestyle joins Backstory. Eleven steps

Owner ruling, and it corrects a grouping this project had wrong from the start rather than merely reshuffling.

ORIGIN, step 2: Homeworld and Upbringing merged and renamed. The justification was already sitting in SKILLS-01 11.2, which lists Background aptitude as coming from HOMEWORLD and UPBRINGING ALWAYS  one category, two halves, treated as a pair by the rules before any screen existed. Splitting them across steps 2 and 11 cut across our own taxonomy. Origin is the honest name for where you are from and how you were raised.

BACKSTORY, step 4: now Profession and Lifestyle, correcting PT-1198 which had paired Profession with Upbringing. Backstory is what you did and how you lived; Origin is where you came from. Cleaner than the earlier split, and it puts Lifestyle with the other background choice rather than stranded at step 10 alone.

ELEVEN STEPS, down from thirteen originally and twelve after PT-1199: Species, Origin, Gender, Backstory, Class, Ability Scores, Skill Points, Feats, Force Powers, Equipment, Name and Appearance.

Every aptitude source still resolves before points are spent at step 7, which was PT-1198s whole purpose and survives the reshuffle: species at 1, homeworld and upbringing at 2, profession at 4.

DROID HANDLING PRESERVED THROUGH BOTH MERGES, and worth stating because merging steps could have hidden it. A droid takes its MODEL in place of the homeworld half of Origin  PT-958  and SKIPS THE UPBRINGING HALF ENTIRELY, PT-962, organic only. A droid gets no Lifestyle by owner ruling. So both merged steps render partially for droids rather than being skipped or shown whole, consistent with PT-1099s hide-what-cannot-apply rule operating INSIDE a step rather than only on whole steps.

⚠ CARRIED FORWARD UNRESOLVED: whether a droid takes a Profession at all. Backstory is now Profession plus Lifestyle, and droids are excluded from Lifestyle but nothing on record excludes them from Profession. If they do take one, Backstory renders half for a droid; if not, the whole step hides.

## PT-1206 — Owner ruling: a droid takes PROGRAMMINGS, not a Profession, and no Lifestyle. Backstory renders half for droids

> **⚠ PARTLY WRONG — CORRECTED AT `PT-1207`.** The ruling below claims programmings do not exist and need authoring. **They do exist:** `rules/PROGRAMMINGS-01.md` is a complete 142-line document with seventeen entries, ruled at `PT-773`/`PT-774`/`PT-777`, and its opening line already states that a droid takes a Programming rather than a Profession. The negative below was a **wrong-shape search** — it grepped file contents for a string and never checked for a document by that name, in the directory it was searching. What survives: the droid-takes-programmings ruling itself, and the substitute-or-hide pattern named below.

Owner ruling. Checked the corpus first rather than assuming it was already recorded, and it was not.

WHAT THE CORPUS ACTUALLY SAYS. Programming appears throughout the droid documents but NEVER as a counterpart to Profession. Every occurrence is hardware, upgrade capacity, or flavour prose  monster-droid lore in DROID-CONSTRUCTION-01, protocol-droid language databases in DROID-MODELS-01, Droid Upgrade 1-3 describing a chassis capacity to receive hardware in FEATS-LIBRARY-01. DROID-INSTALLATION-01 66 actively rules programming OUT as installable, and states why: if programming is installable, every droid feat is  a droid that can buy its skills, its reflexes and its judgement is a droid that never advances at all.

And PROFESSIONS-01 excludes droids from LIFESTYLE only, at 3 and PT-692, never from Profession. So the droid half of Backstory was genuinely undecided, exactly as PT-1205 flagged.

THE RULING, recorded as new content rather than dressed up as pre-existing: a droid takes PROGRAMMINGS in place of a Profession, and takes no Lifestyle at all. Backstory therefore renders HALF for a droid  the Profession slot becomes Programmings, the Lifestyle tab does not appear.

WHY IT FITS. This is the third instance of the same substitution shape this project has already used twice: Gender becomes VOICE for a droid, Homeworld becomes MODEL. Now Profession becomes PROGRAMMINGS. In each case the step survives and its content is replaced, rather than the step being hidden  which is distinct from PT-1099s hide-what-cannot-apply rule and worth naming as its own pattern: SUBSTITUTE WHERE AN EQUIVALENT EXISTS, HIDE WHERE NONE DOES. Lifestyle is hidden because PT-692 found no droid equivalent  a droid was built, and what were you before this has no answer. Profession has one, because what you were BUILT TO DO is a real question with a real answer.

⚠ OUTSTANDING, AND SUBSTANTIAL: the programmings themselves do not exist. PROFESSIONS-01 carries twelve professions each granting an item OR an aptitude per PT-695. An equivalent programmings list needs authoring  how many, what each grants, and whether the item-or-aptitude trade carries across. Until then the droid branch of this screen cannot be built, only the organic one.

## PT-1207 — ⚠ PT-1206 CORRECTED. PROGRAMMINGS-01 already exists, fully authored, seventeen entries. This agent filed a wrong negative

Owner pointed at a more recent decision and named a search term. It found rules/PROGRAMMINGS-01.md immediately  a complete document, 142 lines, seventeen programmings, ruled at PT-773, PT-774 and PT-777.

WHAT PT-1206 GOT WRONG. It stated that programming appears throughout the droid documents but NEVER as a counterpart to Profession, and that the programmings do not exist and need authoring. Both claims are false. The documents own opening line is A DROID DOES NOT TAKE A PROFESSION  PT-692. IT TAKES A PROGRAMMING. The ruling was filed as new content when it had been settled for hundreds of rulings.

HOW THE NEGATIVE FAILED, named in this projects own taxonomy: a WRONG-SHAPE NEGATIVE. The search was for the string programming inside rules/*.md content, which matched hardware and flavour prose in other files and buried the real hit. It never checked for a DOCUMENT BY THAT NAME, and PROGRAMMINGS-01 sits in the same directory that was being searched. The instrument matched the wrong shape and the absence was reported as a finding. Same failure class as TRACE-67s null-colour report.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON RECORD, verified by reading it:

    SEVENTEEN programmings. THIRTEEN mapped from professions, and FOUR
    chassis-locked with no organic equivalent  Probe (Remote only),
    Utility (Astromech only), Security (Battle and Assassin),
    Scavenged (any chassis).

Each carries a grant, a credit cost, and an upgrade path, in the same item-shaped form professions use  Medical Droid from Doctor grants 2 Medpacs at 80cr upgrading to Advanced Medpacs; Slicer Droid from Slicer grants 2 Computer Spikes at 500cr. The substitution pattern named there  SUBSTITUTE WHERE AN EQUIVALENT EXISTS, HIDE WHERE NONE DOES  still holds and is still worth having named. Only the it does not exist half is withdrawn.

## PT-1209 — ⚠ PT-1208 CORRECTED. Chassis IS species, not a substitute for it. Class stays Class. Backstory stays at step 4

Owner caught two structural errors in PT-1208s droid path diagram. Both checked against the corpus and both confirmed.

CHASSIS IS NOT A SUBSTITUTION. SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2 states it directly: Four droid chassis are full species records  Droid, Astromech, Droid, Assassin, Droid, Battle, Droid, Remote  with a shared Droid block above them. CHASSIS IS SPECIES. So step 1 is not Species becomes Chassis. Step 1 is Species, the player selects Droid, and chassis resolves BENEATH it.

AND THE SHAPE IS ALREADY BUILT. A shared parent record with variant records under it is EXACTLY PT-1182s subrace structure  the same pattern as Aqualish resolving to Aquala, Quara or Ualaq. Chassis is to Droid what a subrace is to a species, and the Species screen already handles that case: it does not resolve until the second-level pick is made. No new mechanism, no substitution. The droid path uses a screen this session already locked.

MODEL IS DOWNSTREAM OF CHASSIS, not the reverse. DROID-MODELS-01 is titled makes and models, BY CHASSIS and organised that way, so chassis chosen at step 1 constrains the model menu at step 2  the same relationship D-CARD-01s cardinality bands create between species and homeworld.

CLASS STAYS CLASS. PT-958s Specialisation was naming the concept, not renaming the step. There is no droid-facing rename; the closed-class rules differ per chassis and that is all.

BACKSTORY STAYS AT STEP 4, confirmed after the owner asked whether it belonged later with Name and Appearance. It cannot move. Profession carries a conditional third aptitude at PT-695, aptitude changes what a skill rank COSTS, and skill points are spent at step 7  so Profession must resolve before then or points are spent at prices a later step revises. That was PT-1198s entire purpose. Lifestyle has no such constraint and rides along as the other background choice.

⚠ AND THE SAME HOLDS FOR THE DROID BRANCH, verified rather than assumed: PROGRAMMINGS-01 shows Navigation Droid granting NOTHING but the aptitude  the aptitude IS the grant, PT-703. Aptitude is the shared currency across all seventeen programmings, so Programming sits at step 4 for exactly the reason Profession does.

The corrected droid path: Species (droid, chassis as subrace) at 1, Origin (model only) at 2, Gender/Voice at 3, Backstory (programming only) at 4, Class at 5, and steps 6-11 unchanged with Force Powers hidden. Three substitutions, not four  step 1 was never one.

CHARACTER-CREATION-01 step 1 now records that a droid is selected there with chassis resolving beneath it as a subrace, and step 5 records that Class is not renamed for droids.

⚠ THE REAL LESSON, recorded rather than resolved: filing a ruling FEELS like completing the work and is not. Nine screens were locked, pushed, and celebrated across this session while the document a builder would actually read stayed silent about all of them. Worth checking the doc side explicitly at each lock rather than trusting that the ruling covered it.

## PT-1212 — Origin runs as TWO STAGES inside one step: world first, then the panel becomes the upbringing menu

Owner ruling on how the merged step actually behaves rather than merely what it contains.

The world is chosen first, on the map, with its three-skill aptitude menu. Confirming it TRANSITIONS THE PANEL IN PLACE into the upbringing menu  not a new screen, not a scroll, not two panels side by side. The chosen world and skill carry into the upbringing header, and a change control returns to stage one without leaving the step. A stage indicator sits top right so the player can see where they are in a two-part decision.

WHY THIS SHAPE RATHER THAN TWO PANELS AT ONCE. There is a real dependency between the halves: the skill menu belongs to the world, so it cannot render until a world exists. Showing both simultaneously would mean showing an empty or speculative menu beside an unmade choice. Sequence expresses the dependency honestly; side-by-side would hide it.

And it keeps the merged step feeling like ONE step. PT-1205 merged Homeworld and Upbringing because they are one category  where you came from. Splitting them visually across a screen would undo in presentation what the merge established in structure.

Consistent with PT-1182s subrace behaviour on the Species screen, which also refuses to resolve until a second-level pick is made. Same principle: a step with an internal dependency resolves in order, not all at once.

Filed after the gate caught this ID being cited in APP-UI-VISION-01 before the ruling existed  audit_rulings.py blocking on CITED BUT NEVER WRITTEN. The check worked exactly as designed.

## PT-1214 — Step 11 renamed IDENTITY, runs portrait then name, and ends with Accept. Play belongs to the hub, confirmed in custpnl_p

Owner ruling, and the file check confirmed the instinct behind it.

RENAMED from Name and Appearance to IDENTITY. Two stages inside one step, the same shape PT-1212 locked for Origin: portrait first, Accept, then the name box.

STAGE ONE, portrait, built on portcust_ps real geometry: a 90x90 portrait flanked by 25x50 arrows at x157 and x281, inside a 572x270 head area. Our version keeps the flanking-arrow arrangement and adds a preset strip plus a CUSTOM UPLOAD SLOT, per PT-1180s finding that NWN ships genuine custom-portrait support via a player-side folder.

STAGE TWO, name, built on name_ps real proportions: a small centred 340x150 panel rather than a full screen, with NAME_BOX_EDIT at 320x30 and a FULL-WIDTH BTN_RANDOM above two equal-width footer buttons. The random-name generator is real source behaviour, strref 48760, not an addition.

THE FINAL BUTTON QUESTION, checked rather than assumed. The owner asked whether the last button is Play and asked for the files to be consulted. name_ps END_BTN carries strref 1580  the SAME string every BTN_ACCEPT uses across every chargen screen. So on that screen it is a generic Accept and Play would have been our invention.

BUT custpnl_p, KOTORs real chargen HUB, tells a different story. Six numbered steps, each a button with a number label. BTN_STEPNAME6 carries strref 235, a string used NOWHERE ELSE in the chargen suite, in its own half-width slot beside step 5. Every other footer button in the suite reuses 1580 and 1581. So the source DOES give its final step a distinct label rather than another Accept, and the owners memory was structurally right even though the string cannot be read without dialog.tlk.

RESOLVED ACCORDINGLY: Identity ends with ACCEPT, consistent with every other step. PLAY lives on the hub as the final entry, which is where the source puts its own distinct final label.

## TRACE-73 — NWN cg_main.gui. The ENCOURAGED state is the real find, and NWNs GUI format carries NO appearance data at all

Claude Code report with clear source discipline, separating panel file from engine and naming what it could not establish.

cg_main.gui, 5,859 bytes, aurora_gui.bif index 33. Eight step buttons at uniform Y pitch  Gender, Race, Portrait, Class, Alignment, Abilities, Packages, Customize  all referencing ONE shared template, ctl_btn_pre_176. Three action buttons on a separate row using a narrower template: PLAY, RESET, CANCEL. No Back, no Next, confirming TRACE-08.

⚠ INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF PT-1214: NWNs chargen hub carries a PlayButton. PT-1214 put Play on our hub on the strength of custpnl_ps BTN_STEPNAME6 alone, strref 235, used nowhere else. NWN reaches the same answer by a different route. Two engines in the same family, same conclusion.

NWNs GUI FORMAT CARRIES NO APPEARANCE DATA WHATSOEVER. No BORDER, HILIGHT, SELECTED or HILIGHTSELECTED blocks  each control has only layer, parent hook, tag, type and coordinates. No textures named, no colours. All eight step buttons are identical but for position and caption. This is a structural difference from KOTORs format, not an omission, and it means the file cannot answer appearance questions even in principle.

THE ENGINES BUTTON MODEL, four named animations: Up, Down, HighLight, and ENCOURAGED. ⚠ REAL NEGATIVE: there is NO Disabled animation and NO Completed animation. So locked and completed are not animation states. Enable/disable is a separate axis via SetEnabled, with panel-level machinery alongside.

THE FIND WORTH STEALING. Step buttons are instances of a dedicated class, CGuiCharGenCompleteableButton  a subclass existing specifically to know whether its step is complete, used for these buttons and nothing else. And the panel carries SetNextEncouragedButton. So the model is three axes, not two:

    ENABLED / DISABLED    availability
    ENCOURAGED / NOT      do this one NEXT
    COMPLETEABLE          the button knows its own completion

NWN does not merely grey out what you cannot do  IT ACTIVELY POINTS AT THE NEXT STEP with its own animation state. The hub tells you where to go, not only where you cannot. That is a third affordance beyond locked and unlocked.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and correctly handed back rather than inferred: what a locked step actually LOOKS like  the animation set rules out a dedicated disabled animation but not a shader tint or overlay; whether a completed step is visually distinct from a merely available one; and the re-lock behaviour.

ON RE-LOCK, an honest negative with its scope stated: roughly 90,000 string-table entries searched for confirmation or warning patterns around changing an earlier choice. Nothing relevant found. The panel method list carries Handle methods for all eight buttons plus Ok, Reset and Cancel, and NO method resembling a confirmation step. Both point toward NWN silently re-locking and discarding, and Reset existing as a separate explicit button is what you would expect if changing a step quietly invalidated what follows. Presented as evidence, not proof  the behaviour could be implemented with no user-facing text and produce the same silence.

## PT-1215 — Step strip states locked: four of them, padlock for locked, PULSING for the next step. Re-lock warns, departing from NWN

Closes an item PT-1100 left explicitly open  the lock icons, numbering treatment and visual polish were deferred there, and every mockup this session has been drawing a default nobody ruled on.

FOUR STATES: completed shows a teal tick and stays revisitable; the encouraged next step shows a bone numeral and PULSES; the current step shows a bone numeral, static; a locked step shows a PADLOCK, dimmed.

PADLOCK OVER DIMMED NUMBER, owner ruling. A dimmed numeral says you cannot click this. A padlock says WHY. TRACE-73 confirms NWN has no disabled animation at all, so this restores nothing  it is ours, chosen because progressive unlock is a rule the player has to understand rather than merely obey.

THE PULSING ENCOURAGED STATE IS TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM NWN and is the best thing TRACE-73 found. NWN ships SetEncouraged, a Gui_Anim_Button_Encouraged animation, and SetNextEncouragedButton on the chargen panel  a genuine third affordance where the hub POINTS AT THE NEXT STEP rather than only greying out what is unavailable. Adopting it costs us no new mechanism: the house pulse rule from PT-1177 already means this is waiting for your input, hovering already cancels it, and everything pulsing already breathes on one shared clock. Encouraged IS waiting-for-your-input. The rule fits without amendment.

⚠ RE-LOCK WARNS, AND THIS IS A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM SOURCE. TRACE-73 searched roughly 90,000 string-table entries for confirmation text around changing an earlier choice and found none, and the chargen panel carries no confirmation method  real evidence NWN silently re-locks and discards. We do not follow it. Changing Class at step 5 invalidates skill points spent at step 7, and silently destroying an allocation the player built is a worse failure than one extra dialog. THE CONFIRMATION MUST NAME WHAT IS LOST, not merely warn that something will be  a dialog saying this will reset later steps is nearly as bad as no dialog.

This also makes PT-1200s every step is final once left enforceable rather than aspirational: the lock state is the mechanism, and the warning is what makes reopening a step an informed act rather than an accident.

## PT-1216 — Step strip finalised: named buttons, circular numerals, NWN width, grey-completed corrected, Play as step 12

Owner screenshot of custpnl_p rendered settled three things no file could, and corrected one error in PT-1215.

THE NUMERAL IS A CIRCLE beside the button, not a box or an inline number. That matters structurally rather than decoratively: the padlock replaces the NUMERAL while the step NAME stays readable, so a locked step still tells the player what is coming. A bare padlock would not.

COMPLETED RENDERS GREY, NOT HIGHLIGHTED  and PT-1215 had this backwards. The screenshot shows Portrait, the finished step, rendering grey while every unfinished step stays teal. Corrected: a finished step dims, an unfinished one is bright. The intuition that completion should be celebrated with colour is wrong for a hub whose job is showing you where to go next.

PLAY IS A NUMBERED STEP  step 6 of 6 in K2, visible in the screenshot. This confirms PT-1214 visually where strref 235 had only implied it, and TRACE-73 had corroborated from NWNs PlayButton. Three independent routes to the same answer. Ours is step 12, set slightly apart by a hairline, and it is the ONLY non-teal entry in the strip  amber, pulsing once all eleven are done, because it ends creation rather than advancing it.

WIDTH TAKEN FROM NWN, NOT KOTOR, on the owners reasoning that our ordering discipline is NWNs already. KOTORs step buttons are 268px against 800  a third of the screen, which crowds out the content panel entirely, as the first mockup showed. NWNs template names encode their widths: ctl_btn_pre_176 for step buttons, ctl_btn_pre_118 for actions. 176 of 800 is roughly 22 percent, and it leaves the content real room.

Cancel and Back sit below the strip as separate actions, matching K2s own arrangement in the screenshot rather than being folded into the step list.

## PT-1217 — Equipment screen locked. The Purse renamed CREDITS, and the profession trade resolves here, not on both screens

Step 10, the last undesigned screen of the eleven.

THE SCREEN IS A FORK, NOT A SHOPPING LIST. STARTING-EQUIPMENT-01 1 gives three routes and two are the players: take the class ASSORTMENT, or take its value in CREDITS and spend freely, keeping whatever is left. Route 3, a campaign package imposing equipment, OVERRIDES both  it replaces this screen rather than appearing on it, so it is not a third button.

RENAMED AT OWNER RULING: The Purse becomes CREDITS. The Purse is this projects own coinage; credits is the games own currency term and the one a player already knows.

Both routes state PT-728s reasoning on screen rather than leaving it in the rules: the assortment is worth MORE than the credits, because it can hold items a purse would never prioritise  an Engineers two Computer Spikes are 500cr of consumables alone, a Machinists frag grenade is 100cr nobody would choose to buy. Credits buy freedom; the array buys value. Neither is strictly better, which is what makes it a choice rather than a calculation.

The array itemises with its slot mapping and names the five slots that DELIBERATELY START EMPTY  Implant, Head, Hands, Arms, Belt  because STARTING-EQUIPMENT-01 states the reason plainly: fill every slot at creation and every profession grant becomes a sidegrade.

⚠ A DUPLICATION CAUGHT AND RESOLVED. The owner asked whether the profession item-or-aptitude trade belonged here or at Backstory, and checking found it was on BOTH  the Backstory screen built at PT-1206 carries the same toggle. PROFESSIONS-01 places the grant with the profession, one item, at creation, which is why it was drafted there; PT-1200 said the give-up decision resolves at step 10, which is why it was drafted here too. Owner ruled it stays at Equipment. Resolved as: BACKSTORY SHOWS THE OFFER, EQUIPMENT RESOLVES IT. The same live choice must not appear on two screens, and seeing the item beside the rest of your gear is the moment the trade actually means something.

This discharges PT-1200s standing obligation: choosing the aptitude states Applies from level 2, your skill points at step 7 are already spent at the old price. An unstated forward-looking benefit reads as a bad trade discovered late.

ALL ELEVEN CREATION STEPS ARE NOW DESIGNED.

## PT-1218 — Equipment routes renamed STANDARD GEAR and PURCHASE GEAR

Owner ruling, refining PT-1217s naming a second time.

STARTING-EQUIPMENT-01 calls the two player routes The Assortment and The Purse. Both are this projects own coinage rather than game terms, and neither says what the route DOES. Purse was already replaced with Credits at PT-1217; the owner then judged that Assortment did not read as the default it is, and that Credits named a resource rather than an action.

Locked: STANDARD GEAR and PURCHASE GEAR.

The pair works because it shares a noun and puts the whole distinction in one word  what you are ISSUED against what you BUY. Standard also carries the right weight for a route that is the sensible default rather than a lesser option, which Assortment did not. And Purchase Gear names an action, where Credits named only the currency you would spend.

The rules document keeps its own vocabulary; this is a SCREEN LABEL ruling. STARTING-EQUIPMENT-01 is not being rewritten, since the routes themselves are unchanged  only what the player is shown.

## PT-1220 — Species and Class move BEFORE the hub. This restores KOTORs own architecture rather than departing from it

Owner ruling, and checking the source found it is not a new idea at all  it is what KOTOR already does.

THE EVIDENCE. custpnl_ps six numbered steps, visible in the owners own screenshot, are Portrait, Attributes, Skills, Feats, Name, Play. CLASS IS NOT AMONG THEM. Class is resolved on classsel_p, an entirely separate screen, BEFORE the hub is ever drawn. The hub only ever shows steps whose shape is already settled. This project had folded Class into the strip as step 5 and thereby invented a structure the source does not have.

THE FLOW, locked: New Game offers CREATE A NEW CHARACTER or PLAY AN EXISTING ONE. Creating opens the SPECIES screen with no strip at all, then CLASS, and only then does the hub appear with its step strip.

THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN PRESENTATIONAL, and it is the strongest argument for the change. The strip cannot render honestly until it knows two facts. First, whether this character is a DROID  which turns Origin into model-only, Gender into Voice or nothing at all depending on chassis, and Backstory into programming-only, per PT-1208 and PT-1209. Second, whether the class GRANTS FORCE POWERS  which decides whether step 9 exists at all under PT-1099. Choosing both before the hub appears means the strip is CORRECT THE FIRST TIME IT DRAWS, instead of reshaping itself under the player after they have already read it.

That reshaping would have been a real defect. A player who picked Astromech at step 1 would have watched Gender vanish and the numbering shift beneath them. PT-1099s rule is that a player never sees the door that was never going to open  a door that opens and then disappears is worse than either.

NINE STEPS IN THE HUB, PLUS PLAY: Origin, Gender, Backstory, Abilities, Skills, Feats, Powers, Equipment, Identity. For a droid, Powers is absent and the strip renumbers per PT-1190.

⚠ NOTHING ALREADY BUILT IS WASTED. The Species and Class screens are unchanged  they simply render without a strip beside them. The nine remaining steps keep their locked designs. Only the strips contents and the entry sequence change.

⚠ OPEN: the create-new-or-play-existing menu itself is not designed. qorcpnl_p is the nearest source screen, offering QUICK_CHAR_BTN and CUST_CHAR_BTN with a description box, but that is quick-versus-custom rather than new-versus-existing, so it is a starting point and not a template.

## PT-1221 — New Game entry screen locked: two options, a description pane, and Back alone

Built on qorcpnl_ps exact structure rather than invented. The source panel is minimal and instructive: two stacked buttons at (410,356) and (410,388), 300x28 on a 32 pitch  the SAME geometry and pitch custpnl_p uses for its step buttons, so the choice screen and the hub occupy the same panel region and swap. Below them LB_DESC, a description listbox. At the foot, BTN_BACK at 300 wide.

NO CONFIRM BUTTON, and this is the sources own answer rather than a simplification. qorcpnl_p carries ONLY BTN_BACK. The two option buttons are the commit; a separate Continue would add a click to a decision already made. Owner reached the same conclusion independently and asked for it removed.

The footer stays UNIFORM IN TREATMENT with every other screen in the flow  same height, border, radius and position  while carrying one button rather than two. Uniformity of treatment, not of button count.

Labels trimmed at owner ruling to CREATE NEW CHARACTER and SELECT PREMADE CHARACTER, dropping the article from both.

TWO ADDITIONS THE SOURCE HAD NO NEED FOR. The campaign package is named at the top, because premade characters belong to a package and which package you are in determines what is on offer  KOTOR had no packages, so this problem did not exist for it. And the premade option states HOW MANY exist, so a player knows whether that path is worth opening rather than clicking through to find out.

⚠ OPEN: the Select Premade Character screen itself is not designed. It needs a real list of package-supplied characters with enough detail to choose between them, and nothing in the source corresponds to it  KOTORs quick-character path generated a character rather than offering prepared ones.

## PT-1222 — Droid MODEL becomes a fourth pre-hub screen, and a droid consequently has NO Origin step

Owner ruling completing the pre-hub sequence, plus three smaller corrections.

MODEL IS ITS OWN PRE-HUB SCREEN, sitting between Species and Class. The ordering is forced rather than chosen: chassis is picked at Species, and DROID-MODELS-01 is organised BY CHASSIS, so the model menu cannot render until chassis is known. Same dependency shape D-CARD-01 creates between species and homeworld.

⚠ THE REAL CONSEQUENCE, followed through rather than left to surface later: A DROID NOW HAS NO ORIGIN STEP AT ALL. Origin is Homeworld plus Upbringing per PT-1205. The model replaced homeworld and has now moved before the hub; upbringing does not apply to a droid under PT-962. Nothing remains in the step, so it does not render. This is BETTER than PT-1209, which had Origin rendering half for a droid  a half-empty step was always the weaker answer, and moving Model out resolves it cleanly rather than papering over it. A droid runs seven or eight hub steps against an organics nine.

THE HUB CARRIES A HEADER OF CHECKED CHIPS naming every pre-hub choice: species with its subrace or chassis, the model where there is one, and class. Three chips for a droid, two for an organic. Without it the strip would be shaped by decisions the player can no longer see.

CHOOSE A CHASSIS, NOT A SUBRACE. On the Species screen a droids second-level pick uses the droids own vocabulary. The MECHANISM is unchanged  it is still PT-1182s shared-parent-with-variants structure, and chassis really is species per SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2  but calling it a subrace would import organic language into a droid record for no reason.

ACCEPT, NOT THE NEXT SCREENS NAME. The affirmative button on Species and Model reads Accept rather than Class or Model. These are DISCRETE SCREENS, unlike Origin and Identity where a forward-naming button was right precisely because those are two stages INSIDE one step. Naming the destination there was honest about an unfinished step; here it would imply the same thing falsely.

## TRACE-74 — NWNs premade roster is HARDCODED, with no panel and no field ordering to lift. But pre_chartype.gui corroborates PT-1221 almost verbatim

⚠ DIRECT CORROBORATION OF PT-1221, reached independently. pre_chartype.gui, 1,848 bytes, carries exactly THREE buttons: CreateNewButton reading Create New Character, UsePremadeButton reading Select Premade Character, and CancelButton. This project built that same two-option entry screen from qorcpnl_ps structure, and the owner trimmed the articles by instinct  landing on NWNs actual label wording. Two engines, two routes, same answer. Backed by CChooseCharTypePanel with HandleMakeNewCharButton and HandleUseExistingCharButton.

⚠ AND THEN THE HONEST NEGATIVE. THE ROSTER ITSELF IS NOT A .gui PANEL AT ALL. All 104 GUI panels searched; the only hit is the button that LEADS to the list, never the list. The roster is hardcoded as CCharacterList, a container exposing only Add and Delete. Same situation as NWNs character sheet, also hardcoded. NWN puts character-facing screens in code and chargen steps in data. So there is NO geometry, no control tags, and no answer to split-versus-separate from the data. That needs the running game.

pregen.2da EXISTS AND TELLS US NOTHING. 75 rows, and the complete column set is LABEL and FILENAME. It is a MANIFEST, not an identity record. This inverts the expectation this project brought to the question: the table considers nothing part of a premades identity, because everything a premade IS lives inside its .bic  a full creature blueprint, 114 top-level fields, roughly 13KB each. A premade is simply a saved character with no curated subset.

THE ONE ORDERING NWN COMMITS TO ANYWHERE, from pre_char_version.gui, a sibling screen shown when a character exists in two places and correctly flagged as not the premade pane: NameLabel, FirstClass, SecondClass, ThirdClass, XP. Identity, then class, then progression. NO race, alignment, portrait, description or ability scores. Whatever else it proves, NWN leads with IDENTITY rather than NUMBERS.

NARRATIVE CONTENT IS ONE FIELD. A premades entire narrative is Description, a localised string running 131 to 203 characters, and EMPTY on some. No Bio, no Background, no Origin, no role tag, across all 114 fields. So NWN HAS NO PRECEDENT TO OFFER for the origin and background material the owner wants on our detail side. That is ours to author, and our corpus genuinely has those fields where NWNs does not.

⚠ THE MOST USEFUL FINDING IS A WARNING. NWNs 75 premades are NOT homogeneous  they split three ways: named level-1 story characters with written descriptions; level-15 class archetypes with generic labels; and multi-level build sets at 5/10/20/30/40 whose DESCRIPTIONS ARE OFTEN EMPTY. The list mixes a person you can be with a stat block at level 30. Explicitly flagged as the thing NOT to copy if the roster has a narrative purpose. Ours does, so ours should not mix them.

## PT-1223 — Select Premade Character locked: one split screen, sheet in creation order, every field labelled

Owner ruling. TRACE-74 established there is nothing to lift  NWNs roster is hardcoded with no panel file, pregen.2da is a two-column manifest, and a premades entire narrative is one Description string. So this screen is authored rather than restored, and the ordering question had no source answer.

ONE SPLIT SCREEN, not two. An early draft used a roster screen with a View Sheet button leading to a detail screen; the owner corrected it. Choosing between premades is a COMPARISON task, and comparing means watching the sheet change as you move between candidates. A navigation step between them would break exactly the thing the screen is for.

THE SHEET RUNS IN CREATION ORDER  identity, homeworld with its aptitude, upbringing, profession with its grant, lifestyle, languages, abilities, then vitality, Force points, defence and saves. NWN offered no ordering to borrow; its one committed format, from the sibling pre_char_version.gui, is name then class then XP, which only tells us it leads with identity rather than numbers. Creation order was chosen because it reads as the ACCOUNT OF HOW THE CHARACTER WAS ASSEMBLED, which means the sheet and the eleven steps cannot disagree about what matters.

EVERY BACKGROUND FIELD CARRIES ITS LABEL, at owner ruling. Coruscant and Persuade alone does not say what it is. Homeworld, Upbringing, Profession, Lifestyle, Languages are named explicitly.

SECTION BUTTONS BELOW THE STATS: Skills, Feats, Powers, Gear. Powers appears only for a Force user. Background is deliberately NOT a button  the owner moved it into the always-visible block, because it belongs with the material a reader needs regardless of which pane is open.

THE PANES MATCH THEIR CREATION SCREENS EXACTLY, at smaller scale. Skills as PT-1201s alphabetical aptitude-marked list; feats and powers as identical chain grids per PT-1202 and PT-1204. Rendered through one shared function so they cannot drift apart.

ALL 24 SKILLS RENDER, INCLUDING UNTRAINED ONES AT 0, at owner ruling, in three states: amber with a diamond for aptitude, pale for a rank without it, dimmed for zero. What a character LEFT EMPTY is real information when comparing premades  a Soldier with nothing in Repair tells you something the old four-line list could not.

FORCE POINTS SHOWN ALONGSIDE VITALITY, and ABSENT rather than zeroed for a non-Force character, consistent with how every other inapplicable element in this project renders.

EVERY REGION SCROLLS INDEPENDENTLY  roster, description, stat block, section pane  so a package with thirty premades needs no redesign. Owner explicitly confirmed that saves and defence sitting below the fold is CORRECT rather than a defect: they are reachable by scrolling, same as skills, and compressing them to force them above the fold was declined.

⚠ CARRIED FROM TRACE-74, and worth acting on when premades are authored: NWNs 75 premades mix named story characters with generic level-30 build sets, and their description field is populated for the former and EMPTY for the latter. Flagged in the source report as the thing not to copy. Ours has a narrative purpose, so ours should not mix them.

## PT-1224 — ⚠ PT-1202 CORRECTED. The feat grid carries chain ARROWS, matching powers

Owner caught that the feat and power grids had been built differently, and that feats never got the arrows and spacing powers have. Re-reading the evidence, PT-1202 misread it.

WHAT PT-1202 SAID. Describing the owners feat-screen screenshot, it recorded a green arrow marking the SELECTED ROW  read as a selection cursor. That reading was wrong.

WHAT IT ALMOST CERTAINLY IS. PT-1204, built from the later Force-powers screenshot, established that GREEN ARROWS SIT BETWEEN THE COLUMNS to mark chain progression, and that rows stop where their chain stops. Same engine, same three-column grid, same chain concept, same arrow glyph in the same position between the first and second icon. The feat screens arrow is a CHAIN ARROW, not a cursor.

CORRECTED: the feat grid carries arrows between tiers exactly as the power grid does. Both are now rendered through ONE SHARED FUNCTION in the mockup rather than two similar implementations, so identical arrow glyph, identical cell size, identical gutters and row pitch. They cannot drift apart by accident, which is how they drifted in the first place.

THE ONE REMAINING DIFFERENCE IS PALETTE, and it is real rather than incidental: power icons carry alignment colouring from spells.2das goodevil column per PT-1204, feats do not. Structure identical, colour differs for a documented reason.

⚠ THIS DOES NOT CLOSE PT-1202s ACCURACY DEBT. Cell dimensions, gutters and row pitch still need matching against the real render  85.7 x 56 inside a 257x56 row with 4px padding for feats, 264 wide with padding 0 for powers. This ruling fixes a structural misreading, not the measurements.

## TRACE-75 — leveluppnl_p resolved. Class choice is DIALOGUE, not a panel. No aggregate summary exists anywhere

All five strrefs resolved, both guesses correct: 209 Attributes, 233 Skills, 232 Feats, 1072 POWERS, 1073 ACCEPT, 219 Back. Two neighbours worth holding: 1071 Level Up, used as the title on the Powers screen, and 1074 Remaining Powers.

THE CHARGEN COMPARISON IS SHARPER THAN FIVE VERSUS SIX. Level-up does not drop one step. It drops TWO FROM THE ENDS  Portrait at the front, Name at the back  and INSERTS Powers before the commit. Attributes, Skills and Feats shift up one slot and keep their exact strings.

Three layout differences to copy or reject deliberately. Chargen SPLITS its last row, Name at x442 and Play at x594, both 116 wide; level-up keeps step 5 full width at 268. Chargens commit carries a FILL, uibit_fill_2bt, and none of its other steps do  level-ups Accept has NO fill, so chargen visually distinguishes its commit and level-up deliberately does not. And chargen has BTN_BACK and BTN_CANCEL while LEVEL-UP HAS BACK ONLY: there is no cancel path off the level-up hub.

⚠ CLASS CHOICE IS DIALOGUE, NOT A PANEL. Definitive, from shipped script source. a_pc_jedi.nss, dated 10-6-04, is parameterised: GetScriptParameter(1) selects from six prestige classes and each branch calls AddMultiClass. GetScriptParameter is the dialogue-node mechanism, so it fires FROM A CONVERSATION. A companion script a_makejedi.nss does the same for party members. THE STEP LIST DOES NOT GROW TO SIX  there is no class step in any of K2s 159 panel files, and the only class-selection panel is classsel_p, which belongs to chargen. By the time the player opens the level-up hub, class is already decided.

⚠ NO AGGREGATE SUMMARY, A CLEAN NEGATIVE. Sixteen controls: five discs, five numerals, five step buttons, one Back. No summary label, no vitality readout, no skill-points-gained display, and no control that could hold one. Checked elsewhere too  statussummary_p is the general world-event popup, not this. The engine class CSWCLevelUpStats exists, so level-up statistics ARE computed as an object, but nothing in the panel can display them and K2s binary is stripped of method symbols.

THE SCHEDULE THAT WOULD DRIVE SHOW/HIDE, from featgain.2da: 50 rows, one per level, two columns per class. Regular-feat levels are NOT uniform  a Soldier gets one at nearly every level to 16 then every other, while a Consular gets one at roughly every third. So the Feats step has something to spend at wildly different frequencies by class, which is exactly why show/hide matters. ⚠ AND EVERY BONUS COLUMN READS 0 AT EVERY LEVEL: bonus feats are authored as a mechanism and granted nowhere, the same authored-but-dead pattern as the XXXX_ feats at TRACE-68.

NEEDS THE RUNNING GAME, correctly handed back rather than inferred: whether a non-granting step is hidden, disabled or shown empty; whether Powers appears for a non-Jedi; the attribute cadence, for which no driving table was found and which is likely hardcoded; and whether CSWCLevelUpStats surfaces anywhere.

## TRACE-76 — Automatic class grants confirmed as level-indexed. And K2 NEVER ANNOUNCES THEM  three independent confirmations

_granted values are the CLASS LEVEL at which a feat is automatically gained, running 1 to 30. -1 is a sentinel meaning never granted and is the dominant value, 215 to 237 of 245 rows in any given column. ⚠ A REAL TRAP RECORDED: filtering on non-empty rather than not -1 returns essentially the whole table. The blanks that do appear sit on three rows with EMPTY labels  padding, not feats.

Verified independently in this container. Scout takes nine grants at level 1  two armour proficiencies, Flurry, Rapid Shot, three weapon proficiencies, Targeting 1, Close Combat  then UNCANNY_DODGE_1 AND PRECISE_SHOT_I AT LEVEL 4, then a long progression to level 29. Soldiers entire automatic kit is eight feats, ALL AT LEVEL 1, and never grows. Two classes, two completely different shapes.

_pc_granted exists for exactly three classes, the base Jedi trio, and does a different job from _granted. jgd_granted is the class kit on a progression to 30; jgd_pc_granted is 10 feats ALL AT LEVEL 1 and nothing after  armour proficiencies and the four attack forms, which is precisely what sol_granted and sct_granted hand out for free. Read as a CATCH-UP BATCH: a character who is a Jedi from level 1 with no prior class would otherwise never receive the basic combat feats every non-Force starting class gives away. Flagged as inference; the content matches the reading exactly and the columns exist only for classes a player can start as, but the table does not state it, and whether the engine applies it INSTEAD OF or IN ADDITION TO the level-1 _granted entries needs the running game.

⚠⚠ THE HEADLINE FINDING: K2 NEVER TELLS THE PLAYER. An automatic grant is silent. Three independent confirmations.

    NO STRING. A 200,000-entry sweep, run tight and loose, found no
    Feat Gained, no New Ability Received, nothing naming a granted
    feat. What EXISTS is the inverse: four strings nagging about
    UNSPENT choices  42187, 48730, 42188, 125861  every one a
    prompt to go and choose, not an announcement of receipt.
    NO ROW. statussummary_ps thirteen event types include journal,
    credits, XP, stealth XP, both alignment sides, net shift, both
    influence directions, both max-Force-point directions, and items
    in and out. Not one is a feat or an ability. The panel that
    exists to announce what you just received has no slot for this.
    NO CONTROL. leveluppnl_ps sixteen controls are five discs, five
    numerals, five step buttons and Back. Nothing could display it.

The engine DOES read the table  its own error string, CSWClass::LoadFeatGain: cant load featgain.2da, proves it. There is no matching feedback symbol.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE THING WORTH CARRYING: K2 tells you when it needs something FROM you, and never when it has given something TO you. A Scout hitting level 4 silently acquires two real combat capabilities with no popup, no log line, no highlight and no summary row. Combined with TRACE-75s finding that the level-up hub has no aggregate summary at all, K2 gives a levelling player nowhere to see what the level actually did.

⚠ SO ANNOUNCING GRANTS IS AN ADDITION, NOT A RESTORATION  and statussummary_ps icon-plus-description row list is the obvious shape to borrow, since it already handles Maximum Force Points Increased, the closest thing K2 has to an automatic-gain notice.

## TRACE-77 — THERE ARE NO LEVEL-UP VARIANTS. Three of four steps reuse the chargen panels exactly, and the one exception explains itself

Checked the full K2 panel set for level-up versions of the ability, skill and feat screens. There are none. The complete relevant set is abchrgen, skchrgen, ftchrgen, abilities, skillinfo, and pwrlvlup  and only pwrlvlup is level-up-specific.

So Attributes, Skills and Feats at level-up ARE abchrgen_p, skchrgen_p and ftchrgen_p. The same panels, reused.

⚠ AND THIS EXPLAINS TRACE-75s STRREF FINDING RATHER THAN MERELY MATCHING IT. leveluppnl_ps steps 1 to 3 carry chargens exact strings  209 Attributes, 233 Skills, 232 Feats  and step 4 carries a new one, 1072 Powers. The reason is not that the labels happen to agree. It is that THEY ARE THE SAME SCREENS. The strref reuse and the panel reuse are one fact, and TRACE-75 recorded the symptom without the cause.

⚠ WHY POWERS IS THE EXCEPTION, and it is a real structural difference between KOTOR and this project. KOTOR HAS NO FORCE CLASS AT LEVEL 1. A player begins as Soldier, Scout or Scoundrel and becomes a Jedi later through story. So a Powers step CANNOT exist in chargen, and pwrlvlup_p is the only powers screen in the entire game.

OUR SYSTEM DIFFERS: Jedi Guardian, Consular and Sentinel are BASE classes, selectable at level 1. So our chargen needs a powers screen where KOTORs does not. PT-1204 built one from pwrlvlup_p, which was the only available source, and this finding explains that call rather than merely justifying it.

DESIGN CONSEQUENCE: our level-up needs NO NEW SCREENS. It reuses the four already locked  PT-1197 Abilities, PT-1201 Skills, PT-1202 Feats, PT-1204 Powers  differing only in budget. Creation spends a starting allocation; level-up spends one levels worth.

## PT-1225 — Level-up locked. Class step first, real source data throughout, grants announced

Owner locked the level-up flow after four passes and three Claude Code research rounds.

STRUCTURE FROM SOURCE, per TRACE-75: level-up drops TWO steps from chargens ends, Portrait and Name, and inserts Powers before the commit. Commit reads ACCEPT, strref 1073, and is deliberately NOT visually distinguished  chargen gives Play a fill, level-up withholds one, and that difference is preserved rather than normalised. Back only; there is no cancel path off the level-up hub.

NO NEW SCREENS, per TRACE-77. Attributes, Skills and Feats reuse the chargen panels exactly; only Powers has a level-up-specific panel, because KOTOR has no Force class at level 1 and therefore no chargen powers screen at all. Our four locked screens carry over with level-up budgets.

TWO ADDITIONS, BOTH MARKED AS OURS ON SCREEN rather than blended in.

A CLASS STEP AT POSITION 1. MULTICLASS-01 3 permits taking a level in any class at any level-up, while K2 grants prestige class through a dialogue script, a_pc_jedi.nss firing from a conversation node, and has no class step in any of its 159 panels. Class must be FIRST because everything downstream depends on it: hit die and skill points come from the class taken that level, whether Feats renders depends on that classs featgain schedule, and whether Powers exists at all depends on whether it is a Force class. Three-class maximum enforced per PT-723, with ineligible classes padlocked once three are held.

A GRANT SUMMARY ON COMMIT. TRACE-76 established K2 announces NOTHING  no string in a 200,000-entry sweep, no row among statussummary_ps thirteen event types, no control on the level-up hub. It carries four strings nagging about UNSPENT choices and none about things given. Ours announces, using statussummary_ps own icon-plus-description shape, with AUTOMATIC GRANTS IN A SEPARATE AMBER BLOCK so what the player chose and what the class gave are never conflated.

CONDITIONAL STEPS, driven by real schedules rather than invented cadence: Attributes every fourth level; Feats on the classs own featgain.2da row, which is wildly non-uniform  a Soldier gains one at nearly every level to 16, a Consular at roughly every third; Powers only for a Force class. Accept stays locked until every step above is complete, which is the level-up equivalent of the chargen strips progressive unlock.

SELECTABLE LISTS ARE REAL, at owner instruction. The _list column decodes as 1 selectable, 3 granted, 4 unavailable, and cross-checks perfectly against _granted. Real per-class counts differ substantially and are shown on the class screen: Jedi Guardian 69, Soldier 60, Scout 50, SCOUNDREL 20. A Scoundrel has barely a third of a Soldiers options, which an invented placeholder list had entirely concealed.

⚠ CARRIED OPEN: the mockups selectable lists are truncated samples of the real sets. Names and counts are source; the full lists are not enumerated in the mockup.

## TRACE-79 — RECOMMENDED is a RANKED PREFERENCE ORDER, not a flag. Two authoring traps verified. And TRACE-76 corrected by its own author

Claude Code returned with a self-correction first, which is worth recording as such.

⚠ TRACE-76 WAS WRONG AND ITS AUTHOR SAID SO. It reported that K2 never announces an automatically granted feat, presented as a clean negative from a 200,000-entry sweep. Two strings do exist  42258 for feats, 111635 for powers  both phrased you have been granted the following this level. The sweep missed them because it expected noun before verb, feat granted, and the strings are written verb-first, granted the following feat. A wrong-shape negative in this projects own taxonomy, and the third this session. What survives from TRACE-76: there is still no feat row on the status summary and no grant summary on the level-up hub. What is withdrawn: the game never says so.

THE DATA MODEL IS NOT WHAT WAS ASSUMED, and the correction improves it. The column is _recom in feat.2da, not _reco. And neither it nor skills.2das _reco is a BOOLEAN  both are PRIORITY RANKS. A classs recommendation data is an ORDERED PREFERENCE LIST: rank 1 is the first pick, blank means not on the list at all. So RECOMMENDED is not a filter lighting up eligible options; it is a WALK DOWN A PREFERENCE ORDER.

⚠ TWO AUTHORING TRAPS, BOTH VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY IN THIS CONTAINER. RANKS ARE NOT UNIQUE  Soldier ties at rank 26, Jedi Guardian ties at 24 and 25, and ten of fifteen classes carry at least one tie. A consumer keying a map on rank silently drops one of each pair. AND RANKS ARE NOT CONTIGUOUS  Jedi Guardian runs 1 to 26 WITH 12 MISSING, so walking i=1..N and stopping at the first miss truncates its list at eleven of twenty-seven. Any consumer must sort the populated ranks and iterate that.

NO CLASS HAS AN EMPTY LIST. Fifteen classes, from droid experts 15 ranked feats to Soldiers 37. The skills-side blanks are not missing data either  they line up exactly with skills that class cannot take, so the recommendation set IS the selectable set.

THE REACHABLE FAILURE IS EXHAUSTION, not absence: a character holding every ranked feat still eligible leaves the recommender nothing to apply. Most reachable on a short list  droid experts 15 ranked against 17 selectable.

⚠ AND NO FAILURE STRING EXISTS. Sweeping recommend returns three UI entries only: the button label at 221 and the two popup lines at 42256 and 42257. That absence carries real weight, because the surrounding neighbourhood is K2s chargen refusal block and it is thorough  the attribute floor of 8 and ceiling of 18, refusals for deselecting a held feat, refusals for deselecting a granted one, prerequisite failures for feats and powers, and prompts for unspent selections. K2 authors a message for every case where it must say no. It authored none here.

RECOMMENDED APPEARS ON EXACTLY FOUR PC PANELS at identical geometry, (335,516) 160x28, strref 221: abchrgen_p, ftchrgen_p, skchrgen_p and pwrlvlup_p. Absent from portrait, name, class selection, and both hubs. All four carry BORDER and HILIGHT only  no selected or disabled block, the same defect family as the 42 buttons already logged.

AND ONLY TWO OF THE FOUR CONFIRM. The popup strings exist for feats and powers only. Attributes and skills apply SILENTLY. That matches the owners screenshots exactly and yields a real rule: a popup announces what you might not otherwise notice. A feat is a named entry in an icon grid; an attribute number changes in front of you.

NEEDS THE RUNNING GAME: whether the button greys when exhausted, what a second press does, and whether it overwrites a manual selection.

    POWERS      RECOMMENDED ANNOUNCES

## PT-1237 — ⚠ SPECIES SENSES ARE A REAL MECHANICAL CATEGORY AND THE SPECIES PANEL OMITS THEM

Owner caught that the Species information panel locked at PT-1233 shows ability adjustments, skills, trait, size and speed, and lore  and NOTHING ABOUT SENSES. Checked against SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2 and the omission is real and substantial.

SENSES ARE NOT FLAVOUR. They are rollable abilities with ranges and DCs, sourced and cited:

    Bith          Heightened Smell  identify an individual by scent at
                  10 metres on a Wisdom check, DC 15. Their vision is
                  extraordinary at close range and poor at distance,
                  so smell is the COMPENSATING sense  the mechanic
                  and the prose explain each other.
    Aqualish      Low-Light Vision on the Aquala. Eyes built for deep
                  water, not daylight.
    Kaleesh       Hunter's Scent  detect by smell within 10 metres,
                  20 upwind, 6 downwind, doubled for strong scents and
                  tripled for overpowering ones. UAA p.183.
    Miraluka      NO EYES AT ALL. Perceive entirely through the Force,
                  and every Miraluka is Force-sensitive from birth.

⚠ AND THE CHAPTER ALREADY WARNED ABOUT THIS. Line 41: how a species communicates is not a feat  scent, radio, lekku, signal fires, hive consensus  all of it belongs in the species PROSE, where a player reads it, rather than on the mechanical block. That ruling correctly separates COMMUNICATION from mechanics. It does not cover PERCEPTION, which is mechanical and does belong on the block. The Species panel currently shows neither.

RESOLVED: the panel gains a SENSES section, rendered on the same conditional basis as trait  present when the species has one, absent when it does not. It sits after skills and before size and speed, since a sense is closer to a capability than to a physical measure.

⚠ THIS IS A CONTENT GAP AS WELL AS A UI ONE. Whether every species entry actually carries a senses line is not established; four are confirmed above. A sweep of all 47 records is needed before the section can be relied on, and species with no distinct sense should be confirmed as genuinely having none rather than merely unwritten.

## PT-1241 — Equipment restyled as the full hybrid. The frame earns its place here more than on any other screen

Sixth screen restyled. Header bars, every region boxed, CANCEL and OK footer, stock and cart entries as rounded option boxes per PT-1239.

Equipment carries THREE DISTINCT REGIONS  the route toggle between Standard Gear and Purchase Gear, the gear content itself, and the profession trade at the foot. Unboxed, all three ran together into a single column of text.

THE TRADE IS A DIFFERENT DECISION FROM THE GEAR ABOVE IT. Choosing Standard against Purchase is about what you carry; choosing components against an aptitude is about what your PROFESSION gave you, and PT-1223 deliberately moved that choice here rather than leaving it at Backstory. Two unrelated decisions stacked in one unbroken column invites a player to read them as one, and boxing is what prevents it. On Class the frame was slightly better; here it is structurally necessary.

PT-1200s standing obligation survives intact and is the reason the trade needs its own visible region at all: choosing the aptitude states Applies from level 2, your skill points are already spent at the old price. An unstated forward-looking benefit reads as a bad trade discovered late, and it cannot do that job buried in a run of text about boots and medpacs.

## PT-1243 — Identity gains a third stage, YOUR STORY. This closes PT-1199s open prose question

Owner ruling.
