This answers it: IT BELONGS IN CREATION, as Identitys third stage.

WHY IDENTITY RATHER THAN A TWELFTH STEP. Identity is already the text layer  portrait, name, and now the story. A separate step would mean twelve entries in a strip settled at eleven, for content that is the same kind of thing as the two stages beside it.

WHAT THE STAGE CARRIES. A FULL RUNDOWN above: portrait, name, species, class, all six abilities, then every flavour choice as a rounded chip  origin, upbringing, profession, lifestyle. The aptitudes chip was REMOVED at owner ruling: aptitude is a mechanical consequence rather than a choice, and this rundown is about who the character IS.

Three variations of the same character, all true to the same inputs.

⚠ IT IS A REAL TEXT FIELD, NOT A DISPLAY. Type, erase, select, scroll. Try another regenerates from the same inputs; CLEAR empties it and focuses the cursor. Owner asked for both controls specifically. The status line tracks three states  assembled from your choices, edited by you, empty  so a blank field reads as deliberate rather than broken.

⚠⚠ AND THE CAMPAIGN READS IT. This is the reason the stage exists rather than being decoration: names, places and events a player writes here become available to the engine as hooks for generated content. A player who invents a sister or a debt has handed the campaign a thread. That is a real commitment  it means the story field is INPUT to systems, not just flavour text on a sheet  and it should be treated as such when the engine is specified.

## PT-1245 — CHARACTER-RECORD-01 written. The contract every creation screen writes into, which did not exist

Owner asked what else a builder needs. Checked rather than guessed, and found four real gaps: chargen data exists only as markdown prose, there is NO character record schema, there are no design tokens, and there is no asset manifest. The schema was written first because the other three are easier once it exists  it is the contract every screen depends on.

TWO PRINCIPLES GOVERN THE SHAPE, both stated so a builder does not have to infer them.

STORE THE CHOICE, DERIVE THE CONSEQUENCE. A record holds species aqualish and subrace quara; it does NOT hold the resulting +2 Strength, because that is a lookup. Storing derived values means two sources of truth and one of them going stale. SKILLS-01s aptitude rule changing should change every character, not none of them.

ABSENT, NOT ZEROED. A droid has no upbringing key at all  not null, not empty string. This mirrors how every screen renders under PT-1099, and it makes an unset field distinguishable from a field set to nothing.

⚠ THE SECTION THAT MATTERS MOST IS 3, DERIVED NEVER STORED, and specifically THE APTITUDE SET. Five sources contribute and they STACK per PT-1201  a skill can hold aptitude from class AND species AND homeworld  so the derivation must return the SET OF SOURCES, not a boolean, because the UI names which granted it. And it is MUTABLE MID-CAMPAIGN: a Skill Focus feat taken at level 8 adds aptitude the character did not have at level 1, per TRACE-68, so any cached set invalidates on feat gain. That is the single most likely thing to be implemented wrong.

SEVERAL FIELDS CARRY BEHAVIOUR A BUILDER WOULD NOT GUESS. gender holds the VOICE for a droid and is absent entirely for Astromech and Remote  one field, three behaviours, and the chassis tells you which. origin is absent entirely for droids. backstory.grant_taken is WRITTEN BY THE EQUIPMENT SCREEN, not Backstory, per PT-1217 and PT-1223. feats carry a source field distinguishing granted from chosen, because a granted feat cannot be removed.

⚠ AND VALIDATE ON LOAD, NOT ONLY ON SAVE. A record can become illegal without being edited  a rules change to SKILLS-01s caps invalidates existing characters, and silent breakage is worse than a refusal.

Four open items recorded honestly, including that story_origin is proposed here rather than ruled, and that nothing in this schema addresses multiplayer.

## PT-1246 — The three remaining build documents written: UI-STYLE-VALUES-01, UI-ASSETS-01, CHARGEN-DATA-01

Owner asked to get as much ready as possible ahead of a build that is not imminent. With CHARACTER-RECORD-01 at PT-1245, that closes all four gaps found when the question was asked.

UI-STYLE-VALUES-01  the palette as VALUES rather than prose. Extracted from forty mockups where these were used consistently but recorded only inside widget code, which is not a place a builder can read. ⚠ Stated plainly at the top: THESE ARE OUR VALUES, NOT KOTORS. TRACE-69 established authored .gui colour is intent rather than output, so parsed source colours were never a usable palette. Each accent carries ONE meaning and the document says which  amber is the privileged member of a set, alert is unselectable, terminal is in-world prose. And the two-channel warning from PT-1231 is repeated where it will be read: border and icon artwork can both be red and mean different things.

UI-ASSETS-01  what art this needs and what stands in now. Every mockup uses placeholders and says so; this enumerates what they stand for. ⚠ THE CHARACTER MODEL IS FLAGGED AS THE LARGEST COMMITMENT IN THE PROJECT rather than being allowed to arrive quietly: maincg_ps 3D viewport implies a rigged model per species, equipment rendering on it, and a viewport that updates as gear changes. A priority order is given so incremental commissioning unblocks the most  popup glyphs and chrome first, character model last. And a real trap recorded: feat icon cells are 85.7 by 56, WIDER THAN TALL, so art commissioned to a square ratio would be wrong.

CHARGEN-DATA-01  extracting roughly 6,100 lines of prose across nine documents into structured data. ⚠ NAMED AS THE HIGHEST-RISK WORK REMAINING, and the reason is stated: not difficulty, but that a transcription error in a table nobody re-reads is invisible until play. Six traps listed, EVERY ONE OF THEM SOMETHING THIS PROJECT HAS ALREADY HIT  minus one is a value not an absence; ranks tie and skip so sort rather than index; XXXX_ means disabled; _p versus _x; authored colour is not output; 2DA needs a position-based parser. Plus the hardest one to guard against, from PT-1210: two documents can disagree and the more recent is not always right, so follow the ruling trail rather than the file date.

⚠ AND A COUNT CHECK IS SPECIFIED as validation  47 species, 24 skills, 156 feats, 21 professions, 17 programmings, 9 upbringings. The cheapest possible check and the most likely to catch a silent drop, since a parser that loses one row of 156 is otherwise invisible.

Extraction order given dependency-first, starting with skills because everything references it and ending with equipment because it depends on nearly everything.

## PT-1247 — ⚠ A DESIGN DOCUMENT WAS SILENTLY EXCLUDED BY THE CREDENTIAL-SAFETY GITIGNORE. Renamed to UI-STYLE-VALUES-01

Owner asked whether the files had actually been created. Four of five were tracked. UI-TOKENS-01.md existed on disk, had been reported as written and committed, and was NOT IN THE REPOSITORY.

THE CAUSE, found by git check-ignore rather than guessed: .gitignore line 3 is *TOKEN*, a rule added after this projects TWO PAT EXPOSURES to stop credentials being committed. It was doing exactly its job. It caught a design document because the word TOKENS appears in the filename.

⚠ AND THE FAILURE MODE IS ONE THIS PROJECT HAS NAMED: a silent no-op. git add reported success, git commit reported success, git push reported success. All three were true  for the four other files. The fifth was dropped without a single error, and every check this agent ran afterwards passed, because the checks were on the commits rather than on the file list. METHOD-RECORD-01 records print-success-inside-branch and tail-swallowing as members of this family; this is another.

⚠ THE ONLY REASON IT WAS CAUGHT IS THAT THE OWNER ASKED. Nothing in the gate, the commit output or the push output would have surfaced it. A builder reading the repository months from now would have found four documents and one dangling reference.

RESOLVED BY RENAMING THE FILE, NOT BY LOOSENING THE RULE. UI-TOKENS-01 becomes UI-STYLE-VALUES-01, and every reference in the design documents and ruling log is updated. The gitignore rule stays exactly as it is: a credential-safety rule that occasionally catches a false positive is correct, and the alternative  narrowing it so a real token slips through  is how this project lost two PATs.

⚠ WORTH A SWEEP: any other file whose name collides with a safety pattern is invisible in the same way. The check is git ls-files against a directory listing, not git status, because status does not report ignored files either.

## PT-1248 — ⚠ THE PACKAGE SCHEMA IS THE CONTRACT WHERE THE BUILDER AND THE APP MEET, and it does not exist. Flagged on both sides

Owner asked whether the package and home menus need a schema too. They do, and the answer sharpened into something worth recording rather than just adding to a list.

THE CAMPAIGN PACKAGE IS NOT ONE MORE DOCUMENT. It is THE INTERFACE BETWEEN TWO OF THIS PROJECTS FIVE DELIVERABLES  the Builders entire OUTPUT and the apps entire INPUT are the same artefact. Everything either side does passes through it, and nothing specifies what it is.

WHAT ALREADY DEPENDS ON IT, all locked, none of it able to be built without it:

    CONSOLE HOME          lists packages as a library     PT-1146
    PACKAGE MAIN MENU     opens one                       PT-1101
    PREMADE SELECTION     premades live inside a package  PT-1223
    ENTRY SCREEN          names the package at the top    PT-1221
    CHARACTER-RECORD-01   carries a package field
    BUILDER               art packs, areas, freeform mode PT-1106, PT-1130
    AUTHOR-CREATED RULES  new feats, powers and skills    PT-1203
    STARTING EQUIPMENT    route 3, a package imposing gear PT-1217

⚠ AND IT IS LARGER AND MORE LOAD-BEARING THAN CHARACTER-RECORD-01 WAS. A character record is one object with a known field list. A package is a container of everything  areas, dialogue, quests, premades, art, overrides, and authored rules content  and the Builder writes it while the app reads it, so the two must agree exactly or neither works.

FLAGGED ON BOTH SIDES DELIBERATELY: in APP-UI-VISION-01 8 and BUILDER-VISION-01 8, not one or the other. A contract recorded only on one side of an interface is how the two drift apart, and this project has already recorded that pattern once  F-OVERLAP-01 sat nine days in an incoming folder because a finding was filed but never relayed.

NOT WRITTEN NOW, at owner direction  it goes on the list rather than being drafted in the same breath as the question. But it should be the NEXT schema written, ahead of anything else on the app side, because seven locked screens and two deliverables are waiting on it.

## PT-1254 — Party Selection locked as a roster list. ⚠ THE FIRST SCREEN WHERE THE SOURCES SHAPE WAS REJECTED

Sixth in-game screen, and the first in this entire pass where the source arrangement was examined and turned down rather than adopted or hybridised.

KOTOR ARRANGES EIGHT SLOTS IN A RING with a character preview inside it, confirmed at TRACE-80. It is distinctive and this project has no equivalent. It was still the wrong choice for us, for two reasons that are structural rather than aesthetic.

⚠ FIRST, POSITION IN THE RING CARRIES NO MEANING. Slot three is not better than slot seven, closer to the leader, or first in initiative. They are eight places for eight companions. An arrangement that looks like it encodes something and does not is worse than a list, because a player will look for the meaning.

⚠ SECOND, IT WORKS ONLY BECAUSE KOTORS ROSTER CAPS AT EXACTLY EIGHT. A campaign package shipping nine companions has nowhere to put the ninth, and PT-1101s whole package model means we cannot know the number in advance. The ring is a solution to a fixed problem we do not have.

OURS IS A ROSTER LIST inside the games frame: nav bar, title bar, CANCEL and OK footer. Icon, name and class per row with an IN FIELD marker; class, level and description in the panel; and an action button that toggles membership, reading PARTY IS FULL and greying at the cap with the count turning amber.

⚠ AND THE RINGS REAL ADVANTAGE IS CONCEDED RATHER THAN DISMISSED. It makes a party feel like a FORMATION instead of a checklist, which matters more than it sounds in a party-based game. The rejection is on scaling, not on taste, and if the roster ever gains a positional meaning  marching order, formation, initiative seating  the ring becomes the better shape and this ruling should be revisited.

## PT-1255 — Options reworked as a FIRST PASS, not a lock. The screen that could not be copied

Seventh in-game screen, and the one where the source list is least transferable. Owner named it directly: our app and campaigns are not video games, and KOTORs options are a video games options.

FOUR REPLACED, and each replacement changes what the setting IS rather than renaming it:

    Gameplay    becomes TABLE RULES  difficulty, death handling and
                rest pacing are a GMs calls scoped to a campaign,
                not a slider a player moves for themselves
    Auto-Pause  becomes TURN PACING  the concern is a WAITING TABLE
                and a turn sitting unanswered, not a distracted player
    Graphics    becomes DISPLAY  theme, text size, motion. There is
                nothing 3D to configure, so the whole category changes
                subject rather than shrinking
    Exit Game   becomes LEAVE SESSION  you leave a session, not a game

TWO KEPT: Sound, unchanged, and Feedback as ROLLS AND FEEDBACK  worth keeping and worth widening, because a tabletop app should be able to SHOW ITS WORKING in a way a video game never needed to.

TWO NEW WITH NO SOURCE EQUIVALENT: SESSION, covering who is present and whether the game is publicly listed per PT-1144s host-is-server ruling, and ACCOUNT for sign-in, friends and sync.

⚠ AND TWO DROPPED ENTIRELY, WHICH IS THE REAL QUESTION THIS RAISES. Save Game and Load Game are absent. With host-is-server and local-first, SAVING MAY NOT BE A THING A PLAYER DOES AT ALL  the host holds state, and a session either continues or it does not. That is not decided here and should not be decided incidentally.

⚠ FILED AS A FIRST PASS RATHER THAN A LOCK, deliberately. PT-1140 has flagged a real Settings screen as undesigned since the very first main menu mockup, and PT-1148 left the broader pregame-settings category unscoped on the owners own framing that which settings are universal, per-campaign or per-session is not yet known. This screen cannot be locked ahead of that scoping without guessing at it.

## PT-1259 — ⚠ GAP-002 MIS-CITED AS OPEN FOR THE SIXTH TIME, TWICE BY ME TODAY. Fixed with a CHECK rather than another ruling

Owner said GAP-002 was already closed and asked that it be closed WHEREVER the stale claim lives, because it has come up several times. It has come up more than several.

⚠ PT-640 ALREADY RECORDED THIS EXACT FAILURE, under the title GAP-002 has been closed since PT-248, and I called it open four times today. GAP-002.md line 3 has said CLOSED the whole time. And I did it again TWICE TODAY, writing pending GAP-002 into UI-ASSETS-01 and GAP-002 is unresolved into CHARGEN-DATA-01  BOTH BRAND-NEW DOCUMENTS WRITTEN HOURS AGO.

⚠ THE MECHANISM, which matters more than the count: THE PHRASE largest open design decision ATTACHED ITSELF TO THIS ID EARLY AND KEEPS BEING REPRODUCED FROM MEMORY OF THE PHRASE RATHER THAN FROM THE FILE. It is not a lookup failure. Nothing was looked up. A ruling recording the mistake does not prevent it, because rulings are read AFTER the error, not before.

FIXED THREE WAYS, only one of which is new:

    1  THE INSTANCES  five live stale claims corrected. Two written today
       (UI-ASSETS-01, CHARGEN-DATA-01) and three older ones all saying the
       same thing  9.1 incoming effect class blocked on GAP-002  in
       SPECIES-FEATS-DRAFT, IMMEDIATE-ITEMS-BATCH and AGENDA-UPDATED.
       That item is NOT blocked; the answer exists.

    2  THE SOURCE  GAP-002.md gains a STOP block directly under its status
       line, naming the failure, the count, and the correct answer, so a
       skim-read cannot miss it.

    3  ⚠ A CHECK, scripts/check_closed_gaps.py, WIRED INTO THE GATE AS
       BLOCKING. It scans every markdown file for a closed gap ID within
       reach of open-sounding language  unresolved, pending, blocked on,
       largest open  and fails the gate. The append-only ruling log is
       excluded, since it RECORDS the mistake rather than making it.

⚠ AND THE GENERAL LESSON IS THE THIRD ONE. This project has now written a ruling about this failure TWICE and the ruling did not stop it either time. A CLOSED DECISION NEEDS A MECHANICAL GUARD, NOT A DOCUMENTED ONE. The check takes any future closed gap by adding one line to its CLOSED dict.

## PT-1260 — ABILITY GENERATION RULED: 30-point buy from a base of 8. And ⚠ the Species screens 10 to 12 notation was wrong

Owner raised that the ability base needs to be 8, not the 10 the Species screens arrow notation implied. Checked before ruling, and the corpus had already half-answered it.

SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2 LINE 380 ALREADY SAYS 30-POINT BUY, in the course of ruling that droids do NOT use it  their abilities come off the assembly line. That is the same budget KOTORs own screen shows, and KOTORs screen starts EVERY SCORE AT 8. So the mechanic was never genuinely open; it was stated in passing inside a droid exception and never given its own ruling. PT-1197 has carried it as UNRULED since, and the ability screens were built assuming point buy without a ruling to point at.

RULED, and now written where it can be found: ALL SIX ABILITIES START AT 8. THE PLAYER SPENDS A 30-POINT BUDGET. Costs escalate  1 point per step to 13, 2 per step to 15, 3 per step to 18. CEILING 18 AT LEVEL 1, floor 8. DROIDS DO NOT USE IT, per line 380; their scores are set by chassis and model.

⚠ AND THE CONSEQUENCE THE OWNER CAUGHT: THE SPECIES SCREENS ARROW NOTATION WAS WRONG. It read Str 10 to 12, which implies a base of 10. THERE IS NO BASE OF 10 ANYWHERE IN THIS PROJECT. That notation was introduced at PT-1233 on this agents own initiative, carried through four revision passes, locked, and reproduced into every Species mockup since  and nobody checked it against the generation rule because the generation rule had never been written down.

⚠ THE FIX IS NOT TO RENUMBER IT TO 8 TO 10. SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2 LINE 17 SAYS ADJUSTMENTS APPLY AFTER YOU GENERATE YOUR SCORES. A species adjustment is not a change to a starting value; it is a MODIFIER APPLIED TO WHATEVER THE PLAYER BOUGHT. A Bith who buys Intelligence to 16 ends at 18, not at 12. So the arrow was expressing something that does not happen in that order at all, and any before-and-after pair is a lie about the sequence.

RESOLVED: the Species panel shows PLAIN SIGNED MODIFIERS  Int +2, Con minus 2  which is what the record actually holds and what SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2 itself prints. The Abilities screen is where a number becomes a number.

## PT-1262 — A general staleness guard, replacing the narrow one. And a SEVENTH GAP-002 instance found by it

PT-1259 added a check for one closed gap. PT-1261 extended it for one superseded ruling. Owner asked for gate checks that prevent this class of incident generally rather than case by case. scripts/check_stale_claims.py replaces both, and scripts/check_closed_gaps.py is retired.

⚠ IT FOUND A SEVENTH GAP-002 INSTANCE ON ITS FIRST RUN. comms/AGENDA-UPDATED line 102 still read GAP-002, which Force content. Framed, undecided, four axes. Branch A recommended weakly  an agenda item describing a decision closed at PT-248 as unframed and undecided, with a recommendation for a branch the owner later ruled dead. Neither PT-640s pass nor PT-1259s pass caught it, because both were looking where the error had last appeared rather than everywhere.

⚠ AND THE DESIGN DECISION WORTH RECORDING IS WHY THE REGISTRY IS DECLARED RATHER THAN HARVESTED. The obvious build is to parse the ruling log for closures. That was tried and abandoned: closures are recorded in AT LEAST EIGHT DIFFERENT PHRASINGS  IS CLOSED, was closed by, closed by implication, CLOSED colon, has been closed since, WHICH CLOSED AT, and more. A harvester over that is unreliable, and AN UNRELIABLE HARVESTER IS WORSE THAN NONE because it manufactures false confidence about coverage. So closures are DECLARED in one place in one format, and adding one is a single line in the same commit that closes the thing.

WHAT IT CHECKS, across design, rules, force, playtest and comms:

    CLOSED       a settled gap cited with open-sounding language
    SUPERSEDED   a ruling whose question a later ruling answered
    exemptions   struck-through text is a recorded correction; a line
                 naming its own closing ruling is a correction; the
                 append-only ruling log and generated index record
                 history rather than assert state; and a gaps OWN file
                 is exempt because it quotes the phrases it forbids in
                 order to forbid them

TESTED AGAINST THREE PROBES rather than assumed working: a fresh pending GAP-002 claim, a fresh PT-1197 unruled claim, and a correction naming its closing ruling. First two blocked, third passed.

⚠ THE STANDING INSTRUCTION: WHEN A QUESTION CLOSES, ADD A LINE TO THE REGISTRY IN THE SAME COMMIT. A ruling recording a closure has now failed to prevent recitation three times. The registry is the only thing that has ever caught it.

## PT-1265 — Engine specs reconciled against 127 rulings of drift. ⚠ ONE REAL CONTRADICTION FOUND, plus a spec that did not know player prose is now an input

Owner asked to go through the engine work systematically and fix what is stale. The six specs cite nothing newer than PT-1137 and we are at PT-1264, so the drift is 127 rulings wide. Most of it is harmless  the specs cover ledger, generator, dialogue, combat, resolution and engagement, and the recent work was UI. TWO PLACES WERE NOT HARMLESS.

⚠ THE CONTRADICTION: ENGINE-SPEC-01-LEDGER RULES THAT STATE IS DERIVED BY REPLAY OF AN APPEND-ONLY EVENT LOG AND STATE IS NEVER THE PRIMARY ARTIFACT. CHARACTER-RECORD-01, written today, DESCRIBES A CHARACTER AS AN OBJECT WITH FIELDS and says validate on load, not only on save  which reads as state being exactly the primary artifact. Both documents were internally coherent and together they were incoherent.

RESOLVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS RATHER THAN ONE: the record is A PROJECTION OF THE LOG, not a competing store. Creation writes EVENTS  a species chosen, a point spent, a feat taken  and the record is what replaying them produces. It is worth specifying precisely because every screen reads it, but THE LOG IS WHAT PERSISTS. Three consequences stated so the reconciliation is usable: validate-on-load means validate the projection after replay; A CORRECTION IS A NEW EVENT, NOT AN EDIT; and multiplayer falls out of the logs visibility sets rather than out of the record document.

⚠ AND THE APTITUDE SET IS THE CASE THAT PROVES IT. Five sources stack, and a Skill Focus feat taken at level 8 changes what a level-1 characters aptitude set computes to. Cached it goes stale; replayed it is always right. CHARACTER-RECORD-01 3s derived, never stored is the ledgers own principle applied one level down.

⚠ THE SECOND GAP: ENGINE-SPEC-02-GENERATOR DID NOT KNOW PLAYER-WRITTEN TEXT IS AN INPUT. Two rulings landed after it and point opposite ways  PT-1243 made the Identity story field READ BY THE CAMPAIGN as a source of hooks, and PT-1253 with PT-1160 made Personal Notes FULLY PRIVATE and unreadable by any scripted content. THE DISTINCTION IS CONSENT, NOT FORMAT: a story written during creation is offered to the game, a note written mid-campaign is not.

AND A CONSTRAINT ON HOW THE STORY FIELD MAY BE USED, derived from the generators own design rather than invented: symbols bind to a KIND WITH CONSTRAINTS, never to a specific thing. PLAYER PROSE IS NOT A SYMBOL SOURCE  a name in a backstory is not a resolvable entity, and binding to it would reintroduce exactly the specificity that spec exists to avoid. THE SAFE USE IS AS A SEED FOR CONSTRAINT SELECTION: it can make a sibling or debt constraint more likely to be chosen; it cannot make Vashs sister Kaila a bindable object.

⚠ LEFT UNRESOLVED AND SAID SO: HOW a story field is parsed at all  keyword, author tagging at creation, or not automatically. PT-1243 committed to it being read; nothing has ruled how.

## PT-1266 — ⚠ NO SOURCE GAME EVER READS A SENTENCE A PLAYER WROTE. Daggerfalls biography system is the precedent, and we are two-thirds of the way to it already

Claude Code checked all three source games for how player-supplied text reaches content. THE PREDICTION HELD AND THE USEFUL FINDING WAS SOMEWHERE ELSE.

⚠ THE NEGATIVE, AND IT IS CLEAN AND SCOPED. Across KOTOR 1, KOTOR 2, NWN and Daggerfall, the complete set of player-typed text anything consumes is: A CHARACTER NAME (all), a save-file name (KOTOR, never read back), an account login name (NWN, identity only), and LIVE CHAT (NWN). NOTHING IN ANY OF THEM PARSES AN AUTHORED BACKSTORY.

The structural evidence is stronger than a string sweep: KOTOR HAS NO TEXT-INPUT CONTROL TYPE AT ALL. A control-type census across all 84 K1 panels and all 159 K2 panels returns only Panel, Label, Button, ListBox, ScrollBar, ProtoItem, Progress, CheckBox and Slider. The two fields a player types into  NAME_BOX_EDIT and the save-name EDITBOX  are ordinary Labels the engine writes keystrokes into. And even the name ships with a BTN_RANDOM beside it: the single typed field in the game has a do-not-type path.

⚠ AND A CORRECTION TO THIS AGENTS OWN EXPECTATION, worth recording because it was stated confidently. I expected name, gender pronouns, class and alignment tokens. CLASS AND ALIGNMENT TOKENS DO NOT EXIST IN EITHER KOTOR. Gender exists in K2 ONLY and is used FIVE TIMES TOTAL; K1 has no gendered token anywhere in 200,000 strings. NWN has class and race tokens and KOTOR DROPPED THEM  every class-conditional line in KOTOR is authored as a separate branch rather than templated. That is a deliberate trim, not an omission.

⚠⚠ THE PRECEDENT WORTH TAKING IS DAGGERFALLS BIOGRAPHY SYSTEM, and it solves PT-1243s problem WITH NO PARSING AT ALL. Eighteen files, 216 questions, 1160 answers. Each answer carries THREE THINGS AT ONCE:

    a PROSE FRAGMENT      spliced into a fill-in-the-blank prompt
                          the shipped prompts literally contain ___
    a MECHANICAL PAYLOAD  skill bonuses, items, reputation, gold
                          692 skill grants, 420 item grants across the set
    an ADDRESSABLE HANDLE %q1 to %q12, which later text references by number
                          and the shipped TEXT.RSC uses them  %q1 25 times

⚠ AND WE ALREADY HAVE TWO OF THE THREE. Our Origin world, upbringing, profession and lifestyle are closed sets of answers carrying prose and mechanical payload. WHAT THEY LACK IS THE HANDLE. Checked: nothing in UPBRINGING-01 or PROFESSIONS-01 assigns a stable reference by which later content could name a choice. That is the entire gap, and it is one field per record.

RESOLVED, and it amends PT-1243 rather than overturning it. PT-1243 said names, places and events you write here can surface later as hooks, which implies parsing prose. THE HONEST VERSION IS THAT THE CHOICES SURFACE AS HOOKS AND THE PROSE IS A RENDERING OF THEM. The generated story is already assembled FROM the structured choices  Coruscant supplies the towers, Orphan supplies nobody came for him  so the hookable content was never in the sentences. It was upstream of them.

⚠ THE PLAYERS EDITS THEREFORE DO NOT FEED THE ENGINE, and that should be said plainly on the screen rather than left implied. Editing the story changes what the player reads, not what the campaign can hook.

AND ONE GENUINELY TYPED EXTENSION IS SAFE, on the names own precedent: A NAMED SLOT. A mentors name, a homeworld a player invents, a debt-holder  a SHORT STRING SUBSTITUTED VERBATIM AND NEVER INTERPRETED. The player types the noun; the generator owns the sentence. That is the name mechanism with a different label and it carries zero parsing risk.

⚠ ONE COUNTER-EXAMPLE EXISTS AND IS CORRECTLY EXCLUDED: NWNs OnPlayerChat receives raw typed text and can rewrite it before delivery. That is unambiguous free-text-in mechanical-action-out, and it is the basis of every NWN persistent world chat-command system  but it is A LIVE MULTIPLAYER CHANNEL, not authored character content.

⚠ AND A SCOPED NEGATIVE STATED AS SUCH: NWNs GetDescription and SetDescription CAN read a players typed biography, and the API distinguishes the ORIGINAL description from a script-set one, which is deliberate provision rather than a generic getter. But NO SHIPPED CAMPAIGN SCRIPT WAS FOUND READING IT  the official campaigns scripts ship as compiled bytecode and were not decompiled. The capability is certain; shipped usage is unverified and must not be cited as established.

⚠ FINALLY, A TOKEN-LAYER DETAIL WORTH COPYING: KOTOR resolves tokens at display time inside the TLK fetch and replaces an unknown token with a literal UNRECOGNIZED TOKEN marker rather than blanking it. An authoring error surfaces on screen where someone will see it. And a warning from NWN: it OVERLOADS THE SAME ANGLE-BRACKET DELIMITER for formatting as well as substitution  StartCheck, StartAction and friends appear thousands of times. If we copy the syntax, one delimiter must not carry both jobs.

## PT-1268 — THE HANDLE PRINCIPLE, locked. One mechanism serving creation choices, campaign carry, and AI generation

Owner asked for the reasoning behind PT-1266 and PT-1267 explained accessibly, and locked the result. This is that ruling. It is a PRINCIPLE rather than a screen or a schema, and it governs three things that were being treated as separate problems.

⚠ A HANDLE IS A NAME FOR A DECISION THAT OUTLIVES THE SENTENCE DESCRIBING IT. When a player picks Orphan, three things could exist: the PROSE, the MECHANICAL PAYLOAD, and A NAME FOR THE CHOICE ITSELF  upbringing.orphan. We have the first two everywhere and the third nowhere. That is the entire gap and it is one field per record.

WHY IT MATTERS. A later quest that should fire differently for an orphan has exactly two ways to ask. SEARCH THE PROSE  fragile, catches orphanage and not an orphan, and PT-1266 established that NO SOURCE GAME HAS EVER DONE IT. Or ASK WHETHER upbringing.orphan IS SET  exact, instant, testable. Only the second is available without a handle existing.

⚠ AND IT IS THE SAME PROBLEM AT CAMPAIGN SCALE, which is why PT-1267 and PT-1266 should not be worked separately. A sequel campaign asking whether the party spared someone on Dxun cannot read a prior saves prose either. It needs quest.dxun.outcome = spared. A CREATION CHOICE AND A CAMPAIGN OUTCOME ARE THE SAME SHAPE, one small and one large, and solving the handle once serves both.

⚠⚠ THE AI ARGUMENT, AND IT INVERTS THE OBVIOUS ASSUMPTION. The intuitive reading is that AI removes the need for handles because it could just read the backstory. That is backwards, and THIS PROJECTS OWN LEDGER ALREADY EXPLAINS WHY.

ENGINE-SPEC-01-LEDGER rules that state is derived by replay of an append-only event log and REPLAY IS BIT-IDENTICAL, with every event recording its RNG seed and draw index. AI OUTPUT IS NOT DETERMINISTIC. So if AI interpretation sits UPSTREAM  deciding what a backstory means, with the game branching on that  REPLAY BREAKS. Two replays of one log produce two different campaigns and the guarantee the entire ledger was built around is gone.

PUT AI DOWNSTREAM AND NOTHING BREAKS. The handles are the facts; the AI writes the prose. Same log, same handles, same decisions  the words vary and nothing that matters does.

SO AI MAKES STRUCTURE MORE VALUABLE, NOT LESS, for three reasons worth keeping:

    IT CAN BE CHECKED     you can test that upbringing.orphan fires a hook
                          you cannot test that a paragraph means orphan
    IT FAILS SAFELY       bad prose is disappointing; a bad INTERPRETATION
                          is a quest firing wrongly, which reads as a bug
    IT PLAYS TO STRENGTH  turning handles into a paragraph is GENERATION
                          extracting facts from prose is INFERENCE, and
                          inference is the weaker of the two

⚠ THE CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: THE HANDLE WORK IS NOT PREPARATION FOR THE AI FEATURE, IT IS THE SUBSTRATE THE AI FEATURE RUNS ON. It should be done before, not after, and it is small  one field per record across UPBRINGING-01, PROFESSIONS-01, PROGRAMMINGS-01 and the world menus, plus whatever a quest conclusion turns out to be.

AND THE RULE THAT FALLS OUT OF IT, stated once: AI OUTPUT IS A PRODUCT OF THE LEDGER, NEVER AN INPUT TO IT. Anything an AI writes may be shown, stored as text, and regenerated. Nothing an AI decides may be branched on.


---

## PT-1269 — ⚠ KOTOR EXPORT RULED A HOPE, NOT A REQUIREMENT. And it is now a NO, on evidence

Owner asked for an honest feasibility evaluation of exporting our content as a playable KOTOR mod, explicitly inviting a no. Claude Code investigated. THE ANSWER IS SPLIT AND THE SPLIT FALLS EXACTLY WHERE IT HURTS.

⚠ MY OWN REASONING WAS WRONG TWICE, AND BOTH CORRECTIONS MATTER.

FIRST: I said the engine is the wall because it executes its own rules. RIGHT CONCLUSION, WRONG MECHANISM, AND THE REAL ONE IS WORSE. The binding constraint is STORAGE, NOT EXECUTION. A creature blueprints SkillList is LIST[8] and each entry contains ONLY a Rank  no skill id. POSITION IN THE ARRAY IS THE SKILL IDENTITY. Execution can sometimes be worked around with scripts; A MISSING STORAGE SLOT CANNOT. Both games headers declare SKILL_MAX_SKILLS = 8.

⚠ AND THE NATURAL EXPERIMENT IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IN THE REPORT. Obsidian had ENGINE SOURCE ACCESS. Between K1 and K2 they grew classes 9 to 17, feats 125 to 245, powers 132 to 282  and SKILLS 8 TO 8. They expanded every id-referenced table, some by 150 rows, and did not add a single skill. The people best placed to add a ninth declined to, and left SKILL_MAX_SKILLS at 8 in their own header. Twenty years of community modding has never added one either; the workaround is to fake a skill as a feat plus dialogue checks, which is a tell.

SECOND CORRECTION, AND IT IS GOOD NEWS: I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE WALKMESH. It is NOT inside the .mdl  it is a separate .wok resource, 3237 MDL against 1236 WOK in K2. More importantly, GEOMETRY IS FULLY SEPARABLE FROM CONTENT. An area references its rooms BY NAME ONLY  RoomName: 262tela  and that string is the entire coupling. Every creature, placeable, door, trigger and conversation can be replaced wholesale on shipped geometry with ZERO 3D WORK. The second wall I named is optional and most mods never touch it.

THREE FURTHER CEILINGS ON THE SCRIPT ROUTE, which was my proposed workaround: NO SetCurrentHitPoints, so state can be read but not set. NO PRE-RESOLUTION HOOK  every combat function is past tense, GetLASTAttackResult, so you observe the engines resolution and cannot replace it. AND ⚠ KOTOR HAS NO NAMED LOCAL VARIABLES: SetLocalBoolean(object, int nIndex, value), integer slots only, no strings, floats or objects. Globals must be predeclared in globalcat.2da and THE ENTIRE GAME SHIPS TWO STRING GLOBALS. A script-side rules layer would be an interpreter written in a spreadsheet.

⚠ AND A STRUCTURAL FINDING WORTH KEEPING FOR OUR OWN DESIGN: THE JOURNAL IS A SINGLE GAME-WIDE FILE. Exactly one JRL resource exists in the archive set, named global. A quest is a category inside it. So CONTENT IS MODULE-LOCAL BUT RULES AND QUESTS ARE GLOBAL, and any real exporter needs MERGE LOGIC rather than file emission. That is what TSLPatcher exists for.

THE RULING: EXPORT IS A HOPE, NOT A REQUIREMENT, AND WE ARE NOT BUILDING IT NOW. Exporting a KOTOR-RULES campaign is feasible  formats writable, PyKotor already carries a full NSS compiler, geometry separable. EXPORTING OUR RULES IS NOT. Our 24 skills cannot exist: eight positional slots, no ids, no room. Not difficult, ABSENT.

⚠ THE FRAMING WORTH REMEMBERING: KOTOR IS AN OUTPUT FORMAT FOR A KOTOR CAMPAIGN, NOT A RUNTIME FOR OUR SYSTEM. An exporter would be a lossy transpiler onto someone elses rules, and the lossy part is exactly the part that makes our system ours.

⚠⚠ AND THE CONSEQUENCE THAT UNBLOCKS THE NEXT PHASE: THE EXPORTER NO LONGER CONSTRAINS OUR FORMAT. Combined with the owners ruling that we should not mirror KOTORs structure, the format decision is now FREE. That was the decision the owner wanted to make first and it can now be made on its own merits.

## TRACE-81 — STUDY batch 1, container layer. ⚠ Precedence NOT established, one of my stated facts corrected, and the save is an archive of archives

First of seven structural study batches delivered to HANDOFF STUDY/01-container. Six records, README, FLAWS with 12 entries, NAMING. Template followed unmodified.

⚠ PRECEDENCE COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED, AND THAT IS THE HONEST HEADLINE. Shipped data cannot show precedence directly. What it CAN show is NECESSITY  if a layer ships a file shadowing another with DIFFERENT BYTES, that layer must win or the file is inert. On that argument, proven: patch.erf beats BIF (10 of 11 shadowed entries differ, keymap.2da grows 79 to 80 rows), Override beats BIF (all 10 K2 override files differ from their BIF copies), module beats BIF (K1 189 differing shadow occurrences, K2 105).

⚠ WHAT REMAINS UNKNOWN IS THE ORDER OF OVERRIDE, MODULE AND PATCH AGAINST EACH OTHER. The necessity argument only works against BIF. The install contains genuine three-way collisions  spells.2da in two layers, skills.2da in two, 75 textures in two  so the engine MUST have a rule and nothing in the data says what it is. The mechanism is a SINGLE FLAT REGISTRY: both binaries carry CExoKeyTable::AddKey: Duplicate Resource, so every layer registers into one table keyed on ResRef and ResType with collisions detected at insert. WHETHER AddKey REJECTS OR REPLACES IS THE WHOLE QUESTION and needs a disassembly or the running game.

⚠ AND ONE OF THE TWO FACTS I SUPPLIED IN THE PROMPT WAS WRONG. I stated 40 K1 modules ship as .mod rather than paired .rim. There ARE 40 .mod files, but 34 OF THEM ALSO HAVE A .rim PAIR. Only 6 are .mod-only, the Rakata endgame. Of the 34 coexisting: 12 hold the same resource set, 21 are a STRICT SUPERSET, 1 is neither  danm13.mod carries four UTC blueprints its pair lacks. So .mod in K1 is mostly a DUPLICATE of the pair, not a replacement, AND NOTHING DECLARES WHICH LOADS. That is the most consequential open question in the batch.

## TRACE-83 — STUDY batch 3, blueprint layer. ⚠ GFF is self-describing in SHAPE and not in MEANING, and a creature instance can override NOTHING

Every blueprint in both games read  2,656 K1 and 1,741 K2 creature blueprints, 13,000+ across nine types, plus all 199 GIT files for the instance comparison.

⚠ A REAL ACCESS PROBLEM, NOW FIXED. CHARACTER-RECORD-01 lives in MAIN_WORK, which the study agent cannot open, so 3s comparison ran against INFERENCE from the docs visible in HANDOFF and said so plainly rather than pretending otherwise. A copy is now at STUDY/_reference/ so the comparison can be redone properly.

⚠ AND THE AGENT FLAGGED A DISCREPANCY THAT IS ITSELF THE RELAY FAILURE. It read SKILLS-01 1 as heading Twenty-two skills against a brief saying 24, and asked which was stale. NEITHER. Line 15 is the QUOTED TEXT OF A HISTORICAL ERROR  PT-865 recording that the header once read that and was corrected. The live count is 24. A quoted correction read as a current claim is exactly METHOD-RECORD-01 1.5: a claim carries the warrant of its reading, not of its relay. Noted in the reference README so the next batch does not repeat it.

⚠⚠ GFF IS SELF-DESCRIBING IN SHAPE AND NOT IN MEANING, which answers the question flagged as mattering most to us. A reader with NO SCHEMA can walk any blueprint and print every field name, type and value correctly. What it CANNOT know is that Appearance_Type = 452 is A ROW INDEX INTO appearance.2da while Str = 14 beside it is A QUANTITY. Same type, same shape, no target named. THE REFERENCE GRAPH IS NOT IN THE DATA  IT LIVES ONLY IN CODE. And it compounds with batch 2: an untyped integer in a blueprint points at a row in a table whose columns are also untyped.

Also: 8 of 19 GFF field types are NEVER USED by any blueprint, including THE DEDICATED StrRef TYPE  every string reference travels inside a CExoLocString instead. And Struct is never used; all nesting is via lists. Scoped to blueprints; ARE, IFO, DLG and JRL are later batches.

⚠ THE STRUCT TYPE ID CARRIES PAYLOAD, which is a genuine trap. GFF gives every struct a Type field meaning what shape is this, and most lists use it that way  SkillList 0, FeatList 1, ClassList 2. But Equip_ItemList STORES THE EQUIPMENT SLOT BITMASK THERE, 13 values matching baseitems.equipableslots, and ItemList stores THE INVENTORY SEQUENCE NUMBER. Practical consequence: A GENERIC GFF READER CANNOT ROUND-TRIP A UTC. Normalising struct types silently unequips every item.

⚠⚠ A CREATURE INSTANCE CAN OVERRIDE NOTHING, AND THE SURFACE IS INVERTED. Every creature placement in every area file of both games carries EXACTLY SIX FIELDS  TemplateResRef plus five position and orientation floats. 100% of 1,619 K1 and 1,700 K2 instances. No inheritance, no copy-on-write, no partial override. TWO GUARDS DIFFERING ONLY IN HIT POINTS NEED TWO COMPLETE BLUEPRINTS, and the counts show it: 1,589 distinct blueprints for 1,619 placements in K1s modules, roughly ONE TEMPLATE PER INSTANCE.

Meanwhile A WAYPOINT  an eleven-field blueprint  CAN OVERRIDE SEVEN THINGS per placement including Appearance, Tag, LocalizedName and Description. THE RICHEST BLUEPRINT GETS THE POOREST INSTANCE AND VICE VERSA. That is the template-versus-instance answer, and it is the wrong way round.

ITEMS ARE ENTIRELY DATA, no scripts anywhere in an items mechanical effect. A property is FIVE LEVELS OF INTEGER INDIRECTION: UTI.PropertiesList to itempropdef.2da row, that row NAMES ANOTHER 2DA BY STRING, Subtype indexes into it, with parallel chains for cost and param. Subtype targets include appearance, classes, feat and gender, SO A PROPERTY CAN BE GATED ON A FEAT PURELY BY TABLE REFERENCE. 573 of 1,170 K1 items have no properties at all.

POSITION-IS-IDENTITY EXTENDED, AND SKILLLIST IS CONFIRMED AS THE ONLY ONE. ClassList, FeatList, KnownList0 and SpecAbilityList all carry explicit ids, verified across all 4,397 creature blueprints. ⚠ AND THE PROOF THAT NOTHING VALIDATES IT: THREE K1 BLUEPRINTS SHIP 20-ENTRY SKILL LISTS  c_drdg, c_sebulba and partymember  WITH REAL RANKS PAST SLOT 8. One is c_sebulba, a prequel-film character with no role in either game, shipped in the BIF layer for twenty years. With no id there is nothing to validate against.

Range-checking every 2DA index field found LIVE OVERFLOWS: K1 Appearance_Type runs 1 to 546 against a 509-ROW appearance.2da.

⚠ AND A CROSS-BATCH FINDING THAT SHARPENS F08. ALL 82 APPEARANCE OVERFLOWS ARE IN .mod FILES. Zero in .rim, zero in BIF. They include the exact four extra blueprints batch 1 found in danm13.mod, carrying ids 541 to 544. READING: THE .mod COPIES WERE BUILT AGAINST A LARGER appearance.2da THAN THE ONE THAT SHIPPED. They are not a repackaging of the same content; they are FROM A DIFFERENT DATA SET. 36 of the 78 affected resrefs also exist in a _s.rim with a valid value. This does not prove which the engine loads, but it establishes the two copies are NOT EQUIVALENT and one set contains references that cannot resolve.

## TRACE-84 — ⚠ THE STUDY TURNED ON OUR OWN SPEC AND FOUND TEN GAPS. CHARACTER-RECORD-01 IS A CREATION-TIME CONTRACT, NOT A CHARACTER

Batch 3s comparison redone against the real CHARACTER-RECORD-01 rather than inference. It is the most valuable output of the study so far because it is the first to examine OUR work, and it does not flatter it.

⚠⚠ THE ROOT FINDING, WHICH EXPLAINS MOST OF THE OTHERS: WE SPECIFIED A PLAYER-CHARACTER CREATION RECORD AND CALLED IT A CHARACTER RECORD. It holds what a player CHOSE. It holds nothing about what a character IS DURING PLAY, and nothing about a character nobody created.

THE TEN GAPS, in the agents own order of how much they will hurt:

     1  NO CURRENT-STATE LAYER ANYWHERE  no current HP, no current Force,
        no conditions, no position. Nothing specifies what a character IN
        PLAY is.
     2  NO NPC RECORD, and the PC record cannot cheaply become one
     3  NO ALIGNMENT FIELD  ⚠ and ALIGNMENT-01-v2 has SEVEN BANDS,
        hysteresis, drift and atonement. An entire chapter with no key.
     4  NO EQUIPMENT SLOTS  flat items[], no stacking, no wield model,
        despite PT-1252 locking an ELEVEN-SLOT LATTICE
     5  no faction handle
     6  ⚠ NO NARRATIVE-PROTECTION FLAGS. KOTOR carries Plot, Min1HP and
        NoPermDeath  THREE BOOLEANS THAT SOLVE THE STORY-NPC PROBLEM
     7  no embodiment beyond a portrait; organics have no body model
     8  no script handle  a uuid is identity, not a name to author against
     9  no behaviour attachment
    10  no IsPC equivalent

⚠ AND ONE PLACE WHERE FREEZING BEAT DERIVING: HIT POINTS. A designer cannot make ONE GUARD TOUGHER without inventing a class or a feat for it. A derived-only model has no escape hatch, and AUTHORED CONTENT NEEDS ONE. That is a direct hit on PT-1265s projection ruling, which I wrote, and it is correct.

⚠ THE STORAGE MODELS ARE NOT COMPETING  THEY SERVE DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. The agent argued KOTORs side properly when asked. A frozen record buys O(1) load with no replay budget across 2,656 blueprints, direct authoring with no author-an-event-stream problem, A PORTABLE STANDALONE ARTIFACT (an event log needs the replay engine AND version-pinned tables to mean anything, SO IT IS NOT AN INTERCHANGE FORMAT), and trivially correct save/restore.

⚠ AND A HAZARD PT-1265 DID NOT ADDRESS: if a rules change reaches every existing character, A LIVE CAMPAIGNS CHARACTERS CHANGE UNDER ITS PLAYERS BETWEEN SESSIONS. Validate on load catches a record that became ILLEGAL, not one that quietly became DIFFERENT.

THE CONCLUSION, which I accept: AN EVENT LOG IS RIGHT FOR A PLAYER-OWNED CHARACTER THAT EVOLVES. A FROZEN RECORD IS RIGHT FOR AUTHORED CONTENT THAT IS PLACED, NOT PLAYED. WE SPECIFIED ONLY THE FIRST.

⚠ AND AGAINST ITS OWN 4 FINDING: OURS COLLAPSES HARDER THAN KOTORS. KOTOR at least HAS a template-instance split, even with the instance side nearly empty. CHARACTER-RECORD-01 has NO SPLIT AT ALL  every character is a full record with a uuid. And the event log makes templating HARDER: replay output cannot inherit, so inheritance would be a shared log prefix, which is either event-copying (the same collapse one layer down) or a fork model nothing specifies. Two things soften it  storing choices means near-identical characters diverge in a few events rather than forty derived values, and package avoids KOTORs flat global namespace  but neither addresses the absence of an NPC record.

⚠ WE ARE ON THE WRONG SIDE OF OUR OWN PRINCIPLE ONCE. feats[].source stores granted-versus-chosen. GRANTED-NESS IS A CONSEQUENCE of the class feat schedule, not a choice, and KOTOR DERIVES IT from feat.2das <cls>_granted column. A change to the schedule leaves stored source values describing a schedule that no longer exists. That is store-the-choice-derive-the-consequence violated in the document that states the principle.

AND A NEAT CORROBORATION: racialtypes.2da CARRIES OUR DERIVE-ON-READ MECHANISM, DISABLED. stradjust, dexadjust, intadjust, chaadjust, wisadjust, conadjust  exactly the species-modifier-on-read PT-1260 ruled  and EVERY VALUE IS ZERO in both games, with five of seven rows unlabelled. Another dead capability, and evidence that bought-versus-final was a real design question BioWare also faced and abandoned.

FLAWS.md is now hard-separated: F24-F33 for KOTOR, OF01-OF07 for our format under distinct numbering so a later merge cannot blend them. Nothing in _reference/ was edited; two observations reading as spec gaps were REPORTED rather than fixed.

Owner ruled that the gaps TRACE-84 found get specs written before the study continues, since the remaining batches would keep producing findings against a spec with known holes.

⚠ THE TEN GAPS ARE NOT TEN PROBLEMS, THEY ARE FOUR, and clustering them is most of the work:

    A  PLAY-STATE LAYER    gaps 1, 3, 5. No current HP, Force, conditions,
                           position, alignment or faction. ⚠ NOTHING
                           SPECIFIES WHAT A CHARACTER IN PLAY IS. Biggest,
                           and it blocks B.
    B  AUTHORED CHARACTER  gaps 2, 6, 10. No NPC record, no narrative
                           protection, no is_pc. KOTORs blueprint is a
                           TEMPLATE PLACED IN THE WORLD and we have no
                           such thing.
    C  ATTACHMENT POINTS   gaps 8, 9. A uuid is identity, not a name to
                           author against, and no behaviour can be bound.
    D  EMBODIMENT AND GEAR gaps 4, 7. ⚠ PT-1252 LOCKED AN ELEVEN-SLOT
                           LATTICE AND THE RECORD STORES A FLAT LIST.
                           The screen and the spec disagree.

⚠ AND THE HP ESCAPE HATCH IS FILED INTO CLUSTER B DELIBERATELY, because it is the same conversation as the NPC record. TRACE-84s sharpest finding: in a derive-only model A DESIGNER CANNOT MAKE ONE GUARD TOUGHER without inventing a class or feat for it. Authored content needs an override and that is what an authored-character model is for.

THE TWO PRINCIPLE VIOLATIONS BOTH HAVE FIXES, and both are small.

⚠ OF07, RULES-CHANGE DRIFT. A rules change reaches every existing character on next replay, so A LIVE CAMPAIGNS CHARACTERS CHANGE UNDER ITS PLAYERS BETWEEN SESSIONS, and validate-on-load catches ILLEGAL rather than DIFFERENT. FIX: VERSION-PIN THE LOG. It records which rules version it was played under; replay uses THAT version; a campaign OPTS IN to an update explicitly and can be shown what changed. Same model as a save knowing its patch. That makes the projection model SAFE rather than merely elegant.

⚠ OF03, feats[].source. It stores granted-versus-chosen, but GRANTED-NESS IS A PROPERTY OF THE CLASS SCHEDULE, NOT OF THE CHARACTER  KOTOR derives it from feat.2das <cls>_granted column. ⚠ AND THE NAIVE FIX HAS A WRINKLE: deriving it breaks when a player CHOSE a feat the schedule LATER GRANTS, since derivation would call it granted though a slot was paid. So STORE WHETHER IT COST A FEAT SLOT  a genuine fact about what happened  AND DERIVE GRANTED-NESS. One field, but the right one.

⚠ AND TWO GUARDS ON THE WORK ITSELF, stated in the document. THIS IS NOT A REDESIGN: no ruling in CHARACTER-RECORD-01 is overturned, and the projection model, both principles and the derived-not-stored table all stand. AND IT IS NOT A LICENCE TO ADD FIELDS SPECULATIVELY: every one of the ten is a gap the source games DEMONSTRABLY NEEDED, and anything not on the list needs its own argument.

Order: A, then B, then C and D independently, with OF07 fixed inside A and OF03 inside B. Then study batch 4 resumes.

## TRACE-85 — KOTOR live state. ⚠ THE SAVE REPLACES BLUEPRINTS, THE PLAYER EXISTS 21 TIMES, and KOTOR SHOWS THE PLAYER THE ENTIRE ARITHMETIC

Read from four real K1 saves plus the exploded working set: 184 saved creature records across 21 module snapshots, 321 effects, 21 copies of the player. ⚠ K1 ONLY  no K2 save data exists in this install, searched exhaustively, so K2 claims rest on the script API alone.

⚠ THE SAVED GIT IS NOT A PLACEMENT FILE. A shipped GIT creature entry has SIX FIELDS. A SAVED one has 112  the whole creature inline, current HP, effects, action queue, position. ONCE A MODULE IS VISITED THE SAVE REPLACES ITS BLUEPRINTS rather than referencing them. That completes batch 1s archive-of-archives finding: the save is not a diff, it is a REPLACEMENT WORLD.

⚠ AND THE PLAYER IS NOT IN ANY CREATURE LIST. 0 of 184 saved creatures have IsPC=1. The player lives in Mod_PlayerList inside EACH module snapshots IFO  and it is in ALL 21 OF THEM, WITH DIFFERENT VALUES. tar_m02ad holds HP 10/22 and XP 5,045; tar_m03ab holds HP 0/22 and XP 18,285; tar_m03ae holds HP 10/22 and XP 33,310. EACH IS THE PLAYER AS THEY WERE WHEN THEY LAST LEFT THAT MODULE. The save contains AN ACCIDENTAL PARTIAL HISTORY AT MODULE GRANULARITY  twenty stale copies and one live one, and you tell which is current by matching PT_XP_POOL. Companions sit outside the world entirely: full records with live values but NO ObjectId, where every in-world creature has one.

⚠ AND KOTOR HAS AN EVENT LOG, FOR ONE THING ONLY. The PC alone carries LvlStatList  a PER-LEVEL RECORD of class, hit die, force, skill points, skills and feats for each level taken. That is the closest thing in KOTOR to our append-only log, and it exists ONLY FOR THE PLAYER AND ONLY FOR LEVEL-UPS. They needed replay exactly where we do and nowhere else.

EFFECTS are a list on the creature with one universal entry shape. Duration is A FLOAT IN SECONDS with an absolute expiry on a game calendar, and only two values appear across all 321: 0.0 and 5000.0. ⚠ SkipOnLoad IS PER-EFFECT  190 keep, 131 drop  so what happens to a buff on reload is DECIDED PER EFFECT AT CREATION rather than by blanket rule, which is good design worth taking. IsExposed is 0 on 6 of 321: THE ENGINE CARRIES EFFECTS IT DOES NOT SHOW YOU. What is absent: no names, no stacking rules, no dispel info.

⚠ ALIGNMENT IS ONE INTEGER, GoodEvil, 0 to 100, AND NOTHING ELSE. Scoped: every field of all 184 saved creatures searched, plus the 112-field player record, PARTYTABLE, GLOBALVARS and both blueprint field sets. No band, no direction, no history, no hysteresis. LawfulChaotic exists on blueprints, is dead, and is dropped from live records. SO THIS IS ONE PLACE WHERE OUR RECORD NEEDS A FIELD KOTOR NEVER HAD, rather than the usual direction  ALIGNMENT-01-v2s seven bands and hysteresis have no precedent to copy.

⚠ THE REAL-TIME SPLIT, which was the point of asking. WOULD BE WRONG TO PORT: float-second durations; ⚠ ActionList, WHICH PERSISTS A SUSPENDED SCRIPT VM  106KB of bytecode plus an instruction pointer, caught mid-execution; CombatRoundData tracking position inside a 3-second round; Animation state; MovementRate; PerceptionList; DetectMode; AIState; ExpressionList; PT_PLAYEDSECONDS. The action queue is the clearest case  KOTOR persists a half-executed script BECAUSE A SAVE CAN LAND ANYWHERE IN CONTINUOUS TIME. If our design ever grows one, something has gone wrong.

PORTS CLEANLY: current versus max HP and Force; the effect list as a list on the creature, with only the duration UNIT being real-time; IsExposed; SkipOnLoad; XP, Gold, SkillPoints; GoodEvil; LvlStatList; per-creature script variables; Plot, Min1HP and IsRaiseable.

GENUINELY ARGUABLE, and the agent argued it well: CombatInfo is A FULLY DERIVED BLOCK FROZEN ONTO THE RECORD. For real-time, caching is obviously right. For turn-based it is not obviously wrong either  A CACHED, VISIBLE DERIVATION IS WHAT A CHARACTER SHEET IS. Its position, which I accept: CACHE IT AS A PROJECTION WITH A STATED INVALIDATION RULE, NOT AS STORED TRUTH. KOTOR does not distinguish, which is why ArcaneSpellFail  a D&D field with no KOTOR meaning  sits in CombatInfo on every creature in the game.

⚠⚠ AND THE BEST FINDING IN THE STUDY SO FAR. PARTYTABLE carries a 64-ENTRY FEEDBACK RING BUFFER, PERSISTED IN THE SAVE. Real entries: Attack Breakdown: Mainhand 25 = roll 20 Automatic Hit! and Defense Breakdown: 18 = base 10 + dex mod 4 + class 4.

KOTOR SHOWS THE PLAYER THE ENTIRE ARITHMETIC. Not a result  the roll, each modifier NAMED, and the total. That last line is A SENTENCE EXPLAINING A DERIVED VALUE IN TERMS OF ITS SOURCES, PRINTED DURING PLAY. For a system whose record DERIVES vitality, defence and saves rather than storing them, that is THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT IN THE STUDY FOR DERIVATION BEING A FEATURE YOU SHOW RATHER THAN A COST YOU HIDE. And ours is turn-based  we are not fighting a 3-second round for attention.

It also persists a 64-entry dialogue log, which panel was last open, a tutorial-seen bitmask, and party-control mode. INTERFACE STATE IS PART OF THE SAVE.

ONE DISCREPANCY, honestly reported: the save declares 819 booleans and 376 numbers against globalcat.2das 809 and 369. Ten and seven more, and patch.erf contains no globalcat. ⚠ BUT THE STRUCTURAL POINT SURVIVES AND IS GOOD: GLOBALVARS.res CARRIES ITS OWN NAME LIST, so a save does not depend on globalcat being unchanged to load. Values pack tightly  819 booleans in 103 bytes, bit-packed. Why the counts differ was not determined and the agent says so.

## PT-1271 — ⚠ UNBOUNDED LOG GROWTH bound into cluster A as a constraint, before play-state is specified

Owner recalled a size limit from the corpus and was right  58 KB, TRACE-04, recorded in ENGINE-SPEC-01 5 and never resolved.

THE EXISTING PROBLEM: if generated content writes into the fact ledger without bound, the ledger stops being the flat 58 KB file and becomes the 13.6 MB one. And 5.1 names why NEITHER SOURCE GAME SOLVES IT FOR US  Daggerfall EXPIRES QUESTS after an in-game week; KOTOR NEVER EVICTS AND NEVER NEEDED TO, because roughly a hundred authored modules bounds it. Our generated facts are meant to be PERMANENT, which is the case neither engine has.

⚠ AND PLAY-STATE MAKES IT WORSE IN A WAY NOTHING HAS RULED ON. That passage is about generated FACTS. Play-state adds a second growth source entirely: every HP change, every effect applied and expired, every position update is an event on an append-only log. THIS GROWS PER COMBAT ROUND, NOT PER QUEST  a different order of magnitude and a different shape.

⚠ TRACE-85 SHOWS KOTORS ANSWER AND IT IS THE OPPOSITE OF OURS. It logs none of it. A save carries A REPLACEMENT WORLD  112 fields inline per creature, one snapshot per visited module  which is BOUNDED BY CONSTRUCTION. WE CANNOT COPY THAT WITHOUT ABANDONING REPLAY, so the answer has to be ours rather than borrowed.

⚠ BUT THE SHAPE OF THE ANSWER IS ALREADY IN THE LEDGER SPEC: A KINDS LIFETIME IS PART OF ITS DECLARATION, 2.1. Some events are PERMANENT FACTS  you spared the Sith on Dxun. Some are TRANSIENT  you took 4 damage in round 3 of a fight that ended an hour ago. IF THE LOG DOES NOT DISTINGUISH THEM AT WRITE TIME IT CANNOT COMPACT LATER WITHOUT RETROACTIVELY DECIDING WHAT MATTERED, and that is a judgement no compactor can make safely.

BOUND INTO CLUSTER A AS A CONSTRAINT rather than filed as a separate task, because a field set specified without it would need respecifying. Cluster A must answer three things before any field is written: WHICH play-state changes are events at all versus pure projections; WHAT LIFETIME each event kind declares  permanent, campaign, session or transient; and WHAT COMPACTION IS PERMITTED.

⚠ AND THE THIRD CARRIES A CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING NOW: IF A COMPACTED LOG DOES NOT REPLAY BIT-IDENTICALLY, PT-1265s REPLAY GUARANTEE NEEDS RESTATING RATHER THAN QUIETLY WEAKENING. That guarantee is what PT-1268 rests its AI-downstream argument on, so weakening it silently would undermine a ruling two steps away.

## PT-1272 — PLAY-STATE-01 written. Cluster A closed except alignment, and PT-1265s replay guarantee RESTATED rather than weakened

First of the four RECORD-GAPS-01 clusters. It answers PT-1271s growth constraint before specifying any field, which was the required order.

⚠ THE SHAPE FINDING, WHICH RESOLVED A CONFLATION: three things were being treated as two. CHARACTER-RECORD-01 is what you CHOSE. PLAY-STATE is what is TRUE RIGHT NOW. THE LOG is what HAPPENED, and is the only thing that persists. PLAY-STATE IS A SECOND PROJECTION OF THE SAME LOG, NOT A SECOND STORE  a character has one log, replaying to the end gives current state, replaying to a point gives state then. There is no save file for how much health I have.

⚠ EVENT LIFETIME, ANSWERED FIRST AS PT-1271 REQUIRED. Four lifetimes declared AT WRITE TIME: PERMANENT, never compactable, a fact about the campaign forever. CAMPAIGN, compactable on close. SESSION, compactable on session end. TRANSIENT, compactable when its own stated condition fires.

AND THE RULE THAT MAKES COMPACTION SAFE: A TRANSIENT EVENT DECLARES ITS OWN EXPIRY CONDITION, AND A COMPACTOR MAY ONLY COLLAPSE EVENTS WHOSE CONDITION HAS ALREADY FIRED. It never decides what mattered  the event said so when it was written. Compaction replaces a run with ONE CHECKPOINT EVENT carrying the resulting state, itself permanent.

⚠⚠ AND THE CONSEQUENCE PT-1271 REQUIRED STATING RATHER THAN LEAVING QUIET. A COMPACTED LOG DOES NOT REPLAY BIT-IDENTICALLY TO THE ORIGINAL  it replays to THE SAME END STATE BY A SHORTER PATH. PT-1265s guarantee is therefore RESTATED: replay of a GIVEN log is bit-identical; COMPACTION PRODUCES A DIFFERENT LOG WITH THE SAME END STATE, and is AN EXPLICIT, RECORDED OPERATION, NEVER AUTOMATIC AND NEVER SILENT. A compacted log cannot replay to a point before its checkpoint. That is a real price and a campaign should be told before it is paid. PT-1268s AI-downstream argument survives intact because it depends on determinism WITHIN a log, not on logs being immortal.

THE FIELD SET IS COLLECTED, NOT INVENTED. Pools reuse PORT-01 3s capacity-and-current and ENGINE-SPEC-04s working maximum. pool.wounds is NOT added, per PT-1060.

⚠ TWO CONDITION FIELDS TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM KOTOR because twenty years of shipped content needed them: EXPOSED, since the engine carries effects it does not show  IsExposed is 0 on 6 of 321 real effects  and SURVIVES_LOAD, DECIDED PER EFFECT AT CREATION rather than by blanket rule, 190 of 321 keeping and 131 dropping. That is better than most games manage.

AND DURATION IS IN ROUNDS OR CONDITIONS, NEVER SECONDS. KOTORs float-second durations are an artefact of continuous time.

⚠ ALIGNMENT IS BLOCKED AND LEFT UNSPECIFIED DELIBERATELY. ALIGNMENT-01 is CITED BY ATTACKS-06 AND MULTICLASS-01 AND DOES NOT RESOLVE TO A FILE IN THIS REPOSITORY  audit_docrefs reports it among many, and it is presumably in the Library repo. Known: seven bands, and MULTICLASS-01 315 makes its HYSTERESIS LOAD-BEARING ON CLASS ACCESS. TRACE-85 established KOTOR carried ONE INTEGER 0-100 and nothing else. So this is a place where WE NEED A FIELD KOTOR NEVER HAD and the shape must follow the rules rather than precede them. NOT INVENTED.

EXCLUSIONS ARE DELIBERATE AND CITED. No action queue  KOTOR persists a SUSPENDED SCRIPT VM, 106 KB of bytecode mid-execution, because a real-time save can land anywhere, AND IF OUR DESIGN EVER GROWS ONE SOMETHING HAS GONE WRONG. No combat-round position, no animation or perception or AI state, no played-seconds. And no frozen derived block  KOTORs CombatInfo freezes defence and saves onto the record, which is why ArcaneSpellFail, a D&D field with no KOTOR meaning, sits on every creature in the game.

⚠ AND SECTION 5 IS A DESIGN INSTRUCTION RATHER THAN A FIELD: SHOW THE WORKING. TRACE-85 found KOTOR persisting Defense Breakdown: 18 = base 10 + dex mod 4 + class 4  the entire arithmetic, each modifier named, printed during play. FOR A SYSTEM THAT DERIVES RATHER THAN STORES, THIS CONVERTS THE MODELS COST INTO ITS FEATURE. And turn-based gives us MORE room to show working, not less. It binds PT-1255s Rolls and Feedback setting, which is currently one line on a first-pass options screen and is a bigger idea than that.

## PT-1273 — AUTHORED-CHARACTER-01 written. ⚠ Cluster B was LESS NEW THAN IT LOOKED, because BEASTS-ENTRIES-01 already had the model

Second RECORD-GAPS-01 cluster. Checking before writing paid off immediately: THERE IS ALREADY AN AUTHORED-CREATURE MODEL IN THIS CORPUS, five documents of it, and it is good. Most of this generalises rather than invents.

⚠ THREE THINGS THE BEAST MODEL ALREADY GETS RIGHT THAT THE PLAYER RECORD DOES NOT. IT IS A TEMPLATE and templating is the point  one Cannok entry, many cannoks. VITALITY IS A DIE PER LEVEL, NOT A NUMBER, so a creature scales without anyone authoring a value and two of a kind at different levels need one entry. And IT CARRIES senses AS A FIRST-CLASS LINE  which PT-1237 had to add to the player record afterwards and PT-1238 then had to propagate across five surfaces.

⚠ PROTECTION FLAGS TAKEN FROM KOTOR EXACTLY, per TRACE-85: plot, min_1_hp and raiseable. THEY ARE NOT ONE FLAG AT THREE STRENGTHS  a quest-giver mid-conversation is plot, a companion in a fight they must survive is min_1_hp, a character who SHOULD die and return is raiseable. Twenty years of shipped content needed all three.

⚠⚠ THE HP ESCAPE HATCH, WHICH WAS TRACE-84s SHARPEST FINDING, AND THE RESOLUTION IS NOT A HOLE IN THE PRINCIPLE. The problem: in a derive-only model A DESIGNER CANNOT MAKE ONE GUARD TOUGHER without inventing a class or feat for him.

THE ANSWER: STORE-THE-CHOICE-DERIVE-THE-CONSEQUENCE IS A RULE ABOUT A PLAYERS RECORD. A players vitality is a consequence of choices they made. AN AUTHORED CHARACTER HAS NO CHOICES  AN AUTHOR DECLARES WHAT IS TRUE ABOUT THEM. A DECLARATION IS A CHOICE; IT IS JUST THE AUTHORS RATHER THAN THE PLAYERS. So vitality die d8 is derived and vitality die d8 override 40 is declared, and BOTH ARE CHOICES. The override is authored data on a template exactly as Defence 15 already is on a Cannok.

AND THE GUARD ON IT: AN OVERRIDE IS DECLARED ON THE TEMPLATE, NEVER PATCHED ONTO AN INSTANCE.

⚠ TEMPLATE VERSUS INSTANCE, AND TRACE-83 IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. Every KOTOR creature placement carries SIX FIELDS  a template name and five position floats  100% of 3,319 instances, both games, no inheritance and no partial override. THE CONSEQUENCE IS MEASURABLE: two guards differing only in hit points need two complete blueprints, and K1 ships 1,589 distinct blueprints for 1,619 placements. THE TEMPLATE SYSTEM STOPPED FUNCTIONING AS ONE.

OUR RULE: AN INSTANCE IS A TEMPLATE PLUS A NAMED SET OF PERMITTED OVERRIDES, AND THE TEMPLATE DECLARES WHICH FIELDS AN INSTANCE MAY OVERRIDE. Why the template rather than a global list: A plot FLAG SHOULD BE INSTANCE-OVERRIDABLE ON A GENERIC GUARD AND NOT ON A STORY CHARACTER. The template author knows; a global rule cannot.

is_pc DOES NOT DISTINGUISH IS THIS A PERSON  TRACE-85 found 0 of 184 saved KOTOR creatures carrying IsPC=1 because the player is stored somewhere else entirely. IT DISTINGUISHES WHICH MODEL A CHARACTER USES: BUILT from a log of choices, or AUTHORED from a template.

⚠ AND THE COMPANION IS THE INTERESTING CASE, RULED HERE: A COMPANION IS AUTHORED, AND THE LOG APPLIES TO IT FROM THE MOMENT IT JOINS. One character can be DECLARED AND THEN ACCUMULATE A LOG; it cannot be built by creation and then re-declared.

OPEN: faction named but not specified, FACTIONS-01 exists and was not read for this. Behaviour deferred to cluster C. ⚠ WHETHER BEASTS AND PEOPLE SHARE ONE DOCUMENT OR TWO  a merge would be cleaner and would touch a locked corpus. And companion levelling  who spends its level-up choices, player or author, is not ruled.

## PT-1274 — ATTACHMENT-01 written. ⚠ THE BEHAVIOUR ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS UNBOUND, and reactions are the one genuinely new thing

Third RECORD-GAPS-01 cluster, and checking first paid off again. GROUND-AI-01 and SPACE-AI-01 specify COMBAT DOCTRINE PER FACTION  the Sith you will not be permitted to leave, the Mandalorians an honourable one first  and ENGINE-SPEC-03 3 specifies A TOPIC SPACE for everyone nobody wrote. ⚠ BOTH DESCRIBE BEHAVIOUR AND NEITHER SAYS HOW IT REACHES A CHARACTER. The gap was never the behaviour. It was the binding.

THE HANDLE, applying PT-1268 to characters. A uuid says WHICH character; a handle says WHICH CHARACTER AN AUTHOR MEANT. Three rules, and the third is the one that matters:

    DECLARED, NOT GENERATED   a generated handle is a uuid with extra steps
    SCOPED TO ITS PACKAGE     PT-1248s boundary doing real work, and the
                              thing KOTORs flat global namespace could not do
    ⚠ REUSABLE ACROSS         the town guard is a handle; WHICH TEMPLATE
      TEMPLATES               FILLS IT CAN CHANGE BETWEEN ACTS. The author
                              binds A ROLE; the engine resolves it at spawn

⚠ AND THE THIRD RULE IS WHAT STOPS TRACE-83s COLLAPSE. KOTORs 1,589 blueprints for 1,619 placements happened partly because EVERY REFERENCE WAS TO A SPECIFIC BLUEPRINT. A handle referencing A ROLE rather than a record means replacing the character DOES NOT BREAK EVERY LINE OF DIALOGUE THAT MENTIONS THEM.

FOUR ATTACHMENT KINDS, and two of them already exist unbound: DIALOGUE per ENGINE-SPEC-03, DOCTRINE per GROUND-AI-01 and SPACE-AI-01, REACTION which is new, and SCRIPT as the escape hatch. This document supplies the FIELD; it does not restate the doctrine.

⚠ REACTIONS ARE THE ONE GENUINELY NEW THING. Dialogue answers what if I talk to them. Doctrine answers what if I fight them. NOTHING ANSWERED WHAT DO THEY DO WHEN SOMETHING HAPPENS NEAR THEM. A reaction BINDS AN EVENT KIND TO A RESPONSE and is a DECLARATION, not a script.

WHY DECLARED RATHER THAN SCRIPTED, and it is PT-1268s reasoning applied one level down: A DECLARATION CAN BE LISTED, TESTED AND SHOWN IN THE BUILDER. A script can only be read. A reaction that fires on a named event is checkable; one that fires on a scripts opinion is not.

⚠ AND IT MUST FIRE OFF THE EVENT LOG, which PLAY-STATE-01 2 already provides. A REACTION LISTENS FOR AN EVENT KIND AND DOES NOT POLL STATE  polling has no place in a turn-based game and would reintroduce exactly the continuous-time machinery PLAY-STATE-01 4 excluded.

SCRIPTS ARE THE LAST RESORT AND CARRY TWO HARD LIMITS. ⚠ PT-1268 binds absolutely: AI OUTPUT IS A PRODUCT OF THE LEDGER, NEVER AN INPUT. A script may READ state and WRITE events; A SCRIPT MAY NOT DECIDE SOMETHING THE ENGINE THEN BRANCHES ON WITHOUT THAT DECISION BEING AN EVENT, or replay breaks and PT-1272s guarantee is void. And ⚠ TRACE-85s warning is explicit: KOTORs ActionList persists A SUSPENDED SCRIPT VM, 106 KB of bytecode mid-execution, BECAUSE A REAL-TIME SAVE CAN LAND ANYWHERE. A SCRIPT THAT CAN BE SUSPENDED MID-EXECUTION IS ONE THAT MUST BE SERIALISED MID-EXECUTION. Ours run to completion within a turn or they do not run.

OPEN: the reaction event vocabulary, which should follow PLAY-STATE-01s event kinds rather than be invented separately. Doctrine selection for a character with no faction, since GROUND-AI-01 is organised by faction and a lone bounty hunter belongs to none. Whether a handle can be reassigned mid-campaign. And script language and sandbox, which is engine work rather than record work.

## PT-1275 — EMBODIMENT-01 written. ⚠ ALL FOUR RECORD-GAPS CLUSTERS COMPLETE, and an illegal state must be storable

Fourth and final cluster. ITEMS-08 already carried the slot rulings, so this collects and reconciles rather than invents  the same pattern as clusters B and C.

⚠ THE FIRST GAP WAS NOT A DESIGN QUESTION. The record stored a flat items list while PT-1252 locked an eleven-slot lattice. THAT IS A DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN A LOCKED SCREEN AND A SPEC, AND THE SCREEN IS RIGHT. Named slots, not a list.

⚠ AND THREE ITEM KINDS ITEMS-08 ALREADY ESTABLISHED THAT A FLAT LIST CANNOT EXPRESS: SLOTTED, which occupies a slot and can be swapped and sold; INTEGRAL, which OCCUPIES NO SLOT AND CANNOT BE UNEQUIPPED, SOLD OR LOOTED  droid chassis hardware; and FIXED-SLOT, which occupies a slot but cannot be removed. That is the concrete cost of the old shape rather than a stylistic complaint.

AN EMPTY SLOT IS null AND PRESENT, per CHARACTER-RECORD-01s absent-not-zeroed rule: a slot a character HAS but has not filled differs from a slot they DO NOT HAVE. A droid with no boots slot has NO boots KEY AT ALL. And STACKING LIVES ON carried, NOT ON SLOTS  a slot holds one thing; three medpacs are one carried entry with a count.

BOOTS HAS NO SOURCE PRECEDENT, per ITEMS-08 and PT-690: KOTORs baseitems masks cover implant, head, armour, hands, arms, belt and weapons AND THERE IS NO FOOT SLOT. Ours is an addition and sits with Belt as a worn item.

⚠ WIELD LEGALITY IS DERIVED, NOT STORED. EQUIPMENT-01 4c defines wield classes and ACTION-ECONOMY-01 is the authority on pairing. The record stores WHAT IS IN EACH SLOT and NOT whether the combination is legal  a stored is_valid_pairing would go stale the moment ACTION-ECONOMY-01 changed, WHICH IS OF03s MISTAKE IN A NEW PLACE.

⚠⚠ AND A RULING THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS DOCUMENT: AN ILLEGAL STATE MUST BE STORABLE. A character can be carrying a configuration they cannot legally use  picked up mid-fight, or made illegal by a rules change. The record holds it, the derivation reports it, the UI shows it. REFUSING TO STORE AN ILLEGAL STATE MEANS A RULES CHANGE CAN MAKE A SAVE UNLOADABLE, which is PT-1272s drift hazard with the safety valve removed.

EMBODIMENT SPLITS THREE WAYS: portrait, already ruled at PT-1214; appearance, A HANDLE NOT A MODEL, per ATTACHMENT-01 1, so the record never knows about file formats or rigging; and overlay, DERIVED, where UI-ASSETS-01 already flags the character model as the largest asset commitment in the project. THE RECORDS JOB IS TO SAY WHAT IS WORN; THE PRESENTATION LAYERS JOB IS TO SHOW IT.

⚠ AND A TRAP AVOIDED ON TRACE-83s EVIDENCE: KOTORs Appearance_Type runs 1 TO 546 AGAINST A 509-ROW TABLE, live overflows, all in .mod files built against a larger table than shipped. AN APPEARANCE HANDLE THAT IS AN INDEX INTO A TABLE IS A POSITION-AS-IDENTITY TRAP. Ours is a name.

OPEN AND NAMED RATHER THAN GUESSED: the droid slot map, which belongs with the chassis records in SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2 rather than here. Encumbrance, which is NOT RULED ANYWHERE and which carried assumes does not exist. Whether appearance varies by equipment or only by species. And two-slot items  the lattice implies a two-handed weapon occupies both weapon slots in a config, and nothing states it.

## TRACE-86 — STUDY batch 4, world layer. ⚠⚠ F08 SETTLED BY RETRACTION: THE .mod FILES DO NOT SHIP, THE RUNNING GAME WRITES THEM. And the journal answers what a quest conclusion is

Every IFO, ARE and GIT in both games, both global.jrl files, all 21 saved module snapshots, all 40 K1 .mod files.

⚠⚠ THE RETRACTION FIRST, BECAUSE IT INVALIDATES FINDINGS FROM TWO EARLIER BATCHES AND THE AGENT FOUND IT ITSELF. THE .mod FILES IN modules/ DO NOT SHIP. THE RUNNING GAME WRITES THEM ON LEAVING A MODULE.

The evidence is overwhelming and none of it needed a running process. Every .rim is dated to the install; all 40 .mod are from the last fortnight. ERF BuildYear is 126 against an epoch of 1900, confirmed two ways  lips/*.mod are year 103, matching the 2003 release, and patch.erf is 104 day 47, matching the Feb 2004 patch. ⚠ AND THE CONTROL IS DECISIVE: K1 HAS BEEN PLAYED HERE, FOUR SAVES, AND HAS 40 .mod. K2 HAS NEVER BEEN PLAYED AND HAS ZERO. The literal modulesave sits in both binaries  batch 1 found it and did not follow it.

⚠ WHAT THIS COSTS: BATCH 3s F25 EXPLANATION GOES WITH IT. The 82 out-of-range Appearance_Type values are REAL, but they were not a stale BioWare build  THE ENGINE WROTE THEM BACK DURING THIS PLAYTHROUGH. That is a better question and it is now open: THE ENGINE EMITTED A ROW INDEX PAST THE END OF THE TABLE IT INDEXES AND NOTHING REJECTED THE WRITE.

⚠ AND THE LESSON IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT KEEPS RELEARNING: TREATING PRESENT IN modules/ AS PART OF THE PRODUCT WAS AN UNCHECKED ASSUMPTION. Neither batch checked a timestamp or a build date, both one command away. In a game directory SHIPPED AND RUNTIME-WRITTEN FILES SIT SIDE BY SIDE AND THE FORMAT DOES NOT DISTINGUISH THEM  a written .mod carries the same Mod_IsSaveGame=0 as a shipped .rim. That is a wrong-place error in the sense METHOD-RECORD-01 names: a correctly scoped search in a directory whose contents were misclassified.

THREE TIERS OF MODULE STATE, which KOTOR gives no distinct names: SHIPPED rim and _s.rim, read-only, never written. WRITTEN .mod, produced on leaving a module, INSTALLATION-SCOPED, still template-based. And SAVED .sav, one per VISITED module, full inline records, carrying the player. Loaded versus visited is exactly the tier-three distinction  VISITING CREATES A SNAPSHOT AND A VISITED MODULE IS NEVER REBUILT FROM TIER ONE AGAIN.

⚠ UseTemplates IS THE SWITCH behind the six-versus-112 field split. Set to 1 in all 239 shipped GITs, ABSENT in all 21 saved ones. ONE FLAG CHANGES WHAT EVERY LIST BELOW IT MEANS  and the two producers disagree on how to say it, the toolset writing 1 and the engine OMITTING THE FIELD rather than writing 0.

THE COMPLETE INSTANCE TABLE CONFIRMS THE INVERSION ACROSS THE WHOLE LAYER. Creatures override NOTHING at six fields. Waypoints override five things at fourteen. ⚠ AND CameraList IS THE EXCEPTION TO EVERYTHING  NO BLUEPRINT AT ALL, defined entirely per placement, and the only place Vector and Orientation are used. That closes batch 3s scoped negative, which correctly said those types were unused BY BLUEPRINTS.

THE GEOMETRY COUPLING IS CONFIRMED AS THE WHOLE OF IT: Rooms[].RoomName is a string and nothing else in the ARE touches geometry, across all 75 fields of all 239 areas. ⚠ AND THE GENERAL FINDING IS BETTER THAN THE SPECIFIC ONE: THE WORLD LAYER IS THE MOST NAME-COUPLED LAYER IN THE GAME  rooms, areas, scripts, blueprints, modules, objects and quests all by NAME, while rules and blueprint internals are ROW INDICES. THAT IS WHY AREAS CAN BE REUSED FREELY AND RULES CANNOT BE SCOPED.

⚠⚠ AND THE JOURNAL, WHICH IS WHAT PT-1267 NEEDED. Four properties:

    QUESTS ARE NAME-ADDRESSED by Tag, used by script, save and UI alike, and
    NEARLY UNIQUE IN KOTOR. A tag survives renumbering; an index does not.

    A QUESTS ENTIRE LIVE STATE IS ONE INTEGER  the stage id  plus a
    timestamp. No sub-objectives, no flag set.

    ⚠ STAGE IDS ARE AUTHORED, SPARSE AND NON-MONOTONIC, 1-150 in K1 and
    1-100 in K2, NOT SORTED WITHIN A QUEST IN EITHER GAME. So they are
    LABELS, NOT ORDINALS  YOU CANNOT COMPARE TWO STATES TO SEE WHICH IS
    FURTHER ALONG.

    ⚠⚠ COMPLETE IS NOT A STATE. End is set on MULTIPLE STAGES in 47 of 101
    K1 quests and 63 of 117 K2 quests, UP TO NINE ON ONE. A BOOLEAN DID THEY
    FINISH IT HIDES WHICH ENDING HAPPENED. THE STAGE ID IS WHAT IS WORTH
    CARRYING.

AND NOTHING LINKS A MODULE TO A QUEST  the only connection is a script naming a tag in a game-global file.

K1 vs K2: the clearest shift is transitions, K1 DOOR-LED at 114 doors to 40 triggers, K2 TRIGGER-LED at 39 to 85. IFO is byte-for-byte the same 43 fields in both games.

NOT ESTABLISHED AND SAID SO: whether tier 2 or tier 3 wins on load. LinkedToFlags semantics. PlotIndex matches no table found.
