## PT-1971 -- FOUR ITEMS BUILT, INCLUDING A GENUINELY SERIOUS FOUNDATIONAL MATH BUG (DART'S TRUNCATING DIVISION USED WHERE d20's FLOORING DIVISION WAS REQUIRED, SILENTLY MISCALCULATING EVERY ODD ABILITY SCORE BELOW 10). TERMINAL PANEL RESOLVED TO TWO REAL, DISTINCT DEFECTS. EXTRACTION GAP CORRECTLY NAMED AND CORRECTLY NOT RUSHED

[entry].at approved -- fixed in three of four places the first time, correctly found and fixed the fourth (the save condition only checking area, not arrival, meaning changing arrival alone silently saved nothing) rather than declaring the job done at three.

The DC ladder fix is approved in full: keeping the ladder as the labelled default while correctly recognising a free value simply has no tier to assign, rather than inventing an approximate one, is precise. Refusing a malformed entry outright rather than defaulting to zero, on the correct reasoning that zero would be worse (a lock nobody could ever fail), and extending the fix to every ladder-using DC rather than only locks, is thorough rather than narrowly scoped to the reported case.

⚠⚠ THE TERMINAL PANEL FINDING VALIDATES THE EARLIER CAUTION EXACTLY: two genuinely separate defects, not one. The text-wrap overflow (A) is a good, satisfying root cause -- the layout had already reserved the correct scrollbar space since the geometry was first lifted, meaning the fix space existed before the question was even asked, it simply was not connected to what needed it. The dual-grid scaling conflation (B) is the more serious find -- two genuinely different design grids (the app's own 340-wide grid and the terminal's own lifted 640x480 source grid) sharing one scale factor that was only ever correct for one of them, producing a panel roughly 40% too large and silently clipped rather than crashing. Correctly isolated as two problems rather than one blurred explanation, and correctly confirming that flagging the original candidate mechanism as unconfirmed rather than asserted was the right call -- the real answer was more complex than any single guess would have been.

⚠⚠ WORTH NAMING DIRECTLY AS THE MOST SERIOUS FIND IN THIS REPORT: the ability modifier calculation itself was wrong, using Dart's truncating integer division where d20's own flooring rule is required -- these disagree specifically on negative results, so every odd ability score below ten was calculated one point too generous (9 giving 0 instead of the correct -1). Correctly recognized as not a rare edge case -- while pure point-buy rarely lands on an odd sub-10 score, an ordinary species penalty makes it common, with the concrete example (an 11 reduced by -2 landing exactly on 9) showing precisely how. This has been silently shaving vitality, initiative and attack for every affected character since the code was written, not a newly-introduced regression -- a genuinely significant, foundational correctness fix.

Good, disciplined methodology reading the actual class-table data directly rather than reverse-engineering the clean d20 formula it mostly follows, specifically because doing the latter would have silently overwritten the Engineer's own deliberate, already-ruled exception (PT-96) -- recognizing that a pattern holding for nineteen of twenty classes is not the same as it being safe to implement as a universal rule. Good, precise Defence verification distinguishing where the cap actually applies (the Dexterity contribution, not the total) and testing for genuine equality across two very different builds reaching the same final number, a stronger check than verifying each independently.

The organic-armour extraction gap is correctly diagnosed (extraction missing, not a rules gap, EQUIPMENT-01's own table already exists) and correctly not acted on unilaterally -- adding shelf rows without the matching extraction is precisely the drift check_shelf.py exists to catch, and citing that directly rather than taking a shortcut around it is exactly right.

Correctly, appropriately not rushing the retry reversal into this batch -- "whenever it fits" was never meant as licence to squeeze a real behavioural reversal in behind two urgent items, and sending the lock/terminal change together with the mine proposal as one coherent piece is the right call.

Everything approved, no corrections needed. Continue on the character screen and the extraction pass whenever it fits your own sequencing.

A separate, required recover field would be more expressive but has no grounding for what its actual values should be -- not worth the cost for expressiveness nothing currently needs.

⚠⚠ RULED ON B, A SET MINE'S OWN NUMBERS: OPTION C, DERIVED FRESH FROM THE SETTER'S OWN DEMOLITIONS SKILL AT THE MOMENT OF PLACEMENT. This is the one option that makes a highly skilled character's own placed mines meaningfully more dangerous and harder to detect than a novice's -- both options A and B make a set mine's danger purely a function of its origin, completely divorced from who is actually setting it down, which does not hold up thematically or mechanically: a genuine expert should be able to hide a trap better than an amateur, using the same physical mine. This is also the option directly grounded in section 5.2's own already-established principle (the skill governs grade and radius) extended one step further, rather than requiring something invented from nothing. Build it this way -- setMinesIn correctly returning the square and the item rather than a constructed Hazard was the right call, and deriving the numbers from the setter's skill at the point of use is the natural next step from there.

disarm confirmed correctly unchanged and already correct under the reversal -- its own failure was always the safer one, and retry now applies to it by the same ruling that freed the locks.

GO AHEAD, both numbers ruled, nothing left unresolved in this slice.

## PT-1990 -- A GENUINELY CATASTROPHIC SILENT DATA-LOSS RISK FOUND AND CLOSED: RE-RUNNING equipment.json's EXTRACTOR WOULD HAVE DELETED NINE REAL ROWS (ALL ARMOUR, THE SUPPLY ECONOMY, EVERY CARRIED OBJECT) WITH BOTH EXISTING CHECKS BLIND TO IT. HONEST CORRECTION TO CODER'S OWN PRIOR DIAGNOSIS. RULED ON ALL THREE OPPOSED-CHECK QUESTIONS AND THE INTERRUPT PROPOSAL

⚠⚠ WORTH ADDRESSING DIRECTLY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: this is one of the most significant findings in this entire session. Re-running equipment.json's own documented extractor would have silently deleted six armour classes, spikes, parts, and the entire object base type -- Defence for every armoured organic, the whole supply economy, and every carried narrative item, gone without a word, demonstrated by actually happening twice during the investigation. Both existing checks were genuinely blind to it by construction: one compares an extract against an unchanged source, the other compares a shelf against an extract, and a regeneration that corrupts the extract would make both comparisons agree with each other while both were simultaneously wrong. "The only thing standing between us and that loss was nobody happening to re-run one extractor" is not an overstatement.

⚠⚠ THE SELF-CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS IS EXACTLY THE RIGHT INSTINCT, WORTH NAMING DIRECTLY: tracing the real cause properly before building, rather than implementing the already-approved fix on faith, found that hashing the generator -- the specific direction already approved -- would NOT have caught the actual defect that prompted the whole investigation, since the real fault was a hand-edit that updated content and its own recorded fingerprint together, leaving nothing to disagree with. Saying plainly that an already-approved direction would not have worked, rather than building it anyway because it was already blessed, is real intellectual honesty. The actual fix (running each generator and comparing bytes directly, subsuming every possible staleness cause in one check) is more robust than what was originally proposed, and confirming it churns nothing (17 of 24 extracts already rebuild identically) closes the loop properly.

APPROVED: everything built for item 3. The five extracts with no runnable generator correctly named individually rather than silently skipped -- "a derived file nobody can regenerate is one nobody can check" is exactly right. The optional destination argument, preventing a verification run from destructively overwriting the very file under examination, is good, necessary defensive design.

RULED ON FIXING THE EXTRACTOR ITSELF: approved as real work, not urgent now that the actual danger is safely contained behind a working check. The immediate catastrophic risk is closed; properly teaching extract_equipment.py to read section 5.1's armour table and section 5.2's supplies, and handling object separately given its ruled source is the catalogue rather than EQUIPMENT-01, is real, valuable follow-up work rather than an emergency. Sequence it whenever it fits.

════════════════════════════════════════════════

RULED ON PROPOSAL A, OPPOSED CHECKS, ALL THREE QUESTIONS:

1. Wire the runtime first, exactly as proposed -- closing a live defect (opposed already silently resolving as a flat DC-10 check) before exposing the option to authors is the correct order, avoiding building a wizard question that would let people author more broken content on an already-broken foundation.

2. The line's speaker rolls back, as proposed. Grounding this in PT-1607's already-established rule (the speaker is the real placement walked into) means there is always a genuine creature with genuine ranks, no new authoring burden, and nothing that can dangle. Thread the speaker creature into DialogueView as needed.

3. A NAMED OPPOSING SKILL, OPTIONAL, DEFAULTING TO THE SAME SKILL ON BOTH SIDES. This matches real d20 convention more closely than a same-skill-only model -- most genuine opposed checks pit different skills against each other (deception against insight, stealth against perception), and an optional field defaulting to the simpler same-skill case when unspecified gives authors the expressive option without forcing complexity on every use.

4. THE OLD gatesNotAsked EXCLUSION IS OVERTURNED. Correct reasoning: that comment's implicit concern was presumably an author picking a nonsensical or dangling opponent, and deriving the opponent automatically from the speaker eliminates exactly that risk. The excuse does not survive under the new design -- opposed should be wizard-authorable. Update the comment to state why the exclusion no longer applies rather than simply deleting it silently.

RULED ON PROPOSAL B, INTERRUPT: approved exactly as proposed, including not surfacing the reaction cost to the author. The cost is a mechanical consequence of the choice to interrupt, not itself an authoring decision -- correctly distinguished, and correct instinct checking rather than assuming this was obvious.

GO AHEAD on both proposals. Continue to item 4 (reading the 54 dual-game prose rows) then item 1 (TARGETING-01) as planned.

⚠⚠ THE BOARD FIX IS ALSO EXCELLENT, AND THE SELF-CAUGHT FIRST GUARD IS WORTH NAMING: correctly root-causing the resize to a shared layout column rather than an isolated overlay, and fixing it by reusing an already-proven pattern from the play screen itself rather than inventing something new, is good, disciplined engineering. Honestly catching that the first attempted regression guard didn't actually replicate the real shipped structure and therefore proved nothing, then fixing the guard to test the actual shipped code, is exactly the standard this project has run on all session -- a check that cannot fail is worth the same scrutiny whether it's freshly written or appears to be working. Good instinct delivering a stale reload directly in the test rather than writing a sleep-based race test, correctly recognizing that a timing-dependent test carries the same fragility as the defect it's meant to catch.

RULED ON requires: SKIP WRITING ONLY WHEN THE KEY WAS ALREADY ABSENT, exactly as proposed. This correctly preserves the real semantic distinction -- an author deliberately clearing existing entries needs that clearing to actually persist as a real empty list, while a field nobody ever touched should not have an unused section artificially injected into a fresh file. Writing the guard before believing the wiring, having it fail, and reverting known-broken work rather than leaving it in an unproven state or shipping a guess, is exactly the discipline this entire session has been building toward -- demonstrated here under real pressure, after real, honest effort, rather than as an abstract principle. The precise articulation -- a full suite passing is evidence of not breaking anything, which is categorically different from evidence of the new capability actually working, and only a guard aimed specifically at the new behaviour can tell the two apart -- is one of the clearest, most useful statements of this session's whole running theme, worth keeping as its own reference point going forward whenever a broad green suite might otherwise be mistaken for proof of a specific new claim.

Correctly, honestly stopping the diagnosis at the point of good judgement rather than continuing to guess -- tracing the failure to roughly where it lives, noting the genuine contradiction with a neighbouring test using the identical harness, and recognizing that further guessing in the same sitting would cost more than the question was currently worth -- is mature pacing, not giving up. Returning to it with fresh attention rather than forcing a resolution under diminishing returns is the right call.

Correctly naming this as the fourth time this session a targeted test has disagreed with something that otherwise looked finished is continued, valuable tracking of exactly why this discipline keeps earning its cost -- each instance reinforces the same lesson from a different angle rather than becoming routine and unremarked.

The status is left honestly precise rather than rounded up: slices 1 and 1b fully live, slice 2 correctly described as live in the engine and unfed in play, with the specific, narrow, bounded question (why enemyTurn exits early on this one path against contrary evidence twenty lines away) named clearly as the next thing to resolve, not a vague or open-ended gap.

## PT-2023 -- DAMAGE-KIND RESISTANCE CHAIN SCOPED WELL, THREE REAL QUESTIONS ANSWERED. LIGHTSABERS RULED energy. physical MAPS TO piercing, NOT A NEW KIND. RESISTANCES RULED TO LIVE ON THE BASE TYPE, MATCHING THE ARMOUR-CLASS PRECEDENT. TRAINING LIGHTSABER DATA DEFECT CONFIRMED REAL, FIX BEFORE THE CHAIN GOES LIVE

Good, thorough scoping -- confirming the resistance data is real and substantial (150 effects across 83 items, ten of eleven kinds covered) before treating this as worth building, and correctly identifying that link 2 alone would be worthless (a kind reaching applyDamage with nothing to resist it changes no number, the exact typed-bonus shape already sitting inert) is precisely the right instinct not to add a second inert layer on top of the first.

RULED ON QUESTION 1: LIGHTSABERS DEAL energy. This is well-grounded on two independent lines of evidence pointing the same direction -- it matches the franchise's own consistent, canonical treatment of a lightsaber blade as literally energy/plasma, and it is also the one place in the corpus that states a lightsaber's damage type at all, even though it sits in the wrong cell. Correctly not treating that misplaced cell as authoritative on its own, but it is real corroborating evidence rather than nothing, and combined with the broader canon it is decisive enough to rule on.

RULED ON QUESTION 2: physical MAPS TO piercing, IT DOES NOT BECOME A TWELFTH KIND. A disruptor-class weapon is a projectile/bolt weapon in the source material, which maps naturally onto piercing rather than bludgeoning or slashing. The more important reason: adding physical as its own kind, when nothing in the real 150 resist effects covers a kind by that name, would create a damage type that can never be resisted by anything that currently exists -- a dead kind by construction. Mapping onto an existing, already-covered kind is the functional choice, not merely the tidier one.

CONFIRMED REAL, FIX BEFORE THE CHAIN GOES LIVE: the Training Lightsaber row sitting in the wrong table's shape. Correctly diagnosed as the same family as the phantom encounter.began -- a row whose actual shape disagrees with the table it lives in, currently harmless only because nothing reads the affected column yet. This must be corrected as part of this work, not left for later, since the whole point of the chain being built is to make that column start mattering.

⚠⚠ RULED ON LINK 3: RESISTANCES LIVE ON THE BASE TYPE BY DEFAULT, MIRRORING THE ARMOUR-CLASS PRECEDENT DIRECTLY. Resistance to a damage kind is fundamentally a property of what an armour is made of or how it's constructed, not something that should vary wildly per individually authored instance -- the same reasoning already applied successfully when armour class itself was resolved onto the base type rather than requiring every item to restate it. An item-level override can exist later if real evidence ever shows two items sharing one base type genuinely needing different resistances, following the same override pattern already built for damage -- but default to the base type, don't build the override first for a case nothing currently demonstrates.

## PT-2024 -- VERIFIED AGAINST THE REAL GAMES, AS OWNER REQUESTED. LIGHTSABER = energy DECISIVELY CONFIRMED, MULTIPLE INDEPENDENT SOURCES AGREE. DISRUPTOR RULING REVISED: NOT A SINGLE PHYSICAL SUB-KIND, THE REAL SOURCE DATA SHOWS A COMBINED BLUDGEONING+PIERCING+SLASHING BITMASK

Owner asked to verify both open damage-kind questions against the real games rather than rely on inference alone -- checked directly.

LIGHTSABER: CONFIRMED, energy, NO LONGER JUST WELL-GROUNDED BUT DECISIVE. StrategyWiki's own lightsaber tables state "Damage: Energy" for every lightsaber type without exception, and independent player sourcing states it in as many words: "lightsaber damage in general is energy damage." The earlier ruling stands, now on much firmer footing than the single misplaced data point it was originally grounded in.

⚠⚠ DISRUPTOR RULING REVISED: NOT piercing ALONE. The real source data (confirmed via the actual damage-flag bitmask, cross-checked against how Mandalorian Shields and single-type resistance items interact with it in practice) shows disruptor damage is a COMBINED bludgeoning+piercing+slashing value (flag 7 = 1+2+4), not a single physical sub-kind. In practice this means it is stopped by any ONE of the three physical resistances -- a shield resisting all three blocks it, and an item resisting only slashing specifically still reduces it. This is meaningfully different from a pure piercing classification, which a bludgeoning- or slashing-only resistance would not touch at all. The earlier single-kind mapping was a reasonable guess but is now confirmed wrong in a real, specific way -- disruptors need to be treated as vulnerable to any of the three physical kinds, not assigned to just one of them.

This needs Coder's read on how to express "resisted by any of three kinds" given the actual grammar and resistance model being built -- routed as an update to the in-progress damage-kind chain work rather than a full restart, since the rest of the scoping and the other two rulings (lightsaber energy, resistances on the base type) stand unchanged.

⚠⚠ THIS IS ONE OF THE MOST SIGNIFICANT FINDINGS IN THIS ENTIRE SESSION, WORTH ADDRESSING DIRECTLY AND AT LENGTH. The character sheet has correctly computed and displayed EQUIPMENT-01 section 5's own rule since PT-1957; the actual combat resolution an attack roll is compared against never carried an armour term or a cap at all. Wearing armour has never once made anyone -- the player or any creature -- harder to hit, for the entire time armour has existed in this project. Precisely traced to its exact cause (armourBonus reaching exactly one call site in the whole app, the sheet, never the fight) rather than patched blind, and correctly, precisely recognized as PT-1468's own shape -- two answers to one question -- discovered on Defence itself, a place neither of us had thought to specifically check.

Good, honest framing of how this surfaced: bundling Defence into slice (c) because it appeared to be the same gap as creature armour going unread was correct reasoning on its own terms, and it also happened to surface something genuinely separate that neither of us knew was there. That is worth naming plainly rather than claiming the bundling decision was prescient about a defect it was never actually aimed at.

Correctly, proactively flagging that this changes the balance of every existing fight, and that Tester should expect and recognize this as the rule finally applying rather than a new bug, is exactly the right way to hand off a change with real, felt consequences -- silence here would have made a genuine, deliberate correction look like an unexplained regression.

Good, disciplined architecture avoiding restating the Dexterity cap a second time, correctly recognizing that would reintroduce the exact two-copies shape this fix exists to remove into the very code removing it. Good, efficient unification building both the resistance map and the Defence calculation from one shared armour read rather than duplicating it.

⚠⚠ THE TWO GUARD FINDINGS ARE BOTH GENUINELY VALUABLE. The slice-(b) fixture's armour class being harmless until armour started mattering, then correctly caught by that same group's own existing controls, is a satisfying, concrete validation that well-written guards keep earning their cost across time, not just at the moment they're written -- "the controls did exactly the job they were written for, one slice after they were written" is worth remembering as a case where testing discipline paid off on a delay.

The second finding is the more subtle and more valuable one: a mutation to the screen's own armour map killing no tests, not because nothing was checking armour at all, but because an adjacent, superficially similar group (resistance) created the appearance of coverage for a genuinely distinct, uncovered claim (Defence). "A green suite is not proof of a new claim, and here the missing claim was invisible because a neighbouring claim looked so similar" is a real, distinct variant of this session's recurring lesson -- not merely that passing tests don't prove a new thing works, but that a nearby test asking a related-looking question can actively obscure the fact that the actual question was never asked at all. Worth watching for specifically: two claims that look like the same kind of thing are not the same claim.

Good, sophisticated verification asserting the sheet's route and the fight's route are equal to each other rather than each pinned to a literal -- correctly reasoning that two independently-pinned values could theoretically both drift together and still agree, while asserting mutual equality catches exactly the disagreement this whole fix was about.

## PT-2039 -- OWNER RECONSIDERATION, HOLDING SLICE (a): PER-ROUND POISON DAMAGE SHOULD BE ROLLED, NOT A FLAT PORTED NUMBER -- THIS IS A TABLETOP GAME, AND A FIXED PER-TICK VALUE IS A VIDEO-GAME CONVENTION

Owner raised a genuine, important reconsideration before the go-ahead was sent: the proposed per-round poison values (8 vitality/round for Naga Sadow's blade, etc.) are flat, fixed numbers ported directly from the video game's own raw numeric data. In real tabletop, d20-style games, damage-over-time effects are conventionally expressed as a rolled die, not a fixed amount, specifically to preserve the same rollable tension and variance every tick that a flat number removes entirely. This was the owner's own original intent when establishing the broader poison framework -- finding the genuine tabletop equivalent of the video game's mechanic, not simply porting its numbers as-is.

Held rather than approved as originally proposed. Routed back to Coder: check whether this project already has an established convention for converting a flat video-game value into a dice expression (any other damage-over-time or variable-damage effect already built this way), and if so follow it; if not, propose a sensible conversion for the poison values specifically (something that averages close to the already-ported totals while introducing real dice variance) rather than have a conversion formula invented from outside the data.

## PT-2040 -- DICE CONVERSION PROPOSAL APPROVED IN FULL. RULED: THE MEAN-EXACT 2d4+1/2d6+1/2d8+1 LADDER, APPLIED TO ALL TEN EXISTING POISON EFFECTS INCLUDING ALREADY-SHIPPING CONTENT, WITH KYBER DART CORRECTLY LEFT FLAT AS THE ONE NAMED EXCEPTION

⚠⚠ WORTH RECOGNIZING DIRECTLY: finding that this ladder already exists across nine other shipping effects, independently confirming the same three numbers by a completely different derivation route, and correctly recognizing that any ruling here has to cover all ten or recreate the exact same-effect-different-behaviour-by-delivery-method inconsistency this session has repeatedly guarded against, is exactly the right scope check before building anything. The convention search is precise and correctly resists inventing a formula -- finding that both real precedents (Stun Baton, the beast poison dice) share one underlying principle, find a real die in a real source rather than computing one, and correctly falling back to the next most specific stated rule (die size scales, dice count does not) when no directly-matching precedent exists for poison specifically, rather than picking an arbitrary shape.

RULED: THE MEAN-EXACT LADDER, 2d4+1 / 2d6+1 / 2d8+1. Preserving the exact already-verified mean, rather than the structurally tidier but 17%-inflated one-die-per-tick alternative, is the right priority -- the entire value of the deep forensic tracing that led here was fidelity to the real, ported numbers, and trading that fidelity for a nicer metaphor would undercut the reason this was worth doing carefully in the first place. Good, correct reasoning on two dice over one specifically to cluster results around the ported mean and make the extremes rare across a five-round tick, rather than a flat, uniform single-die spread.

RULED: APPLIES TO ALL TEN, INCLUDING THE NINE ALREADY SHIPPING. Correct call not to fold this in silently as an afterthought, but the actual decision is yes -- the same poison should behave the same way regardless of whether it arrives by blade, mine, or grenade, and rolling is meant to be a property of the poison mechanism itself, not of any one specific delivery method. The gas mines and poison grenades should start rolling alongside the blade.

RULED: KYBER DART STAYS FLAT AT 25, NAMED AS THE ONE EXCEPTION IN THE EXTRACT. Correct instinct not forcing an ugly, awkward formula onto the one value the rule genuinely doesn't fit cleanly, purely for uniformity's own sake -- an honestly-named exception is better than a contorted fit, consistent with how every other genuine outlier has been handled throughout this whole investigation.

## PT-2043 -- TEST 087: A SEVERE FINDING -- THE ENTIRE PT-2029 CHAIN WORKS CREATURE-TO-CREATURE, BUT NONE OF IT REACHES THE PLAYER'S OWN BLOW OR THE PLAYER'S OWN DEFENCE. THE PLAYER CANNOT EVEN BE ARMOURED. PRECISELY TRACED TO play_screen.dart's CALL SITE NEVER PASSING resists OR armourBonus, EXACTLY THE PARAMETER strike's OWN DOCSTRING SAYS EXISTS FOR THIS REASON

⚠⚠ THIS IS A SEVERE, WELL-DIAGNOSED FINDING, WORTH NAMING PLAINLY. All four creature-versus-creature claims confirmed with real, controlled, felt measurement (armour genuinely changing hit outcomes, a mask granting resistance with correctly zero Defence contribution, per-part reduction correctly applied rather than blocking or ignoring the whole blow, a worn weapon correctly excluded from contributing resistance). But none of it reaches the player at all -- measured directly, same room, same items, player swinging: an armour-class-9 creature still needs only 13, and 99 points of fire resistance on a target removes exactly 0 damage from the player's own hits.

The root cause is precisely traced rather than merely observed: play_screen.dart's own combat call site never passes resists or armourBonus to strike at all, so the shared resolver's own defaults silently win. Correctly quoting strike's own docstring, which explicitly states resists exists specifically because both sides come through here, and that a reduction applied in only one side would be the twelfth instance of exactly this defect shape -- the parameter was built for this exact case, and the one call site that matters most simply never uses it.

Even more foundational: the player currently cannot be armoured at all. Building a separate ignores-resistance concept would be inventing machinery for something the existing architecture already expresses correctly once the right classification is applied. Treat them as untyped.

## PT-2120 -- THE ITEM-PROPERTY FORMAT QUESTION STARTS NOW. SCOPE IT WHOLE BEFORE DESIGNING ANY OF IT, THEN BUILD ONE CATEGORY -- ARMOR -- FIRST

RULING. This is the queue's biggest open item, ruled to start now that the sweep above closed clean. It is a real design decision, not an extraction, so it opens in stages rather than as a single slice.

**Stage one -- the inventory.** Before any format is designed, build a full, real accounting of every stat or property an item in this corpus can carry -- not just the four already-ruled ones waiting on a home (Enhancement's attack half, AttackBonus, Massive Criticals, Keen), but everything: every property kind that appears anywhere across weapons, armor, and the slot items already built out for the palette. Read it from the real source documents and the real extracted data the same way every other inventory in this project has been built -- do not reason from memory of what an item "probably" carries. This is a scope map, not a design. It tells us the size and shape of what stage two has to hold; it does not yet decide how.

**Stage two -- divide by category.** Once the inventory is real and whole, split it by item type -- weapons, armor, and the various slot categories built out during the palette work each likely need a different shape of answer, since a weapon's properties and an armor's properties are not the same kind of thing wearing different names.

**Stage three -- one category, first: armor.** Of all the categories, build armor's answer first. Do not start on weapons' 300-plus waiting rows yet, even though they are the more visible backlog -- armor is smaller, more self-contained, and will surface the real shape of the format decision (what a blueprint can state beyond a flat number, how a property attaches, how the engine reads it) without the weight of Enhancement/AttackBonus/Massive Criticals/Keen all landing on the first attempt at once.

**Before designing armor's format, look at how it has actually been solved twice already.** Both KOTOR games and Neverwinter Nights modelled armor properties as real, shipped design -- go read how each one actually did it before inventing a third scheme. This project has leaned on both sources before exactly this way: NWN and KOTOR terminology were deliberately blended for the poison severity ladder when KOTOR's own naming ran short, and the base-item taxonomy was built from neither game's incompatible tree alone. The same discipline applies here -- the question is not "what format should we invent" until it is first "what format did the real games already use, and does either answer it outright." If the two disagree, that disagreement is itself a finding to bring back, not something to resolve by picking one silently.

This displaces nothing else on the queue -- the 141 upgrade rows, the 16 alignment terms, shields, chargen descriptions, the other OnHit families, the two unclaimed armour base rows, and the five hand-placed endar-spire blueprints all remain correctly parked, none urgent.

## PT-2121 -- STAGES 1 THROUGH 3 APPROVED CLEAN. STAGE 4's KOTOR/NWN DISAGREEMENT RULED: ARMOUR STATES ITS RUNG, KOTOR'S NUMBERS ARE AUTHORITATIVE, NO CHECK PENALTY EXISTS IN OUR RULES, ARCANE FAILURE IS OUT OF SCOPE ENTIRELY

**Stages 1-3 approved in full.** The vocabulary is real and sourced from the actual 2DA data rather than reasoned from memory, the category split comes from the games' own `itemprops.2da` matrix rather than authored judgement, and the confirmation that none of the four still-waiting weapon properties touch armour at all is genuinely useful -- it means armour's work can proceed without waiting on or interacting with the weapon side's open question.

⚠⚠ THE STRREF-VS-LABEL JOIN DEFECT IS THE SAME RECURRING SHAPE NAMED SEVERAL TIMES THIS SESSION: A WRONG JOIN PRODUCING A RESULT THAT LOOKS LIKE AN ANSWER RATHER THAN FAILING LOUDLY. Losing 55 of 60 rows silently and printing a table where `Damage` reads as not-allowed on weapons -- plausible enough on its face to almost pass, wrong enough on inspection to catch -- is exactly the `only`-counter and damage-term-census shape again. Caught the same way those were: the result was absurd, not the code. Good instinct to check by matching join keys rather than trusting a label that happened to look right.

═══ THE RULING, STAGE 4

**Armour states its rung. It does not derive it.** KOTOR's shape -- `baseac`, `dexbonus`, `accheck`, `armorcheckpen` carried directly on the item, one settled value per armour class -- is the one to build. NWN's alternative depends on which modelled chest part is equipped, which is an answer to a rendering question we do not have; nothing in this project derives a stat from which 3D part a character happens to be wearing, and a format built to support that lookup would be solving a problem that does not exist here. KOTOR's shape also matches how every other property in this corpus already works -- a blueprint states its own numbers -- so this is not a new precedent, it is the existing one applied to the one place it had a real alternative on offer.

**KOTOR's numbers are authoritative, including the sum-of-nine.** This is our game. `§5.1`'s "AC plus max Dex is always nine" is now confirmed as a fact about KOTOR specifically rather than a universal armour law -- which does not weaken it. It is still the real, correct rule for the game this ruleset is built on, and NWN not sharing it is NWN describing a different game, not a correction to ours.

**No check penalty exists in our rules.** KOTOR ships the column and puts zero in it on every single row -- the mechanic is present in shape only, never in effect, anywhere in the real source data. Source discipline says build what is real, not what a column's existence implies could theoretically be built; the real answer here is that our primary source does not use this mechanic at all. This is not a deferral pending future work the way the alignment terms or ability-damage poisons are -- there is nothing to defer. It is ruled out of armour's format. If a real design reason to add a check-penalty mechanic surfaces later, that would be a deliberate new addition made on its own merits, not something pulled in by default because NWN happens to have a column for it.

**Arcane spell failure is out of scope entirely, not deferred.** It answers a problem -- gear interfering with arcane spellcasting -- that this game does not have. Force powers are not modelled as D&D-style arcane spellcasting with a somatic-interference mechanic, and nothing about this project's design gives that column a home to eventually move into. Leave it off the vocabulary going forward the same way a genuinely inapplicable NWN mechanic should be treated: noted as found, not carried as unbuilt.

Between `Armor` (164 uses) and `DEXBonusMax` (5 uses), this ruling resolves the two AC-ladder properties. The other seventeen already-used armour properties -- `UseLimitationRacial`, `DamageResist`, `Ability`, `DamageImmunity`, `Use_Limitation_Feat`, `Immunity`, `UseLimitationAlignmentGroup`, `Regeneration_Force_Points`, `Skill`, `UseLimitationPC`, `ImprovedSavingThrowsSpecific`, `BonusFeats`, `DecreaseAC`, `Regeneration`, `DecreaseAbilityScore`, `Disguise`, `UseLimitationGender` -- still need their own pass. Proceed through those now that the ladder question is settled; several likely have real precedent already in how this project built damage-kind resistance and immunity for the weapon side, so check there before designing armour's version from scratch. If any of the seventeen turn up a second real cross-game disagreement, bring it back the same way -- this was not assumed to be the only one, and it should not be treated as though it were.

Nothing else on the queue is displaced. Proceed to armour's remaining properties.

## PT-2122 -- THREE OF THE SEVENTEEN ARE ALREADY EXTRACTED, THE WORK IS A READER NOT A PARSER. DAMAGEIMMUNITY RULED PERCENT-ONLY, NO ERA CLAMPING NEEDED, AND THE SHIPPED "DR" FIGURE IS RULED INVALID. GATES SPLIT FROM EFFECTS. ABILITY AND BONUSFEATS JOIN THE DEFERRED-ON-ARCHITECTURE LIST

Measurement approved in full, and the framing against `PT-2090` in reverse is exactly right -- a fact sitting in already-extracted data with nothing reading it is the same shape of gap as a fact sitting in prose with nothing reading it, just on the other side of the extraction line. Confirming the count match (`resist` 150 against `DamageResist`'s own 150, `ability` 399 against `Ability`'s 48-on-armour slice, `regenerate` 40 against `Regeneration` plus `Regeneration_Force_Points`) before trusting the identification is the right discipline -- it is a real join check, not a label match, and this session has had enough of the other kind to know the difference matters.

═══ RULING -- DAMAGEIMMUNITY

**Percent-only. No points conversion, ever, for this property.** The source carries a percentage and nothing else; a format that also carries a computed `DR` figure would be stating something the source never said.

**No era clamping.** This was flagged as a possible `§4b` question and it is worth having asked, but on inspection it isn't one -- `§4b` governs what to do when two games disagree about the *same* item's value, which is not what is happening here. K2 simply authored more rungs on a shared percentage scale than K1 did; nothing about a 15% item conflicts with anything K1 states, because K1 never produced a 15% item to conflict with. Read every item's own real percentage, from its own real source, regardless of which game it belongs to. A K1 item will only ever show one of the seven K1 rungs because that is genuinely all K1's data contains -- no mapping, no snapping, no computed adjustment. This is a passthrough, not a conversion.

**The shipped `DR N` figure is ruled invalid.** `percent divided by five, with zero exceptions across 103 instances` is not a coincidence, it is someone's unruled arithmetic sitting in `ITEMS-01` long enough to look authoritative. Good, thorough diligence checking `ITEMS-01` through `09` and the rulings themselves before concluding nothing backs it. When the DamageImmunity reader is actually built, `ITEMS-01`'s rendering gets corrected to state the real percentage alone -- this does not need to happen today, but it is now a known, named defect rather than a live question, and it should not get carried forward into the new format by habit just because it has always been there.

═══ RULING -- GATES ARE A SEPARATE CHANNEL FROM EFFECTS

Correct instinct, and correct to stop and ask rather than fold `UseLimitationRacial`/`Use_Limitation_Feat`/`UseLimitationAlignmentGroup`/`UseLimitationPC`/`UseLimitationGender` into the same list as `DamageResist` and `Ability` by default. "Who may wear this" and "what does wearing this do" are answered at different moments -- one at the equip check, one on the character afterward -- and a format that mixes them would make an eligibility rule read like a stat bonus. These five get their own channel, built separately from the effect properties, once effects' own shape is further along.

⚠ Before that channel is designed, confirm what `(Human) 0` on every single `UseLimitationRacial` row actually means against the real cost table -- whether it is a genuine active restriction that happens to be uniform across our corpus, or a structurally-present but practically-inert default that never actually gates anything. This is worth knowing before designing a channel for the largest single block on armour's list (162 of 470 instances) is worth knowing before it's built, not after.

═══ WHAT PROCEEDS NOW, UNBLOCKED

Build armour's reader for `DamageResist` and for `Regeneration` + `Regeneration_Force_Points`. The data is already extracted, the vocabulary already exists, this is connection work, not design work -- proceed on it directly.

═══ WHAT IS DEFERRED, NOT DESIGNED

**`Ability` joins the ability-damage poison deferral from `PT-2038`.** Same wall exactly -- an armour granting +1 to a score needs a score to modify, and `Combatant` does not carry real ability scores yet. Do not build a reader for this one; it is correctly identified and correctly has nowhere to go yet.

**`BonusFeats` is the same shape of wall, once removed.** The feats exist; the channel that lets an item grant one to a wearer does not. Queue it alongside `Ability` rather than inventing a grant mechanism as a side effect of armour's format -- that is its own piece of architecture and deserves its own ruling when it comes up, not one improvised here.

`DecreaseAC` and `DecreaseAbilityScore` are simple negative rungs of `Armor` and `Ability` respectively once those have real shape -- `DecreaseAC` can follow `Armor`'s format directly; `DecreaseAbilityScore` inherits `Ability`'s same wall and waits with it.

`Immunity` (flag-only, three real kinds), `ImprovedSavingThrowsSpecific`, `Skill` (check the existing species skill-bonus channel before inventing one), and `Disguise` (cosmetic, no mechanical hook at all, lowest priority) remain correctly queued -- none need a decision today, and none are blocked on anything, they simply have not been reached yet.

Nothing else on the standing queue is displaced.

## PT-2123 -- CORRECTION TO PT-2122. THE OWNER CAUGHT IT: DAMAGEIMMUNITY WAS NOT AN OPEN QUESTION. `PT-475`/`PT-629` ALREADY RULED PERCENTAGES OUT OF THIS CORPUS ON TABLE-PLAY GROUNDS AND CONVERTED THIS EXACT PROPERTY TO FLAT DR. THE "INVENTED" NUMBER WAS THE REAL RULING

I ruled PT-2122's DamageImmunity section from the fresh measurement without checking whether the corpus had already answered it. That is exactly the discipline this whole session has spent building -- grep the rulings before assuming a question is open -- and I did not apply it to my own ruling. Recorded plainly rather than glossed over, since the habit only holds if it applies at this level too, not only to Coder's own checks.

### What was already decided

**`PT-475`: percentages are wrong for a reason that has nothing to do with sourcing.** *"A percentage makes the player know a total, compute a fraction, and round. Flat points, dice and fixed steps do not."* This is a table-play decision about cognitive load during actual play, made once, corpus-wide, and it predates this armour pass entirely. It is not a sourcing dispute and my "percent is the source, so percent is the format" reasoning in `PT-2122` answered a question this corpus had already closed on different grounds.

**`PT-629`: the conversion was already done, to this exact property, on this exact instance count.** *"103 converted across four files. None left."* 103 is the same figure Coder just re-measured. The ladder:

    5% -> DR 1 · 10% -> DR 2 · 15% -> DR 3 · 20% -> DR 4 · 25% -> DR 5
    30% -> DR 6 · 50% -> DR 10 · 75% -> DR 15 · 90% -> DR 18 · 100% -> IMMUNE (not a DR value -- a distinct state)

It lands on `PT-527`'s existing `armoured`/Large DR ladder exactly at the 50% rung, and it is deliberately generous at realistic damage rather than exact, which was the ruled direction for gear a player paid for.

**And the source percent was never discarded -- it sits beside the conversion, not under it.** `PT-629`, verbatim: *"the record survives because the conversion sits beside it, not over it: `DamageImmunity (Fire) DR 2 (10%)`."* This is the exact format Coder found in `ITEMS-01` and reported as an unsourced invention. It is not an invention. It is this ruling, correctly applied, sitting exactly where it was ruled to sit.

### What this reverses from PT-2122

Armour's `DamageImmunity` format is **not** percent-only -- withdraw that instruction entirely. It carries `DR N (X%)` per the ladder above, both numbers together, matching `PT-629` and matching what `ITEMS-01` already correctly shows. `ITEMS-01` needs no correction; the "known defect" language in `PT-2122` is itself withdrawn. `100%` is its own state (immune), not a DR figure computed from the formula.

### And it dissolves the K1/K2 question I raised, more cleanly than my original "no clamping" answer did

There is no rung to disagree about once the real mechanic is flat DR. A K2-only 15% converts to `DR 3` under the same universal formula that handles every other value -- it is not a foreign rung on a K1 ladder, it is an ordinary point on a continuous scale. Percent remains in the display as sourcing and flavour, exactly as `PT-629` specified, but it is not the mechanic and never needed an era ruling once that was understood.

### The actual lesson, for both of us

Coder's check was scoped to `ITEMS-01` through `09` plus a search "for it" -- narrow enough to miss two rulings that used the word "percentage" explicitly and one of which converted this exact 103-instance set. My own check was no check at all. Both are the same shape: a real search that answers a narrower question than the one being asked, because the search was scoped to where the answer was expected to live rather than searched broadly across the whole ledger. Worth naming at both levels, not just Coder's.

Nothing else in `PT-2122` changes -- DamageResist and Regeneration remain unblocked and ready to build now, Ability and BonusFeats remain deferred with the poison wall, gates remain split from effects, and the `UseLimitationRacial` semantic check is still the next open question.

## PT-2124 -- RE-CHECKED THE WHOLE SWEEP AS ASKED. IT WAS NOT COMPLETE. THE FOUR FORCE FORMS STILL CARRY LIVE, SHIPPED PERCENTAGES IN `FORMS-01.md` AND `POWER-COSTS-01.md` TODAY -- WRITTEN AFTER `PT-629`-`632` CLOSED, AND NEVER CHECKED AGAINST THE RULE

Swept the ledger broadly rather than trusting the original closure, per the owner's direct instruction to check once more. Most `%` hits after `PT-630` are exactly the categories `PT-629` already ruled fine to leave -- measurement statistics about the corpus itself, probability tables already expressed as a d20 target with odds shown beside it, and analysis prose reasoning about a design choice rather than stating one (a `+2` Defence upgrade described as "10% fewer hits," a third turret described as "a 50% increase" -- these are Coder's own reasoning about an already-flat mechanic, not the mechanic itself, the same shape `PT-629` already approved).

**One real one survived, and it is not a stale ledger discussion -- it is live in the shipped documents right now.**

    force/FORMS-01.md        Force Focus     FP regen +50% out of combat
                              Force Potency   Force power damage +30% · FP cost +20%
                              Force Mastery   duration +50% · FP cost +20%
    force/POWER-COSTS-01.md  Force Mastery   degradation −10% (aggregate, not per-cast)
                              Force Affinity  degradation −5%  (aggregate, not per-cast)

`PT-978`/`PT-979` built and closed the Force Forms system chronologically after `PT-629`-`632` closed the percentage sweep. Nothing re-checked the new content against the standing rule, and both rulings explicitly confirm these percentages as correct and complete along the way -- they were never flagged, because nobody was looking for this class of defect anymore by the time they were written.

### A first read against `PT-629`'s own test, not a ruling

`PT-629`'s test was explicit: *does a player compute this at the table, or once?* Applying it honestly rather than assuming all six need the same treatment:

**Likely real violations -- computed repeatedly, at the table, off a number that changes:** Force Potency's damage `+30%` (recomputed on every Force-power hit while the form is active) and Force Mastery's duration `+50%` (recomputed on every cast) read as the exact "tax on every roll" shape `PT-475` objected to.

**Possibly already inside the exception `PT-475` already carved out:** Force Focus's `+50%` and the two FP-cost `+20%` figures may land closer to Force ceiling degradation's kept exception -- computed once per rest or once per cast, off a figure already on the sheet, not recomputed per swing. `POWER-COSTS-01`'s two degradation percentages are explicitly applied at the aggregate, once per encounter, not per cast -- which is closer to the spirit of the rule than a raw player-facing percentage even though it is still nominally one.

This is a read, not a disposition. Which of the six actually need conversion, and what they convert to, needs the same care `PT-629` gave the DamageImmunity ladder -- landing new numbers on existing precedent rather than inventing them cold. Not something to decide inline against an unrelated armour pass.

### The standing gap, which matters more than these six numbers

`PT-475`/`629`-`632` was a one-time historical sweep. Nothing catches a new percentage mechanic as it gets written afterward -- which is exactly how this survived two full rulings' worth of explicit sign-off. This is the same shape as `audit_featsync`'s own origin: a one-time catch that should have become a standing check and did, eventually, only after the gap bit twice. Worth naming now rather than after it recurs a third time in some future power or feat.

### Queued, not assigned

This does not touch the armour work in progress and does not block it. Added to the standing queue as its own item: a design pass on the Four Force Forms' remaining percentages, and a decision on whether a lightweight standing check belongs in the gate for future percentage mechanics the way `audit_featsync` now catches markdown/JSON divergence. Neither is urgent enough to interrupt armour.

## PT-2125 -- THE FOUR FORCE FORMS' REMAINING PERCENTAGES CONVERTED, CLOSING WHAT `PT-2124` FOUND. THE SEVENTEENTH FAMILY `PT-629` NEVER REACHED

Owner ruling. `PT-2124` found six live percentages in `FORMS-01.md` and `POWER-COSTS-01.md`, written after `PT-629`-`632` closed the percentage sweep and never checked against it. This closes that gap, using the same two idioms the corpus already established rather than inventing a third:

    Force Focus     FP regen out of combat      +50%  ->  half again, rounded down
    Force Mastery   power duration               +50%  ->  half again, rounded down
    Force Potency   power damage                 +30%  ->  roll one extra die of the
                                                            power's own damage type
    Force Potency   FP cost                      +20%  ->  flat +1 FP
    Force Mastery   FP cost                      +20%  ->  flat +1 FP
    Force Mastery   saves vs Force (+/-2, +/-4)   --    no change, already flat
    Mastery/Affinity  degradation reduction      -10%/-5%  no change -- see below

**The dividing line: does the modified quantity already scale, or is it a small fixed number.** Regen and duration scale with level and power -- a flat bonus would be trivial at level 20 and oversized at level 1, so both stay proportional. FP cost is a small single-digit number on most powers -- a percentage of it is exactly the rounding problem `PT-475` was built to kill, so both flatten to `+1`. Potency's damage bonus spans 106 powers of wildly different size -- neither a flat percentage nor a flat die fits all of them, so it borrows the power's own die instead, which scales itself with zero lookup and zero math at the table.

**The two degradation percentages are explicitly NOT converted.** `POWER-COSTS-01` already applies them once per encounter, at the aggregate, off a number already being tracked -- not per-cast, not recomputed on every roll. That is exactly the exception `PT-475` carved out for Force ceiling degradation, applied correctly here on first principles even though nobody checked it against the rule by name. Converting it now would not fix a violation; it would break something that was already right.

**Affinity's "reduced rate" needs its own number confirmed before touching it.** No explicit percentage backing it turned up in the document text read for `PT-2124`. If a real figure exists elsewhere, it gets Focus's treatment (half again, rounded down) for the same reason; if none exists, it may already be qualitative and needs nothing.

`FORMS-01.md` and `POWER-COSTS-01.md` both need updating to the converted values. `AGENDA-CURRENT.md`'s item 8 ("THE PERCENTAGE MECHANICS -- DONE, PT-629, PT-630") should note this closes the one family that scope missed, rather than opening a new agenda item for it.

## PT-2126 -- FORCE FORM SWITCHING STAYS ONE ACTION, NO REST REQUIREMENT. CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: GATING NON-COMBAT SWITCHING BEHIND A LONG REST

Owner ruling, after real deliberation across several options -- recorded because the corpus records why, not only what, and because a design question that got this much genuine back-and-forth deserves the reasoning on file for whoever reads this later.

**The question, from actual play:** a player can currently see a fight coming, spend one action, and switch into whichever Force Form best answers it, with zero real cost. Is that a problem worth fixing?

**Considered: gate switching outside combat behind a long rest and meditation, leave in-combat switching alone.** Rejected. A rest gate on non-combat switching does not stop the behavior it was aimed at -- it only makes the player wait one turn and pay the same one action they were always allowed to pay, on turn one of the fight itself, for the identical result. `PT-978`'s action cost was never a real barrier to this in the first place; a rest gate stacked on top of an unrestricted in-combat switch adds bookkeeping (tracking whether a character has rested) without closing anything it was meant to close.

**Considered: full lock, switching only possible after a long rest, in or out of combat.** Rejected. This does close the loophole, but at a real cost that is not proportional to the problem: a character who guesses wrong walking into a dungeon with no rest point ahead is simply stuck fighting badly for as long as that dungeon takes, with no way out until the next rest -- a trap, not tension. It also deletes, rather than taxes, the mid-combat reactive switching `PT-978` built on purpose, breaking the stated design symmetry between lightsaber stances (earned by acting, live every round) and Force Forms (chosen by intent, meant to still be a real choice in the moment) -- "one reactive, one deliberate" becomes "one reactive, one close to permanent for the day."

**Ruled: no change from `PT-978`.** Switching a Force Form costs one action, any time, including mid-combat, exactly as already built. The free pre-fight foreknowledge case remains technically possible at the cost of one action -- but this is now a considered trade-off rather than an unexamined gap: neither alternative actually closed it without creating a worse problem of its own, and a rule that pretends to solve something it cannot is worse than one that does not claim to.

Nothing changes in any document for this ruling. It is recorded so the next person who has this same instinct does not have to re-walk the same three options to arrive back here.

## PT-2128 -- RULED: `UseLimitationRacial` IS OMITTED FROM ARMOUR'S FORMAT ENTIRELY. THE THIRD KOTOR/NWN DISAGREEMENT, AND WHY THIS ONE RESOLVES BY KOTOR'S OWN ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR RATHER THAN BY ADJUDICATION. THE GATES BLOCK SHRINKS FROM 209 INSTANCES TO 47

Measurement approved in full, and it is worth saying plainly: the control test is the strongest single piece of evidence this armour pass has produced. Seven real, shipped organic items carrying no racial property at all, every one still unequippable by a droid because `droidorhuman` alone already decides it -- that is not an inference about what the property probably does, it is a direct empirical demonstration that its presence or absence changes nothing observable, across the entire shipped corpus of both games. Sweeping all 1551 files rather than only our 163 rows, and reporting the exact count (172, 80/92 split, all subtype 6) rather than a characterisation, is exactly the standard this project has been holding itself to all session.

⚠⚠ THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN "THIS PROPERTY NEVER VARIES" AND "THE RACIAL CATEGORY SYSTEM IS MEANINGLESS" IS THE RIGHT ONE TO HAVE DRAWN, AND IT WOULD HAVE BEEN AN EASY OVERREACH TO COLLAPSE THE TWO. `DamageRacialGroup` at subtype 5 is real, live, 215 real uses, and it is the same mechanism already backing the racial damage terms built on the weapon side -- nothing about this ruling touches that, and nothing should be read as reopening it. Human-as-target in K2's droid interface item is a genuinely interesting, correctly-noted piece of evidence that the categories themselves are not inert; it is specifically Human-as-a-use-limitation that never decides anything.

### THE RULING

**Option A. Omit `UseLimitationRacial` from armour's format entirely.**

The reasoning is the same source-discipline test this pass has applied throughout: build what is real, not what a column's existence implies could theoretically be built. This case clears that bar more cleanly than check penalty did in `PT-2122` -- check penalty was real in shape and simply zero everywhere in our data; this property is proven, by direct controlled test against the shipped game's own behaviour, to be fully redundant with a gate that already exists at the base-item level and that this project already carries structurally, more finely than KOTOR itself does (the droid/organic/chassis feat split from `PT-614`, on top of droid plating already being its own equipment section separate from Armour and Robes). Carrying a per-row line that states the same fact 163 times, when the section a row already sits in states it once, for free, is redundancy without fidelity -- it does not preserve information the format would otherwise lose, because there is no variance to lose.

**Record it as a decision, not a gap.** `EQUIPMENT-01` gets an explicit note: `UseLimitationRacial` was measured across the full shipped corpus of both games, found to carry zero variance and zero magnitude, and confirmed redundant with the existing section/feat structure by direct empirical test -- omitted deliberately, not overlooked.

**Build the safety net regardless.** Extraction keeps refusing any future row whose racial subtype is not 6, exactly as proposed. This costs nothing and is the correct protection against a mod or a future upgrade row introducing a real restriction that this ruling's own evidence did not anticipate -- an omission justified by "it never varies" must keep checking that it still doesn't.

### THE SECOND DISAGREEMENT, AND WHY IT DOES NOT NEED ADJUDICATION THE WAY THE AC LADDER DID

Correct to bring this back rather than fold it into the ruling quietly. But this one has a different shape than stage 4's, and it is worth naming why: stage 4 was two games disagreeing about a VALUE, and the two values were both real, both live, and something had to be chosen between them. This is not that. NWN's racial property genuinely varies -- 18 uses across nine real subtypes, a live mechanic doing real work. KOTOR inherited the whole family byte-for-byte and then, deliberately, gutted the table underneath it and built a different, KOTOR-specific column to do the actual gating instead. There is no KOTOR value competing with an NWN value here for us to pick between -- there is only KOTOR's own real, singular, shipped behaviour, which is what `droidorhuman` and the section structure already are. Recorded as a finding -- inherited scaffolding, repurposed gate -- not adjudicated, because nothing here disagrees with KOTOR about what KOTOR itself does.

### WHAT THIS CHANGES ON THE MAP

The gates block drops from five properties and 209 instances to four and 47 -- `Use_Limitation_Feat` (27), `UseLimitationAlignmentGroup` (12), `UseLimitationPC` (7), `UseLimitationGender` (1). All four genuinely vary per instance and still belong in their own channel, separate from effects, per `PT-2122`. Proceed to design that channel at its real, now-smaller scope.

The upgrade-row `DamageRacialGroup` question is correctly flagged as unchecked rather than claimed covered -- it does not block this ruling (a damage-bonus mechanic, not an equip-gate) and does not need action now, but the boundary is noted rather than assumed closed.

### WHAT PROCEEDS NOW

`DamageResist`, `Regeneration`, and `DamageImmunity` readers -- all three design-closed, build them.
The four-property gates channel, at its corrected scope.
Continue through the remainder: `Immunity` (three flag-only kinds), `ImprovedSavingThrowsSpecific`, `DecreaseAC` (follows `Armor`'s format once built), `Skill` (check the existing species channel first), `Disguise` (cosmetic, lowest priority).
`Ability`, `BonusFeats`, and `DecreaseAbilityScore` remain correctly deferred on the Combatant-ability-score and item-grant-channel architecture.

## PT-2129 -- OWNER RULING: LOOM GETS A "USABLE BY RACE" AUTHORING OPTION. NOT A REVERSAL OF `PT-2128` -- A DIFFERENT SURFACE. THE SHIPPED CATALOGUE STAYS EMPTY; THE BUILDER GETS THE CAPABILITY KOTOR NEVER HAPPENED TO USE

**This does not touch `PT-2128`.** That ruling was about how the existing, shipped, ported KOTOR catalogue extracts -- correctly empty, proven by testing every item in both full games. This ruling is about a different surface entirely: what a person authoring a NEW item in Loom can set, which is not bound by what KOTOR's own data ever happened to contain. The two do not conflict, because they answer different questions -- "what does the port carry" and "what can an author add."

**Owner: the Aurora Toolset exposed this as a real authoring option, and Loom's players should have it too, even though no shipped item ever used it meaningfully.**

### RULING

**Loom gains a usable-by-race field on item authoring.** This is a general equip-gate capability, not scoped narrowly to armour -- it surfaces here because armour is the category currently under construction, but the field belongs to Loom's item-authoring surface broadly, the same as any other author-settable property.

**`PT-1496` governs how it gets built: check Aurora Toolset's own actual implementation before designing a shape for this.** Aaron named Aurora directly as the reference, and this is exactly the standing mandate already in place for any Builder surface -- go read how Aurora Toolset actually presents and stores this option before inventing our own version of it.

**Default is unrestricted, matching the proven real-world default.** `PT-2128`'s finding was not that this restriction is fictional -- it was that KOTOR's shipped content never happened to use it. Loom's field opens blank on every new item, exactly matching what every existing item in both games actually does, and an author sets it only when they deliberately want a real restriction. Nothing about giving Loom the option requires or implies retroactively applying it to anything already in the catalogue.

**The safety-net refusal from `PT-2128` stays as designed.** It was already built to catch a future row whose racial subtype is real and non-default -- an author-created item using this new field is exactly the case that refusal exists to let through correctly rather than silently swallow.

### THE EXAMPLE, AS ITS OWN QUESTION

Wookiees and chest armour is a genuinely good, concrete, genre-correct test case for the option once it exists -- worth having in hand precisely because it is not hypothetical. Two different things could happen with it, and they are not the same decision:

**Loom supporting the option at all** is ruled above, and needs nothing further.

**Whether Wookiee-and-chest-armour becomes an actual ruled restriction in this project's own species or armour data** is a separate, real content decision -- it would affect real Wookiee player characters at an actual table, not just demonstrate that the field works. Was this offered as the illustration that motivated the ruling, or as a request to actually rule it in now? If the latter, it is worth checking what the existing Wookiee species record already says about body type first, since 31 organic species already carry mechanical values and this may already be answered or half-answered there.

## PT-2131 -- AMENDS PT-2130's MECHANISM, NOT ITS SUBSTANCE. THE RESTRICTION MOVES FROM A PER-ITEM LOOM CHECK TO A SPECIES-LEVEL CHARGEN RULE, PAIRED WITH A "NATURAL ARMOUR" TRAIT THAT ALREADY HAS FOUR REAL PRECEDENTS IN THIS CORPUS

**Owner: not tied to every armour and headgear row individually -- surfaced once, at character creation, when a Wookiee is built.** And the missing piece that makes the whole thing make sense: Wookiees already carry heavy racial power (`+4` Strength, `Wookiee Rage`, `Extraordinary Recuperation`) with no real mechanical cost attached to any of it. No chest armour, offset by an innate defence of their own, is the trade-off that power has been missing.

**This changes `PT-2130`'s mechanism, not its fact.** The restriction is exactly as real as `PT-2130` ruled it. What changes is where it lives: not a per-item exclusion checked against every one of the 163-plus armour and robe rows through `PT-2129`'s Loom field, but a single rule attached to the Wookiee species record and enforced once, at the equipment step of chargen (already one of the nine built steps). `PT-2129`'s field is not withdrawn -- it remains the right tool for a genuinely per-item restriction an author creates later (one cursed blade only a Duros can wield, say). It was simply the wrong tool for a restriction that applies to an entire species across an entire category, which is exactly the shape `PT-2128` already argued against once this session: don't restate the same fact 163 times when one rule at a higher level says it for free.

### THE COMPENSATING TRAIT ALREADY HAS REAL PRECEDENT -- THIS IS NOT INVENTED FROM NOTHING

`Natural Armour` is a standing mechanic in this corpus already, on four species, every one of them cited to a real page:

    Gand         +1 natural armour bonus to Defence   exoskeleton   UAA pp.62-63
    Trandoshan   +1 natural armour bonus to Defence   scales        RCR p.31
    Verpine      +1 natural armour bonus to Defence   chitin        (Legends physiology; mechanical value ours)
    Weequay      +2 natural armour bonus to Defence   thick, sun-cured hide (`Leathery Hide`)   UAA pp.181-182

`+1` is the standard value. Weequay is the one exception, and the reason given is explicitly physiological -- a thicker hide than the +1 baseline. Wookiees are described, in this project's own held sources, as an average 2.3 metres tall with a dense fur coat -- a real, comparable case for the `+2` exception rather than the `+1` default, on the same grounds Weequay already earned it. Not decided here -- flagged as the actual open question, `+1` or `+2`, rather than picked without saying so.

### THE PROVENANCE NOTE -- THIS CORPUS ALREADY HAS THE EXACT FORMAT FOR THIS SITUATION

Kaleesh's entry already carries the template this needs: *"No d20 source exists for the Kaleesh in any edition. This entry was authored... The ability line is the least defensible value in the record -- nothing sources it."* *Source: Authored for this setting.*

Wookiee's new trait gets the same treatment, not folded in as though it were always part of the record: **no chest armour, offset by Natural Armour, authored for game balance against the species' existing power budget -- not sourced to RCR, UAA, or the Campaign Guide, because the source check in `PT-2130` already confirmed none of them say this.** State the actual reasoning in the note, the same way Kaleesh's does, rather than a bare "authored" tag with nothing behind it.

### WHAT PROCEEDS NOW

`SPECIES-MASTER.md` / `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2.md`: add `No Chest Armour` and `Natural Armour` (`+1`, pending the size question above) to the Wookiee traits block, with a provenance note in the Kaleesh format.

Chargen's equipment step: for a Wookiee character, the chest-armour category is excluded from what's offered, enforced once at that step rather than per item.

`PT-2129`'s Loom field is unaffected and still gets built for its own, narrower use case.

Confirm the `+1`/`+2` question before finalising the trait line -- everything else can proceed in parallel.

    Str 20 · Dex 13 · Con 20 · Int 10 · Wis 12 · Cha 8
    MaxHitPoints 52 · Scout, ClassLevel 4 · ChallengeRating 3.0
    NaturalAC = 0
    Equip_ItemList = [] (empty in the raw template, both games)

Identical across K1 and K2 on every field checked -- not a fluke of one game's export.

**What this confirms:** the ability-score half of the reasoning is real and grounded. `Str 20` and `Con 20` are both at the high end of any companion in the corpus, driving attack/damage and survivability directly. The "already very powerful, with no real cost attached" half of `PT-2131`'s reasoning is not an impression -- it is what the actual file says.

Zaalbar was never restricted from wearing chest armour in the source game, so the source game never needed a compensating bonus to offset a restriction that does not exist there. Zaalbar's file cannot answer a question about a mechanic that only exists in this project's own ruleset. ## PT-2133 -- WOOKIEE RESTRICTION CLOSED: NATURAL ARMOUR IS +1, NOT +2 -- MY OWN SUGGESTION, CORRECTLY REJECTED. HEADGEAR RATIFIED AS PART OF THE RESTRICTION, OWNED AS AN AMBIGUITY IN HOW I WROTE PT-2131 RATHER THAN CREDITED AS SOMETHING I ACTUALLY RULED

**Owning the attribution first.** `PT-2131`'s opening line echoed the owner's own "armour and headgear" phrasing to frame the request, but the operative ruling only ever specified chest armour -- I never actually extended scope to headgear as its own rule. That is an ambiguity in how I wrote the entry, not a misread on the build side: reading a framing sentence as part of the ruling it introduces is a reasonable way to read a ruling, and the fault is in leaving it unclear which it was. Worth naming plainly rather than letting an unclear ruling get credited as a clear one after the fact.

**Ratified on the merits, not merely allowed to stand.** A Wookiee's head is exactly as mismatched to standard humanoid-cut gear as a Wookiee's torso is -- fur coverage, skull shape and size all argue for the same restriction on the same grounds, and every piece of Star Wars media agrees a Wookiee is never shown in a fitted helmet. The scoping is exactly right: masks, visors, helmets and neural bands restricted; gauntlets, forearm bands, belts, boots and implants explicitly named as unaffected rather than left to guesswork. This stands as ruled, going forward, cleanly -- not as a technicality that happened to survive an ambiguous instruction.

### NATURAL ARMOUR: +1, AND MY OWN +2 SUGGESTION WAS WRONG

Both legs of the rejection are correct and both catch a real error in how I reasoned about it.

**The integument argument is decisive on its own.** Every existing `+1` species has a hard covering -- exoskeleton, scales, chitin -- and a `+2` for fur would rank Wookiee pelage above Verpine chitin inside a ladder that is visibly organised by covering hardness, not by any other axis. I did not check what the ladder was actually organised by before proposing an exception to it.

**The size argument catches something sharper: I conflated two mechanical levers this ruleset deliberately keeps separate.** `BEASTS-01`/`BEASTS-LEVELS-01` already give size its own independent term in Defence -- `10 + size + tier natural armour` -- and Wookiee's own species record is Medium, the same class as Weequay and Nikto. A `2.3` metre average height is real, but it is not a fact the natural-armour mechanic can read at all without changing the size classification itself, which is a far larger, separate change than the one being made here. Proposing `+2` on size grounds was reaching for the wrong lever.

**The magnitude reasoning is exactly right and should be stated as the standing principle, not just this instance's justification:** shipped armour runs `+4` to `+9` Defence. `PT-2131` asked for a trade, not a make-whole -- a compensating bonus that closed most of that gap would quietly erase the cost the restriction was meant to impose. `+1` leaves it biting, which is the point.

`PT-2132`'s `NaturalAC = 0` finding is correctly recorded as real and non-dispositive, in exactly the terms that ruling set -- good discipline not letting a clean, if-only-it-answered-the-question number get read as settling something it structurally cannot settle.

### THE THREE IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS -- APPROVED ON THEIR MERITS, NOT ON MY SAY-SO

I had not specified withheld-vs-refused framing, the exact profession-grant handling, or the explicit armour-proficiency preservation at this level of detail. All three are sound, and worth approving as good engineering judgement rather than silently absorbed as though they'd been dictated:

Withholding the offer entirely for the two affected professions, rather than drawing it and refusing it, is the right UX call and matches how this project has always preferred a restriction to read -- a reason stated once, not an error surfaced after a choice.

Explicitly stating armour proficiency is retained, backed by a real test that a species filter appearing anywhere near feat-granting would fail it, is exactly the kind of protective instinct this project rewards -- a plain restriction stated once creates room for someone later to over-read it, and the test closes that room before it opens.

### VERIFICATION -- APPROVED IN FULL

Good, honest correction on the warning count (two cleared, not five, caught from a complete log rather than a truncated one) -- worth noting since it is the same self-correcting discipline this whole session has valued, applied to your own prior report rather than someone else's.

The mutation survivor handling is exactly right: rather than leaving an unreachable branch unexplained, the code itself now states the unreachability and is mutation-tested as asserting it, which turns a silent gap into a documented, verified invariant.

The spelling-hazard protection -- matching PROFESSIONS-01's column by exact text, failing open, and pinning the withheld set by name in a test that would catch a reworded column before it could silently hand a Wookiee a helmet -- is the same shape of cheap, well-placed safety net this project has built for exactly this kind of drift throughout.

### WHAT THIS LEAVES OPEN

The Conscript grant needs its actual armour implementation before the chest-armour guard is validated against real, live chargen data rather than a constructed array -- queued, not urgent, correctly disclosed as a real gap rather than implied to be already covered.

`SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2`'s `Extraordinary Recuperation` formatting defect (unclosed bold, missing terminator) is correctly flagged rather than ridden along under an unrelated change -- small, low priority, but noted so it does not get lost.

See the next entry for the Weequay discrepancy this pass surfaced -- it is real, it is ruled, and it should not sit as an open question.

## PT-2134 -- WEEQUAY'S LEATHERY HIDE IS +2. `RACIAL-FEATS-01.md` FLATTENED IT TO +1 IN AN UNCHECKED "REGENERATION" AND HAS BEEN WRONG SINCE. THE HEADER GETS ADDED NOW, BECAUSE THIS IS EXACTLY THE FAILURE IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT

**Ruled: `+2` is correct for Weequay.** `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2.md` is the richer, physiology-justified source -- "Weequay skin is thick and sun-cured," explicitly distinguished from Nikto's plain "Leathery Hide" at `+1`. `RACIAL-FEATS-01.md` claims in its own prose to be regenerated FROM `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2`, which makes `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2` the source of truth by the derived file's own stated relationship to it -- not a coin flip between two disagreeing tables. Its "in each case the effect is identical" line is the error, not a second data point. Two species sharing a trait NAME does not mean they share a trait VALUE, and flattening them to one number under one label is exactly the kind of silent compression this corpus has caught in other shapes all session.

**Correct `RACIAL-FEATS-01.md`'s table:** `Leathery Hide` splits into two rows under the shared name -- Nikto at `+1`, Weequay at `+2` -- removing the false "identical" framing rather than just changing a number and leaving the claim that produced the wrong number still standing.

### THE DIAGNOSIS IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX, AND IT WAS THE RIGHT INSTINCT NOT TO RIDE A HEADER CHANGE IN SILENTLY

Correct to trace this all the way down rather than stop at "one number is wrong." `RACIAL-FEATS-01.md` has never actually been checked against its own claimed source, because `check_derived.py` finds derived files exclusively by a `<!-- derived-from: -->` header, this file has never carried one despite claiming the relationship in prose, and a claim in prose that nothing enforces is exactly the "warrant without reading" shape this project has named before -- a claim acquiring authority it never earned by being checked.

**Add the header now.** This is not a routine tidy-up decided in passing -- it is the direct, demonstrated answer to the question of whether it was worth it: this file just produced a real, live, wrong number specifically because nothing was checking it, and starting to check it is the fix that actually closes the hole rather than only patching the one number it happened to expose.

⚠⚠ THE TOOL'S OWN LIMITATION IS A GENUINELY VALUABLE FINDING, SEPARATE FROM THE FIX ABOVE. `check_derived.py` can prove a derivation incomplete -- something present in the source and missing downstream -- but its own docstring admits it cannot prove one incorrect. A regeneration that flattens two distinct values sharing one label into a single wrong value is complete, by the tool's own test, and wrong -- precisely the shape the tool is built to miss even once the header exists. Adding the header here closes the "never checked at all" gap; it does not close the "checked and still wrong in this specific way" gap, and conflating the two would be claiming more coverage than the fix actually provides.

Queued, not mandated now: whether `check_derived.py` should gain a value-level check for exactly this shape of silent flattening, given it has now caused one real, live, shipped defect rather than a hypothetical one. Worth having on record as a concrete argument for it next time capacity opens up, not urgent enough to interrupt the armour work in progress.
