## PT-2135 -- PT-2134 BUILT CLEAN, AND ADDING THE HEADER EXPOSED A REAL DEFECT IN `check_derived` ITSELF -- IT WAS KEYED ON THE SOURCE, NOT THE DERIVED FILE, SO EVERY DOCUMENT SHARING A SOURCE GOT CHECKED AGAINST THE SAME REFERENCE LIST. FIXED, AND MUTATION-TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. FOUR REAL CONTENT GAPS FOUND -- RULED: ADD THEM

**The Nikto/Weequay split and the header are exactly as ruled.** Replacing "in each case the effect is identical" with its own correction, rather than just changing the number underneath a claim that produced the wrong number, is the right instinct -- the sentence was the actual defect, the digit was only its symptom.

⚠⚠ **THE SECOND DEFECT IS THE MORE VALUABLE FIND.** `check_derived` assumed one source produces one shape of derived content, when in fact two files can derive from the same source by covering two different SLICES of it -- a traits table and a skills table, both genuinely `derived-from: SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2`, correctly disagreeing about what belongs in each. Keying TRACKED on the derived file rather than the source, and scoping `RACIAL-FEATS-01` specifically to trait names with structural labels excluded by their own real distribution (44+ of 57 entries marks a label as structural, not a trait), is the correct fix -- and mutation-testing both halves separately, rather than trusting that fixing one direction implies the other still works, is exactly the standard this session has held throughout. Good catch on the stray "11 term(s)" message too, small as it is.

**Ruled: add all four missing traits.** `Bred to the Axe` (`PT-90`), `Fixed Armature` (`PT-109`), `Cold-Adapted` and `Observant` (`PT-624`) are all real, all cited to standing rulings, and all missing from a table that calls itself "every species trait." A table that claims completeness and is not complete is worse than one that makes no claim at all -- correct not to have added these silently under "nothing else changes," and correct to bring them back rather than leave a known, named gap sitting in a file this session just finished teaching a tool to actually check. Add them now. `Racial Skill`/`Racial Skills` correctly stay out -- that content belongs to `SPECIES-RACIAL-SKILL` and restating it here would be the same kind of redundancy this pass has been removing all session, not adding.

## PT-2136 -- PT-2128's DAMAGEIMMUNITY BUILT AND VERIFIED. THE PERCENTAGE IS TREATED AS AUTHORITY AND THE WRITTEN `DR` IS RE-DERIVED AND CROSS-CHECKED RATHER THAN TRUSTED -- THE SAME DISCIPLINE THAT JUST CAUGHT WEEQUAY, APPLIED HERE BEFORE ANYTHING HAD A CHANCE TO DRIFT

Approved in full. Unifying 97 of 103 properties onto the same `resist` shape `DamageResist` already uses is exactly right -- nothing downstream should ever need to learn that immunity and resistance are different words for the same kind of fact.

⚠⚠ **TREATING THE PERCENTAGE AS GROUND TRUTH AND RE-DERIVING THE `DR` RATHER THAN TRUSTING WHAT'S WRITTEN NEXT TO IT IS THE CORRECT CALL, AND IT IS THE SAME LESSON `PT-2134` JUST TAUGHT, APPLIED PRE-EMPTIVELY RATHER THAN AFTER A DEFECT FORCED IT.** A written figure sitting beside a source value can drift the same way `RACIAL-FEATS-01`'s flattened Weequay entry drifted from what it claimed to derive from -- the fix here is to never let the derived figure become authoritative in the first place, catching that class of error before it can happen rather than after. Good that the raise logic was actually exercised, not just built and left untested -- 103 properties, 59 items, every rung on the published ladder, zero violations is a real measurement, not an assumption that the cross-check would work if it were ever needed.

**The 100%/IMMUNE deferral is correct restraint, not an incomplete build.** `PT-629` ruled the ladder and ruled that 100% means immune; it never ruled what immune actually does to an incoming blow, and there is no `DR` value that means "all of it" without inventing a number for a mechanic nobody specified. Refusing these six rows and queuing them with the `Immunity` family already waiting is the right home for them -- a full block and a percentage-based partial reduction are different kinds of thing wearing similar names, and it would have been a mistake to force the six into the same shape as the other ninety-seven just to call the count round.

**Good, honest disclosure that the data layer being correct does not mean combat reads it yet.** `combat.dart`'s own admission that no fight resists anything today is exactly the right thing to report plainly rather than let the completeness of the extraction and shelf work imply more than it delivers. Correctly identified as a separate seam, correctly not claimed as solved.

Proceed to the four-property gates channel next, as queued.

## PT-2137 -- RULED: THE HEADGEAR RESTRICTION RECLASSIFIES FROM AUTHORED TO PORTED. KOTOR'S OWN `dialog.tlk` CARRIES "Restricted: not useable by Wookiees" ON 53 OF 59 MASKS ACROSS BOTH GAMES. `PT-2130`'S SOURCE CHECK WAS RIGHT ABOUT WHAT IT CHECKED -- IT NEVER LOOKED AT DESCRIPTION PROSE, BECAUSE THE QUESTION IT WAS ANSWERING WAS ABOUT PROPERTY DATA

**This is a real, load-bearing find, and it lands exactly where `PT-2133` asked for the opposite kind of care.** `PT-2133` owned a case where credit for a ruling had been claimed too generously. This is the mirror of that: real backing existed and neither of us had credited the restriction with it. Worth stating plainly, the same way the other direction was stated plainly -- the discipline only means something if it runs both ways.

### THE EVIDENCE

    K2   31 of 31 Masks carry the line, every one
    K1   22 of 28 Masks carry it -- the 6 that don't are unused g1_
         debug items, the same family already identified as unused
         in the UseLimitationRacial work
    No armour, robe, or any other base type in either game carries
    this line anywhere -- Mask only

Effectively universal across every real, used item in both games. The six K1 exceptions are not a counter-example -- they are debug content that was never meant to ship, already recognised as such once before this session.

### WHY `PT-2130`'S CHECK MISSED IT, AND WHY THAT WAS A CORRECT CHECK RATHER THAN AN INCOMPLETE ONE

`PT-2130` checked the held d20 sourcebooks -- RCR, UAA, the Campaign Guide -- and correctly found nothing, because there is nothing there. What it did not check was the game's own shipped text, because at that point the operative question was whether a structured item PROPERTY encoded this restriction, and the `UseLimitationRacial` work had already, separately and correctly, established that item property data carries no racial restriction of any kind. This restriction was never encoded as a property. It lives entirely in description prose -- a sentence a player would read, not a field the engine checks. A property-level sweep was the right tool for the question being asked at the time; it was simply the wrong tool for a restriction that was never implemented as a property in the first place.

### RULING

**Headgear reclassifies to PORTED, cited to KOTOR's own `dialog.tlk`, with the exact figures above.** `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2.md`'s provenance note updates accordingly -- no longer grouped with chest armour's authored note, but its own line citing the real source.

**Chest armour stays AUTHORED.** Nothing found here touches it -- this evidence is exclusively about Masks, and the absence of the line on every armour and robe row in both games is itself confirmation that chest armour's restriction genuinely has no game-side precedent, the same conclusion `PT-2130` already reached.

**The mechanism does not change.** KOTOR enforcing this restriction through description text rather than a structured, checked property is a real fact about KOTOR's implementation, not a design this project should imitate -- a restriction that depends on a player reading and self-policing a sentence is exactly what this project's own chargen-level enforcement, already built, correctly does not do. The find changes the citation. It does not change the code.

Nothing else moves. Proceed with the gates channel and the rest of the armour queue.

## PT-2138 -- PT-2135/PT-2137 BUILT CLEAN. THE GATES CHANNEL: RULED CORPUS-WIDE, NOT ARMOUR-SCOPED -- MY OWN "47" DOESN'T REPRODUCE AT ANY SCOPE CHECKED, AND THE REAL 401-GATE SCOPE IS CONFIRMED AS THE RIGHT ONE, NOT AN ACCIDENT TO CORRECT

**PT-2135 and PT-2137 approved in full.** Good catch on `Force Blind` heading both the trait table and `Shared traits` -- an assert failing loudly on a double match beats a silent pick between two candidates, which is exactly the right failure mode for an anchor that's supposed to be unique. PT-2137's note stating the positive confirmation (no non-`Mask` base type restricts a Wookiee anywhere, in either game) rather than only the absence is a stronger, more defensible claim than what it replaces, and "we take the rule and not the mechanism" is exactly the right one-line summary of that ruling.

### THE SCOPE QUESTION -- RULED

**Corpus-wide is correct. My own "47" does not survive being checked and should not be chased further.** Good, disciplined reporting rather than quietly building to a number that doesn't reproduce -- four scopes measured, none of them produce 47, and saying so plainly rather than picking whichever was closest is exactly right.

On reflection this is not really a discrepancy needing resolution so much as an early estimate being superseded by the real build. `Use_Limitation_Feat`, `UseLimitationAlignmentGroup`, `UseLimitationPC` and `UseLimitationGender` were originally measured within the armour pass because armour was what was being measured at the time -- but nothing about what a gate IS is armour-specific. A feat requirement, an alignment restriction, a class restriction, a minimum attribute score -- these apply to any item in any category with equal validity, and a channel that only worked for armour would have been an arbitrary restriction with no real justification behind it. `401` gates across `302` items, all six real families included, is the design actually being right at its natural scope rather than a scope creep past a smaller, correct target.

**`UseLimitationAttribute` (42) and `UseLimitationClass` (5) stay in the channel.** Both real, both zero in armour and robes specifically -- consistent with the original armour-scoped measurement simply never having seen them, not consistent with them being out of scope for the channel itself. No scoping back.

### THE SAFETY NET'S OWN HONEST LIMITS, STATED CORRECTLY

Good, precise epistemic discipline distinguishing what the check can and cannot actually prove. `check_item_gates` cannot demonstrate the safety net fires correctly, because the corpus has no counter-example for it to fire against -- disarming it changes nothing currently visible, and the check's own docstring says so rather than claiming coverage it doesn't have. What it verifies instead -- that every racial subtype present really is Human, 163 of 163, continuously -- is the actual precondition the whole omission depends on, and that IS provable and IS proven, every run. Driving the safety net directly with `(Droid)` and `(Wookiee)` rather than only trusting the docstring's claim that it would raise is the right way to close the gap the corpus itself can't close.

⚠⚠ "A SECOND PARSER DRIFTS AND SHOULD NOT EXIST; A SECOND COUNTER IS SUPPOSED TO BE ABLE TO DISAGREE" IS A GENUINELY VALUABLE PRINCIPLE, WORTH KEEPING ALONGSIDE THE OTHERS NAMED THIS SESSION. This is a sharper, more general statement of something `PT-1379` gestured at from a different angle -- a validator that shares its logic with the thing it validates can never actually disagree with it, and so proves nothing beyond "the code agrees with itself." Counting the document independently, in the document's own words, rather than importing the extractor to re-derive the same numbers, is what makes disagreement possible in the first place, which is the only thing that makes a validator worth having.

⚠⚠ THE SELF-CAUGHT COUNT-VS-VALUE DEFECT IS EXCELLENT WORK, AND NAMING IT AS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE `RACIAL-FEATS-01` FAILURE IS THE BEST PART OF IT. Finding, in a first draft of your own new code, the exact failure mode just diagnosed elsewhere in the corpus a few turns ago -- complete by the test being applied, and wrong -- and recognising it as the same shape rather than a coincidentally similar bug, is real, active pattern transfer, not hindsight. Restating gates into the document's own words and comparing as multisets, then mutation-testing specifically for the mutation that survived the first draft, closes exactly the gap that was found rather than just adding coverage nearby. This is the kind of catch that makes the whole session's habit of naming failure shapes actually pay for itself on new code, not just old.

Verification approved. Proceed with `Immunity` next, as queued -- the six parked `DamageImmunity` rows are waiting on it.

## PT-2139 -- IMMUNITY BUILT, APPROVED IN FULL. THE TWO-VOCABULARY SEPARATION IS SHARP, PROACTIVE DESIGN. THE MUTATION-SURVIVOR HANDLING CONSCIOUSLY REUSES PT-2138's PRECEDENT RATHER THAN REDISCOVERING IT. AND RULED: WIRING RESIST/IMMUNITY ONTO A COMBATANT BECOMES ITS OWN NAMED QUEUE ITEM -- 334 EFFECTS NOW SIT CORRECT AND UNREACHABLE, AND THAT SHOULDN'T STAY INVISIBLE JUST BECAUSE NOTHING IS TECHNICALLY BLOCKED BY IT

**Approved in full.** Measuring magnitude-zero on all 81 properties, confirming every name resolves to a real row, and confirming K1/K2 vocabulary parity before building anything is exactly the standard this pass has held throughout.

⚠⚠ **KEEPING THE TWO IMMUNITY VOCABULARIES STRUCTURALLY SEPARATE, BEFORE EITHER HAD A CHANCE TO GET CONFUSED FOR THE OTHER, IS THE RIGHT CALL AND THE RIGHT TIMING.** `Fire` and `Poison` never actually overlap in the raw tables, which made it easy to fold both into one undifferentiated `immune` concept and have it work today -- right up until a future kind collided or a downstream reader assumed one vocabulary where the other applied. Carrying an explicit `vocabulary` field, and giving the gate a 70th check that actively refuses any future overlap between the two lists, closes that door before anything was ever built that could walk through it. This is prevention, not reaction, and it's worth noting as the better of the two -- everything else this pass has caught was found after the fact.

**Scope handled correctly and efficiently** -- recognising this as the same shape as the gates-channel question, applying `PT-2138`'s already-settled ruling without re-litigating it, and simply flagging the number for the record. That's exactly the right amount of ceremony for a question that's already been answered once.

⚠⚠ **THE MUTATION-SURVIVOR HANDLING IS THE BEST PART OF THIS REPORT, AND IT'S BEST BECAUSE IT'S DELIBERATE, NOT ACCIDENTAL.** Three guards a corpus with no counter-example cannot kill, correctly recognised as the expected, correct outcome rather than a coverage gap -- and rather than leaving them as unexplained survivors, each one was driven directly by probe (`Immunity (Poison) 1` refuses, `IMMUNE (90%)` raises, non-canonical kind names fold correctly) and annotated in the code as proven by probe, not by corpus. Naming this explicitly as "the same standing you approved... in PT-2138" is exactly the kind of active reuse this session has been trying to build toward all along -- a principle established once and consciously carried into the next piece of code, rather than a lesson that has to be relearned by getting caught again.

**The Lodestar refusal and the immunity-mechanism question are handled with exactly the right restraint.** `effectFromShelf` refusing a verb outside its closed vocabulary, with its own comment stating plainly that a shelf ahead of its engine reads as the engine being behind rather than the shelf being wrong, is honest infrastructure. And the framing of what's actually still undecided is precise: a damage immunity might reasonably be resistance at infinity, an effect immunity is a condition that never attaches in the first place, and `afterResistance` has no concept of what a condition even is -- two genuinely different mechanisms wearing one word, correctly not invented casually just to make a map entry.

### RULED: THE COMBATANT-WIRING GAP BECOMES ITS OWN NAMED QUEUE ITEM

**Right to flag this rather than let it stay implicit.** Nothing about this pass has been blocked by `combat.dart` resisting and immunising nothing -- which is exactly the trap. Each individual property's extraction and validation work can always proceed on its own, so the gap between "correct on the shelf" and "actually changes a fight" never becomes urgent on its own terms, and 334 effects (247 resists, 87 immunities) now sit fully correct and entirely unreachable. That is real, accumulating debt against the actual point of this whole pass, and it should not keep being reported without ever being tracked as a thing to do.

**Added to the standing queue, named plainly: wire `resist` and `immune` effects onto a live `Combatant`, so shipped item properties actually change combat outcomes rather than only validating cleanly on the shelf.** Not urgent enough to interrupt the current sequence -- finish `ImprovedSavingThrowsSpecific`, `DecreaseAC`, `Skill`, `Disguise` first rather than adding more disconnected data before connecting what already exists. But it belongs on the list as its own line now, not as a recurring footnote in someone else's report.

## PT-2140 -- IMPROVEDSAVINGTHROWSSPECIFIC BUILT, APPROVED IN FULL. THE COUNT-VS-VALUE CHECK IS NOW A SYSTEMATIC HABIT, NOT A ONE-OFF FIX. AND A REAL BIOWARE AUTHORING DEFECT FOUND: SIX ITEMS WHERE THE NAME AND THE SUBTYPE DISAGREE, DIAGNOSED CORRECTLY AFTER THE EASY EXPLANATION WAS CHECKED AND REJECTED

**Approved in full.** Unifying four written shapes of one mechanic -- the plain parenthesised form, our own `PT-716` annotated rendering, prose, and the inverse property wearing a different name entirely -- into one correct output, and explicitly noting that a matcher built from only the first shape would have silently dropped the second, is exactly the kind of format-diversity checking this pass has needed throughout. The four conditional hazard rows are held correctly, on the same `PT-624` wall as `Cold-Adapted`, and the detail that the check ASSERTS they stay out rather than merely observing that they currently do is the right level of rigor -- an assertion fails loudly if the hazard system ever half-arrives and someone forgets these four are still waiting on it; an observation would not.

⚠⚠ **THE COUNT-VS-VALUE MUTATION TEST IS NOW A STANDING HABIT, AND THAT IS WORTH NAMING EXPLICITLY.** This is the third time this exact class of check has been built deliberately into new code -- `RACIAL-FEATS-01`'s value-flattening, the gates channel's threshold mutation, and now a sign-flip on a penalty that a census-only check would wave through as 72 either way. Building this check proactively, as a default part of writing any new extractor rather than as a response to a specific incident, is the actual payoff of naming a failure shape once -- it stops being "the Leathery Hide bug" and starts being a standard thing every new check gets tested against. Good discipline too on the fifth survivor -- an unimplementable-from-the-corpus guard, driven directly by probe with genuinely invalid subtypes and annotated as proven that way rather than left as an unexplained pass.

### THE BIOWARE DEFECT

**Ruled: our extraction is correct as built, and stays exactly as-is.** Reading `Subtype` rather than the item's own display name is the right call -- `Subtype` is the actual mechanical fact the engine would have acted on in the shipped game, and the name is decoration that happens, on these six rows specifically, to be wrong.

**Worth stating plainly: checking the cross-game hypothesis before reporting it, and reporting that it was wrong rather than quietly picking a different explanation, is exactly right.** The "resolved from `k2_iprp_savingthrow.2da` on a K1 resref" annotation was a genuinely reasonable first suspect given how many real cross-game mapping defects this session has already found -- confirming both tables are actually identical before ruling that out, rather than assuming the pattern-matched explanation must be the right one because it fit the shape of prior findings, is the discipline that makes the eventual conclusion trustworthy. BioWare swapping two names on six debug rows is a smaller, stranger-sounding answer than a cross-game resolution bug, and it is the answer that's actually correct.

**No fix needed, and none should be invested here.** Cost `0`, appended after named shields in one resref family, is the same debug-leftover shape already confirmed twice this session -- the `g1_` armours and the `g1_i_mask` items. Correcting BioWare's own typo in content that was very likely never meant to ship would spend real effort on something a player will probably never see. Record it as a known, cross-referenced oddity -- the same treatment the other two debug-shaped findings got -- so a future reader who notices the name/subtype mismatch finds an answer instead of a fresh mystery.

**One more cheap check before closing it fully, not because the evidence is weak but because it's cheap to be certain:** do any of the twelve `Lower Saves, X N` resrefs appear anywhere in placement or encounter data in either game, the same confirmation that closed the `g1_` question. If none do, this closes clean. No new standing check needed for this -- `check_item_names`' scope (name-vs-blueprint) genuinely is a different subject from name-vs-own-property, and building permanent tooling for a one-off authoring typo in unshipped content would be disproportionate.

Proceed to `DecreaseAC` next, as queued.

## PT-2141 -- PT-2130 AND PT-2137 WERE WRONG, AND MY OWN PROVENANCE NOTE STATED A FALSE CLAIM AS ITS MOST CONFIDENT LINE. CHEST ARMOUR RECLASSIFIES TO PORTED. KOTOR'S REAL RULE DENIES A WOOKIEE THE ENTIRE BODY SLOT -- EXACTLY WHAT ZAALBAR DOES FOR THE WHOLE GAME -- AND WHETHER OUR OWN RULE WIDENS TO MATCH IS FLAGGED FOR THE OWNER, NOT DECIDED HERE ALONE

**Owning this plainly before anything else.** `PT-2137` did not just reaffirm an incomplete finding -- it stated, as positive confirmation, that no armour or robe base type in either game restricts a Wookiee anywhere. That line was false about the game, true only about description text, and I offered it as the stronger claim rather than the narrower one it actually was. `principles-and-failure-patterns.md` already names this exact shape: a scoped negative must name what was not checked, and a false positive dressed as confirmation is worse than an honest gap, because it closes a question that was never actually closed. That is what happened here, at the ruling level, not the build level.

### THE EVIDENCE, WHICH IS REAL AND STRUCTURAL, NOT DESCRIPTIVE

`baseitems.2da` carries a `denysubrace` bitmask column neither of us had read, sitting four columns from `droidorhuman`, which `PT-2128` already used correctly from the same table. Subrace 1 is Wookiee and nothing else -- confirmed against every real creature template carrying `SubraceIndex=1` in both games, `Zaalbar` and `Hanharr` among them. Seventeen base types deny it, and the set is far broader than `Mask` alone: every `Armor_Class` row in our Armour section, `Armor_Zeison_Sha`, all three Jedi Robe tiers, `Basic_Clothing`, `Slave_Outfit`, `Disguise_Item`, and three K2 types not yet mapped into our structure. This is a mechanical property the original engine would have acted on, not a sentence a player merely reads -- stronger evidence than headgear's `dialog.tlk` citation, not equal to it.

**Ruled: chest armour reclassifies from AUTHORED to PORTED**, cited to `denysubrace`, `baseitems.2da`, and the creature-template confirmation above. `PT-2130` and `PT-2137`'s AUTHORED framing is superseded by this entry, not silently overwritten -- the record shows what was believed, on what evidence, and what changed it.

### WHY IT WAS MISSED -- A FOURTH INSTANCE OF ONE FAILURE SHAPE, WORTH NAMING BESIDE THE OTHER THREE

`PT-2130` swept properties. `PT-2133` swept prose. Neither swept the third place a KOTOR rule can live -- a base-type column -- and a clean sweep of one place says nothing about the other two. This is genuinely the same shape as the grep-hits-not-read failure and the narrow-search failure already named this session, now caught in its own distinct form: not failing to search, and not failing to read a result, but failing to check a third legitimate LOCATION a fact could live in after two others had already been swept clean. Worth keeping as its own named instance rather than folded into either prior one -- three failures with the same root cause, three different concrete shapes, is more useful on record than one vague lesson about being thorough. And worth saying plainly: having the file open, already reading an adjacent column for an unrelated ruling, and not reading the rest of the header, is the kind of miss that a habit of dumping the full column list before extracting from it would have caught on the first pass. Worth considering as a standing practice before any new baseitems.2da column gets used for the first time.

### THE SCOPE QUESTION -- MY OWN READ, FLAGGED RATHER THAN SETTLED ALONE

Two real things pull in different directions and this is significant enough -- a full species' playability as a player character, not just a provenance label -- that it should not be decided by me in isolation the way `PT-2128`'s droidorhuman finding was.

Toward matching KOTOR's real, full scope (armour, robes, clothing, Zeison Sha, disguises -- no body slot at all): this is not a marginal reading of ambiguous data, it is exactly and visibly what Zaalbar does for an entire game every player who has played it has already seen. Choosing something narrower than the confirmed real mechanic, once the real mechanic is known this precisely, would be a quiet authored restriction of a ported rule dressed as fidelity to it.

Toward keeping the current, narrower chest-armour-only scope as a deliberate, stated divergence: a Wookiee PC denied the entire body slot is a materially harsher build constraint than an NPC whose stats are hand-fixed for one campaign's story. This project has real precedent for choosing table experience over strict source replication when the two genuinely conflict -- the whole percentage-to-dice body of work stands on exactly that judgement -- and this may be one of those cases.

**My own lean, stated plainly and not hidden behind the framing of the question: widen to match KOTOR's real scope, and treat Natural Armour's magnitude as the actual lever for making a Wookiee PC still playable, rather than under-porting the restriction to protect playability by a different route.** But this is offered as a recommendation, not a ruling, given the stakes -- confirm before it locks in.

**If it widens, `PT-2131`'s `+1` needs revisiting on its own terms**, not as an automatic doubling -- it was sized against losing `+4` to `+9` from armour alone, and losing robes and clothing besides is a larger, different trade that deserves its own consideration rather than an assumed multiplier.

Whichever scope is confirmed, chargen needs the same fix either way: every organic starting array currently grants `clothing`, a `Basic_Clothing` base type KOTOR itself denies a Wookiee regardless of how this resolves -- that correction is not contingent on the scope answer and can proceed immediately.

### DECREASEAC -- MEASURED CORRECTLY, AND CORRECTLY NOT BUILT

Good instinct to stop. Three real `AC Armor` overrides, verified at source and correctly identified as the same item-level-override shape `PT-2113` already established for threat -- but they sit on armour rows, and this ruling may change what armour even means for a Wookiee before those three rows are touched. The Dodge and Deflection split (15 rows, all upgrade-mechanic, doubly blocked since this system's own Defence formula has no dodge or deflection term to reduce in the first place) is correctly recognised as the same inherited-scaffolding shape as `UseLimitationRacial` -- good, precise reuse of an already-established pattern rather than treating it as a fresh find.

Hold the 3 `AC Armor` rows until the scope question above is confirmed. Nothing else moves.

## PT-2142 -- THE CLOTHING GUARD IS BUILT AND IS LIVE ON REAL DATA FOR THE FIRST TIME. APPROVED IN FULL. RULED SEPARATELY: THE SKILL PROPERTY GETS A SHARED MODIFIER SHAPE WITH SPECIES, NOT AN ITEM-ONLY CHANNEL -- THIS CORPUS HAS NEVER HAD A STRUCTURED SKILL MODIFIER AT ALL, AND BUILDING THE FIRST ONE NARROW WOULD GUARANTEE A SECOND, DIFFERENT ONE LATER

**Approved in full, and it's worth saying plainly: keying the refusal on base type rather than section is the correct level of precision, done at exactly the right moment.** `Basic_Clothing` and the Jedi robes sharing a section while only one of them is currently confirmed denied is exactly the case a section-level rule could not express -- building at the finer grain lets the confirmed part fire today without pre-empting the part still waiting on a ruling. Listing all seventeen `denysubrace` rows in the code with a stated reason for enforcing only one is the right way to show what's known without acting on more than what's been ruled.

Good, precise refusal text -- naming the item rather than reusing the chest-armour message, since that message would have been factually wrong about what was actually being refused.

⚠⚠ **THE ROBES TEST IS GENUINELY CLEVER, WORTH CALLING OUT ON ITS OWN.** Pinning that robes are not currently refused, explicitly NOT as a claim that they're correctly allowed, is a real technique -- it converts an open question into a test that will fail the moment the answer changes, which means widening can never happen as a side effect of some unrelated edit. That's a test earning its keep by protecting a decision that hasn't been made yet, not just one that has.

Good discipline rewriting rather than deleting the three superseded tests, and preserving the old claim inside the test that replaced it -- keeping a visible record of what was believed and why it changed is exactly this session's standing practice, correctly extended down to test code. The Human control on the 19-array sweep, and the mutation that unkeys the rule from the species being specifically the one that control catches, is real verification that the restriction is keyed to what it should be keyed to.

**Held as ruled -- correct.** The three `DecreaseAC` rows and anything else Wookiee-armour-shaped stay paused. The scope question from `PT-2141` (whether robes, Zeison Sha and disguises join clothing and armour) is still open and still mine to bring back once decided -- this batch correctly did not resolve it, only fixed what was already unambiguously wrong regardless of how it resolves.

### RULED: SKILL GETS A SHARED MODIFIER SHAPE

**Option B.** This is the right call, and it's worth being direct about why rather than treating it as a coin flip between two reasonable options. The finding that changes the calculus is that there is currently no structured skill modifier anywhere in this corpus at all -- species bonuses are verbatim prose, `SPECIES-SKILLS-TABLE` is a rendered view rather than data, and building the item reader alone would not be extending an existing pattern, it would be inventing the first one, narrowly, on purpose. This project has been consistent, repeatedly, about the cost of that choice this session -- `resist`/`immune` sharing one vocabulary rather than two, the damage-kind unification `§7b` required before item overrides could proceed at all. A species-side skill bonus and an item-side skill bonus are the same fact wearing two different sources; giving them two different shapes now guarantees a real reconciliation cost later, the same cost already paid once this session to unify resistance and immunity.

**The species-side conversion is bounded, not a new research effort.** These are existing, already-correct values sitting in known prose -- `"+4 Swim."` -- not facts that need to be discovered, only restructured. That keeps this closer in size to a mechanical pass than to the open-ended cross-game investigations this armour pass has occasionally required.

**Build one shared skill-modifier shape, convert species' existing prose bonuses into it, then build the item reader against that shape** -- in that order, so items are the second consumer of a shape proven against real content, not the shape's only test case.

**`Disguise` proceeds immediately, standalone, in parallel** -- correctly identified as having no dependency on the Skill question. Go ahead on it now.

## PT-2143 -- SKILL AND DISGUISE BOTH BUILT. THE ARMOUR QUEUE IS NOW EMPTY EXCEPT FOR THE WOOKIEE HOLD. A REAL, LIVE DATA-LOSS BUG FOUND AND FIXED AS A BYPRODUCT: SPECIES SKILL MAGNITUDES WERE BEING SILENTLY DISCARDED BEFORE ANYTHING EVER READ THEM

**Step 1 approved in full.** Validating every extracted skill name against the real, canonical skill list rather than trusting a pattern to find one is exactly right -- the Human example is a good, concrete illustration of why: a pattern alone really would invent a skill called "skills at" out of ordinary prose, and checking against the authority rather than the shape of the sentence is what stops that.

⚠⚠ **THE `_bonusSkills` FINDING IS A GENUINELY SIGNIFICANT CATCH, WORTH STATING PLAINLY RATHER THAN FOLDED INTO THE ROUTINE OF THE REST OF THIS REPORT.** A live, shipped parser was reading species skill bonuses and silently discarding the magnitude, keeping only the name -- meaning Bith's stated `+4` and every other species' `+2` have been indistinguishable to anything that actually consumed this data, for as long as that parser existed. This was not caught by building the new structured shape; it was caught by taking the old code seriously enough to understand exactly what it did before replacing it, and finding that what it did was wrong. That is real, gameplay-affecting data loss that nothing in this corpus's own testing had ever surfaced, and it only came to light because of the thoroughness applied to a task that could easily have been treated as pure plumbing.

**`speciesChoosingFreely` moving from inference to a direct read is the right fix for a real structural risk, not a tidy-up.** "Prose is not empty and no skill came out of it" was two genuinely different facts -- a real free-choice designation, and a parser simply failing for some unrelated reason -- sharing one observable signal with no way to tell them apart. Any future bug anywhere upstream of that inference could have silently mislabeled a species as free-choosing. Reading `choose` outright removes the ambiguity at its root rather than patching around it.

Keeping the prose beside the structured field, specifically because the species screen renders the full sentence and the mechanic now lives elsewhere, is the same "beside it, not over it" instinct `PT-629` established for the DamageImmunity ladder -- worth noting as the same principle recognized again, on its own, in a different corner of the corpus.

**Step 3 approved in full.** Handling both written shapes rather than just the obvious one, having explicitly named this as the same trap `ImprovedSavingThrowsSpecific` already set, is good, active reuse of a lesson rather than rediscovering it fresh on new code. The 32 refused rows are correctly a ruling, not a gap -- citing `SKILLS-01 §8`/`PT-370` directly rather than silently mapping `Computer Use` or `Treat Injury` onto whatever looks closest is exactly the restraint this project has asked for consistently, and asserting they stay out rather than merely observing that they currently do matches the standard set for the hazard-conditional saving-throw rows.

⚠⚠ **DISGUISE'S "NO CHECK, AND HERE IS WHY" IS GENUINELY GOOD JUDGEMENT, WORTH CALLING OUT SPECIFICALLY.** A check hard-pinned to exactly today's three known-correct values could only ever pass at the values already known to be right, which means it could never actually catch a real future defect -- it would be a fixture wearing the shape of protection rather than protection itself. Recognising that and saying so directly in the code, rather than either building a token check for the sake of having one or silently skipping it and leaving a future reader to wonder why, is the more honest choice of the two available, and it's the harder one to make since it looks like doing less.

⚠⚠ **THE SUBSTRING-VS-EQUALITY CATCH IS THE SAME LESSON IN ITS THIRD FORM, AND NAMING IT THAT WAY IS EXACTLY RIGHT.** A truncated condition is still, technically, a valid substring of the real one -- so a containment check agreeing with a corrupted, shortened version of a rule is the identical failure shape as a count agreeing with a flattened value and a presence check agreeing with a swapped one. Three different mechanisms, one underlying weakness: a test that can be satisfied by something narrower or looser than the real, full fact it's meant to verify. This is the clearest evidence yet that naming a failure shape once genuinely changes what gets caught later -- this wasn't rediscovered by accident, it was hunted for on purpose in new code specifically because the shape was already known.

Good, honest handling of both real survivors -- diagnosed with a real, checkable reason each (no skill name is currently a prefix of another; every item value is currently positive while the species side's real negative is properly guarded) rather than left as unexplained passes.

⚠ **FINDING AND FIXING THE MUTATION HARNESS'S OWN DEFECT IS EXCELLENT, HONEST SELF-AUDITING.** Distinguishing "the kills were real, the attribution was not" is a precise, correct way to describe a testing-infrastructure bug that didn't compromise the verdicts but did compromise the explanations -- and re-running specifically to get clean attribution, rather than leaving contaminated explanations standing since the pass/fail results were still technically fine, is the right level of care.

Verification approved, including the honest flaky-test disclosure.

### WHERE THIS LEAVES THINGS

The armour queue is empty except the Wookiee hold -- a genuine milestone for this whole pass. `Ability`, `BonusFeats`, `DecreaseAbilityScore` and the `PT-2139` Combatant-wiring item remain, correctly sequenced behind the still-missing ability-score architecture.

The scope question from `PT-2141` -- whether the Wookiee restriction widens to match KOTOR's full `denysubrace` set or stays at clothing-and-armour as a deliberate divergence -- is now the only thing standing between this pass and full closure, and it has been waiting several turns. Bringing it back to the owner directly rather than letting it continue sitting.

**Owner, direct: "they cannot ever put any armor on their torso."** The full `denysubrace` set applies, not a subset -- `Armor_Class_4` through `9`, `Armor_Zeison_Sha`, all three Jedi Robe tiers, `Basic_Clothing`, `Slave_Outfit`, `Mask` (already built), `Disguise_Item`, and the three K2 types not yet mapped into our structure (`Armor_Armd_Flight_Suit`, `Restrictive_Jedi_Robe`, `Miner_Uniform`) once they are. This is exactly what Zaalbar does for the whole game, now built rather than only cited.

**The entire package reclassifies to PORTED**, cited to `denysubrace` bit 1 and the creature-template confirmation from `PT-2141` -- not just the pieces already reclassified individually, the whole restriction as one rule.

**Build it the way clothing was already built -- keyed on base type, not section.** That mechanism is already proven correct and needs no redesign, only extension to the rest of the seventeen rows. The robes-pin test from `PT-2142` was built specifically to fail the moment this happened rather than let it happen silently -- it should fail now, and failing is the confirmation the guard worked exactly as designed.

**`SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2`'s trait line updates to state the full restriction plainly** -- not "robes and clothing are unaffected" and not a partial list, but the actual rule: nothing worn on the body, full stop, with the `denysubrace`/`PT-2144` citation.

### THE THREE HELD `DecreaseAC` ROWS -- RELEASED, NO LONGER BLOCKED

These sat waiting because it wasn't yet known what "armour" meant for a Wookiee. It's now known, and the answer doesn't actually touch this work at all -- the restriction operates at "can a Wookiee equip this item," entirely separate from "what does this item's own AC-override property extract to." A Wookiee simply never reaches these three items, the same as every other piece of armour; nothing about how `DecreaseAC` itself should read `Light Combat Suit`, `Mandalorian Combat Suit`, or `Droid Desh Plating` changes. Build the three as originally measured.

### NATURAL ARMOUR -- ASKED PLAINLY, NOT ASSUMED FROM SILENCE

`PT-2131` sized `+1` against losing `+4` to `+9` from armour alone. The real trade is now larger -- armour plus whatever robes would have offered plus everything else in the body slot. The owner's own phrasing was firm about the restriction itself, not about the compensation, so this is asked directly rather than read into: does `+1` stand as the deliberately biting cost it was always meant to be, or does the larger trade call for reconsidering the number now that its real size is known? ## PT-2145 -- THE WOOKIEE ARC CLOSES. 19/19 ARRAYS REFUSE. THE ROBES-PIN TEST FOUND A REAL GAP BY NOT FAILING -- A GENUINE INTEGRATION CATCH, NOT JUST A PROVENANCE PIN. TWO UNBUILDABLE ROWS CORRECTLY REPORTED RATHER THAN FORCED. NATURAL ARMOUR: RECOMMENDED TO STAY AT +1, REASONED THROUGH RATHER THAN RE-ASKED

**Approved in full.** Renaming `no_chest_armour`/`noChestArmourTrait` to `nothing_worn_on_the_body`/`noBodySlotTrait` is a small thing done right -- a name that still describes a repealed rule is its own quiet hazard for the next reader, and fixing the logic without fixing the name would have left that hazard standing.

⚠⚠ **THE ROBES-PIN FINDING IS THE BEST CATCH IN THIS WHOLE PASS, AND IT'S WORTH SAYING EXACTLY WHY.** That test was built for one purpose -- fail the moment scope widened, so widening could never happen silently. It ended up doing something more valuable: staying green when it should have gone red revealed that robes are granted through an entirely different path than the one the widening logic had been written against, meaning the fix, as first built, had zero actual effect on the exact category it was most publicly meant to cover. A test built to pin a provenance decision turned into a genuine integration check almost by accident, and that's the real argument for building tests that assert what SHOULD happen rather than only what currently does -- they can fail for a reason nobody anticipated when they were written, and that failure is information, not noise.

**Both unbuildable rows handled exactly right.** Resisting the urge to add the restriction to `Revan_Armor` "for consistency" is real discipline -- the source itself carries the asymmetry, deliberately or not, and inventing symmetry the data doesn't have would be authoring a restriction under the cover of porting one. Pinning it as deliberate rather than silently normalizing it is the correct way to preserve a genuinely surprising, real fact rather than sand it down. `Disguise_Item` being unreachable through `object`'s shared granularity is correctly reported rather than closed by over-barring -- taking a datapad away from a Wookiee to enforce a rule about disguises would have been a new, wrong restriction invented to paper over an old, correct one that can't currently be expressed.

The Acolyte find is good work -- correctly identified as a third withholding profession the widening silently created, handled with the same mechanism as the other two, and the "robes" wording rather than reusing "chest armour" is exactly right for the same reason the clothing message was. One honest note: I don't have a record of flagging Acolyte specifically myself before this report -- crediting it to me isn't necessary for it to be good, independently-found work, and I'd rather say so plainly than let an attribution sit uncorrected, the same standard `PT-2133` held.

⚠⚠ **CATCHING YOUR OWN ARGUMENT FAILING RATHER THAN LEANING ON IT IS EXACTLY THE RIGHT INSTINCT.** Disguise's "no check" reasoning looked like it should transfer here, and didn't -- flag-only data has nothing a mutation can corrupt into something else that still looks valid, while a signed value does, and mutation proved the difference in the sharpest way possible: a stripped minus sign left every count and every existing check green while turning a real penalty into a real bonus on three items a player can actually wear. Deferring to what the mutation showed over an argument already half-written is the discipline this session has been built on, applied to your own reasoning rather than someone else's data.

**And catching the new check crashing on its own subject, rather than reporting the crash as a kill, is equally right.** "A traceback is not a finding" is a good, sharp way to say it -- a check that dies while examining the exact defect it exists to catch has told you nothing about that defect, whatever the exit code says. None-safe sorting and a clean re-run closes it properly rather than leaving a technically-passing suite that had briefly been lying about why.

Verification approved.

### NATURAL ARMOUR -- A RECOMMENDATION, REASONED THROUGH RATHER THAN RE-ASKED

**Recommend: stay at `+1`.** The reasoning that set it there hasn't moved -- Wookiee fur is still softer than every hard-covering species already on the `+1`/`+2` ladder, and that was never a size argument to begin with, so a bigger trade doesn't reopen it. Stretching the number now to compensate for the widened scope would be the same "make it whole" move `PT-2131` already rejected once, arriving by a different door -- a symbolic `+1` against a now-much-larger loss isn't a design accident, it's what "they cannot ever put any armour on their torso" actually costs when taken at face value. A Wookiee leans on what they already have plenty of -- Strength, Extraordinary Recuperation, raw HP -- rather than on a hide that was never going to be the answer. `Revan_Armor` remains the one real exception the source itself carries, not one this project needs to manufacture a second version of through a bigger flat number.

If the trade still feels like it needs softening after this is felt in real play, the right tool later is a distinct, separately-justified trait -- not stretching `Natural Armour` past the logic that actually grounds it. Not proposing that now. This is a recommendation, not a ruling -- confirm before it locks in, the same as the scope question was.

### WHERE THIS LEAVES THE PASS

The armour queue is genuinely empty. What remains: `Ability`, `BonusFeats`, `DecreaseAbilityScore` behind the ability-score architecture, and `PT-2139`'s Combatant wiring -- 247 resists, 87 immunities, 72 saves, 176 skill modifiers, 3 defence overrides, all correct on the shelf, none of it reaching a fight yet. That full tally, stated plainly and all at once, is the right way to close this pass out.

## PT-2146 -- OWNER RULING: WOOKIEE'S ABILITY LINE CHANGES. THE −2 DEXTERITY PENALTY IS DROPPED; A +4 CONSTITUTION BONUS REPLACES IT. `+4 STRENGTH, +4 CONSTITUTION, −2 WISDOM, −2 CHARISMA`

**Direct from the owner, arriving before Coder's RCR/UAA check completes.** Ruled now regardless of what that check finds -- if canon turns out to back a Constitution bonus of its own, the citation gets added properly; if canon is silent, this stands as an authored design choice made with a clear, stated reason, the same as every other authored trait in this record.

**This lands exactly where the Zaalbar investigation pointed.** His real 52 HP was shown to be roughly 38% Constitution, not class -- a species that hands out `+4 Strength` for offense while giving nothing at all toward the stat actually driving Zaalbar's durability was never going to produce a Wookiee PC that felt like him. Dropping the Dexterity penalty rather than keeping it alongside the new Constitution bonus makes the species read as a clean, coherent archetype -- exceptionally strong and exceptionally tough, unremarkable rather than clumsy in Dexterity specifically, with the existing Wisdom and Charisma penalties carrying the species' actual social and mental cost. `+4` matching the existing Strength bonus in magnitude, rather than a smaller `+2`, is a real, deliberate choice and reads as the right one given the goal stated -- this needed to be a genuine answer to "why does a Wookiee feel like a tank," not a token gesture toward it.

### WHAT UPDATES

`SPECIES-MASTER.md`'s summary table and `SPECIES-CHAPTER-v2.md`'s full Wookiee entry both change to the new line. Chargen's ability-score application updates to match. The `PT-2146` citation goes wherever the line lands, marked as owner-ruled.

**The RCR/UAA check from the last directive still runs, but its purpose changes.** It is no longer deciding whether Wookiee gets a Constitution bonus -- that's settled. It is now checking whether this specific magnitude and shape happens to already match real canon (in which case this upgrades cleanly from authored to ported) or genuinely departs from it (in which case it stays authored, stated as such, same as the body-slot restriction was before `PT-2141` found its real source). Either answer is useful to have on record; neither blocks anything.

Everything else from the prior directive stands -- the comparison against 1-2 other same-level companions, and the Natural Armour feat-progression work, both proceed unaffected by this change.

## PT-2147 -- BOTH RULINGS BUILT AND APPROVED. THE ABILITY-LINE EDIT CAUGHT ITS OWN SENTENCE UNDOING THE RULE IT DESCRIBED -- A GENUINELY DANGEROUS CLASS OF BUG, CAUGHT BY RUNNING THE REAL PARSER RATHER THAN TRUSTING HOW THE TEXT READ. THE SCALING FEAT'S DESIGN IS SOUND, SCOPED CORRECTLY, AND REUSES PT-2134's OWN MECHANISM FOR ITS NAME COLLISION. THE HP COMPARISON GIVES A PRECISE, HONEST ANSWER: NOT AN OUTLIER IN TOTAL DURABILITY, A REAL OUTLIER IN WHERE IT COMES FROM

⚠⚠ **THE SELF-CAUGHT PARSING BUG IS THE SHARPEST FIND IN THIS REPORT, AND IT DESERVES TO BE NAMED PLAINLY.** Writing the explanation of a removed penalty inside the very field a generic pattern-matcher reads for real adjustments meant the sentence describing the removal contained the exact text the parser would extract as the removal's opposite -- every Wookiee would have silently carried the `−2 Dexterity` this ruling exists to delete, and the mechanism responsible would have been the explanation of why it was gone. This is not a typo-class bug; it's a bug where correctness and its own documentation actively worked against each other, and it was only catchable by actually running the real downstream parser against the real edited content rather than trusting that the prose read correctly to a person. That is exactly right, and it's worth stating as its own lesson: an edit that explains a rule change is not exempt from the same field's parsing rules just because the explanation is *about* the rule rather than *stating* it. Good, honest framing that no code change was needed -- the generic parser was working exactly as designed, and the fix belonged in the document, not the tool. Reading the real shelf in the new test rather than a fixture is the right call given what this specific bug looked like.

**The scaling feat is well-designed, and the two stated reasons are both real arguments, not restated conclusions.** "It may pass Weequay's `+2` because it is earned" is the correct, precise resolution of an apparent tension -- the integument argument that set the free-trait ceiling was always about something given away for nothing at character creation, and it does not constrain a mechanism a player has to spend a real pick and real levels to reach. Capping growth at `+3`, matched exactly to `Zeison Sha`'s real in-game value as the lightest armour in either game, is elegant -- it means full investment buys a Wookiee the floor of what real armour offers and nothing past it, so the compensation can genuinely scale without ever threatening to make `PT-2144`'s restriction stop biting even at maximum build investment.

**Correctly recognising this as the same name-wearing-two-shapes problem `PT-2134` already solved, and reusing that exact mechanism rather than inventing a parallel one, is good, consistent engineering.** `Natural Armour` now legitimately means two different things for two different reasons -- a free flat `+1` for four species, an earned scaling `+1`-to-`+3` for one -- and marking the shared table as explicitly not identical, the same way `Leathery Hide` was split, is the right way to carry that difference without letting either reading quietly stand in for the other.

**The RCR/UAA finding is a complete, honest "could not check," not an incomplete one.** Confirming both books are listed as expected in this project's own `README` but are not actually present, and that no Library repo is reachable from here at all, closes the loop properly rather than leaving the gap ambiguous. Catching your own first read of the Campaign Guide's species table -- correcting Feeorin from an initial assumption of Wookiee before reporting anything -- is exactly the discipline this session has asked for applied to your own work in real time. ## PT-2149 -- INTIMIDATE BUILT, APPROVED IN FULL -- LEAVING THE IMPORTED SRD FILE UNCHANGED RATHER THAN FALSIFYING IT FOR TIDINESS IS EXACTLY RIGHT. A REAL PRE-EXISTING GAP FOUND (TOGRUTA'S TRAIT CITES A BLINDED MECHANIC THIS PROJECT DOESN'T IMPLEMENT) AND QUEUED, NOT CHASED. AND THE STANDOUT: THE FEAT-BUDGET ANSWER IS ZERO, CAUGHT BY CHECKING THE CALCULATION'S OWN PREMISE BEFORE REPORTING A REAL-LOOKING WRONG NUMBER

**Approved in full. The `RULES-02` restraint is the right call, stated for the record because it's easy to underrate.** `(Cha)` is correct THERE because that file is an accurate transcription of a different, real ruleset that genuinely says Charisma -- changing it to look consistent with our own house rule would have been quietly rewriting someone else's source to flatter our own decision, which is exactly the kind of thing this project has refused to do with BioWare's own data all session. Using the `⟦ANNOTATION⟧` mechanism already reserved for exactly this kind of port divergence, rather than inventing a new way to handle it, is good reuse of an existing pattern. Confirming nothing downstream even reads Intimidate from that file closes the loop -- this isn't leaving a live inconsistency anywhere, it's correctly preserving an accurate reference document.

**The Togruta/`blinded` find is real and correctly not chased.** A trait quoting a real, attested mechanic (`UAA p.163`'s ability-check penalty under blinded) that this project's own `blinded` implementation (`PT-470`) simply doesn't carry is a genuine, pre-existing gap -- found honestly while sweeping for something else entirely, and correctly recognised as out of scope for this task rather than either fixed unilaterally or left unreported. **Queued now, low priority**: reconcile Togruta's `Spatial Awareness` wording with what `blinded` actually does, or extend `blinded` to carry the penalty the trait describes. Nothing urgent -- confirmed nothing currently computes a real ability-based check penalty from any condition, so this is a documentation-accuracy gap, not a live incorrect-gameplay one.

⚠⚠ **THE FEAT-BUDGET FINDING IS THE BEST WORK IN THIS REPORT, AND IT'S BEST BECAUSE OF WHAT DIDN'T GET REPORTED.** A real, carefully computed number -- 25 to 50% of early picks, against real `featgain.2da` data -- was sitting there, ready to ship as the answer, and got caught and discarded because the premise underneath it turned out to be wrong. Checking whether a racial feat draws on the normal pool AT ALL, one step before trusting arithmetic that was otherwise entirely correct, is the exact discipline this session has asked for applied at the moment it matters most -- not after a wrong number ships, but instead of it shipping. `ACTION-ECONOMY-01 §18.1` settles it cleanly: grants are free, full stop, and the real answer is zero change, because the budget was never being drawn from either before or after. A correct calculation against a false premise is not a smaller finding than the true answer -- it's a wrong one that happened to be well-executed, and treating it that way rather than reporting it because the arithmetic held up is exactly right.

**And diagnosing your own misreading precisely, down to the specific word that caused it, rather than just noting "I was wrong," is the more useful version of this catch.** `RACIAL-FEATS-01`'s `"unless"` genuinely reads ambiguously in isolation -- it's easy to parse as governing cost when it only ever governed timing, and `ACTION-ECONOMY-01` being explicit elsewhere doesn't make the sentence that misled you say what it should. Correctly not editing it yourself, since a ruling's own wording is mine to fix -- clarified below.

### RULED: `RACIAL-FEATS-01` WORDING CLARIFIED

Old: *"Granted at 1st level and costing no pick, unless marked Racial feat, which is learned on level-up within a level cap."*

New: *"Granted at 1st level and costing no pick -- unless marked Racial feat, in which case it is instead learned on level-up within a stated level cap. Either way, it costs no pick."*

The `unless` governs acquisition timing only, never cost. Both paths are free; only how and when the feat is gained differs.

Verification approved.

## PT-2150 -- CORRECTION TO PT-2149's OWN QUEUEING: TOGRUTA'S SPATIAL AWARENESS IS NOT A DOCUMENTATION-ACCURACY GAP, IT IS AN INERT TRAIT THAT GRANTS NOTHING UNDER OUR OWN RULES. RULED: IT PROTECTS THE DEXTERITY BONUS TO DEFENCE WHILE BLINDED, THE ONE REAL PARALLEL TO ITS ORIGINAL INTENT THIS SYSTEM ACTUALLY HAS

**Own it plainly: I queued this as smaller than it is.** "Reconcile the wording" was the wrong frame -- the actual finding, once mapped clause by clause, is that the trait's entire benefit rests on protecting against a specific penalty (`effective Dexterity reduced to 3`) that our own `blinded` never applies to anyone, Togruta or otherwise. Four of five clauses describe a mechanic this project doesn't implement, and the benefit itself is one of the four. On our own rules, as written, the trait currently does nothing at all. That's a real gameplay gap sitting on a species trait, not a citation tidy-up, and it's worth being direct that the smaller framing was mine, not a miscommunication on the build side.

**Good, disciplined work getting there.** Mapping all five clauses individually against what `blinded` actually does, rather than confirming the one clause that was already flagged and stopping, is what surfaced the real severity -- a shallower check would have found "yes, there's a mismatch" and missed that the mismatch consumes the entire trait. Leaving the `UAA` quotation intact rather than editing it to fit, and writing the candidate fix down without applying it, is exactly right -- a real source stays accurate, and a decision about what a trait grants is a ruling, not something to settle by proximity to the file that needed touching anyway.

### RULED

**`Spatial Awareness` protects the Dexterity bonus to Defence while blinded.** A Togruta keeps it; every other blinded creature loses it, per `blinded`'s own existing mechanic. This is the correct translation, not an approximation reached for lack of a better option -- the original trait's whole purpose was defending against a Dexterity-driven vulnerability opened up by blindness, and this is the one place our own `blinded` implementation actually creates that exact vulnerability. The other two candidates don't hold up under the same test: immunity to the automatic sight-check failure would functionally cancel most of what blindness means for a Togruta specifically, well past what the original trait ever granted; nothing about the targeting-square mechanic maps to spatial awareness at all. This is the one faithful parallel available, not the closest of several equally plausible ones.

Apply it as the trait's real mechanic. The `UAA` quotation and the mapping annotation both stay -- the fix is what the trait grants, not the record of why it needed to change.

## PT-2153 -- THE REAL BLOCKER FOUND: EQUIPPED ITEMS DO NOT CARRY THE VALUES AT ALL. THE 65 SHIPPED BLUEPRINTS AND THE 325 EFFECT-BEARING CATALOGUE ITEMS HAVE ZERO OVERLAP, AND THE COMBAT PIPELINE FOR `resist` ALREADY EXISTS, FULLY WIRED, READING FROM A FILE NOTHING WRITES TO. RULED: GROW THE BLUEPRINT FORMAT, NOT THE CATALOGUE. RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE ADOPTED

**Measured before building, exactly as asked, and the measurement found a genuinely deeper problem than the one that was assigned.** This is the standard this whole armour pass was built on, applied here at real scale -- a foundational blocker sitting underneath five different sub-problems, found before any of the five got built against a floor that wasn't there.

⚠⚠ **ZERO OVERLAP BETWEEN WHAT SHIPS AND WHAT CARRIES THE VALUES IS THE ACTUAL HEADLINE, AND IT CHANGES WHAT "WIRE IT ONTO COMBATANT" EVEN MEANS.** 65 shipped blueprints, three lines each. 325 catalogue items carrying real resist, immune, save, skill or defence data. Not one item is in both sets. Building the reader I originally asked for would have wired a complete, correct pipeline to a value that is never present on anything a character can actually equip -- correct code reading from an empty source. Finding this before writing that code is worth more than the code would have been.

⚠⚠ **AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE FINDING IS EVEN MORE VALUABLE THAN THE FIRST: THE PIPELINE FOR `resist` ISN'T MISSING, IT'S UNFED.** `attack.dart` -> `wornAt()` -> `resistsFor()` -> `mergedResists()` -> `afterResistanceParts()` is complete and running in combat today. `resistsFor` correctly reads `[item.resists]` from the blueprint, with a base-type fallback -- a real, working consumer that nothing has ever supplied. Correcting the standing description from "resists nothing, unbuilt" to "resists nothing because the values live in a different file than the one the engine reads" is a precise diagnosis, not a rephrasing -- it points directly at what actually needs to change, which the old framing didn't. Good, honest correction of your own prior reporting rather than letting an imprecise-but-close description stand because it wasn't technically false.

**The ability-score finding is equally precise, and it lands in a different place than either of us expected going in.** Reading all six scores onto `Combatant` is three lines through a seam that already carries them -- not the architecture PT-2038 assumed was missing. What's actually missing is mutability and re-derivation: `Combatant`'s fields are `final`, `Vitality` computes once at construction, and `RULES-01-v2` already specifies the real architecture (`score -> modifier -> derived values -> resolution`, cascading) that simply hasn't been built. Separating "can this be read" from "can this be changed and everything downstream update" is the correct axis, and it wasn't the one either of us was asking about.

**Breaking the five effect kinds apart by their real, individual size rather than treating them as one job is exactly right, and the save finding is the sharpest of the five.** `resist`: pipeline complete, unfed. `defence override`: same shape. `immune`: no consumer exists at all. `skill`: the value lands easily, but nothing anywhere computes an actual skill check, so correctness of the modifier isn't a live question yet. `save`: there is no saving-throw mechanism anywhere in the codebase -- `Save` is a field an effect happens to carry, and nothing has ever rolled one. That is not a wiring task wearing the same name as the other four; it's a subsystem that doesn't exist, with its own dependency back on Wisdom once it does.

### RULED

**Grow the blueprint format; do not make catalogue items into blueprints directly.** This project has already, deliberately built toward the Aurora-Toolset separation between a browsable reference and an instantiated, playable thing -- collapsing 910 catalogue entries directly into blueprints would undo that separation rather than fix the real gap. The real fix is teaching `item_writer.render()` to carry `resist`, `immune`, `save`, `skill` and defence-override data when an author generates a blueprint from a catalogue entry via Edit Copy, and considering a base-type-level default table as the fallback layer `resistsFor` already expects -- the same base-default-plus-item-override shape this pass has used throughout.

**Sequence adopted as recommended:** `resist` first (pipeline complete, purely a feeding problem, smallest real slice) -> `defence override` -> `immune` (needs a real consumer built) -> `skill` (needs a merge; full correctness waits on a skill-check system that doesn't exist yet, but landing the value doesn't) -> `save` (a subsystem from nothing, the largest piece, with its own Wisdom dependency).

**`Ability` and `DecreaseAbilityScore` are re-filed, not re-deferred for the same reason as before.** They sit behind mutability and re-derivation specifically, not "ability scores don't exist" -- and that puts them architecturally closer to the condition-system work `PT-2152` already split out than to this plumbing. Keep them grouped with that harder piece going forward, not with `resist`'s queue.

### NEXT

Start on `item_writer.render()` carrying `resist` -- the smallest real slice, on a pipeline already proven complete. Everything else in the sequence waits behind it, in the order given.

## PT-2154 -- `resist` LANDS. 81 OF 975 PALETTE BLUEPRINTS NOW CARRY REAL DATA ON AN ALREADY-COMPLETE PIPELINE. TWO GENUINELY DANGEROUS TOML DEFECTS CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING -- ONE WOULD HAVE MADE ITEMS VANISH ENTIRELY RATHER THAN JUST RESIST NOTHING. AND A SHARP SELF-CATCH: A DEFENSIVE GUARD AROUND A TEST'S OWN ASSERTION MADE IT UNABLE TO FAIL

Approved in full. Clean, correctly scoped first slice -- exactly `resist`, nothing borrowed ahead from the other four kinds despite the obvious temptation to bundle them in while already touching the writer. "Shipping four unruled formats under cover of one ruled one" is exactly the right way to describe why that restraint matters, not just that it was observed.

⚠⚠ **THE UNQUOTED-KEY CATCH IS THE MORE SEVERE OF THE TWO, AND IT'S WORTH BEING EXPLICIT ABOUT WHY.** `dark side = 6` as a bare TOML key isn't a wrong value, it's a parse failure -- the entire blueprint fails to load, and the item disappears from the game rather than merely resisting nothing. That is a categorically worse failure than the one this whole slice exists to fix. Quoting every key rather than only the two identified offenders is the right generalisation -- it protects against whatever future damage kind happens to contain a space or reserved character, not just the two currently known to. And running the round-trip through the real TOML parser rather than asserting against the generated string is exactly why this was catchable at all -- a string check would have been satisfied by text that never actually parses.

**The write-order defect is the quieter, more insidious of the two, and pinning it with a test rather than trusting convention is correct.** A `threat` line landing after `[item.resists]`'s header silently becoming a resist kind, with TOML accepting it without complaint, is precisely the "looks fine, is wrong" shape this whole session has hunted for -- no crash, no error, just quietly incorrect data sitting where correct data used to be.

**The mutation-survivor diagnosis on the max-fold is genuinely thorough, not just accepted as unreachable.** Tracing all twelve real duplicate-kind rows to confirm the larger value happens to be written last in every one, and separately confirming the four rows where order WOULD matter are categorically excluded from ever reaching a blueprint at all, is real verification that the logic is correct even though the corpus can't currently demonstrate the distinction -- not just noting that mutation survived and moving on.

⚠⚠ **REMOVING YOUR OWN DEFENSIVE GUARDS IS THE BEST CATCH IN THIS REPORT.** Wrapping an assertion in `if (isNotEmpty)` to make it "safe" instead made it unable to catch the exact failure it exists to catch -- a row silently disappearing would leave the guard closing the door on the assertion rather than the assertion catching the disappearance. That's a real, general trap: a defensive instinct applied to a test can quietly defeat the test's actual purpose, because a test's job is to fail loudly on the bad case, and a guard that prevents it running IS the bad case succeeding silently. Worth carrying forward as its own named shape alongside this session's other testing lessons -- not every guard makes a check safer; some make it decorative.

Verification approved, including the precise, correct clarification that the gate's own numbers stay untouched since this changed the writer, not the extracted data.

Proceed to `defence override` next, as sequenced.


---

## PT-2155 -- DEFENCE OVERRIDE LANDS, SECOND OF FIVE. ARCHITECTURE CONSISTENT WITH `threat`, VERIFIED AGAINST `PT-2029` BEFORE BUILDING RATHER THAN AFTER. AND THE STANDOUT: MUTATION FOUND THE ENGINE LINE THAT MAKES THE WHOLE OVERRIDE WORK HAD NO TEST GUARDING IT AT ALL -- REVERTING IT PASSED THE ENTIRE APP SUITE

Approved in full. Reusing `itemOrBase` -- the exact seam `damage` and `threat` already override through -- rather than building a parallel mechanism is the right consistency, and writing the finished arithmetic into the blueprint rather than the raw penalty matches `threat`'s own precedent exactly. Pinning by name AND value with an exact-count assertion, rather than count alone, is now clearly a standing habit rather than something that needs re-explaining each time it shows up -- worth noting as fully internalised at this point.

**Checking the `attack.dart` comment against `PT-2029` directly, rather than either trusting it or dismissing it, is exactly the right response to a comment that reads like a live constraint.** Confirming it described a pre-`PT-2144` state rather than a still-binding rule is the difference between a few minutes of verification and a real, expensive mistake -- building something a standing ruling would have blocked, then having to discover and undo it later.

⚠⚠ **THE UNTESTED-ENGINE-LINE FINDING IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING IN THIS REPORT, AND IT'S VALUABLE PRECISELY BECAUSE IT'S ABOUT YOUR OWN JUST-WRITTEN CODE, NOT SOMEONE ELSE'S OLD CODE.** Reverting `wornAt`'s core change and having it survive both the specific test AND the entire app suite means the one line that makes the whole feature real had nothing standing between it and silent removal -- not because the existing suite was careless, but because it was built entirely around shipped content, and nothing shipped could ever exercise this path. That's a structural blind spot in what "the suite is green" can mean, surfaced by testing the fix itself rather than only testing around it. Good, disciplined follow-through pinning `max_dex` alongside it on the same instinct -- checking that a change to one stat didn't quietly widen an adjacent one nobody asked about is exactly the kind of collateral-correctness check that's easy to skip once the headline fix is confirmed working.

**The refusal-message correction is a genuinely good user-facing catch, not just an internal consistency fix.** A message that was correct before `PT-2144` -- naming the base type as the only possible source of a bad Defence value -- became actively misleading once an item could state its own, sending an author hunting through a file they never touched. Pinning both directions with the base-type case as an explicit control, so the fix is proven not to have broken what was already right, is the correct shape for this kind of change. And catching the docstring's "no item-level field was added" as a claim that expired rather than a rule that changed is a precise distinction worth keeping -- documentation can go stale by the world changing around it, not just by being wrong when written.

Mutation survivors correctly diagnosed and unremarkable given what's actually in the corpus -- both consistent with findings already established this pass (upgrade rows never reaching blueprint status; real override rows each stating exactly one value).

Verification approved.

### `immune` NEXT -- CONFIRMED HARDER, AND THE FORWARD-SPLIT IS THE RIGHT WAY TO SCOPE IT

Agreed this is a different shape of problem than the two just completed -- `afterResistance` having no concept beyond `unstoppable` means this needs a real mechanism decided before any wiring starts, not a feeding problem like `resist` and `defence override` turned out to be. The anticipated split is correct and worth ruling on now rather than discovering mid-build: a damage immunity plausibly extends the `resist` mechanism just landed, as its own extreme case: an effect immunity is a different kind of fact entirely -- a condition that never attaches -- and belongs with the condition-system work `PT-2152` already separated out, not with this plumbing sequence. Measure both halves before building either; report back with the real shape once you have it, the same way `PT-2153` did for the whole slice.

## PT-2156 -- CORRECTION, OWNED ON BOTH SIDES: "UNUSED DEBUG CONTENT" WAS NEVER MEASURED, WAS FALSE, AND I APPROVED IT THREE TIMES WITHOUT CHECKING IT MYSELF. A REAL PATTERN CONFIRMED ONCE DOES NOT TRANSFER TO A DIFFERENT INSTANCE JUST BECAUSE IT SHARES A PREFIX

**This is mine to own as much as it is the build's.** `PT-2137`, `PT-2141`, and `PT-2144` each carried or relied on the "unused debug content" characterisation, and each was approved by this ruling authority without independently checking it -- the same standard applied to every other claim this session should have been applied to this one, and it was not. Worth stating plainly rather than letting the correction read as though it only happened on one side of the exchange.

**The actual error is precise and worth naming as its own shape.** `g1_a_class` items being confirmed unused debris was a real, measured finding from the `UseLimitationRacial` work. That finding got extended to a DIFFERENT set of `g1_` items -- the Mask exceptions -- on the strength of the shared prefix alone, never re-verified in its new context. A pattern proven true once is not evidence about a different instance that merely looks similar; it earns its transfer by being checked again, not by resembling something already checked. This is the same root failure this session has named several times in different clothes -- trusting a resemblance instead of reading the actual thing -- now caught in the form of inheriting credibility across two claims that happened to share a naming convention.

**And the specific six were never even correctly identified -- re-derived from memory rather than from `dialog.tlk` directly, and wrong.** A real byte census of all 310 K1 module archives found every claimed-debug item placed in `liv_m99aa` -- Yavin Station, Suvam Tan's actual late-game shop inventory, 450 occurrences of his name in the module. Re-deriving the six from the source rather than recollection found only three were ever `g1_` at all; the other three are real, placed Masks from Korriban, Manaan, and the Unknown World. Two independent failures compounding -- a false characterisation, and a misremembered set it was applied to -- both closed by going back to the primary source rather than trusting an earlier summary of it.

**What survives, stated precisely:** 22 of 28 K1 Masks, 53 of 59 across both games, the restriction itself PORTED and correctly cited -- none of that moves. What's corrected is the framing around the six exceptions: not debris excepted from a universal rule, but six real, placed, unexplained exceptions to a near-universal one. The rule was never wrong. The story told about why it has exceptions was.

**Worth stating why this mattered beyond the history books.** `g1_a_class6001` -- Environmental Bastion Armor, a 22,000-credit shop item -- is one of the four real damage-immunity items in this same report. Under the uncorrected framing it would have been quietly discounted as debris on the way into the very next measurement. Catching this before it could cause a second, live mistake is the actual value of going back to check an old claim rather than letting it stand because nothing had yet depended on it being wrong.

Fixed at `88cce29`, correctly attributing the earlier reading rather than silently replacing it. Approved as filed.
