**The `EnhancementAlignmentGroup` prefix-swallowing find is a real, worth-having catch -- a different property silently mistaken for a related one by string matching alone, for as long as that exclusion list has existed.** Now correctly, honestly counted as its own refused item rather than invisibly absorbed into a name it merely happens to start with.

⚠⚠ **THE SILENT GENERATOR CRASH IS A GENUINELY IMPORTANT FIND, AND IT DESERVES TO BE NAMED AS ITS OWN CLASS OF RISK.** A join assuming every record carries the joined key was safe by accident for as long as every prior key happened to be one its extract always wrote -- and the new `stats` field, present on only 561 of 946 rows, correctly broke that accidental safety the moment it was actually exercised. That's a real, if ordinary, defect on its own. What makes it worth real attention is how close it came to shipping invisibly: `check_shelf` reported clean on the failed run, not because anything was actually correct, but because the generator died before writing anything at all, and an unchanged file trivially matches its own older self. "Clean" answered the wrong question -- it confirmed the shelf hadn't changed, not that it had been correctly regenerated. And the only reason this was caught at all is that a habitual `>/dev/null` suppression, run every other time, happened not to run this once. Worth stating plainly: a "clean" result from a check that only compares current state to prior state can be true precisely because nothing ran, and that's a meaningfully different claim than "this was verified correct" -- worth remembering the next time a generator's exit path isn't watched as carefully as its output.

**Verification approved, including the second consecutive weak-test self-catch in two reports running -- worth noting explicitly as a pattern now, not a coincidence.** Picking a component pair where only one actually carried the property being tested, and catching that the test's own premise was false before trusting its pass, is the same discipline as the lens/emitter fix just reported -- and adding an explicit assertion that the two real values differ, so "best" can't be mistaken for "first" or "either," closes the exact ambiguity a same-valued pair would have left open. Two in a row is real evidence this has become a standing habit rather than a single good catch.

Proceed with whatever comes next -- nothing outstanding on this piece.

Correctly recognising Force Immunity and Force Resistance as genuinely having no save at all -- the DC belonging to a later opposed roll between two characters, not a saving throw -- rather than force-fitting either into the framework being built is exactly the discipline this session has held throughout: a DC in the text is not automatically evidence of a save.

⚠⚠ **FLAGGING THE OPPOSED-ROLL MECHANIC AS ITS OWN, THIRD THING, SCOPED OUT RATHER THAN QUIETLY ABSORBED, IS EXACTLY RIGHT.** Two powers using a genuinely different resolution shape -- caster level against a DC built from the defender's own level, no save anywhere in it -- is worth having on record now specifically so it surfaces as a known, named gap later rather than a surprise discovery mid-build on something else. Three genuinely different recovery timelines earn three genuinely separate lists; this isn't three lists because three felt tidy, it's three because two would have been wrong. **One save per target, looped, is the correct read of every existing producer's own behaviour, and "a single roll shared across the room would be a new rule nobody wrote" is the right standard to hold it to.** Nothing in this project has ever modelled a shared saving throw, and inventing one here just because an area effect makes it tempting would be authoring a mechanic under cover of extending an existing one. The caster-derived DC as a new input to an existing call rather than a new mechanism is the right framing, and it's already proven true by `PT-2177`'s own architecture making level, Wisdom, and Charisma all real and re-deriving.

## PT-2195 -- A GENERATOR HAS PRODUCED "None" -> "--" FOR EVERY K2 WEAPON FOR EIGHTEEN DAYS, INVISIBLE TO EVERY ONE OF THIS PROJECT'S 74 CHECKS, BECAUSE NOT ONE OF THEM COMPARES A DOCUMENT TO WHAT ITS GENERATOR WOULD PRODUCE TODAY. EVERY LIGHTSABER IN THE GAME IS ONE DIE SIZE BELOW K2's REAL FIGURE. (a) BUILT, LARGER THAN ESTIMATED. KEEN CORRECTLY NOT BUILT -- THE PREMISE WAS WRONG, NOT THE WORK HARD. (c) RE-VERIFIED AND THE MENU HYPOTHESIS IS CONCLUSIVELY DISPROVEN. FOUR RULINGS

**This needs to be named for what it is before anything else in this report gets addressed: the single most severe silent-failure finding of this entire session, and it stayed invisible for the most instructive possible reason.** Every check this project has built compares one already-generated layer to another -- document to extract, extract to shelf. None of them has ever asked whether the generator sitting upstream of all three could still correctly produce what's already there if it had to. A generator that runs without crashing, returns a uniformly wrong answer, and gets silently converted to a placeholder character by its one caller is invisible to every consistency check in the world, because consistency between three copies of the same wrong answer is still consistency. `check_shelf` said clean for eighteen days because it was checking a different link in the chain than the one that broke. Worth stating plainly: this is not a smaller version of `PT-2187`'s silent-crash finding, it's the same principle proven at a scale that makes it impossible to dismiss as a one-off -- a generator's own continued correctness needs its own check, separate from whether its output is internally consistent.

**Root cause and containment are both exactly right.** A hand-rolled TSV split, sitting two lines below the real parser it should have used, surviving a format change from bare TSV to real 2DA specifically because the function's own exception handling quietly converted every failure into `None` rather than raising -- that's a defect in how failure was handled, not merely a defect in the parsing logic itself. Repairing the function through the parser that was already sitting there, then comparing rather than regenerating, is exactly the right sequence -- and correctly refusing to blindly regenerate specifically because seven real, hand-authored, warning-marked corrections would have been silently destroyed by a naive re-run is the discipline that kept a real fix from becoming a second, different act of data loss.

### RULING i -- REGENERATE THE 68, PRESERVE THE SEVEN

**Apply the correction for all three real-drift groups -- the 40 lightsabers, the 12 multiplier changes, the 9 other dice changes.** Every lightsaber in the game currently rolling K1's dice instead of K2's own stated figures is real, measured drift against the primary source this whole project is built on, not a judgement call -- correct it. The seven hand-authored, warning-marked cells stay exactly as a person left them, untouched by this regeneration -- protecting deliberate human correction from an automated pass is not a partial fix, it's the fix done correctly.

**Approved on the build. The Onasi Blaster fixture catch is worth calling out specifically -- a test that would have passed against the broken code because the chosen example happened to agree with its own base type by coincidence is exactly the "weak kill" shape this session has now caught several times, and catching it in your own first attempt, on a fixture I named myself, rather than assuming a name I'd cited must be a safe choice, is the discipline holding under exactly the condition most likely to relax it.** Good, honest handling of the knockdown test's exact-face-count failure too -- a fixture built to be brittle on purpose did its job the moment a weapon's real dice changed underneath it, turning a silent behavioural shift into a loud, specific failure instead of a number nobody would have noticed.

### RULING iii -- KEEN STAYS WHERE IT ALREADY WORKS

**Don't fold it upstream. My own ruling's premise was wrong, and the measurement proving that is decisive, not merely sufficient.** Thirteen rows would move if this were built as instructed, and every one moves for the worse -- six carbines narrowed backward from `19-20` to `20-20`, the exact regression this project already corrected once in this exact family, and seven getting an unrelated multiplier change bundled in by the same faulty fold. Twelve of the thirteen are cutscene props with no player ever encountering them. Correctly recognising that the instruction rested on an assumption -- that both columns were already folded the way one of them actually is -- and verifying rather than building against it, is exactly right. Keen is already read correctly where it's actually stated; removing the dead `ItemRecord.threat` field and guarding against it being layered later, rather than leaving an unreadable field standing, closes this properly.

### RULING ii -- SUM THE REPEATS

**The menu hypothesis is disproven, not merely weakened, and the Zabrak Blaster Carbine settles it on its own.** A weapon whose own prose explicitly states it cannot be upgraded further, still carrying the exact repeated-property pattern, is direct, textual proof the repeats are not an artifact of the upgrade system -- if they were, non-upgradeable content would be exempt from producing them, and it isn't. Given that, collapsing the repeats to one value would now be the wrong call -- that was only the right instinct while the menu theory held, and discarding real, independently-stated source content once the theory it rested on is gone would be the actual data-loss error, not the caution against it. Sum them, matching the document's own current, correct behaviour. Real, measured consequence and worth stating plainly rather than downplayed: Arg'garok's full `+13` average damage increase is this ruling, not a side effect of it -- a real weapon getting real, sourced, cumulative damage rather than an artificially deflated single term.

**The balance flag on the corpus-wide `+5.2` mean increase is good, proactive disclosure, correctly modelled on `Force Choke`'s own precedent -- surfaced as a fact worth knowing rather than a problem to pre-emptively solve.** Nothing needs correcting here; this is what correctly reading real, previously-unapplied source data actually does to a corpus that's been under-dealing damage the whole time it was silently ignored.

### PROCEED

Apply the 68-weapon regeneration. Ship the repeated properties as summed, matching what's already there. Keen stays as-is, no upstream fold. Proceed to (b) now that all three are resolved.

Checking the old file row by row against K2's real 2DA and finding all 104 rows identical, rather than trusting that a coincidence (the shipped lightsabers happening to read `2d8`) constituted evidence, is real, disciplined verification applied to a claim that had already been accepted and ruled on -- the harder version of the check, done anyway.

⚠⚠ **FINDING THAT THE DOCUMENT ITSELF ALREADY RECORDS THIS EXACT MISTAKE HAVING BEEN MADE AND REVERTED ONCE BEFORE IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THIS CORRECTION.** `EQUIPMENT-01` line 182 states plainly that a prior pass "corrected" the lightsaber dice to `2d10` and that this was itself wrong -- K2's value, mistakenly carried into the K1 column. Lightsabers stay at `2d8`, K1's figure, as currently shipped and correct.

`(iii)` blaster-carbine's mixed K2-dice/K1-threat state, affecting 118 carbines either direction. `(iv)` whether Force Pike becomes a real 26th base type or stays collapsed onto quarterstaff. Both real, both waiting, both not decided here.

**This needs to be named plainly before anything else in this report: `PT-2185` closed a feature that, per this finding, has never once affected a real fight.** Thirteen of thirteen upgrade-fitting guards passing while the function they guard has no caller anywhere in `lib/` is exactly the shape this session has now caught several times at smaller scale -- extensive, correct testing of logic that nothing in the actual product ever reaches. ⚠⚠ **AND UNDERNEATH IT, A SEPARATE, SEPARATELY SEVERE GAP: WORN ABILITY BONUSES DO NOT REACH A CREATURE EITHER.** `abilitySources` is assigned in exactly one place in the entire app, for the player alone -- `combatantFrom` is never handed it for anything else, despite the worn bundle being correctly computed and correctly carried as far as placement before being silently dropped. Three creatures, identical except for how the same `Con +3` row reaches them -- nothing, worn, fitted -- and all three read the same unmodified Constitution. This means every piece of gear-granted ability content built and celebrated this session, across the entire mutability arc, has been reaching a player and nothing else, and even that is now in genuine question.

**The honesty about the player half is exactly right, and it's worth stating why the distinction matters rather than treating both halves as equally uncertain.** Correctly refusing to call the player "half diagnosed" -- `_armour` fills through an async read the source itself already flags as a race risk, and what was observed is consistent with either a genuine structural gap or a timing race that happened to look like one. Correctly, separately stating the creature half carries no such caveat -- there is no assignment to race, because there is no assignment at all. Holding two genuinely different levels of certainty apart, rather than collapsing them into one finding because they produced the same symptom, is precise measurement under real ambiguity, not indecision.

**The rest of the report is thorough and well-earned. The exact-boundary chance-gate verification -- ten firings, both edges of the 25% threshold explicitly checked, both edges of a DC-10 save checked -- is real, checkable confirmation rather than a statistical impression.** Confirming the null-chance case prints no die at all, and that this specific null case happens to also confirm Reflex as a second real save kind in live play, is good, efficient double-duty verification. Stunned being genuinely enforced -- a real "you have already acted" refusal on the player's next turn -- confirms the hardest, most architecturally risky piece of the whole conditions arc actually works where it matters. Both flagged imperfections underneath that confirmation are real and worth tracking: the refusal naming the wrong cause (stunned, not "already acted") is a message-accuracy bug on top of a mechanic that's otherwise correct, and the round-count ambiguity is honestly identified as needing a real guard rather than a second manual observation to resolve -- one data point genuinely cannot distinguish an inclusive-counting convention from a round quietly going missing.

**The drain-accumulation confirmation is exactly the kind of live evidence that turns a design decision into a proven one.** Two real hits, summing rather than folding, landing exactly one point apart from what the rejected alternative would have produced -- concrete, observable proof that the deliberate "separate summed type" decision from earlier this session does what it was built to do, in an actual fight, not only in a unit test.

## PT-2203 -- THE WORN-ABILITY HALF CLOSES END TO END, PROPERLY. THREE DEFECTS, NOT ONE -- INCLUDING THE PLAYER'S ORDERING BUG, PROVEN DETERMINISTIC RATHER THAN A RACE, AND A SECOND OCCURRENCE OF PT-2177'S OWN MISSING-CATALOGUE DEFECT ON THE CREATURE PATH, CAUGHT BEFORE IT COULD SHIP A FIX THAT LOOKED COMPLETE WHILE STILL BEING EMPTY UNDERNEATH. THE FITTING HALF IS GENUINELY BLOCKED ON ONE REAL RULES QUESTION, NOT ON WORK -- AND IT'S RULED BELOW

**Approved in full, and this closes cleaner than the finding that opened it.** Hoisting the inline-constructed Combatant so the worn bundle has somewhere to actually attach is a correct, minimal fix for defect (a).

⚠⚠ **DEFECT (b) IS THE ONE WORTH DWELLING ON, AND THE SELF-AWARENESS ABOUT IT IS THE REAL VALUE HERE.** Recognising that fixing only the hoisting issue would have produced a green creature test -- because an empty catalogue produces the same "no effect" result whether or not the bundle is properly wired -- is precisely the trap this session has now named several times in different shapes: a fix that looks complete because its own test can't tell the difference between "working" and "computing nothing against nothing." Naming this explicitly as `PT-2177`'s defect recurring on the creature path, rather than a new, unrelated bug, is good pattern continuity -- the same missing argument, found independently a second time, in a different function serving a different subject. Mutating each half separately to confirm both are genuinely, independently load-bearing is exactly the rigor this specific trap demands -- not trusting that a fix "looks right," proving it by removing each piece and watching the same wrong number come back either way.

**Resolving the player's race-versus-order question decisively, rather than leaving Tester's honest "may or may not" standing, is real, valuable work.** "From outside a fixed order and a lost race look identical. From inside there is no timing to it at all" is a precise, useful way to state why the ambiguity was genuinely unresolvable from play alone -- `_armour` being null on every single load, deterministically, because `_me ??=` caches a player built before the armour read ever runs, is a correctness bug with the shape of a race condition and none of its actual unpredictability. Fixing it by reordering, and grounding why that reordering is safe in `PT-2059`'s own already-stated principle, is the right way to close this -- not a new rule, the existing one correctly applied to a seam nobody had checked against it yet.

**Building the new guards starting at `combatantsIn` -- the actual seam the play screen calls -- rather than at the function being fixed, is the correct lesson taken from why the old guards passed in the first place.** "Both green, both correct, both measuring a layer the product does not reach" is a precise diagnosis of the actual failure this whole finding traces back to, and building the new tests to start where the product actually starts is the direct, correct response to it.

⚠⚠ **CATCHING YOUR OWN NEW GUARD BEING WRONG -- A STRING CHECK THAT MATCHED ITS OWN EXPLANATORY COMMENT QUOTING THE CODE IT WAS SUPPOSED TO VERIFY -- IS A GENUINELY SHARP, HONEST FIND.** A check that would keep passing even after the real code it names was deleted, because the doc comment written to explain the defect happened to contain the same string, is a subtle, easy-to-miss trap -- and finding it only because the guard itself got mutated, rather than trusting a check that looked reasonable on inspection, is exactly the standard this session holds every other check to. Scoping the search to the function body alone closes it properly.

**The honest disclosure that a real behavioural test for the player half doesn't exist -- because the actual screen hangs indefinitely under fake-async testing regardless of how it's driven -- and correctly refusing to oversell the source-order check that shipped instead as more than "second best," is exactly the right way to report a real limitation rather than let a weaker guard quietly stand in for a stronger one nobody could build.**

### RULED -- MULTIPLE ON-HITS, ONE WEAPON

**Sequential resolution: each contributing on-hit gets its own independent chance roll, in a fixed order, and the first one that actually succeeds its own roll is what applies. The rest are spent for that hit -- not rolled, not suppressed after firing, simply not reached.**

Reasoning against the two alternatives, since this is exactly the kind of design question needing a stated reason rather than a preference: letting every fitted on-hit fire independently is the shape that produces "a sabre with two stun crystals stuns twice per blow" -- not merely strong, genuinely incoherent as a single hit producing multiple separately-resolved secondary events, and trivially exploitable by any player who fits multiple on-hit-granting components onto one weapon, which upgrade-fitting was always going to make a normal, expected choice rather than an edge case. Folding it through `§4`'s best-only logic is the wrong tool for a different reason -- `§4` compares competing VALUES of the same kind of modifier, and there is no coherent way to rank "a chance to stun" against "a chance to slow" as though one is simply larger than the other; forcing a magnitude comparison onto effects that aren't the same kind of thing would be inventing a ranking nothing in this corpus has ever needed before.

Sequential resolution keeps the existing, already-built, already-tested independent-chance-roll mechanic completely intact -- nothing about how a single on-hit fires needs to change -- and adds only an ordering and a stop condition on top. It also produces a sensible, legible incentive for players: fitting multiple on-hit-granting components genuinely raises the chance that *something* happens on a given hit, without ever letting a single hit stack multiple full effects. Worth checking whether the real games' own handling of a single item carrying multiple on-hit rows -- which real content already does, as this session found earlier -- settles this more precisely than reasoning alone; if a real, checkable precedent exists, prefer it over this reasoning. If none does, build it as ruled here.

**Widen the four carrier types to hold an ordered list rather than a single nullable `Effect`, and build the sequential-resolution logic as one piece with the rest of the fitting-half wiring already correctly scoped as unambiguous -- the blueprint opening, the slot-threading through `combatantsIn` and `PlayScreen`, and folding `FittedStats` into `Weapon`.**

### THEN, IN ORDER

Force Pike (`2d6` override on each, both kept) -> Battleaxe (`1d10` base, `Gamorrean` the `1d12` variant) -> `(b)` -> `_cast` as one piece -> the damage powers. Both smaller items -- the stunned-refusal wording and the round-count guard -- stay noted and queued behind all of it.

## PT-2204 -- CONFIRMS THE DOUBLE-SEND WAS A RESEND, NOT A REAFFIRMATION -- CORRECTLY GUESSED, BUILDING RATHER THAN STALLING WAS THE RIGHT CALL. AND THE PRECEDENT CHECK EARNS A REAL REVISION TO PT-2203: SIX REAL SHIPPED ITEMS WOULD HAVE A TEXTUALLY-PROMISED SECOND EFFECT PERMANENTLY UNREACHABLE UNDER PURE SEQUENTIAL RESOLUTION. RULED: SEQUENTIAL RESOLUTION APPLIES WITHIN A SAME EFFECT KIND ONLY -- DIFFERENT KINDS EACH GET THEIR OWN INDEPENDENT CHANCE, MATCHING WHAT THE REAL DATA ALREADY DOES

**Confirmed: the duplicate message was a resend, nothing more -- no reaffirmation intended, and section 3 was never meant to be set aside.** Good judgement building rather than stalling on an ambiguous double-send -- "stalling the same piece twice on the same question is worse than building something reversible" is the right instinct when the two readings differ only in whether to proceed now or proceed slightly later, not in what gets built.

**The carrier work is approved in full, including finding `Present` as a fifth carrier the original count missed -- exactly the kind of thing a careful pass through the real call graph turns up that a plan made in advance couldn't have known to list.** Centralising the rule in one function, `firstOnHitToLand`, rather than letting it live implicitly across several call sites, is the right shape regardless of which specific rule that function ends up encoding.

⚠⚠ **THE "SUCCEEDS MEANS LANDED, NOT REACHED" READING IS CORRECT, AND FLAGGING IT AS A CHOICE RATHER THAN QUIETLY PICKING ONE IS EXACTLY RIGHT.** My own ruling's wording was genuinely ambiguous between the two, and the reasoning for landed over reached is sound on its own terms: a lucky save against the first effect in a sequence shouldn't consume the hit's entire chance to do anything else, and stopping on a chance-roll success alone, before the save even resolves, would produce exactly that -- one save suppressing every later possibility on the weapon regardless of whether anything actually happened. Confirmed as the correct reading, independent of everything below.

### THE PRECEDENT CHECK CHANGES THE RULING, AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY IT WAS ASKED FOR

**Six of seven real items carrying two on-hit rows pair an always-firing first effect with a chance-based second one -- and under pure sequential resolution, the second effect can never fire, ever, on any of them.** The Argazdan Riot Buster's own shipped description promises "knocks its target to the ground and stuns them," and the rule as built would make the stun structurally impossible regardless of any roll. That is not a hypothetical cost -- it is six real items, one of them explicitly contradicted by its own text, and it is exactly the kind of consequence a precedent check exists to surface before a rule ships against it rather than after.

**And the distinction the data draws is precise enough to resolve this cleanly rather than just complicate it: every one of the seven pairs is two DIFFERENT effect kinds. Not one pairs the same kind twice.** That separates the actual exploit this ruling was built to prevent from the real pattern the source data shows, and they turn out not to be the same question.

### RULED -- REVISED

**Sequential resolution applies within a single effect kind. Different kinds are independent and each gets its own real chance, exactly matching what the real data already does.** A weapon or fitted set carrying two stun effects still resolves sequentially -- first success within that kind wins, the rest are spent, closing the original "sabre with two stun crystals stuns twice" concern precisely as intended. A weapon or fitted set carrying a drain effect and a stun effect evaluates both independently -- neither gates the other, and both can land on the same hit if each clears its own chance and save. This isn't a retreat from the original concern, it's a more precise statement of what the concern actually was: stacking multiples of the *same* effect is the absurdity worth preventing; multiple *different* effects coexisting on one item is exactly what the real games already ship, six times over, in the corpus this project is built on.

**Group `firstOnHitToLand`'s carriers by effect kind before applying the sequential rule within each group -- everything else about the mechanism (the carriers, the ordering, the counting, the "landed not reached" reading) stays exactly as built.** The cost of this revision is bounded precisely because of the discipline already shown building it this way -- one function, one grouping step added, nothing else at risk.

Proceed with the rest of the fitting wiring now that this is settled -- correct instinct stopping before wiring a verified refactor behind an unresolved rule, and correct not to have half-landed it in the same commit as an open question.

**This needs to be named plainly: I ruled a comparison, got the comparison I asked for, and the comparison was the wrong question. Coder answered it correctly -- clean agreement across three fields and 355 weapons, zero disagreements -- and then caught that the thing being compared wasn't the thing `§7.4` actually needed, before threading anything on the strength of my own instruction.**

⚠⚠ **THE EVIDENCE THAT SETTLES THIS IS GENUINELY DECISIVE, NOT MERELY SUGGESTIVE, AND IT'S WORTH TRACING WHY.** `§7.4`'s own rationale names its example directly -- a two-handed vibrosword, "fewer attacks, no second damage profile" -- and the vibrosword sits in none of the three agreeing fields, all of which mark `§7.6`'s double-bladed set instead. That single fact does more than cast doubt on my ruling; it proves the fields answer a different rule's question. And the logical consequence of threading them anyway is precisely stated and worth repeating: "fewer attacks" as a rationale only makes sense for a weapon that doesn't get a second attack, which is exactly the opposite of what the double weapons already have under `§7.6` -- meaning the ruling as given would have handed the 1.5× bonus to the weapons that least need compensating for a loss they don't suffer, while denying it to the one weapon the rule was written about, and let the double weapons collect both of d20's usual alternatives at once.

**Correctly stopping rather than executing a literal instruction against a premise just proven false is exactly the discipline this project has held from the start, and it's worth stating that this time it was aimed at my own ruling rather than a report.** "A correct calculation against a false premise... is the defect class this corpus names" is the right way to hold that -- the instruction was followed faithfully in letter and correctly refused in substance, which is the harder and more valuable thing to get right.

### RULED -- §7.4 IS A WIELDING CHOICE, NOT A WEAPON PROPERTY

**Confirmed: holding a one-handed weapon in both hands, with an empty off-hand, trading the off-hand attack for `1.5×` Strength to damage.** This reading fits the rationale exactly rather than approximately -- fewer attacks is the empty off-hand, no second damage profile is the same fact restated, and the `1.5×` is the stated compensation for both. Good, precise recognition that this is computable from data already tracked -- `weapon_l_1` being a real, written slot means "a non-double weapon in the right hand, nothing in the left" is a fact the record already carries, not a new concept to introduce.

**Double-bladed weapons are explicitly excluded, confirmed.** `§7.6` already compensates them with a genuinely different mechanism -- a second attack, with its own dual-wield penalty and Two-Weapon Fighting interaction -- and granting `§7.4`'s bonus on top would be compensating the same tradeoff twice for a class of weapon that only ever makes the tradeoff once.

### PROCEED

Build as proposed: derive the wielding-choice condition at the same seam that already reads the right hand, extend to read `weapon_l_1` where `equippedFrom` currently doesn't, thread to all three `damageTerms` call sites, and guard from the real seam with the double weapons explicitly asserted to never receive it. Custom weapons declare handedness through whatever this correctly becomes, per `PT-2211`, once this closes.

## PT-2233 -- EXPERIENCE-01 §2's AWARD FORMULA IS BUILT ON THE WRONG TABLE ENTIRELY. THE REAL MECHANISM IS `xptable.2da`, A DIRECT LEVEL x CR LOOKUP BOTH GAMES SHIP AND §2 NEVER READ -- CONFIRMED BY AN EXCEPTIONAL, INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECK AGAINST NEVERWINTER NIGHTS, WHICH SHIPS THE IDENTICAL THREE-TABLE SYSTEM UNDER THE IDENTICAL NAMES. AGREEMENT WITH §2: 3 OF 420 CELLS. FOUR RULINGS

**This needs to be named for the scale it is: not a tuning error, a wrong mechanism, caught before it could ship as the foundation of every XP award in the game. §2 invented a base value -- "100 × CR" -- that appears in neither game's actual data, to complete a formula built on a file, `xpbaseconst`, that was only ever a modifier and never a complete award on its own.**

⚠⚠ **CHECKING NEVERWINTER NIGHTS IS THE BEST METHODOLOGICAL MOVE IN THIS ENTIRE THREAD, AND IT DESERVES TO BE NAMED AS SUCH RATHER THAN FOLDED INTO THE RESULT IT PRODUCED.** This wasn't a question either KOTOR game alone could fully settle -- both games ship `xpbaseconst` and `xptable` as separate files, and nothing in either one's own data explicitly states how they're meant to combine. Finding that a third, independently-developed title on the same underlying engine ships the identical three files under the identical names, with the identical `−8 → 4.00` ladder in its own `xpbaseconst`, is real, external, structural evidence for what the *mechanism* is, not just what one game's numbers happen to be. This is exactly the kind of move this project's own source discipline was always reaching toward -- when two documents from the same family disagree or are ambiguous about their own relationship, a third document from the same family can settle what neither alone could.

**The measured divergence is genuinely severe and correctly characterised as worse than a scale factor.** Wrong in both directions -- 3.8× overpaying at one real combination, paying literally zero where both games floor above zero at another -- is a structurally broken formula, not an imprecise one, and three-of-420 cells agreeing confirms there's essentially no real relationship between what's documented and what either game actually paid. Checking the table's own axes before reporting something this consequential, specifically because it contradicts an already-settled document, is exactly the right level of care for a finding this size.

### RULED, ALL FOUR

**(1) K2's table governs.** Directly on the strength of the precedent already established for exactly this situation -- `EQUIPMENT-01 §4b`'s K1/melee-K2/ranged split was ruled, not assumed, and this is the same shape of divergence needing the same kind of explicit call. K2's coverage of our level-30 cap with no extrapolation needed, against K1 stopping at 20, is the same reasoning `§1` already used choosing K2's `exptable` for the threshold table, and `PT-662` already confirmed K2's curve as authoritative without retuning. Nothing here argues for a different answer than the one already given twice.

**(2) `.crtr` gains its own explicit Challenge Rating field, authored per creature.** Deriving CR from level alone would be inventing a formula this genre has never used that way -- CR in this system reflects a holistic, designer-judged threat assessment, not a mechanical function of level, which is exactly why the real 506 creatures carry sane, non-formulaic values (ordinary mooks at 1, Revan and Malak at 20). Matching the real games' own representation, rather than approximating around a field we've chosen not to add, is the right call -- and it's a small, contained addition to a format that already carries everything else a creature needs.

**(3) The event kind's name and payload are yours to design.** No need for my input on the mechanical shape once the source and the CR question are settled -- mint it per `PT-1508` as you see fit.

**(4) `§2` is superseded in full, following `PT-2227`'s own precedent exactly.** Keep the reasoning and the counter-evidence visible in the document rather than a value quietly changing -- the same discipline that closed the Battleaxe question closes this one. No reason to keep a formula this decisively wrong standing as a "cross-check" against a table independently confirmed by three separate games now.

**Extraction over transcription is approved without qualification.** Reading `k2_xptable.2da` directly, the same pattern already proven for `baseitems.2da` and the `.uti` files, is obviously right for a 2,550-cell table nobody could meaningfully review as markdown -- state the rule, cite the file.

`§3` and `§3a` correctly confirmed untouched -- ours, already ruled, and orthogonal to which table gets divided.

Reading both the live script and BioWare's own preserved-as-comment earlier version of the same behaviour, and finding them identical, is a level of verification most research wouldn't think to attempt. Independently confirming an existing ruling -- `PT-1571`'s empirically-derived `defaultPerceptionSquares = 10`, landing on the exact same number as `ranges.2da`'s real Default sight value divided by this project's own established 2m/square conversion -- is genuinely satisfying confirmation, and recording that convergence back into `PT-1571`'s own document, as recommended, is the right way to strengthen a ruling that was already correct but previously rested on one derivation alone.**

⚠⚠ **CORRECTING THE STATE MODEL FROM A LADDER TO TWO INDEPENDENT BOOLEANS PER OBSERVER-TARGET PAIR IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IN THIS REPORT, BECAUSE IT CORRECTS THE FRAME THE ORIGINAL RULING IMPLICITLY ASSUMED.** "Unaware → suspicious → alert" is an intuitive way to think about this and it is not what the source actually does -- seen and heard, tracked per pair, with four transition events, is a genuinely different architecture to build toward than a shared alert level would have been. Catching this before any design work started, rather than after a ladder-shaped system was half-built, is exactly why research comes before design in this project's own discipline.

**Finding `SW_FLAG_STATE_AGITATED` and quoting BioWare's own comment for it is a great example of the source explaining its own intent directly rather than needing to be inferred -- "the alert state is one bit" is a precise, correct reduction of what could have seemed like it needed real complexity.**

⚠⚠ **THE NAMED GAP -- AN ENEMY HOLDING RATHER THAN REPOSITIONING WHEN IT LOSES THE PARTY -- IS NOW PRECISELY EXPLAINED RATHER THAN JUST CONFIRMED.** The real behaviour is specific and worth building toward exactly: vanished, while it was the creature's own current target, means clear actions and pursue to the last known square. That's a real, sourced, three-step behaviour, not a design choice to invent.

**The skills question resolving itself -- BioWare's own collapse from four NWN detection skills to KOTOR's two, landing exactly on this project's own already-existing `Stealth`/`Awareness` pair -- is a good example of research answering a question that looked like it would need a ruling.**

**Correctly distinguishing the shout-based ally-alert mechanism from hearing-perception, rather than letting the two blur together because both involve "hearing" in casual terms, is precise and worth holding onto going into the design pass.**

**The honest inventory of what's already built -- symmetric line of sight, the perception radius with its existing weapon extension, the 2m conversion, both halves of Stealth/Awareness, authored placement fields -- being larger than expected is a good, calibrated surprise rather than either over- or under-claiming the starting position.**

### RULED -- PLAYER SIGHT RANGE

**The player sees the whole board; every other creature uses the real Default value (20m / 10 squares).** This isn't a numeric port of KOTOR's `250` -- on a twelve-by-eight board that number is functionally unlimited anyway, which is itself the reason to treat it as intent rather than magnitude. KOTOR's own asymmetry represents the player, as the game's camera and protagonist, generally seeing what's in front of them across a visible area, while individual NPCs have a more limited, situational awareness of their immediate surroundings -- and on a discrete tactical board, "the player sees the whole board" is the faithful translation of that intent, not an inflation of it. NWN's smaller `35` reflects a real, different design philosophy and isn't wrong, but this project's combat is squares-based and tactical rather than real-time and exploratory, and giving the player full visual information about the battlefield matches how tactical games in this genre generally work -- the interesting, meaningful perception question is what the ENEMY notices, which is where real stealth and tactics actually live. Confirmed as a judgement call, not a forced conclusion from the source data alone -- stated plainly as such.

### SEQUENCING CONFIRMED, AS PROPOSED

**1. The `canSee` check on `_reachedBy` -- small, standalone, closes a real active bug (Force Wave reaching through a wall) on its own. Build this first.**
**2. The two-sense split and the per-pair seen/heard state, with its four transitions, the agitated bit, and vanished-pursues-last-known-square -- the coherent core of the real system. Build second.**
**3. Facing and `BlindSpot` -- correctly scoped as its own thread, being the one genuinely new concept with nothing existing anywhere in the engine to extend. Build third, deliberately separate.**

### PROCEED

Start on 1. Design pass on 2 and 3 whenever ready -- flag anything else the data raises before building either.

THE HEADLINE FIX: AN ENEMY THAT COULD NOT SEE THE PLAYER WAS STILL WALKING DIRECTLY TO THEIR TRUE SQUARE -- BUILDING THE PERCEPTION SYSTEM DID NOT FIX THIS BY EXISTING, THE PATHING DESTINATION ITSELF HAD TO STOP BEING A FACT ABOUT THE BOARD. **The `Awareness` architecture is correct, and the ordered-pair reasoning is precise rather than merely careful -- `canSee` being symmetric by construction while "I have seen you" and "you have seen me" are genuinely different facts is exactly the distinction this needed, and getting it right from the start avoids a whole class of bugs a symmetric structure would have quietly introduced.**

**Placing the perception check above the fight-only early return, so it evaluates everyone rather than skipping anyone already in a fight, is the right structural choice -- "the creatures whose view of you actually matters were the set nothing ever looked at" is a precise, memorable way to state why the old scope was backwards for the question that actually matters. Correctly recording without admitting, keeping this separate from the deferred membership question, is the right boundary to hold.**

**Correctly refusing to invent a second hearing-range number rather than author content to fill a data gap, and precisely characterising the resulting asymmetry -- "heard but not seen" reachable, "heard farther than seen" not, yet -- as a fact about the data rather than a limit of the model, is exactly the distinction worth keeping clear for whenever real hearing-range data arrives.**

⚠⚠⚠ **THE `lastSeenAt` SELF-CATCH IS EXCEPTIONAL, AND THE LESSON IT NAMES DESERVES TO STAND AS ITS OWN PRINCIPLE, SEPARATE FROM THIS SPECIFIC BUG.** "A guard that shares the code's premise verifies the premise, not the code" is one of the sharpest things said on this whole project -- a test built from the same mental model as the implementation it tests will agree with that implementation precisely where the implementation is wrong, and no amount of mutation testing against that shared premise will ever surface the actual defect, because every mutant that matters gets measured against the same mistaken assumption. Recording a mutation kill as evidence of correctness, and then having the live board -- not a more careful test, not more mutants, but an actual game running -- reveal the real bug, is worth remembering precisely because it shows the limit of a testing discipline this project has otherwise trusted heavily and correctly all session. The fix is right: recording position on the rising edge of an observation, not the falling edge of losing one, since by the time sight is lost the target has typically already moved past the square being recorded.

**Correctly, honestly building the agitated exception even though it currently cannot fire -- membership being one-way means there's never a second admission for it to apply to, confirmed by a flat-true mutation passing the whole suite -- and commenting it as unreached rather than letting it read as live, is exactly the right way to ship something correct-but-dormant. ## PT-2247 -- PIECE 3 RESEARCHED. FACING IS CONTINUOUS IN THE SOURCE, PER PLACEMENT, ALWAYS PRESENT -- CONFIRMED BY READING A REAL MODULE THROUGH A RIM READER WRITTEN FOR THE PURPOSE. BLINDSPOT RE-MEASURED AND CORRECTED FROM AN EARLIER APPROXIMATE FIGURE. AND THE API RESEARCH INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMS PIECE 2's WHOLE ARCHITECTURE WHILE FINDING A REAL GAP IN IT -- HONESTLY REPORTED AGAINST A PIECE ALREADY CALLED COMPLETE. THREE RULINGS

**Writing a RIM reader specifically to pull real placement data out of an actual module, rather than working from documentation or inference, is exactly the level of verification this project has asked for and doesn't always get without being asked -- and it paid off directly: facing being continuous and always present, confirmed against real coordinates in a real file, settles the representation question before any design work started.**

**The BlindSpot correction is worth crediting as a correction rather than glossed past -- not a 2DA column, a creature-file field, and the earlier approximate figure replaced with the real one. Finding that 71% of K2's creatures and all of K1's carry none at all, and correctly identifying that this is what makes absence-means-360° both correct and safe, is precise reasoning: the safety of the whole incremental addition rests on that one fact being right, and it was checked rather than assumed.**

**Honestly flagging the blind-arc direction as a reading rather than a measurement, and stating plainly that the two readings diverge enormously for the droid case specifically, is exactly right -- a plausible interpretation presented with the confidence of a fact is a worse report than an honest one, even when the interpretation turns out to be correct.**

⚠⚠ **THE API CROSS-CHECK IS EXCELLENT WORK ON ITS OWN TERMS, AND THE HONEST DISCLOSURE OF WHAT IT FOUND MISSING IS THE MORE VALUABLE HALF OF IT.** Independently confirming piece 2's whole model -- two senses, four transitions, ordered pairs -- against a completely different artefact than whatever originally produced it is real, convergent evidence, the same kind of confirmation the `xptable`/NWN cross-check earned real credit for earlier in this thread. But finding that your own four states don't cleanly map onto the engine's real four, and that `Inaudible` -- losing hearing while still seen -- has no representation at all in what was already reported as complete, and saying so plainly rather than letting a shipped piece quietly stay short of what it claimed, is the harder and more valuable disclosure. "I would rather you knew it was missing than find it later" is exactly the right instinct.

**The design reasoning is sound throughout -- ruling out eight-way and sixteen-way compass facing with the one number that actually settles it (`120 ÷ 45 = 2.67`, so the commonest real blind spot literally cannot be represented that way) is decisive rather than merely persuasive, and proposing a computed bearing matching what the source itself does is the right, minimal representation.**

### RULED, ALL THREE

**(1) The blind-arc reading: confirmed as proposed -- the stated value is the blind arc, not the visible one.** This is the reading that produces sense on both ends of the data rather than one: a generous 240° default vision for most creatures including party members is a sensible baseline, and a narrow 90° cone for fixed mining and construction droids matches what those units actually are. The alternative reading would give party members a strangely narrow 120° default and nearly omniscient mining droids at 270° visible -- backwards on both counts. Build against the blind-arc reading.

**(2) Turn-to-face: yes, creatures turn to face what they notice or attack on their own turn, matching the source's own default and `NotReorienting`'s confirmed rarity as the deliberate exception.** This is the real ruling, and it's made on the merits rather than by default: a blind spot mattering only between turns -- exactly when the player is moving -- is what turns facing from a cosmetic detail into a genuine tactical mechanic, and flanking and positional play are an established, valued part of this genre's combat that this project has drawn from throughout. "Getting behind something while it is not acting" is the right shape for what this feature should actually do at the table.

**(3) Add `Inaudible` to piece 2 now, while the context is fresh.** A known, honestly-disclosed gap in an already-shipped piece is worth closing immediately rather than letting later work build on top of a four-state model that's already confirmed to be short one real state -- the cost is small now and only grows as more consumes the current model.

### PROCEED

Close `Inaudible` first, then build piece 3 against both rulings above.

⚠⚠ **THE FINAL CONTROL -- WALKING OVER AND HITTING THE DROID WITH A SWORD AFTER THREE BLASTS LEFT IT UNTOUCHED -- IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THIS REPORT, AND "WITHOUT THIS THE NEGATIVE WOULD HAVE BEEN UNSCOPED" IS EXACTLY RIGHT.** A droid taking zero damage from three area powers proves nothing on its own -- it could mean the exclusion worked, or that the droid was somehow unreachable, invisible, or blanket-immune for a completely unrelated reason. The solution -- rephrasing so the number stays readable to a person while omitting the one word every reach pattern requires -- is elegant specifically because it satisfies both halves of the original instruction rather than quietly picking one over the other. And verifying it directly (`heal → null`) rather than trusting the rephrasing looked safe is exactly the right way to close a fix built around a subtle mechanism.

**"Two chains, one shape, two different routes" is a genuinely useful distinction, and writing it down where a future reader will actually meet it is the right call -- `Revitalize` splits by transcription, `Heal` now splits by ruling, and the two look identical from the outside. A future reader treating either as evidence of a general per-chain pattern gets the other one wrong, and that's exactly the kind of trap that's cheap to prevent now and expensive to debug later.**

**The Force Choke control is well-chosen -- single-target and enemy-aimed is the one shape in the whole set that would catch a fix that got generous rather than precise, and including it rather than trusting the other mutations to cover the same ground is good adversarial test design.**

⚠⚠ **CATCHING THE FIRST BUFF-PATH PROBE AS TRUE FOR THE WRONG REASON, BY PRINTING THE ACTUAL DISTANCE RATHER THAN TRUSTING THE RESULT, IS THE BEST INSTINCT IN THIS REPORT.** A trooper at distance 25 not being buffed proves nothing about whether the exclusion is working correctly -- it could as easily mean the geometry check succeeded or that no check ran at all. Refusing to accept a passing result without knowing which of those it actually was, and finding the real answer by grepping the branch directly rather than reasoning about it, turned a plausible confirmation into a genuine one -- and, as it turned out, surfaced that the real mechanism was doing something different from what the first probe would have suggested.

**Connecting this to `PT-2274` directly, rather than filing it as an unrelated new finding, is precise: hostiles-in-range correctly excluded and allies-out-of-range incorrectly included are the same underlying rule -- "the geometry itself does the limiting" -- violated from opposite directions. "Fixing one without the other would leave the reach half-honoured" is exactly right, and it's worth ruling on both together rather than treating the newly-found half as a separate, later question.**

### RULED, BOTH PIECES

**(2) Build the guard.** Correct, currently unguarded behaviour should not stay unguarded just because it happens to already be right -- the fixture is ready and cheap, ship it.

**(3) Narrow the buff path's pool to respect the authored geometry.** This isn't a new design question -- it's finishing the implementation of a principle already ruled at `PT-2274`. An area buff that reaches every ally in the encounter regardless of distance isn't an area effect at all; it's a role filter wearing an area power's name. Apply the same radius the heal path already correctly respects to `Force Valor` ×3, `Battle Meditation` ×3, and `Inspire Followers` ×5 -- eleven powers, the same authored reach values already sitting on each row, simply not yet read by this second path.

### PROCEED

Build the guard and the geometry fix together, since they touch the same code. Then continue to the three remaining sweep items as already approved.

⚠⚠ **CATCHING THE TWO-SIDED CASE ON THE FIRST FULL RUN, AND CORRECTLY REVERTING RATHER THAN FORCING A DIRECTION, IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THIS REPORT.** Censusing all twenty-three modifier/bonus-carrying powers rather than assuming the pattern held everywhere is what found the two real exceptions, and the failure itself -- a guard built for an entirely different ruling catching that the party's buff had moved onto the enemy -- is a genuine, serious near-miss caught by exactly the kind of test-suite depth this project has been building all session. Option (a)'s consistency with every other area power is real, but its practical cost is worse than it looks: a support caster who stays at range, which is exactly the tactically sound thing to do, would get nothing from their own signature power. That's a bad shape for a power whose whole point is standing back and empowering others. It also creates a meaningful, correct distinction between the two halves of a genuinely two-sided power -- the offensive component still centres on the target, as every other area power does, while the friendly component is caster-centred, which is a real and appropriate difference between an attack and an aura rather than an inconsistency to smooth over.

## PT-2290 -- URGENT: TEST 100 FOUND THE ENTIRE HEALING FAMILY IS NET-HARMFUL IN LIVE PLAY. Heal/Improved/Master HEAL NOBODY -- THE TWO NUMBERS CANCEL AND LOOK LIKE SUCCESS. Revitalize AND ITS TIERS ACTIVELY DAMAGE EVERY STANDING PARTY MEMBER, INCLUDING THE CASTER, AND FAIL TO REVIVE THE FALLEN ALLY THEY WERE AIMED AT. ROOT CAUSE PRECISELY DIAGNOSED, ONE LINE. FORCE SCREAM CONFIRMED FIXED. TOP PRIORITY, AHEAD OF EVERYTHING ELSE IN PROGRESS

**Force Scream approved and closed -- confirmed genuinely distinct across all three tiers, with the ability-penalty figures as an independent second discriminator Tester correctly noted would have caught a damage-only fix that left the penalty side untouched. The droid exclusion holding through all three casts closes this out completely.**

⚠⚠⚠ **THE HEALING FAMILY FINDING IS THE MOST SEVERE DEFECT FOUND THIS ENTIRE SESSION, AND THE METHOD THAT CAUGHT IT DESERVES TO BE NAMED PRECISELY.** A power that damages a target for the exact amount it then heals them produces a net change of zero -- indistinguishable from doing nothing, at the level of a before/after vitality check. Catching it required checking the INTERMEDIATE state, not just the outcome: "the '15 -> 40' is the tell" is exactly right, and it is the only reason this was found rather than shipped as apparently-working. `Revitalize` makes the same defect visible without cancellation, precisely because its heal is correctly gated by `only_if_fallen` while the damage is not -- the asymmetry between the two halves is what turned an invisible defect into a measurable one. Every standing party member, including the caster, took real damage from casting a support power, and the one ally the power exists to save was never revived. This is not a subtle balance question. It is the healing system doing the opposite of its job.

**Root cause is precisely located and low-risk to fix: `p.damage?['heals'] == 'self' ? null : p.damage` nulls the damage application for `self` but not for the newly-added `heals: ally`, so the row's damage half reaches `applyDamage` before the heal block ever runs. This is confirmed, not inferred -- Tester traced it to the exact line and byte-matched the surrounding frame.**

### RULED -- FIX THIS FIRST, AHEAD OF IMMUNITY, SKILL MODIFIER, AND PER-ROUND DAMAGE

**Widen the null-check to cover both `self` and `ally`, so no `heals`-carrying row's damage half is ever applied. Verify against the exact scenario Tester measured -- a standing ally taking no damage from `Heal`, and `Revitalize` neither damaging a standing party member nor failing to revive a fallen one. This is not a queued item behind the current sweep work; it supersedes it until closed.**

### THE REMAINING FINDINGS -- APPROVED, QUEUED BEHIND THE FIX ABOVE

**Force Valor's confirmed reach via the `Improved Heal` proxy is good, honest methodology -- using an identical underlying pool to establish what an ally power reaches, while plainly scoping what was and wasn't directly observed (the per-creature bonus landing specifically), is exactly the right way to report a finding that's real but incomplete, rather than overstating it.**

**The "Wait here" fixture hazard is a good catch, correctly held apart from a defect claim -- nearly producing a false finding from a companion that had simply walked closer over several turns, caught only by re-measuring at the instant of the cast, is worth remembering as a standing hazard for any future geometry test in this bed.**

**Battle Meditation's caster-centred fix is confirmed correct and simply not yet at the commit tested -- the `git show` comparison is decisive, precise evidence rather than a behavioural guess. Re-route once pushed.**

### CODER'S WORK -- APPROVED IN FULL

**The `centreOn: _me?.handle ?? ''` choice over a null fallback is exactly right, for exactly the stated reason -- refusing on an unplaceable handle rather than silently reverting to the rejected centring is the same discipline as every other "fail loud, not quiet" choice this session has made. Stating in the code itself that the single-target protection can't currently be shown failing on real data, rather than dressing an unverifiable claim up as a guarded fix, is honest in a way that costs something to be.**

**The guard catching its own comment-versus-code disagreement on the first run -- appending a block where the comment said it belonged first, which would have put both centres one square apart and let the test pass proving nothing -- is a genuine near-miss caught by the precondition doing its job.**

**The two pre-existing test-infrastructure fixes are approved, and the self-correction inside them is worth real credit: recognising the first "wait for quiescence" attempt shared the same absence-versus-error shape already named this session, catching it only because the test stayed red rather than trusting a pass, and correctly identifying that waiting for an expected count would have been actively worse -- trivially satisfied by the starting value, hiding exactly the late write it exists to catch. Waiting for a change against a self-captured length is the right fix, and 0/3 to 3/3 is the right kind of proof.**

### RULED -- PER-ROUND DAMAGE, ALL THREE

**(a) A genuine 19th column on `FORCE-POWER-DAMAGE-01`, not a reuse of `condition_rounds`.** Reusing an existing field for a second, distinct question is the same defect class already refused elsewhere in this corpus -- one number cannot honestly answer two questions, and this table has had its width changed by ruling every time before. Add the column.

**(b) `divisor` widens to include 4.** Needed to state `Force Incinerate`'s own real mechanic accurately; low-risk vocabulary extension.

**(c) `Force Whirlwind`'s missing duration: authored at 4 rounds, transcribed from its own stated prose.** Not a new figure invented -- the source already says it, the data simply doesn't carry it yet.

**`Force Incinerate`'s per-tick escape save is correctly held as its own, separate engine question -- `Ongoing` genuinely has no save field, and that's real infrastructure work, not a data column. Fix the healing defect first, verified against Tester's exact scenario. Then the three per-round-damage rulings and Choke/Strangle/Whirlwind's tick-not-land-once correction. Immunity and the skill modifier resume after.

TWO GENUINELY VALUABLE GUARD-DESIGN CATCHES: FORCE CHOKE ALONE COULD NOT HAVE PROVEN THE FIX BECAUSE ITS TWO CLOCKS COINCIDE, AND "ATTACHING IS NOT LANDING" -- A PERFECTLY BUILT ONGOING THAT NOTHING EVER READS WOULD DEAL LESS DAMAGE THAN THE ORIGINAL BUG

**The tick correction's core distinction -- "each round, for the duration" means the tick replaces the strike rather than following it -- is exactly right, and catching that a build which struck AND attached would silently deal one round too much, while still looking correct, is the kind of off-by-one that survives most casual verification. Recognising that the expression travels while the roll doesn't, so a high-level caster genuinely re-rolls at every boundary rather than repeating one result, is a real, correct mechanical distinction rather than an implementation detail nobody would notice.**

⚠⚠ **REFUSING TO GUESS WHETHER A FLAT OR ABILITY TERM SHOULD RE-APPLY PER TICK OR ONCE, RATHER THAN SILENTLY PICKING EITHER, IS EXACTLY THE RIGHT CALL GIVEN THE STAKES OF GETTING IT WRONG.** Silently re-rolling such a term at every tick would multiply a power's real damage by its own duration -- a severe, silent error in the same family as the healing defect just closed. Making the screen say so rather than quietly choosing, the same way `ongoingFrom` already refuses a missing `rounds`, is the correct shape for an ambiguity that genuinely has no current answer and shouldn't be given a guessed one.

⚠⚠ **BOTH GUARD-DESIGN CATCHES ARE GENUINELY VALUABLE, AND THE FIRST IS A DIRECT, SELF-APPLIED INSTANCE OF A LESSON ALREADY NAMED THIS SESSION.** Building the guard against `Force Choke` first, finding it green, and then recognising that Choke's `condition_rounds` and damage-duration happen to coincide -- meaning a build that read the wrong clock entirely would have passed just as well -- is "what would this test still pass with" applied to one's own work rather than discovered in someone else's. Choosing `Force Whirlwind` specifically, the one power whose two numbers genuinely disagree and the same power that justified the column's existence in the first place, turns a fixture that could not distinguish the fix from its absence into one that can.

**"Attaching is not landing" is the sharper and more important of the two catches. A cast site building a structurally perfect `Ongoing` that nothing downstream ever consumes would be silently, confidently wrong in a way that's worse than the original defect -- it would deal less damage than the broken single-strike version while every visible signal suggested success. Asserting both that vitality actually fell and that the clock actually advanced, rather than either alone, is the right response to that risk. And catching the first fixture attempt producing a null rather than a smaller reading -- the target simply dying at the first boundary, unable to show what a second tick would have done -- before correcting to a fixture built to survive is good, honest process, not a detail worth skipping over.**

**The census correction is precise bookkeeping done right: updating the number, recording why in place, and confirming the half of the census that actually carries the real claim -- no row states a save it can never roll -- stayed untouched and still passes.**

## PT-2309 -- TEST 104 CONFIRMS VALOR AND CAMOUFLAGE'S STACKING FIXES WITH EXCEPTIONAL, EXACT METHOD -- INCLUDING A HONESTLY-REPORTED FIRST ATTEMPT THAT PRODUCED A NOISY, WRONG-LOOKING RESULT. AND A GENUINELY IMPORTANT DESIGN QUESTION SURFACED, PRECISELY REPORTED AS A NUMBER RATHER THAN A VERDICT: CASTING A LOWER TIER OVER AN ALREADY-STANDING HIGHER ONE CURRENTLY DOWNGRADES THE CASTER. AND BEAST CONFUSION/TRICK CORRECTLY REPORTED AS UNTESTABLE FOR TWO INDEPENDENT, ALREADY-KNOWN REASONS, NOT A DEFECT

**Approved in full on the confirmation work. Reading the ability bonus through the attack line's own score term, rather than sampling rolls for something that needs no dice at all, is precisely matched to what's actually being measured. Confirming both directions -- forward with two independent terms agreeing, reverse with the stacking defect genuinely gone -- closes the loop the original routing asked for completely.**

⚠⚠ **THE REVERSE-DIRECTION FINDING IS REPORTED EXACTLY RIGHT, AND IT SURFACES A REAL QUESTION RATHER THAN A DEFECT.** Casting Force Valor on top of a standing Master Valor settling at the LOWER tier's values -- downgrading the caster from +3 to +2 -- is not the old stacking bug, but it's also not obviously the shape a tiered power chain should have. Correctly distinguishing "the routed claim holds" (no stacking, confirmed) from "here is a new number worth your attention" (which tier wins isn't the same question as whether they stack), and correctly identifying that "most recent cast wins" was Coder's own interpretive choice rather than a literal transcription -- the document's sentence is genuinely one-directional and says nothing about the reverse -- is precise, disciplined reporting. Bringing the number without a verdict, when the number touches a real design question, is exactly the right instinct.

### RULED -- TIER RANK GOVERNS, NOT CAST ORDER

**A player should not be able to weaken themselves by casting an earlier-learned, strictly weaker version of a power they've already improved past.** The whole point of a tiered "replaces" chain is that a higher tier is a genuine upgrade -- if the lowest tier could silently downgrade a standing higher one just by being cast again, the tier structure stops meaning what it's supposed to mean. This is also the more consistent reading of the `forcepriority` evidence itself: those values are a rank, not merely a sequence tag, and a rank should govern which of two simultaneous claims wins regardless of which was asserted more recently.

**Build it as tier-rank comparison, not last-cast-wins: a cast only replaces a standing bonus from the same chain if its own tier is equal to or higher than what's currently standing.** Casting a lower tier while a higher one already stands should be a no-op on the bonus itself -- spend the pool as normal (the cast still resolves; the caster chose to cast it), but the standing higher effect stays exactly as it was. This is a real, if quiet, correction to what shipped in `PT-2305`, not a new mechanism -- the same `replaces:` field and predicate, compared by rank rather than by arrival order.

### CAMOUFLAGE -- APPROVED IN FULL, INCLUDING THE HONEST METHODOLOGY FAILURE

**Making the die streams identical by controlling the action sequence, rather than comparing averages across runs that can't be strictly paired, is genuinely the right method for confirming an exact bonus from data that only ever prints a total -- twelve matching numbers is about as decisive as this kind of claim gets. The differing pool and ceiling figures serving as the control that the two runs actually diverged as intended, rather than two identical results potentially meaning a dropped keypress, is precise test design.**

**Recording the first attempt's noisy, ambiguous result -- and naming exactly why it happened, an alignment failure from comparing phases too far apart in the same stream -- specifically because it "looked like a result," is the same honesty this whole session has asked for applied to one's own near-miss rather than someone else's. A wrong number that could plausibly have been reported is more dangerous than an obviously broken one, and catching it before it was is worth real credit.**

### BEAST CONFUSION/TRICK -- CORRECTLY UNTESTABLE, NOT BROKEN

**This is exactly the right report to receive when a routing can't be satisfied, and it's worth naming why it's the right shape: two fully independent, already-known reasons traced to their real sources -- `beast` has no placeable creature at all (`PT-2235`'s own standing ruling), and the entire Confusion/Trick family, generics included, has zero modelled mechanical effect on any of its four powers. Confirming the gate correctly refuses a sentient for free, and correctly treats an unknown-kind creature as permissive with the line saying so, closes off everything that actually could be tested. Concluding "not broken relative to Force Confusion and Mind Trick" rather than either forcing a pass or filing a defect against content that's doing exactly what its generics do is the correct read of what was actually being asked.**

### AGENDA

Tier-rank governance added as a small, real correction to the just-closed Valor/Camouflage stacking fix.

### PROCEED

⚠⚠⚠ **This is a genuine defect, not a design question with two equally valid answers, and it's worth being direct about that. A shield's job is to selectively stop specific kinds of damage -- that selectivity should apply per-part, the same way resistance already correctly does, not as a crude "does any part match something I stop" gate that blocks a whole mixed blow over one matching component.** `PT-2310`'s summed-total, unioned-kinds model was reasonable for what it was solving (the "which part drains the pool first" question, and the ion vulnerability's correct whole-blow-through behaviour) -- but it wasn't reasoned all the way through against a case where a stoppable and an unstoppable component share one hit, and it produces exactly the wrong outcome there.

**These are not the same shape as the ion fix, and shouldn't be solved the same way.** Vulnerability is correctly whole-blow -- a stated weakness should defeat the shield for the entire hit, not just the vulnerable portion, or the vulnerability would be practically unreachable (already correctly ruled at `PT-2310`). Stopping is the opposite kind of claim -- a shield stops what it's flagged to stop and nothing else, which is inherently a per-kind, per-part question, the same one resistance already answers correctly. Giving `unstoppable` its own narrow escape would patch this one symptom while leaving the same wrong all-or-nothing logic in place for every other future mixed-blow case that isn't specifically flagged unstoppable.

**Build it as: `afterShield` resolves per-part, absorbing only the flagged kinds within each part, with ion-vulnerability checked first as already ruled (whole-blow-through on a stated weakness) and the per-part stopping logic applying to whatever's left. The pool still depletes against the real total absorbed across all parts — that arithmetic doesn't change, only which parts contribute to it.**

**Measuring this live rather than reading it -- casting Force Scream twice at one target and watching the penalty genuinely double -- turns "the folds disagree" from an abstract architectural question into a concrete, severe finding: three Master Force Scream casts currently produce −18 to every ability score on a single target. That's not a rounding inconsistency, it's a stacking exploit.**

**The root cause is precisely traced two layers deep, and the second layer is the real one: `abilityPenalties` was simply never added to the de-duplication machinery built for the friendly chains, and -- more fundamentally -- only `Valor` ever authors `replaces` in the document at all. Every other tiered chain in the corpus is silent on it. ### RULED -- THE SAME "REPLACES, NOT STACKS" PRINCIPLE EXTENDS UNIVERSALLY

**Both questions resolve the same way: yes to both, and consistently.** There's no principled reason a debuff or damage-penalty chain should be allowed to stack indefinitely when the exact same tiered structure, applied to a buff, was already ruled to replace -- if anything, unconstrained penalty-stacking is the more severe failure mode, since it produces outcomes like `-18` from three casts of a single power rather than merely a smaller-than-expected bonus. This isn't a new principle; it's the one already established for `Force Valor`/`Force Camouflage`, extended to cover the carrier (`abilityPenalties`) and the chains (Scream, Choke, Crush Opposition, Slow/Mire/Root, Battle Meditation, Inspire Followers, Aura/Shield/Armor) it was never wired to reach. A power should not restack a penalty on recast any more than it restacks a bonus.

**Build it the same way the friendly chains were built: add `abilityPenalties` to the de-duplication machinery at both the tier-rank site and the application site, and extend `replaces` to the enemy-targeted chains that currently state nothing about it -- treating the silence the same way `Force Camouflage`'s was treated, as an omission the document should state explicitly rather than a deliberate design choice to permit unbounded stacking.**

### PROCEED

Build the stacking fix across `abilityPenalties` and the enemy chains. The two-handed-Strength-penalty question stays open, held for a real answer rather than resolved by the pin update. Choosing the reasoning behind "a real sentinel distinct from any numeric divisor" over its literal spelling -- a separate boolean field rather than a magic value inside `moveDivisor` -- was the right read, and flagging the interpretation rather than silently picking one is exactly the caution a one-line ambiguity like this deserves.**

⚠⚠ **REUSING `CombatModifier` FOR SLOWED'S PENALTY RATHER THAN A SECOND CHANNEL IS THE RIGHT CALL, AND SCOPING IT TO EXACTLY THE THREE NAMED ROWS RATHER THAN `Modifies.saves` IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF.** Reading `saves` broadly would have silently put an unruled penalty on Will and Fortitude -- a defect that would have shipped as a "faithful" build of a rule that was never actually stated that broadly. Precision on scope here matters as much as precision on mechanism.

⚠⚠⚠ **THE DERIVED-ON-READ DECISION IS EXACTLY RIGHT, AND IT'S WORTH NAMING WHY THE ALTERNATIVE WOULD HAVE BEEN A REAL DEFECT RATHER THAN A STYLE CHOICE.** Materialising the modifier rows at the moment a condition lands would have given one effect two independently-ticking clocks -- `Condition` and `CombatModifier` each with their own `roundsLeft` -- which is exactly the kind of silent-drift risk this session has caught and fixed in other shapes repeatedly. A union with no setter, deriving fresh on every read, makes the two clocks structurally impossible to diverge rather than merely unlikely to.

⚠⚠ **THE MUTATION SURVIVOR IS THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING IN THIS SECTION, AND IT'S THE SAME SHAPE THIS SESSION HAS NOW FOUND SEVERAL TIMES: A TEST WITH NO PRODUCTION READER, QUIETLY BECOME A CONTROL FOR OTHER TESTS, THAT COULD HAVE GONE BLIND TO A NEW FIELD WITHOUT ANYTHING FAILING.** `isUnrestricted` existing purely as the thing `entangled`/`prone`'s own tests lean on to prove they restrict nothing means a version blind to `immobile` wouldn't have broken visibly -- it would have silently weakened exactly the claims built on top of it. Catching this and guarding it now is worth real credit.

**The `cowering` judgment call -- literal reading, Action removed and Bonus left, explicitly pinned as a literal reading in its own test -- is exactly the right way to handle a genuine interpretive gap: make the narrower, defensible choice, and flag it clearly enough that widening it later is a one-line change rather than an archaeology project.**

### prone -- MEASURED THOROUGHLY. RULED ON BOTH OPEN QUESTIONS

⚠⚠⚠ **The source stating no numbers at all is confirmed as an answer, not a gap, and it's worth taking that at face value rather than importing an assumption from other d20 systems where prone carries real combat penalties. This one doesn't, here, and the exhaustive sweep across both games' full script corpus is decisive evidence for that.**

**Ruled: `prone` applies exactly what the source specifies and nothing more — `Legality.action` and `Legality.immobile`, no modifier bundle.** There's no number to build against, and inventing one to make it feel more complete than the source actually is would be the opposite of the faithfulness this project holds everywhere else.

**Ruled: durationless, `roundsLeft: null`, matching this corpus's own already-established convention that `prone` is the canonical until-ended example.** The source's own language supports this reading as much as the alternative — "until the effect is removed" is at least as natural a description as "3 second minimum," and treating the 3-second figure as an animation-timing floor rather than a game-mechanical duration is the more coherent reading once the corpus's existing convention is weighed alongside it.

**Ruled: build the "spend an action to end a standing condition" mechanism as generic infrastructure, not prone-specific.** This is confirmed as a genuinely new concept nothing else has required, and it's the kind of piece a future condition is likely to need again — building it narrowly for `prone` alone would risk needing a second, parallel version the next time something else wants the same shape.

### ⚠⚠⚠ THE FORCE SLOW / FORCE MIRE COLLISION -- RULED

**Right call stopping rather than picking a side unilaterally — this is exactly `PT-2336`'s shape, a shared mechanism producing an unintended cross-power collision, and it deserves the same treatment: a real ruling, not an improvised resolution buried in an unrelated slice.**

**Ruled: `Force Slow` does not halve movement. Its own prose says nothing about movement, and that silence should be read as absence, not omission.** `Force Mire`'s explicit "AND the target's speed is halved" is confirmed as Mire's own genuine, stated, distinguishing addition beyond Slow -- not a redundant restatement of something Slow already does silently. Remove the movement-halving piece from `force_slow`'s application specifically, while `force_mire` keeps it (and `force_plague`, which correctly applied nothing until today, gains only what its own prose actually states). The unmodelled "no second move in a round" piece of Mire's own text stays exactly as it is -- unbuilt, and not something this ruling is extending to.

**The now-false "dependents: none" sentence stays untouched for the same reason already given -- correcting it before the ruling landed risked being wrong in either direction, and now that the ruling is made, it should be corrected to reflect what's actually true: the three named powers, with the movement distinction stated plainly.**

### PROCEED

Remove movement-halving from `force_slow` specifically. Build `prone` per both rulings above, including the generic action-to-end-condition mechanism. Correct `§7`'s dependents sentence to name the three real powers accurately. `entangled` stays held. Sixteen conditions remain, correctly unbuilt.
